This regulation applies if:
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft is not a continuing airworthiness management organisation; and
CASA has not, under regulation 42.235, approved another means of recording the required information for the aircraft.

Note: If the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft is a continuing airworthiness management organisation, the person is required to record the required information for the aircraft in the continuing airworthiness records for the aircraft—see regulation 42.200.
Required information
(2) For this regulation, the required information for an aircraft at a particular time is:
information identifying the next maintenance that is due to be carried out on the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft’s maintenance program; and
when the maintenance is due to be carried out.
Information to be recorded before first flight

(3) The person must ensure that the required information for the aircraft is recorded in the aircraft’s flight technical log before the aircraft is operated for its first flight on or after the responsibility start date for the person and the aircraft (the first flight).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Updating record of required information

If, after the first flight, maintenance is carried out on the aircraft in accordance with the aircraft’s maintenance program, the person must ensure that the record of the required information for the aircraft is updated in the aircraft’s flight technical log before the aircraft is next operated for flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Approval of another means of recording next maintenance due to be carried out

content.p: If the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft is not a continuing airworthiness management organisation, the person may apply, in writing, to CASA for approval of:

a means, other than a flight technical log, of recording the required information for the aircraft (within the meaning given by subregulation 42.230(2)) for the purpose of informing the aircraft’s flight crew of the required information; and
the time within which the required information must be recorded by the other means.

Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve the means if CASA is satisfied that the means is at least as reliable a means of recording the required information for the aircraft as the use of the flight technical log.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.

section.heading: Recording details of next maintenance due to be carried out by approved other means

content.p: If:
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft is not a continuing airworthiness management organisation; and
CASA has, under regulation 42.235, approved:
another means of recording the required information for the aircraft (within the meaning given by subregulation 42.230(2)); and
the time within which the required information must be recorded by the other means;
the person must ensure that the required information for the aircraft is recorded in accordance with the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Ensuring flight technical log can contain utilisation information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight if another means not approved

content.p: If CASA has not, under regulation 42.250, approved:
another means of recording the information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight for an aircraft; and
the time within which the information must be recorded by the other means;
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft must ensure that the aircraft’s flight technical log is capable of containing the information.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

Note: Under subregulation 42.1075(2), the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight must record the information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for the flight in the aircraft’s flight technical log if the log is capable of containing the information.

section.heading: Approval of another means of recording utilisation information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight

content.p: The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft may apply, in writing, to CASA for approval of:
a means, other than a flight technical log, for recording the information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight for the aircraft; and
the time within which the information must be recorded by the other means.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve the means if CASA is satisfied that the means is at least as reliable a means of recording the information as the use of the flight technical log.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.

section.heading: Recording utilisation information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight by approved other means

content.p: If CASA has, under regulation 42.250, approved:
another means of recording the information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight for an aircraft; and
the time within which the information must be recorded by the other means;
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft must ensure that the information is recorded in accordance with the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft must retain a record or document mentioned in an item of the following table for the period:
starting on:

if the person created the record or document, and is the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft on the creation date for the record or document—the creation date for the record or document; or

if the person did not create the record or document, and is the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft on the creation date for the record or document—the date that the person receives the record or document; or

if the person is not the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft on the creation date for the record or document—the date the person receives the continuing airworthiness records for the aircraft under regulation 42.265; and
ending on the first-occurring of the following:
the end date (if any) mentioned in the item;
the date the person gives the records to the person who becomes the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft under regulation 42.265.

tr.td: A document kept under regulation 42.215 for the aircraft
The date that the information substantiated by the document is superseded by other information
A copy of a maintenance record, that is not covered by item 1, for maintenance carried out on the aircraft
1 year after the creation date for the maintenance record
A copy of a document that: (a) is equivalent to a maintenance record for maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and (b) is issued under a law of a foreign country; and (c) is not covered by item 1
1 year after the creation date for the document

A certificate of release to service, or an equivalent document issued in accordance with an NAA arrangement mentioned in regulation 42.301, for the aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft
A record of information: (a) that is made in the flight technical log for an aircraft in accordance with this Part; and (b) that is not covered by item 1, 2 or 4
1 year after the creation date for the record
A copy of the design of a modification or repair that is unique to the aircraft

content.p: Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Example 1: For item 1, an authorised release certificate for an aeronautical product that is fitted to an aircraft must be kept until the date the aeronautical product is removed from the aircraft.
Example 2: For item 1, an in-house release document for an aeronautical product that is fitted to an aircraft must be kept until the date the aeronautical product is removed from the aircraft.

Example 3: For item 1, a document mentioned in paragraph 42.440(e) for an aeronautical product fitted to an aircraft as permitted by regulation 42.440 must be kept until the date the aeronautical product is removed from the aircraft.

Example 4: For item 1, a document that substantiates the empty weight of the aircraft and the centre of gravity position on the aircraft at its empty weight configuration must be kept until the date that the aircraft is next weighed and its empty weight, and its centre of gravity in its empty weight configuration, is determined.
Note: For item 5, see the notes to regulation 42.220.
In this regulation:
creation date means:
for a record of information—the date the record is made; and
for a document—the date the document is created.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Transfer of continuing airworthiness records for aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies if:
(a) a person (the first person) ceases to be the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft; and
(b) another person (the second person) becomes the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft.

Within 30 days after the first person ceases to be the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, the first person must give the continuing airworthiness records for the aircraft to the second person.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

If the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft becomes aware of a major defect in the aircraft, the person must, within 2 days after becoming aware of the defect, report the defect, in accordance with subregulation (2), to:
CASA; and
if the defect does not relate to a modification mentioned in paragraph (c), (d), (e) or (f)—the type certificate holder or foreign type certificate holder for the aircraft; and

if the defect relates to a modification made to the aircraft that is covered by a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft—the supplemental type certificate holder or foreign supplemental type certificate holder for the aircraft; and
if the defect relates to a part produced in accordance with an Australian Parts Manufacturer Approval—the holder of the Australian Parts Manufacturer Approval; and
if the defect relates to a part produced in accordance with a Parts Manufacturer Approval issued by the FAA—the holder of the Parts Manufacturer Approval; and
if the defect relates to a part produced in accordance with a parts manufacturer approval issued by a national aviation authority to which subregulation (1A) applies—the holder of the approval; and
if the defect relates to a modification made in accordance with a design covered by any of the following approvals—the holder of the approval:
a modification/repair design approval;
an approval mentioned in regulation 21.475;
an approval that continues in force under regulation 202.054, 202.055 or 202.056.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(ea), this subregulation applies to the national aviation authority of a Contracting State if:
Australia has an agreement (however described) with the Contracting State for the acceptance of parts manufacturer approvals; or
CASA has an agreement (however described) with the national aviation authority for the acceptance of parts manufacturer approvals.
The report must be made:
in writing; and
in the approved form.
Note: Under regulation 11.018, a report in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.
It is a defence to a prosecution under subregulation (1) that relates to a failure to report a defect to the holder of an approval mentioned in subparagraph (1)(f)(iii) that the defendant:
made all reasonable efforts to identify the holder of the approval; and
was unable to identify the holder.
Note 1: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters mentioned in subregulation (3) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Note 2: See also Division 42.D.6 for other requirements relating to defects.

section.heading: Investigating major defects—large aircraft and aircraft authorised to operate under AOC

content.p: If the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for a large aircraft or an aircraft that is authorised to operate under an AOC becomes aware of a major defect in the aircraft, the person must:
investigate the cause of the defect; and
give CASA a report containing the findings of the investigation within 14 days after completing the investigation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: See also Division 42.D.6 for other requirements relating to defects.

section.heading: Action by CASA following report of major defect

content.p: If CASA receives a report about a major defect under regulation 42.270, CASA may, by notice in writing, require the person who made the report:
to give CASA further information in relation to the major defect within a period specified in the notice; or
to keep the aircraft, or the part of the aircraft that is defective, in a state that will allow CASA to investigate the defect; or
to give to CASA any document, aeronautical product or other thing in the possession, or under the control, of the person that relates to the defect.
The person must comply with the notice.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Action by certificate holder or approval holder following report of major defect

content.p: (1) If a person mentioned in paragraph 42.270(1)(b), (c), (d), (e) or (f) (the first person) receives a report about a major defect under regulation 42.270, the first person may, by notice in writing, require the person who made the report (the second person) to give the first person further information in relation to the major defect.
The notice must specify the period within which the further information must be provided.
The period specified in the notice must be at least 14 days from the date of the request.
The second person must comply with the notice.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.D—Maintenance
This Subpart sets out:
who is permitted to carry out maintenance; and
requirements for carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or an aeronautical product; and
requirements for critical control system maintenance; and
requirements for dealing with defects; and
requirements for making and keeping records for an approved maintenance organisation or independent maintainer who carries out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product.

section.heading: Who is permitted to carry out maintenance on aircraft—approved maintenance organisations

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, a person mentioned in column 2 of an item in the following table is permitted to carry out maintenance on an Australian aircraft:
to which this Part applies; and
that is mentioned in column 3 of the item.

tr.td: An aircraft of a kind for which the Part 145 organisation is approved to provide maintenance services
An individual carrying out maintenance on behalf of a Part 145 organisation
An aircraft for which the Part 145 organisation is providing maintenance services

A small aircraft: (a) that is not authorised to operate under an Australian air transport AOC; and (b) that is of a kind for which the Subpart 42.F organisation is approved to provide maintenance services
An individual carrying out maintenance on behalf of a Subpart 42.F organisation
An aircraft for which the Subpart 42.F organisation is providing maintenance services

content.p: Note 1: The kinds of aircraft for which a Part 145 organisation is approved to provide maintenance services are determined by CASA—see regulation 145.030.
Note 2: The kinds of aircraft for which a Subpart 42.F organisation is approved to provide maintenance services are determined by CASA—see regulation 42.515.

section.heading: Who is permitted to carry out maintenance on aircraft—individuals not working for approved maintenance organisations

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act:
an individual mentioned in column 2 of an item in table 42.300 is permitted to carry out maintenance on an Australian aircraft:
to which this Part applies; and
that is mentioned in column 3 of the item; and
the individual is permitted to carry out the maintenance subject to the conditions mentioned in column 4 of the item.
However, an individual mentioned in item 2, 3, 4 or 5 of table 42.300 is not permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual.

p.b: Individuals, not working for approved maintenance organisations, permitted to carry out maintenance on aircraft

tr.td: An aircraft: (a) that is a small aircraft; and (b) that is not authorised to operate under an AOC

The conditions are that: (a) the person’s aircraft engineer licence permits him or her to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance; and (b) the maintenance is not specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for this item
An individual who is carrying out maintenance under the supervision of an individual mentioned in item 1
An aircraft for which the individual mentioned in item 1 is providing maintenance services
A pilot licence holder who is carrying out maintenance other than under an authorisation issued under regulation 42.630 that is in force
An aircraft: (a) that is a small aircraft; and (b) that is not authorised to operate under an AOC; and (c) that the pilot licence holder is authorised, under Part 61, to fly

The conditions are that: (a) the maintenance is specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for this item; and (b) either: (i) the pilot licence holder is the registered operator of the aircraft; or (ii) the registered operator of the aircraft has given the pilot licence holder permission to carry out the maintenance
A pilot licence holder who is carrying out maintenance under an authorisation issued under regulation 42.630 that is in force
An aircraft: (a) that is a large aircraft, or is authorised to operate under an AOC; and (b) that the pilot licence holder is authorised, under Part 61, to fly
The conditions are that: (a) the pilot licence holder is a member of the aircraft’s flight crew; and (b) the maintenance is specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for this item
A flight engineer who is carrying out maintenance under an authorisation issued under regulation 42.630 that is in force

An aircraft: (a) that is a large aircraft, or is authorised to operate under an AOC; and (b) in relation to which the flight engineer is authorised, under Part 61, to perform the duties of flight engineer
The conditions are that: (a) the flight engineer is a member of the aircraft’s flight crew; and (b) the maintenance is specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for this item

content.p: Note 1: For item 2, under regulation 42.320, an independent maintainer who is supervising the carrying out of maintenance by another individual must not instruct or permit the individual to carry out maintenance that the independent maintainer is not permitted to carry out.

Note 2: For items 4 and 5, under subregulation 42.080(2), the registered operator of an aircraft must ensure that a person mentioned in item 4 or 5 carries out maintenance on the aircraft at a place only if no approved maintenance organisation is able to carry out the maintenance at that place

Note 3: For items 4 and 5, an authorisation under regulation 42.630 must include the maintenance services that the pilot licence holder or flight engineer is authorised to provide—see paragraph 42.630(3)(c).

section.heading: Who is permitted to carry out maintenance—organisations under NAA arrangement

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, an organisation is permitted to carry out maintenance outside Australian territory on an Australian aircraft to which this Part applies if:
the organisation is approved to carry out the maintenance by the national aviation authority of a foreign country under a law of that country; and
the country is specified for this regulation in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
(c) there is an arrangement (the NAA arrangement) between CASA and the national aviation authority, or Australia and the foreign country, that permits the organisation to carry out the maintenance.
The permission in subregulation (1) is subject to the condition that the organisation must carry out and certify the maintenance in accordance with the NAA arrangement.

division.heading: Permissions for section 20AB of Act—aeronautical products

section.heading: Who is permitted to carry out maintenance on aeronautical products

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, a person mentioned in column 2 of an item in the following table is permitted to carry out maintenance on:
an aeronautical product in Australian territory:
to which this Part applies; and
that is of the kind mentioned in column 3 of the item; and
an aeronautical product for an Australian aircraft:
to which this Part applies; and
that is of the kind mentioned in column 3 of the item.

tr.td: An aeronautical product of a kind for which the Part 145 organisation is approved to provide maintenance services
An individual carrying out maintenance on behalf of a Part 145 organisation
An aeronautical product for which the Part 145 organisation is providing maintenance services
An aeronautical product of a kind for which the Subpart 42.F organisation is approved to provide maintenance services
An individual carrying out maintenance on behalf of a Subpart 42.F organisation
An aeronautical product for which the Subpart 42.F organisation is providing maintenance services

content.p: Note 1: The kinds of aeronautical products for which a Part 145 organisation is approved to provide maintenance services are determined by CASA—see regulation 145.030.
Note 2: The kinds of aeronautical products for which a Subpart 42.F organisation is approved to provide maintenance services are determined by CASA—see regulation 42.515.

section.heading: Who is permitted to carry out maintenance on aeronautical products—foreign organisations approved by national aviation authority

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, an organisation is permitted to carry out maintenance outside Australian territory on an aeronautical product for an Australian aircraft to which this Part applies if:
the organisation is approved to carry out the maintenance by the national aviation authority of a foreign country under a law of that country; and
the country is specified for this regulation in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
The permission in subregulation (1) is subject to the condition that the organisation must carry out and certify the maintenance:

(a) if there is an arrangement (the NAA arrangement) between CASA and the national aviation authority that permits the organisation to carry out the maintenance—in accordance with the NAA arrangement; or
otherwise—in accordance with the law of the foreign country.

section.heading: General requirements for carrying out maintenance

content.p: Obligation
If an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft or on an aeronautical product, the individual must:
carry out the maintenance:
in accordance with current maintenance data for the maintenance; and
using facilities that are appropriate for carrying out maintenance of the kind that is being carried out; and
if tools, equipment or materials are mentioned in the maintenance data for the maintenance—use those tools, equipment or materials; and
if using measuring or testing equipment—ensure that the accuracy of the equipment:
is appropriate for the maintenance; and
has been verified, at appropriate intervals, by a means that is traceable to a standard that is nationally or internationally recognised.
Example: For subparagraph (c)(ii), of a standard that is nationally recognised
A standard maintained by the National Measurement Institute—see http://www.measurement.gov.au.
Offence—approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Offences—independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must comply with subregulation (1) when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If an independent maintainer is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual, the independent maintainer must ensure that the individual complies with subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).

section.heading: Ensuring individuals are competent to carry out maintenance

content.p: Meaning of competent

(1) An individual is competent to carry out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product if he or she has the skills and knowledge to carry out the maintenance to the standard required by the maintenance data for the maintenance.
Obligation for approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual does not carry out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation unless:
the organisation has assessed the individual as being competent to carry out the maintenance; or

if the organisation has not assessed the individual as being competent to carry out the maintenance—the carrying out of the maintenance by the individual is supervised by an individual that the organisation has assessed as being competent to carry out the maintenance.
Offences for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
before the maintenance is carried out, the organisation has not assessed the individual as being competent to carry out the maintenance; and
the carrying out of the maintenance by the individual is not supervised.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
before the maintenance is carried out, the organisation has not assessed the individual as being competent to carry out the maintenance; and
the carrying out of the maintenance by the individual is supervised; and
before the maintenance is carried out, the organisation has not assessed the individual who supervised the carrying out of the maintenance as being competent to carry out the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Obligation for certain independent maintainers
An independent maintainer mentioned in item 1 or 3 of table 42.300 must not carry out maintenance on an aircraft unless the independent maintainer is competent to carry out the maintenance.
An independent maintainer must not supervise the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual unless the independent maintainer is competent to carry out the maintenance.

Note 1: The competence of an independent maintainer mentioned in item 4 or 5 of table 42.300 to carry out maintenance is dealt with by a continuing airworthiness management organisation—see paragraph 42.630(2)(e).

Note 2: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Offences for breach of obligation
An independent maintainer mentioned in item 1 or 3 of table 42.300 commits an offence if:
he or she carries out maintenance on an aircraft; and
he or she is not competent to carry out the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
the independent maintainer supervises the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the independent maintainer is not competent to carry out the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Restriction on maintenance that independent maintainers may instruct or permit supervised individuals to carry out

content.p: An independent maintainer who is supervising the carrying out of maintenance by another individual must not instruct or permit the individual to carry out maintenance that the independent maintainer is not permitted to carry out.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Maintenance involving modifications and certain repairs

content.p: Obligation
This regulation applies if an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product that involves:
making a modification to the aircraft or aeronautical product; or
a repair of the aircraft or aeronautical product that involves a change to the approved design for the aircraft or aeronautical product.
Before a certificate of release to service is issued for the aircraft or aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance, the individual must ensure that:
there is a Part 21 approval for the design of the modification or repair; and
the modification or repair complies with the design.

Note: For who issues a certificate of release to service for an aircraft, see Subdivision 42.H.3.2. For who issues a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product, see Subdivision 42.H.4.2.
Offence—approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Offences—independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must comply with subregulation (2):
when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
when supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An offence against subregulation (3) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Removal of tools etc after carrying out maintenance

content.p: Obligation

If an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product, the individual must remove from the aircraft or aeronautical product any tools, equipment or other things extraneous to the aircraft or the aeronautical product before a certificate of release to service is issued for the aircraft or aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance.

Note: For who issues a certificate of release to service for an aircraft, see Subdivision 42.H.3.2. For who issues a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product, see Subdivision 42.H.4.2.
Offence—approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Offences—independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must comply with subregulation (1) when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An independent maintainer who is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual must ensure that the individual complies with subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).

division.heading: Requirements for independent inspection of critical control system maintenance

content.p: An independent individual, for critical control system maintenance carried out on an aircraft, means an individual who:
did not perform maintenance certification for the maintenance; and
if the maintenance is carried out by a Part 145 organisation—is a certifying employee of that organisation authorised to perform maintenance certification:
for the maintenance; or
for similar maintenance carried out on another aircraft that has an aircraft control system of similar technology and construction; and
if the maintenance is not carried out by a Part 145 organisation—is 1 of the following:

a licensed aircraft maintenance engineer whose aircraft engineer licence permits the individual to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance, or for similar maintenance carried out on another aircraft that has an aircraft control system of similar technology and construction;
a pilot licence holder who is authorised under Part 61 to fly the aircraft.

section.heading: Requirement for verification and record for critical control system maintenance

content.p: Offence—approved maintenance organisation
If an individual carries out critical control system maintenance on an aircraft on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must ensure that an independent individual has:
verified the matters mentioned in subregulation 42.345(1); and
made a record, in writing, in accordance with regulation 42.345;
before the organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Offence—independent maintainer
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If an independent maintainer carries out critical control system maintenance on an aircraft, or supervises the carrying out of critical control system maintenance on an aircraft by another individual, the independent maintainer must ensure that an independent individual has:
verified the matters mentioned in subregulation 42.345(1); and
made a record, in writing, in accordance with regulation 42.345;
before the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Verification and record for critical control system maintenance

content.p: An independent individual may record the information mentioned in subregulation (3) in the continuing airworthiness records system for an aircraft in relation to critical control system maintenance carried out on the aircraft only if he or she has verified that:
the part of the aircraft control system on which the maintenance was carried out is assembled and configured in accordance with the maintenance data for the maintenance; and
the aircraft control system is functioning correctly.
An independent individual commits an offence if:

he or she records the information mentioned in subregulation (3) in the continuing airworthiness records system for an aircraft in relation to critical control system maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and
the recording of the information is not permitted under subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The information is the following:
that the individual has verified the matters mentioned in subregulation (1);
information identifying the critical control system maintenance to which the verification related;
the individual’s name, signature and licence or certification authorisation number;
the date the verification was performed.

(1) For a defect in an aircraft that is authorised to operate under an Australian air transport AOC or a large aircraft, qualified individual means a certifying employee of a Part 145 organisation who is authorised to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance that would be necessary to rectify the defect.

(2) For a defect in an aircraft, other than an aircraft mentioned in subregulation (1), qualified individual means a licensed aircraft maintenance engineer whose aircraft engineer licence permits the holder to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance that would be necessary to rectify the defect.
If an individual:
is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
is, or becomes, aware of a defect in the aircraft;

the individual must ensure that the defect is recorded in the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft before a certificate of release to service is issued for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: For who issues a certificate of release to service for an aircraft, see Subdivision 42.H.3.2.

section.heading: When qualified individual may defer rectification of defect

content.p: A qualified individual may defer the rectification of a defect in an aircraft only if the deferral is permitted by subregulation (3).
The qualified individual commits an offence if:
he or she defers the rectification of the defect; and
the deferral is not permitted by subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Deferral of the rectification of the defect is permitted only if:
the defect does not adversely affect the airworthiness of the aircraft; or
the operation of the aircraft for a flight with the defect is permitted by any of the following:
the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft;
the minimum equipment list for the aircraft;
the configuration deviation list for the aircraft;
an airworthiness directive; or
the defect is approved as a permissible unserviceability under regulation 21.007; or
the defect is in an item of operational or emergency equipment that:
is fitted to the aircraft; and
is not required by the certification basis for the aircraft; and
is not required by or under these Regulations for the operation of the aircraft for a flight.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: How rectification of defect is deferred

content.p: To defer the rectification of a defect in an aircraft under regulation 42.360, the qualified individual must:
make a record that complies with regulation 42.370; and
sign the record; and
record, in that record:
his or her aircraft engineer licence number or certification authorisation number; and
the date of the deferral.

section.heading: Record for deferral of rectification of defect

content.p: A record of the deferral of the rectification of a defect must be made in:
the flight technical log for the aircraft, if:
the defect affects the operation of the aircraft; or
the deferral was permitted by subparagraph 42.360(3)(b)(ii) or (iii); or
the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft, in any other case.
The record must contain:
a description of the defect; and
a statement of the reasons for the qualified individual’s decision to defer the rectification of the defect; and
any limitations or conditions mentioned in a document mentioned in paragraph 42.360(3)(b) in relation to the deferral of the rectification of the defect and the operation of the aircraft.
A qualified individual commits an offence if:
he or she makes a record of the deferral of the rectification of a defect; and
the record does not comply with this regulation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Major defect reporting—independent maintainer carrying out maintenance on aircraft

content.p: If:
an independent maintainer is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft, or is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the independent maintainer becomes aware of a major defect in the aircraft;
the independent maintainer must report the defect to the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: See also regulations 42.110, 42.115 and 42.270 for other requirements relating to defects.
Note 2: See regulation 42.390 for the requirements for making a report.

Note 3: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).

section.heading: Major defect reporting—approved maintenance organisation carrying out maintenance on aircraft

content.p: If:
an approved maintenance organisation is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
the organisation becomes aware of a major defect in the aircraft;
the organisation must report the defect to the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: See regulation 42.390 for the requirements for making a report.
Note 2: See also regulations 42.110, 42.115 and 42.270 for other requirements relating to defects.

section.heading: Major defect reporting—approved maintenance organisation carrying out maintenance on aeronautical product

content.p: If:
an approved maintenance organisation is carrying out maintenance on an aeronautical product; and
the organisation becomes aware of a major defect in the aeronautical product;
the organisation must report the defect to CASA.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: See regulation 42.390 for the requirements for making a report.
Note 2: See also regulations 42.110, 42.115 and 42.270 for other requirements relating to defects.
A person who is required to make a report under regulation 42.375, 42.380 or 42.385 must:
make the report in the approved form; and
make the report within 2 days after the person becomes aware of the major defect to which the report relates.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: See also regulations 42.110, 42.115 and 42.270 for other requirements relating to defects.
Note 2: Under regulation 11.018, a report in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.

division.heading: Requirements for recording maintenance for aircraft or aeronautical products

content.p: Offence—approved maintenance organisation

If an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must ensure that the information mentioned in subregulation (3) is recorded in writing before the organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Offence—independent maintainer
If an independent maintainer:
carries out maintenance on an aircraft; or
supervises the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual;

the independent maintainer must record the information mentioned in subregulation (3) in writing before the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Information to be recorded
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The information is the following:
the registration mark for the aircraft;
the date on which the maintenance was completed;
a description of the maintenance;
information identifying the maintenance data for the maintenance;
if the maintenance is a modification or repair involving a change to the approved design for the aircraft—information identifying the design of the modification or repair;
if a part was fitted to the aircraft when the maintenance was carried out—a description of the part, including:
the part number for the part; and
the serial number for the part (if any); and
if the part is not a standard part—the information mentioned in subregulation (4).
For subparagraph (3)(f)(iii), the information is:

if the fitting of the part was permitted by subparagraph 42.420(5)(a)(i) or (b)(i)—the number of the authorised release certificate mentioned in that subparagraph for the part, or information that enables the identification of that authorised release certificate; and
if the fitting of the part was permitted by subparagraph 42.420(5)(b)(ii)—information that enables the identification of the in-house release document mentioned in that subparagraph for the part; and
if the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.430—information identifying the aircraft from which the part was removed; and
if the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.435—a statement that the part is a product fabricated by an approved maintenance organisation; and
if the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.440—information that enables the identification of the document mentioned in paragraph 42.440(e) that accompanied the part.

Note 1: The information required under this regulation about maintenance, and the maintenance certification for the maintenance, together constitute the maintenance record for the maintenance—see the definition of maintenance record in regulation 42.015. For maintenance certification, see regulation 42.715.

Note 2: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Note 3: See Division 42.H.3 in relation to the issue of a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft.

section.heading: Making maintenance record for aeronautical products

content.p: (1) If an individual carries out maintenance on an aeronautical product (the first aeronautical product) on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must ensure that the information mentioned in this regulation (the maintenance record) is recorded:
in writing; and
before the organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The information is:
information that identifies the first aeronautical product, including:
the part number for the product; and
the serial number for the product (if any); and
the date on which the maintenance was completed; and
a description of the maintenance; and
information identifying the maintenance data for the maintenance; and
if the maintenance is a modification or repair involving a change to the approved design of the aeronautical product—information identifying the design of the modification or repair.

(3) If an aeronautical product (the second aeronautical product) was fitted to the first aeronautical product when the maintenance was carried out, the information must include a description of the second aeronautical product, including:
the part number for the product; and
the serial number for the product (if any); and
if the product is not a standard part—the information mentioned in subregulation (4).
For paragraph (3)(c), the information is:
if the fitting of the second aeronautical product was permitted by subparagraph 42.420(5)(a)(i) or (b)(i):
the number of the authorised release certificate mentioned in that subparagraph for the product; or
information that enables the identification of that authorised release certificate; or

if the fitting of the second aeronautical product was permitted by subparagraph 42.420(5)(b)(ii)—information that enables the identification of the in-house release document mentioned in that subparagraph for the product.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Provision of maintenance record and other documents to registered operator

content.p: Offence—approved maintenance organisation
If an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must comply with subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The organisation must ensure that the maintenance record for the maintenance is given to the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft within 30 days after the organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Offence—independent maintainer
If an independent maintainer:
carries out maintenance on an aircraft; or
supervises the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual;

the independent maintainer must give the maintenance record for the maintenance to the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft within 30 days after the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An offence against subregulation (1) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Retention of copy of maintenance record by approved maintenance organisations

content.p: If a maintenance record is made for maintenance carried out on an aircraft or an aeronautical product by an individual on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must keep a copy of the record for the period mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The records must be kept for 2 years beginning on the date when the organisation issued the certificate of release to service for the aircraft or aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.E—Aeronautical products
This Subpart sets out requirements for:
fitting parts to, and using materials in, aircraft and aeronautical products; and
the control of unserviceable and unsalvageable parts; and
the control of unapproved parts.

division.heading: Requirements for fitting parts and using materials

section.heading: Fitting parts other than standard parts

content.p: If an individual is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product, the individual must not fit a part that is not a standard part to the aircraft or aeronautical product unless the fitting of the part is permitted under:
regulation 42.450; or
subregulation (2).
For paragraph (1)(b), the part may be fitted if:
either:
the part is serviceable; or
if the part is unserviceable because of a defect in the part—the fitting of the part is permitted under subregulation (3); and
the part is eligible to be fitted to the aircraft or the aeronautical product; and
if the manufacturer of the part has specified a storage life for the part—the storage life for the part has not expired; and
the fitting of the part is permitted under subregulation (5).
Note: For the definition of eligible to be fitted, see regulation 42.015.
For subparagraph (2)(a)(ii), the part may be fitted if:
the operation of the aircraft for a flight with the defect is permitted by the minimum equipment list for the aircraft; and
subregulation (4) does not apply to the part.
This regulation applies to a part if:
before the proposed fitting of the part, the part was fitted to an aircraft; and
the aircraft to which the part was most recently fitted was operated for a flight with the defect; and
the operation of the aircraft for the flight with the defect was permitted by the minimum equipment list for that aircraft.
For paragraph (2)(d), the part may be fitted if:
for a part on which maintenance has not been carried out since its manufacture, and that has not been used in an aircraft since its manufacture:
an authorised release certificate has been issued for the part in relation to its manufacture; or
the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.435 or 42.440; or
for a part on which maintenance has been carried out, and that has not been used in an aircraft since the maintenance was carried out:
an authorised release certificate has been issued for the part in relation to the maintenance; or
if the maintenance was in-house maintenance—an in-house release document has been issued for the part in relation to the maintenance; or
the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.440; or
the fitting of the part is permitted under regulation 42.430.

section.heading: Obligations and offences for fitting parts other than standard parts

content.p: Obligation for approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation 42.420(1).
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
the individual fits a part that is not a standard part to the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
the fitting of the part is not permitted by subregulation 42.420(1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Obligation for independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must:
comply with subregulation 42.420(1) when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
if the independent maintainer is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual—ensure that the individual complies with subregulation 42.420(1).
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Offences for breach of obligation
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
he or she fits a part that is not a standard part to the aircraft; and
the fitting of the part is not permitted by subregulation 42.420(1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the individual fits a part that is not a standard part to the aircraft; and
the fitting of the part is not permitted by subregulation 42.420(1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2), (4) or (5) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Fitting parts removed from aircraft—permission for paragraph 42.420(5)(c)

content.p: For paragraph 42.420(5)(c), the part may be fitted if:
the part is removed from a place on an aircraft; and
maintenance is not carried out on the part after its removal from the aircraft; and
the part is to be fitted in a different place on the aircraft.
For paragraph 42.420(5)(c), the part may be fitted if:

(a) the part was removed from a registered aircraft (the first aircraft) by a person who was, at the time the part was removed, permitted under these Regulations to carry out the maintenance that comprises removing the part from the aircraft; and
maintenance has not been carried out on the part after its removal from the first aircraft; and
for a part that has been stored—the storage was in accordance with the instructions (if any) issued by the manufacturer of the part in relation to storage; and
(d) the part is to be fitted to another aircraft (the second aircraft); and
the part has not been subjected to:
immersion; or
extremes of stress or temperature; and
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the second aircraft agrees to the fitting of the part to the second aircraft.
Note: For paragraph (a), for the definition of registered, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.

section.heading: Fitting parts fabricated by approved maintenance organisations—permission for subparagraph 42.420(5)(a)(ii)

content.p: For subparagraph 42.420(5)(a)(ii), the part may be fitted if:
the part has been fabricated by an approved maintenance organisation; and
the part is to be fitted to an aircraft on which the organisation is carrying out maintenance.

section.heading: Fitting parts for which there is no authorised release certificate—permission for subparagraphs 42.420(5)(a)(ii) and (b)(iii)

content.p: For subparagraphs 42.420(5)(a)(ii) and (b)(iii), a part of a particular kind may be fitted to an aircraft if:
the part is to be fitted by an individual carrying out maintenance on behalf of a Part 145 organisation; and
the aircraft is grounded at a location that is not the organisation’s main location; and
the aircraft is grounded because of a defect in the aircraft that cannot be rectified without fitting a part of that kind; and
a part of that kind in respect of which there is an authorised release certificate is not available at that location; and
the part is accompanied by a document that:
states that the part is serviceable; and
identifies the organisation that issued the document; and
includes details of the national aviation authority under whose authority the document was issued; and
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft agrees to the fitting of the part to the aircraft; and
an entry is made in the aircraft’s flight technical log that, within 36 flight hours after it is fitted:
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft must obtain an authorised release certificate for the part; or
the part must be removed.

Note: Under regulation 42.165, if an aeronautical product is fitted to an aircraft as permitted by this regulation, the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft must, within 36 flight hours after it is fitted, obtain an authorised release certificate for the product or ensure that the product is removed from the aircraft.

An individual who is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product must not fit a standard part to the aircraft or aeronautical product unless the fitting of the part is permitted under:
regulation 42.450; or
subregulation (2).
For paragraph (1)(b), the standard part may be fitted if:
the standard part is serviceable; and
the standard part is accompanied by:
information that identifies the specification with which the part complies; and
information that allows the part to be traced to its manufacturer; and
the standard part is accompanied by evidence that the standard part complies with the specification; and
the standard part is eligible to be fitted to the aircraft or the aeronautical product; and
if the manufacturer of the standard part has specified a storage life for the part—the storage life for the part has not expired.
Obligation for approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation (1).
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
the individual fits a standard part to the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
the fitting of the standard part is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Obligation for independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must:
comply with subregulation (1) when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
if the independent maintainer is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual—ensure that the individual complies with subregulation (1).
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Offences for breach of obligation
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
he or she fits a standard part to the aircraft; and
the fitting of the standard part is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the individual fits a standard part to the aircraft; and
the fitting of the standard part is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (4), (6) or (7) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Fitting parts removed from same place on aircraft—permission for paragraphs 42.420(1)(a) and 42.445(1)(a)

content.p: For paragraphs 42.420(1)(a) and 42.445(1)(a), a part may be fitted to a place on an aircraft or aeronautical product if:
the part was removed from that place on the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
maintenance is not carried out on the part between the removal of the part and its fitting to the aircraft or aeronautical product.
An individual who is carrying out maintenance must not use a material in or on an aircraft or aeronautical product unless:
the material is accompanied by:
information that identifies the specification with which the material complies; and
information that allows the material to be traced to its manufacturer; and
evidence that the material complies with the specification; and
the material is eligible to be used in or on the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
the material appears to be in a satisfactory condition; and
if the manufacturer of the material has specified a storage life for the material—the storage life for the material has not expired.
Note: For the definition of eligible to be used, see regulation 42.015.
Obligation for approved maintenance organisation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who carries out maintenance on its behalf complies with subregulation (1).
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft or aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
the individual uses a material in the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
the use of the material is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Obligation for independent maintainer
An independent maintainer must:
comply with subregulation (1) when carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
if the independent maintainer is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual—ensure that the individual complies with subregulation (1).
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Offences for breach of obligation
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft; and
he or she uses a material in the aircraft; and
the use of the material is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
he or she is supervising the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the individual uses a material in the aircraft; and
the use of the material is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3), (5) or (6) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Requirements for controlling unserviceable and unsalvageable parts

content.p: If an approved maintenance organisation knows that a part that is not fitted to an aircraft is unserviceable, the organisation must ensure that the steps mentioned in subregulation (3) are taken within 2 days after the organisation first knew that the part was unserviceable.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If an independent maintainer knows that a part that is not fitted to an aircraft is unserviceable, the independent maintainer must take the steps mentioned in subregulation (3) within 2 days after the independent maintainer first knew that the part was unserviceable.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The steps are:
applying a label, or attaching a tag, to the part recording the following:
sufficient information to identify the part, including the part’s name, part number and serial number (if any);
that the part is unserviceable;
the origin of the part, including information about the aircraft or aeronautical product from which the part has been removed, if relevant and if known to the independent maintainer or organisation;
the reason that the part is unserviceable; and
if the independent maintainer or organisation keeps the part—storing the part separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location.

If an approved maintenance organisation knows that a part that is not fitted to an aircraft is unsalvageable, the organisation must ensure that the steps mentioned in subregulation (3) are taken within 2 days after the organisation first knew that the part was unsalvageable.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If an independent maintainer knows that a part that is not fitted to an aircraft is unsalvageable, the independent maintainer must take the steps mentioned in subregulation (3) within 2 days after the independent maintainer first knew that the part was unsalvageable.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The steps are:
applying a label, or attaching a tag, to the part recording the following:
sufficient information to identify the part, including the part’s name, part number and serial number (if any);
that the part is unsalvageable;

the origin of the part, including any information about the aircraft or aeronautical product from which the part has been removed, if relevant and if known to the independent maintainer or organisation;
the reason that the part is unsalvageable; and
doing 1 of the following:
storing the part separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location;
if the organisation or independent maintainer is not the owner of the part—giving the part to the owner of the part;
mutilating the part, or arranging for the part to be mutilated, in a manner that ensures that the part cannot be used in aviation.
If the owner of a part receives the part under subparagraph (3)(b)(ii), the owner must, within 3 days of receiving the part:
store the part separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location; or
mutilate the part, or arrange for the part to be mutilated, in a manner that ensures that the part cannot be used in aviation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A part is unapproved if:
the part is counterfeit; or
the part has not been approved in a manner mentioned in paragraph 21.305(a), (b), (c) or (e) or regulation 21.305A; or
the part:
is not a standard part; and
has been produced other than under an authorisation (however described) granted by CASA or an national aviation authority; or
maintenance has been carried out on the part other than in accordance with an authorisation (however described) granted by CASA or an national aviation authority; or
the part has been modified other than in accordance with a design for which there is a Part 21 approval; or
the part:
is unserviceable or unsalvageable; and
has been fraudulently represented as serviceable; or
the part is accompanied by a fraudulent document.

If a person becomes aware that a part is unapproved, the person must ensure that the steps mentioned in subregulation (2) are taken within 2 days after the person first became aware that the part was unapproved.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The steps are:
applying a label, or attaching a tag, to the part recording the following:
sufficient information to identify the part, including the part’s name, part number and serial number (if any);
that the part is unapproved;
the origin of the part, including any information about the aircraft or aeronautical product from which the part has been removed, if relevant and if known to the person;
the reason that the part is unapproved; and
storing the part, and any documents that accompanied the part, separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location; and
making a report about the part in accordance with regulation 42.480.
For paragraph 42.475(2)(c), the person must give a report about the part to:
CASA; and
if the person knows that the part was fitted to an aircraft or aeronautical product—the type certificate holder or foreign type certificate holder for the aircraft or aeronautical product; and
if the person knows that the part was fitted to an aircraft—the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft.
The report must be made in the approved form.
Note: Under regulation 11.018, a report in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.

section.heading: Action by CASA following report of unapproved parts

content.p: If CASA receives a report about a part under regulation 42.480, CASA may, by notice in writing:
require the person who made the report to give CASA further information in relation to the part within a period specified in the notice; or
tell the person who made the report that the part does not have to be kept.
The person must comply with a notice under paragraph (1)(a).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Action required if parts not required to be kept

content.p: If CASA has given a person a notice under paragraph 42.485(1)(b) in relation to a part, the person must, within 2 days after receiving the notice:
if the person is not the owner of the part—give the part to the owner of the part; or
store the part, and any documents that accompanied the part, separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location; or
mutilate the part, or arrange for the part to be mutilated, in a manner that ensures that the part cannot be used in aviation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
If the owner of a part receives the part under paragraph (1)(a), the owner must, within 2 days of receiving the part:
store the part separately from serviceable aeronautical products and in a secure location; or
mutilate the part, or arrange for the part to be mutilated, in a manner that ensures that the part cannot be used in aviation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 42.F—Subpart 42.F approved maintenance organisations
This Subpart sets out matters relating to Subpart 42.F organisations, including:
requirements for approval as a Subpart 42.F organisation; and
requirements that apply to Subpart 42.F organisations.
Note: For other matters relating to Subpart 42.F organisations, see the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
In this Subpart:
accountable manager, for a Subpart 42.F organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for:
ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition, each approval rating that it holds, and these Regulations; and
ensuring that the organisation is able to finance the provision of the maintenance services set out in its exposition; and
ensuring that the organisation has adequate resources available to enable the organisation to provide maintenance services in accordance with its exposition.
approval certificate means a certificate issued under regulation 42.520.
exposition, for a Subpart 42.F organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 42.515 in relation to the organisation, including:
if a change to the document is approved by CASA under regulation 42.540—that change; and
if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under regulation 42.545—the updated part of the document; and
if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 42.550—that change.

responsible manager, for a Subpart 42.F organisation, means an individual appointed by the organisation to be responsible to the accountable manager for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to a particular matter.
significant change, in relation to a Subpart 42.F organisation, has the meaning given by subregulation (2).
Note: See regulation 42.015 and the Dictionary for definitions of other terms used in this Subpart.
(2) A significant change, in relation to a Subpart 42.F organisation, means any of the following changes:
a change to the organisation’s name;
a change to the location of the organisation’s maintenance facility, including the addition of a new maintenance facility;
a change in the personnel holding:
the position of accountable manager in the organisation; or
any of the positions of responsible manager in the organisation;
a change to the maintenance services provided by the organisation, if the change would require a change to the approval ratings mentioned in the organisation’s approval certificate;

a change to the organisation’s facilities, equipment, tools, materials, procedures or certifying employees that could adversely affect the organisation’s ability to provide maintenance services that it is approved to provide.

section.heading: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply in relation to certain matters

content.p: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply to:
a significant change to a Subpart 42.F organisation that is approved by CASA under regulation 42.540; or
a change to a Subpart 42.F organisation of which CASA is notified under regulation 42.545; or
a change to a Subpart 42.F organisation that is made as a consequence of a change made to the organisation’s exposition in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 42.550.
(1) A person (the applicant) may apply to CASA for approval as a Subpart 42.F organisation.
The application must:
be in writing; and
be signed by a person who is, or who proposes to be, the applicant’s accountable manager.
The application must include the following:
a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition;
the approval rating sought by the applicant for:
each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant proposes to provide maintenance services; and
each kind of specialist maintenance the applicant proposes to provide.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant as a Subpart 42.F organisation if CASA is satisfied that:
the applicant has an exposition that complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has facilities, equipment, materials, maintenance data and tools that are suitable for:
providing maintenance services for the kinds of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant proposes to provide maintenance services; and
providing the specialist maintenance that the applicant proposes to provide; and
the facilities, equipment, materials, maintenance data and tools mentioned in paragraph (b) comply with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for the position of accountable manager in the organisation; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for each position of responsible manager in the organisation; and
each individual nominated for a position mentioned in paragraph (d) or (e) is appropriately qualified to hold the position.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
If CASA decides to approve an applicant as a Subpart 42.F organisation, CASA must determine:
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the applicant is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b).
In approving the applicant, CASA also approves the applicant’s proposed exposition.
If CASA approves an applicant as a Subpart 42.F organisation, CASA must issue a certificate setting out the matters mentioned in subregulation 42.515(2).
The certificate issued by CASA must include an approval certificate reference number determined by CASA.
If CASA approves a significant change to a Subpart 42.F organisation under regulation 42.540, CASA may issue a new approval certificate to the organisation.
A Subpart 42.F organisation may provide maintenance services that it is approved to provide.
It is a condition of approval of a Subpart 42.F organisation that:
the organisation must, at all times, comply with the requirements of:
its exposition; and
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the organisation is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the organisation is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in subparagraph (ii) or (iii); and
the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
this Part; and
the organisation must ensure that, at all times, its employees comply with the requirements mentioned in paragraph (a).
Note 1: The approval is also subject to the conditions set out in Part 11.
Note 2: Subpart 11.G empowers CASA to issue directions.

section.heading: Application for approval of significant changes to Subpart 42.F organisations

content.p: If a Subpart 42.F organisation proposes to make a significant change, the organisation must apply to CASA for approval of the change.
The application must:
be in writing; and
set out the proposed change; and
include a copy of the part of the exposition consequentially affected by the change, showing the proposed change.
Subject to subregulation (4), the application must be made before the change is made.
If:
the change is of the kind mentioned in paragraph 42.500(2)(c); and
the organisation does not apply, in accordance with subregulation (2), before making the change;
the organisation must apply in accordance with subregulation (2) within 7 days after making the change.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Note 3: Making a significant change without applying for approval in accordance with this regulation will be a breach of condition of an approval—see regulation 42.530.

Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a significant change to a Subpart 42.F organisation if CASA is satisfied that, after making the change, the requirements mentioned in subregulation 42.515(1) will continue to be met.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
