a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
In approving the significant change, CASA also approves the consequential changes to the applicant’s exposition.

section.heading: Changes to Subpart 42.F organisations that are not significant changes

content.p: A change that is not a significant change to a Subpart 42.F organisation must be made in accordance with the procedure set out in the organisation’s exposition for making changes to the organisation that are not significant changes.
If such a change is made, the organisation must, within 28 days after making the change:
update its exposition; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the updated part of the exposition.

section.heading: CASA may direct Subpart 42.F organisations to change expositions

content.p: CASA may direct a Subpart 42.F organisation to change its exposition:
to remove particular information from the exposition; or
to include particular information in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information in the exposition.

CASA may give a direction under this regulation only if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary to do so to ensure that the exposition complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
Note: The Subpart 42.F organisation must comply with the direction—see regulation 42.565.

division.heading: Requirements and offences for Subpart 42.F organisations

content.p: If a Subpart 42.F organisation provides maintenance services, it must provide the services only in accordance with:
its exposition; and
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the organisation is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the organisation is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in paragraph (b) or (c); and
the privileges that apply to the approval rating under the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

If a Subpart 42.F organisation’s exposition relates to the duties of an employee of the organisation, the organisation must make the part of the organisation’s exposition that relates to those duties available to the employee before the employee begins carrying out the duties.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
If CASA gives a direction to a Subpart 42.F organisation under regulation 42.550, the organisation must comply with the direction within the time mentioned in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.G—Continuing airworthiness management organisations
This Subpart sets out matters relating to continuing airworthiness management organisations, including:
requirements for approval as a continuing airworthiness management organisation; and
requirements that apply to continuing airworthiness management organisations.
Note: For other matters relating to a continuing airworthiness management organisation, see the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
In this Subpart:
accountable manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for:
ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition, its approval and these Regulations; and
ensuring that the organisation is able to finance the provision of the continuing airworthiness management services set out in its exposition; and
ensuring that the organisation has adequate resources available to enable the organisation to provide continuing airworthiness management services in accordance with its exposition.
approval certificate means a certificate issued under regulation 42.595.

continuing airworthiness management service means any of the following services for an aircraft: ensuring that the requirements mentioned in Divisions 42.C.2, 42.C.3 and 42.C.4 are met; the issue of an airworthiness review certificate under Division 42.I.2; the extension of an airworthiness review certificate under Division 42.I.3; the carrying out of an airworthiness review under Division 42.I.4; the approval of: a maintenance program under Division 42.J.2; or a variation of a maintenance program under Division 42.J.4. continuing airworthiness manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a continuing airworthiness manager, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who has continuing airworthiness responsibility for the organisation. continuing airworthiness responsibility, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means responsibility to the accountable manager for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to providing continuing airworthiness management services. exposition, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 42.590 in relation to the organisation, including: if a change to the document is approved by CASA under regulation 42.615—that change; and if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under regulation 42.620—the updated part of the document; and if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 42.625—that change. quality manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a quality management system, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for the organisation’s quality management system. responsible manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means an individual appointed by the organisation to be responsible for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to a particular matter. significant change, in relation to a continuing airworthiness management organisation, has the meaning given by subregulation (2).
ensuring that the requirements mentioned in Divisions 42.C.2, 42.C.3 and 42.C.4 are met;
the issue of an airworthiness review certificate under Division 42.I.2;
the extension of an airworthiness review certificate under Division 42.I.3;
the carrying out of an airworthiness review under Division 42.I.4;
the approval of:
a maintenance program under Division 42.J.2; or
a variation of a maintenance program under Division 42.J.4.

continuing airworthiness manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a continuing airworthiness manager, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who has continuing airworthiness responsibility for the organisation.

continuing airworthiness responsibility, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means responsibility to the accountable manager for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to providing continuing airworthiness management services.
exposition, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 42.590 in relation to the organisation, including:
if a change to the document is approved by CASA under regulation 42.615—that change; and
if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under regulation 42.620—the updated part of the document; and
if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 42.625—that change.

quality manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a quality management system, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for the organisation’s quality management system.

responsible manager, for a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means an individual appointed by the organisation to be responsible for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to a particular matter.
significant change, in relation to a continuing airworthiness management organisation, has the meaning given by subregulation (2).
Note: See regulation 42.015 and the Dictionary for definitions of other terms used in this Subpart.
(2) A significant change, in relation to a continuing airworthiness management organisation, means any of the following changes:
a change to the organisation’s name;
a change to the location of the organisation’s continuing airworthiness management facility, including the addition of a new facility;
a change in the personnel holding:
the position of accountable manager in the organisation; or
any of the positions of responsible manager in the organisation; or
the position of continuing airworthiness manager (if any) in the organisation; or
the position of quality manager (if any) in the organisation;
a change to:
the aircraft types and models for which the organisation provides continuing airworthiness management services; or
the kinds of continuing airworthiness management services that the organisation provides for each aircraft type and model;

a change to the organisation’s facilities, equipment, procedures or personnel that could adversely affect the organisation’s ability to provide the continuing airworthiness management services that it is approved to provide.

section.heading: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply in relation to certain matters

content.p: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply to:
a significant change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is approved by CASA under regulation 42.615; or
a change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation of which CASA is notified under regulation 42.620; or

a change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation that is made as a consequence of a change made to the organisation’s exposition in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 42.625.

division.heading: Approval of continuing airworthiness management organisations

content.p: (1) A person (the applicant) may apply to CASA for approval as a continuing airworthiness management organisation.
The application must:
be in writing; and
be signed by a person who is, or who proposes to be, the applicant’s accountable manager.
The application must include the following:
a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition;

information showing that each individual nominated for a position of accountable manager or responsible manager in the organisation has the qualifications specified for the position in the Part 42 Manual of Standards;

if the organisation is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a continuing airworthiness manager—information showing that the individual nominated for the position of continuing airworthiness manager in the organisation has the qualifications specified for the position in the Part 42 Manual of Standards;

if the organisation is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a quality management system—information showing that the individual nominated for the position of quality manager in the organisation has the qualifications specified for the position in the Part 42 Manual of Standards;
the aircraft types and models for which the applicant proposes to provide continuing airworthiness management services;
the kinds of continuing airworthiness management services that the applicant proposes to provide for each aircraft type and model.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant as a continuing airworthiness management organisation if CASA is satisfied that:
the applicant has an exposition that complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has facilities, equipment, personnel and instructions for continuing airworthiness:
that are suitable for the continuing airworthiness management services that the applicant proposes to provide; and
that comply with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for the position of accountable manager in the organisation; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for each position of responsible manager in the organisation; and

if the applicant is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a continuing airworthiness manager—the applicant has nominated an individual for the position of continuing airworthiness manager in the organisation; and
if the applicant is required by the Part 42 Manual of Standards to have a quality management system:
the applicant has a quality management system that complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for the position of quality manager in the organisation; and
the individual nominated for the position of quality manager is not also nominated for the position of accountable manager, continuing airworthiness manager (if any) or responsible manager; and
each individual nominated for a position mentioned in paragraph (c), (d) or (e) or subparagraph (f)(ii) holds the qualifications specified for the position in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
If CASA decides to approve an applicant as a continuing airworthiness management organisation, CASA must determine:
the aircraft types and models for which the applicant is approved to provide continuing airworthiness management services; and
the kinds of continuing airworthiness management services that the applicant is approved to provide for each permitted aircraft type and model; and
any limitations applying to the approval.
In approving the applicant, CASA also approves the applicant’s proposed exposition.
If CASA approves an applicant as a continuing airworthiness management organisation, CASA must issue a certificate setting out the matters mentioned in subregulation 42.590(2).
The certificate issued by CASA must include an approval certificate reference number determined by CASA.
If CASA approves a significant change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation under regulation 42.615, CASA may issue a new approval certificate to the organisation.

section.heading: Privileges for continuing airworthiness management organisations

content.p: A continuing airworthiness management organisation may provide continuing airworthiness management services that it is approved to provide.
It is a condition of approval of a continuing airworthiness management organisation that:
the organisation must, at all times, comply with the requirements of:
its exposition; and
its approval, including any limitations applying to the approval; and
the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
this Part; and
the organisation must ensure that, at all times, its employees comply with the requirements mentioned in paragraph (a).
Note 1: The approval is also subject to the conditions set out in Part 11.
Note 2: Subpart 11.G empowers CASA to issue directions.

division.heading: Changes to continuing airworthiness management organisations

section.heading: Application for approval of significant changes to continuing airworthiness management organisations

content.p: If a continuing airworthiness management organisation proposes to make a significant change, the organisation must apply to CASA for approval of the change.
The application must:
be in writing; and
set out the proposed change; and
include a copy of the part of the exposition consequentially affected by the change, showing the proposed change.
Subject to subregulation (4), the application must be made before the change is made.
If:
the change is of the kind mentioned in paragraph 42.575(2)(c); and
the organisation does not apply, in accordance with subregulation (2), before making the change;
the organisation must apply in accordance with subregulation (2) within 7 days after making the change.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Note 3: Making a significant change without applying for approval in accordance with this regulation will be a breach of condition of an approval—see regulation 42.605.

Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a significant change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation if CASA is satisfied that, after making the change, the requirements mentioned in subregulation 42.590(1) will continue to be met.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
In approving the significant change, CASA also approves the consequential changes to the applicant’s exposition.

section.heading: Changes to continuing airworthiness management organisations that are not significant changes

content.p: A change that is not a significant change to a continuing airworthiness management organisation must be made in accordance with the procedure set out in the organisation’s exposition for making changes to the organisation that are not significant changes.
If such a change is made, the organisation must, within 28 days after making the change:
update its exposition; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the updated part of the exposition.

section.heading: CASA may direct continuing airworthiness management organisations to change expositions

content.p: CASA may direct a continuing airworthiness management organisation to change its exposition:
to remove particular information from the exposition; or
to include particular information in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information in the exposition.

CASA may give a direction under this regulation only if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary to do so to ensure that the exposition complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
Note: The continuing airworthiness management organisation must comply with the direction—see regulation 42.665.

division.heading: Authorisation of pilot licence holders and flight engineers to provide maintenance services

section.heading: When pilot licence holders and flight engineers may be authorised

content.p: A continuing airworthiness management organisation may issue an authorisation to provide specified maintenance services for a large aircraft or an aircraft that is authorised to operate under an AOC to a pilot licence holder or a flight engineer if:

for an aircraft for which the continuing airworthiness management organisation is not the registered operator—the registered operator of the aircraft asks the organisation to issue the authorisation; and
the organisation is responsible for providing continuing airworthiness management services for the aircraft; and
the requirements mentioned in subregulation (2) are met.
The requirements are that:
the maintenance to be carried out by the pilot licence holder or flight engineer under the authorisation is specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for items 4 and 5 of table 42.300; and
the pilot licence holder or flight engineer is at least 21; and
the authorisation is for a type and model of aircraft:
that the pilot licence holder is authorised, under Part 61, to fly; or
in relation to which the flight engineer is authorised, under Part 61, to perform the duties of flight engineer; and
the pilot licence holder or flight engineer has a written statement from a Part 145 organisation or a maintenance training organisation to the effect that:
the pilot licence holder or flight engineer has been trained and assessed in the maintenance mentioned in paragraph (a); and
the pilot licence holder or flight engineer is competent to carry out the maintenance; and
at the time the organisation issues the authorisation, the organisation is satisfied that the pilot licence holder or flight engineer:
is competent to carry out the maintenance mentioned in paragraph (a); and
has comprehensive knowledge of the requirements of Subparts 42.D, 42.E and 42.H; and
has comprehensive knowledge of the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft in relation to performing maintenance certification and issuing certificates of release to service.
The authorisation must:
be in writing; and

be signed by the responsible manager in the organisation who is responsible for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to authorisations under this regulation; and
include the following information:
the name of the continuing airworthiness management organisation;
the name and licence number of the pilot licence holder or flight engineer being authorised;
the maintenance services that the pilot licence holder or flight engineer is authorised to provide;
the date that the authorisation is issued;
the period for which the authorisation is in force;
the aircraft for which the authorisation is issued;
the name of the registered operator of the aircraft.
The period for which the authorisation is in force:
must not exceed 2 years; and
must not include a period before the date that the authorisation is issued.

section.heading: Ceasing of authorisation if organisation ceases to be responsible for providing continuing airworthiness management services for aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies if:

a continuing airworthiness management organisation has issued an authorisation under regulation 42.630 to a pilot licence holder or a flight engineer to provide maintenance services for an aircraft; and
the organisation ceases to be responsible for providing continuing airworthiness management services for the aircraft.
The authorisation ceases to be in force at the time the organisation ceases to be responsible for providing continuing airworthiness management services for the aircraft.

If CASA is satisfied that, when an authorisation was issued under regulation 42.630, a requirement mentioned in subregulation 42.630(1) or (2) was not met, CASA may give the continuing airworthiness management organisation that issued the authorisation a direction:
to make a change to the authorisation; or
to cancel the authorisation.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
Note: The continuing airworthiness management organisation must comply with the direction—see regulation 42.665.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation cancels an authorisation issued under regulation 42.630, the organisation must give the holder of the authorisation notice in writing of the cancellation, including the date on which the cancellation takes effect.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Requirements and offences for continuing airworthiness management organisations

section.heading: Provision of continuing airworthiness management services

content.p: If a continuing airworthiness management organisation provides continuing airworthiness management services it must provide the services only in accordance with:
its exposition; and
its approval, including any limitations applying to the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation’s exposition relates to the duties of an employee of the organisation, the organisation must make the part of the organisation’s exposition that relates to those duties available to the employee before the employee begins carrying out the duties.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation issues an authorisation under regulation 42.630 in relation to an aircraft, the organisation must, within 14 days after issuing the authorisation, give a copy of the authorisation to the registered operator of the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The continuing airworthiness management organisation must retain a copy of the authorisation for at least 2 years after the authorisation ceases to be in force.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The organisation must keep any record evidencing the matters mentioned in paragraph 42.630(2)(e) in relation to an authorisation under regulation 42.630 for at least 2 years after the authorisation ceases to be in force.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1), (2) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.

If CASA gives a direction to a continuing airworthiness management organisation under regulation 42.625 or 42.640, the organisation must comply with the direction within the time mentioned in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Giving information in accordance with contract

content.p: If:
a continuing airworthiness management organisation enters into a contract with the registered operator of an aircraft as mentioned in regulation 42.040 or 42.045; and
the organisation has information about the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft that relates to a matter mentioned in paragraph 42.050(2)(d);
the organisation must give the information to the registered operator in accordance with the contract.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: See regulation 42.055 for the requirement for the registered operator of an aircraft to give information to the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft.

section.heading: Notice of contravention of Part to be given to CASA

content.p: If:
a continuing airworthiness management organisation enters into a contract with the registered operator of an aircraft as mentioned in regulation 42.040 or 42.045; and
the organisation has reasonable grounds to believe that the registered operator has contravened a provision of this Part;
the organisation must give CASA written notice of the contravention within 7 days after the organisation forms the belief that the contravention has occurred.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If the organisation is an individual, he or she is not excused from giving a notice under subregulation (1) on the ground that the information in the notice might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.
However:
the information in the notice; or
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of giving the notice;
is not admissible in evidence against the individual in criminal proceedings other than proceedings for an offence against subsections 136.1(1) or (4), 137.1(1) or 137.2(1) of the Criminal Code.
Subpart 42.H—Maintenance certification and certificate of release to service

Note 1: Subsections 136.1(1) and (4), 137.1(1) and 137.2(1) of the Criminal Code provide for offences in relation to false or misleading statements in applications and false or misleading information or documents.
Note 2: See regulation 42.075 for the equivalent requirement for a registered operator.
This Subpart sets out requirements for the performance of maintenance certification and the issue of certificates of release to service when maintenance has been carried out.

division.heading: Maintenance certification for maintenance carried out on aircraft

content.p: This Division applies if an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft.

If the maintenance is carried out by an individual on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must ensure that maintenance certification for the maintenance is performed on behalf of the organisation:
by an individual mentioned in subregulation (2); and
before the organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(a), the individual must be a certifying employee of the organisation:
whose certification authorisation permits him or her to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance; and
who carried out the maintenance, or supervised the carrying out of the maintenance by another individual.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Individuals performing maintenance certification on behalf of approved maintenance organisations

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not perform maintenance certification for the maintenance on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation unless:
he or she is a certifying employee of the organisation whose certification authorisation permits him or her to perform maintenance certification for the maintenance; and
he or she carried out the maintenance, or supervised the carrying out of the maintenance by another individual.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she performs maintenance certification for the maintenance on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation; and
either:

at the time of performing the maintenance certification, he or she is not a certifying employee of the organisation whose certification authorisation permits him or her to perform the maintenance certification; or
he or she did not carry out the maintenance, or supervise the carrying out of the maintenance by another individual.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

If the maintenance is carried out by an independent maintainer, the independent maintainer must perform maintenance certification for the maintenance before the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If the maintenance is carried out by an individual mentioned in item 2 of table 42.300, the independent maintainer who supervised the carrying out of the maintenance must perform maintenance certification for the maintenance before the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before performing maintenance certification

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not perform maintenance certification for the maintenance unless he or she has ensured that:
the maintenance has been carried out in accordance with:
this Part; and
Part 145, if applicable; and
the information required by regulation 42.395 for the maintenance has been recorded.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she performs maintenance certification; and
he or she did not comply with subregulation (1) before performing the maintenance certification.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by organisations before performing maintenance certification

content.p: Obligation
An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual who performs maintenance certification on its behalf complies with subregulation 42.705(1).
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual performs maintenance certification on its behalf; and
the individual did not comply with subregulation 42.705(1) before performing the maintenance certification.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
To perform maintenance certification for the maintenance, an individual must:
sign the record that contains the information required by regulation 42.395 for the maintenance; and
record, in that record:
the date of the maintenance certification; and
if he or she carried out the maintenance on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation—his or her certification authorisation number; and
if he or she did not carry out the maintenance on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation—his or her aircraft engineer licence number, pilot licence number or flight engineer licence number.

Note: The information required under regulation 42.395 about maintenance, and the maintenance certification for the maintenance, together constitute the maintenance record for the maintenance—see the definition of maintenance record in regulation 42.015.
This Division applies if an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft.

section.heading: Requirement not to release aircraft without certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation—approved maintenance organisation

If an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must not release the aircraft to another person unless the organisation has issued a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual carries out maintenance on an aircraft on behalf of the organisation; and
the organisation has not issued a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance; and
the organisation releases the aircraft to another person.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Obligation—independent maintainer

If an independent maintainer carries out maintenance on an aircraft, or supervises the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual, the independent maintainer must not release the aircraft to another person unless the independent maintainer has issued a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
Offence for breach of obligation
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
the independent maintainer carries out maintenance on an aircraft, or supervises the carrying out of maintenance on an aircraft by another individual; and
the independent maintainer has not issued a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance; and
the independent maintainer releases the aircraft to another person.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Who may issue certificate of release to service

content.p: If maintenance was carried out on an aircraft on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation may issue a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.

If an approved maintenance organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance, the organisation must ensure that the certificate is issued on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is a certifying employee of the organisation; and
whose certification authorisation permits him or her to issue the certificate for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Individuals issuing certificates of release to service on behalf of approved maintenance organisations

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not issue a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft unless:
he or she is a certifying employee of the organisation; and
his or her certification authorisation permits him or her to issue the certificate for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she issues a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and
at the time of issuing the certificate:
he or she is not a certifying employee of the organisation; or
he or she is a certifying employee of the organisation, but his or her certification authorisation does not permit him or her to issue the certificate for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
If an independent maintainer carries out maintenance on an aircraft, the independent maintainer may issue a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.

If an individual mentioned in item 2 of table 42.300 carries out maintenance on an aircraft, the independent maintainer who supervised the carrying out of the maintenance may issue a certificate of release to service for the aircraft in relation to the maintenance.
Note: A person mentioned in item 1 of table 42.300 is the only independent maintainer who is permitted to supervise the carrying out of maintenance by another individual—see subregulation 42.300(2).
An independent maintainer commits an offence if:
the independent maintainer issues a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and
the issuing of the certificate by the independent maintainer is not permitted by subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Requirements for issuing certificate of release to service

section.heading: Requirements to be met before certificate of release to service may be issued

content.p: The following are the requirements for the issue of a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft:
the certificate complies with regulation 42.760;
the information entered into the certificate is correct;
maintenance certification has been performed for all of the maintenance;

if the maintenance included critical control system maintenance—the information mentioned in subregulation 42.345(3) has been recorded in the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft in relation to the critical control system maintenance;
in respect of the maintenance, the aircraft is airworthy;
if there is a defect in the aircraft, and the rectification of the defect has not been deferred in accordance with Subdivision 42.D.6.1:
the certificate includes details of the defect; and
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft has been notified that:
(A) the certificate is to be issued; and
(B) there is a defect in the aircraft, and the rectification of the defect has not been deferred in accordance with Subdivision 42.D.6.1;
if maintenance requested for the aircraft (other than the rectification of a defect mentioned in paragraph (f)) has not been carried out:
the certificate includes details of the maintenance that has not been carried out; and
the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft has been notified that:
(A) the certificate is to be issued; and
(B) maintenance requested for the aircraft (other than the rectification of a defect mentioned in paragraph (f)) has not been carried out.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by approved maintenance organisations before issuing certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation

An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual does not issue a certificate of release to service on its behalf for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.745 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual issues a certificate of release to service on its behalf for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.745 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before issuing certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not issue a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.745 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she issues a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.745 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Form, content and issue of certificate of release to service

section.heading: Form and content of certificate of release to service

content.p: A document is a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft only if it includes the following information:
information identifying the certificate as a certificate of release to service;
the aircraft’s registration mark;

if the maintenance was carried out by an approved maintenance organisation—the organisation’s approval certificate reference number and the certification authorisation number of the employee issuing the certificate;

if the maintenance was not carried out by an approved maintenance organisation—the name and aircraft engineer licence number, pilot licence number or flight engineer licence number of the individual issuing the certificate.
The certificate must be included in the flight technical log for the aircraft on which the maintenance was carried out.

section.heading: How certificate of release to service is issued

content.p: To issue a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft, an individual must:
sign the certificate; and
record the date and time of issue on the certificate.

section.heading: Retaining copy of certificate of release to service

content.p: If a certificate of release to service for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft is issued on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must ensure that a copy of the certificate is retained for 1 year beginning on the date the certificate is issued.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Certificate of release to service—aeronautical products

content.p: This Division applies if an individual carries out maintenance on an aeronautical product on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation.
Note 1: Maintenance certification is not required for maintenance carried out on aeronautical products.

Note 2: Under regulation 42.305, only approved maintenance organisations and individuals carrying out maintenance on behalf of approved maintenance organisations are permitted to carry out maintenance on aeronautical products.

section.heading: Requirement not to release aeronautical product without certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation

If an individual carries out maintenance on an aeronautical product on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation must not release the product for use in an aircraft or another aeronautical product unless the organisation has issued a certificate of release to service for the aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance.
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual carries out maintenance on an aeronautical product on behalf of the organisation; and
the organisation has not issued a certificate of release to service for the aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance; and
the organisation releases the product for use in an aircraft or another aeronautical product.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Who may issue certificate of release to service

content.p: If maintenance was carried out on an aeronautical product on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation, the organisation may issue a certificate of release to service for the aeronautical product in relation to the maintenance.

If an approved maintenance organisation issues a certificate of release to service for the product in relation to the maintenance, the organisation must ensure that the certificate is issued on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is a certifying employee of the organisation; and
whose certification authorisation permits him or her to issue the certificate for the product in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Individuals issuing certificates of release to service on behalf of approved maintenance organisations

content.p: Obligation

An individual must not issue a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product unless:
he or she is a certifying employee of the organisation; and
his or her certification authorisation permits him or her to issue the certificate for the product in relation to the maintenance.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she issues a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product; and
at the time of issuing the certificate:
he or she is not a certifying employee of the organisation; or
he or she is a certifying employee of the organisation, but his or her certification authorisation does not permit him or her to issue the certificate for the product in relation to the maintenance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Requirements for issuing certificate of release to service

section.heading: Requirements to be met before certificate of release to service may be issued

content.p: The following are the requirements for the issue of a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product:
the information entered into the certificate for the maintenance is correct;
the maintenance is complete;
the maintenance was carried out in accordance with:
this Part; and
Part 145, if applicable;
in respect of the maintenance, the product is serviceable.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by approved maintenance organisations before issuing certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation

An approved maintenance organisation must ensure that an individual does not issue a certificate of release to service on its behalf for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.795 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An approved maintenance organisation commits an offence if:
an individual issues a certificate of release to service on its behalf for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.795 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before issuing certificate of release to service

content.p: Obligation

An individual must not issue a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.795 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she issues a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.795 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

subDivision.heading: Form and issue of certificate of release to service

section.heading: Form of certificate of release to service

content.p: Maintenance that is not in-house maintenance
A document is a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance:
that is carried out on the product; and
that is not in-house maintenance;
only if the document is in the approved form.
In-house maintenance
Note: Under regulation 11.018, a certificate of release to service in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.
A document is a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product in relation to in-house maintenance carried out on the aeronautical product only if the document is:
in the approved form; or
in the form of an in-house release document.
Note 1: Under regulation 11.018, a certificate of release to service in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.
Note 2: For the definition of in-house release document, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.

section.heading: How certificate of release to service is issued

content.p: To issue a certificate of release to service on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product, an individual must:
sign the certificate; and
record the date of issue on the certificate.

subDivision.heading: Record-keeping and dealing with certificate of release to service

section.heading: Additional record for certificate of release to service issued as in-house release document

content.p: This regulation applies if a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product in relation to in-house maintenance carried out on the product is issued in the form of an in-house release document.
The Part 145 organisation that carried out the in-house maintenance must:
ensure that a record is made that contains the information that, if the certificate was issued in the approved form, would have been recorded on the approved form; and
retain the record until the end of 2 years after the date the organisation fits the aeronautical product to an aircraft or another aeronautical product.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For the definition of in-house release document, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.

section.heading: Dealing with certificate of release to service

content.p: If an approved maintenance organisation issues a certificate of release to service for an aeronautical product in relation to maintenance carried out on the product, the organisation must:
give the certificate to the person to whom the product is released for use in an aircraft or another aeronautical product; and
retain a copy of the certificate for 2 years beginning on the date the certificate is issued.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.I—Airworthiness reviews and airworthiness review certificates
This Subpart applies to an aircraft:
that is authorised to operate under an AOC; or
that is a large aircraft.
This Subpart sets out:
requirements in relation to airworthiness review certificates and airworthiness reviews for aircraft operating under an AOC and large aircraft; and
the relationship between an airworthiness review certificate and a certificate of airworthiness.

section.heading: Who may issue airworthiness review certificate

content.p: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may issue an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation issues an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft, the organisation must ensure that the certificate is issued on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is an airworthiness review employee of the organisation; and
whose authorisation as an airworthiness review employee permits the employee to issue an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met for issue of airworthiness review certificate

content.p: The following are the requirements for the issue of an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft:
the information entered into the certificate is correct;

an airworthiness review employee of the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft has carried out an airworthiness review for the aircraft in accordance with regulation 42.900;
a record of the findings of the review has been made in accordance with regulation 42.905;
any corrective action that was necessary to ensure that the requirements of subregulations 42.900(2) and (3) are met for the aircraft has been taken;
a record of action mentioned in paragraph (d) has been made in accordance with regulation 42.910;
the aircraft is airworthy.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by continuing airworthiness management organisations before issuing airworthiness review certificate

content.p: Obligation

A continuing airworthiness management organisation must ensure that an individual does not issue an airworthiness review certificate on its behalf for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.845 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
A continuing airworthiness management organisation commits an offence if:
an individual issues an airworthiness review certificate on its behalf for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.845 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before issuing airworthiness review certificate

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not issue an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.845 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she issues an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.845 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
A document is an airworthiness review certificate only if it is in the approved form.
Note: Under regulation 11.018, an airworthiness review certificate in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.

section.heading: How airworthiness review certificate is issued

content.p: To issue an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft, an individual must:
sign the certificate; and
record the date of issue and date of expiry on the certificate.

section.heading: How long airworthiness review certificate remains in force

content.p: An airworthiness review certificate remains in force:
for 1 year beginning on the day it is issued; and
if the time for which it is in force is extended under Division 42.I.3—until the end of the time for which it is in force is extended.

section.heading: Who may extend airworthiness review certificate

content.p: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may extend the time for which an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft is in force if the organisation:
issued the certificate; and
has been the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft since the date of issue of the certificate.
A continuing airworthiness management organisation commits an offence if:
it extends the time for which an airworthiness review certificate is in force; and
the extension is not permitted by subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation extends the time for which an airworthiness review certificate is in force, the organisation must ensure that the time for which the certificate is in force is extended on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is an airworthiness review employee of the organisation; and
whose authorisation as an airworthiness review employee permits the employee to issue an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met for extension of airworthiness review certificate

content.p: This regulation sets out the requirements for extending the time for which an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft is in force.
The time for which the certificate is in force may be extended only within the period of 90 days before the certificate is due to expire.
The time for which the certificate is in force is to be extended must be no more than 1 year starting immediately after the certificate is due to expire.
The time for which the certificate is in force may be extended no more than twice.
The aircraft must be airworthy.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by continuing airworthiness management organisations before extension of airworthiness review certificate

content.p: Obligation

A continuing airworthiness management organisation must ensure that an individual does not extend an airworthiness review certificate on its behalf for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.880 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
A continuing airworthiness management organisation commits an offence if:
an individual extends an airworthiness review certificate on its behalf for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.880 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before extending airworthiness review certificate

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not extend an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.880 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she extends an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.880 is not met in relation to the issuing of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: How airworthiness review certificate is extended

content.p: To extend the time for which an airworthiness review certificate is in force, an individual must:
sign the certificate; and
record on the certificate the date of the extension and the new date of expiry of the certificate.
This regulation sets out the procedure for carrying out an airworthiness review for an aircraft.

An airworthiness review employee of the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft must examine the continuing airworthiness records for the aircraft to determine whether the following requirements are met:
the details of the utilisation of the airframe, engine and propeller of the aircraft have been recorded in accordance with regulation 42.190;
maintenance required by the maintenance program for the aircraft has been carried out in accordance with the maintenance program;
critical control system maintenance recorded in the records has been dealt with in accordance with Division 42.D.5;
defects in the aircraft have been rectified in accordance with regulation 42.115;
if the rectification of defects in the aircraft have been deferred—the deferral was in accordance with Subdivision 42.D.6.1;
the requirements mentioned in paragraph 39.002(1)(b), (c) or (d) have been complied with for each airworthiness directive:
that applies to the aircraft or an aeronautical product fitted to the aircraft; and
from the operation of which the aircraft or aeronautical product is not excluded under subregulation 39.002(2) or paragraph 39.004(2)(b) or (3)(b);
if a modification has been made to the aircraft—there is a Part 21 approval for the design of the modification;
for each aeronautical product that is fitted to the aircraft and has a life limit, the records:
correctly identify the aeronautical product; and
show that the aeronautical product has not exceeded its life limit at the time the airworthiness review is carried out;
the following information for the aircraft is recorded in the records and is up to date:
the empty weight of the aircraft;
the position of the centre of gravity on the aircraft when the aircraft is in its empty weight configuration;
the aircraft complies with its approved design.

Note: For paragraph (j), the empty weight of the aircraft, and the position of the centre of gravity on the aircraft when the aircraft is in its empty weight configuration, must be determined in accordance with the method set out in Civil Aviation Order 100.7—see regulation 42.185.
The airworthiness review employee must carry out a survey of the aircraft to determine whether the following requirements are met:
markings that are required, by or under these Regulations or by the aircraft’s type certification basis, to be on the aircraft:
are correct; and
are in the correct position on the aircraft;
placards that are required, by or under these Regulations or by the aircraft’s type certification basis, to be fitted to the aircraft are correctly fitted;
the configuration of the aircraft complies with the aircraft’s approved design;
any defect in the aircraft that is apparent to the employee is recorded in the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft;
the aircraft’s flight manual is up to date and reflects the aircraft’s configuration;
the condition of the aircraft is consistent with the continuing airworthiness records for the aircraft.
Note 1: For paragraph (a), see Parts 45 and 90 and the Part 90 Manual of Standards.
Note 2: For paragraph (b), see Part 90 and the Part 90 Manual of Standards.
Note 3: For paragraph (e), for the definition of flight manual, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.

section.heading: Record of findings of airworthiness review

content.p: If an airworthiness review employee of a continuing airworthiness management organisation has carried out an airworthiness review for an aircraft, the organisation must comply with subregulation (2) before the organisation issues an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The organisation must ensure that the findings of the review, including whether the requirements of subregulations 42.900(2) and (3) are met for the aircraft, are recorded in writing.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation takes corrective action to ensure that the requirements of subregulations 42.900(2) and (3) are met for an aircraft, the organisation must ensure that the action taken is recorded in writing before the organisation issues an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Retaining records relating to airworthiness review certificates

content.p: If a continuing airworthiness management organisation issues an airworthiness review certificate for an aircraft, the organisation must retain:
the record mentioned in subregulation 42.905(2) for the aircraft; and
the record mentioned in subregulation 42.910(1) for the aircraft (if any); and
a copy of the certificate;
for 3 years beginning on the date of issue of the certificate.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Documents to be sent to CASA and registered operator

content.p: If a continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft issues an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft, the organisation must give a copy of the certificate to the following persons within 10 days after issuing the certificate:
CASA;
if the organisation is not the registered operator of the aircraft—the registered operator.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If the organisation extends the time for which the certificate is in force, the organisation must give a copy of the certificate, with the extension recorded on it, to the following persons within 10 days after extending the time for which the certificate is in force:
CASA;
if the organisation is not the registered operator of the aircraft—the registered operator.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Notice of decision not to issue airworthiness review certificate

content.p: If:
an airworthiness review employee of the continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft carries out an airworthiness review for an aircraft; and
the organisation decides not to issue an airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft because a requirement mentioned in paragraph 42.845(d) or (f) is not met;
the organisation must, within 2 days after making the decision, notify the persons mentioned in subregulation (2) of the decision and the reasons for the decision.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The organisation must notify:
CASA; and
if the organisation is not the registered operator of the aircraft—the registered operator.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Relationship of airworthiness review certificate to certificate of airworthiness

content.p: If the certificate of airworthiness for an aircraft expires or is cancelled, the airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft ceases to be in force at the same time as the certificate of airworthiness expires or is cancelled.

If the certificate of airworthiness for an aircraft is taken to not be in force under subregulation 21.181(4) for a period, the airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft is taken to not be in force for the same period.
For the purposes of subregulation (1A), the period during which the airworthiness review certificate is taken to not be in force counts as part of the period for which the certificate was issued.

If the certificate of airworthiness for an aircraft is suspended under regulation 21.181, the airworthiness review certificate for the aircraft is suspended for the same period as the certificate of airworthiness is suspended.
Subpart 42.J—Approval of maintenance programs and variations of approved maintenance programs
This Subpart sets out the process and requirements for:
approval of maintenance programs; and
approval of variations of approved maintenance programs.

division.heading: Approval of maintenance programs by continuing airworthiness management organisations

section.heading: Circumstances in which continuing airworthiness management organisations may approve proposed maintenance program

content.p: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may approve a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft if:
the aircraft is not authorised to operate under an Australian air transport AOC; and
the organisation’s approval under Subpart 42.G permits it to approve proposed maintenance programs under this Division for that type and model of aircraft.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation approves a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft, the organisation must ensure that the program is approved on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is a maintenance program approval employee of the organisation; and
whose authorisation as a maintenance program approval employee permits the employee to approve a maintenance program for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note 1: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval of a proposed maintenance program for the aircraft—see subregulation 42.970(1).

Note 2: In some circumstances, the continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft must apply to CASA for approval of a proposed maintenance program for the aircraft—see subregulation 42.970(2).

section.heading: Requirements for approval of maintenance programs

content.p: The following are the requirements for the approval of a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft by the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft:

the program complies with the requirements in the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, and for aeronautical products fitted to the aircraft, that relate to maintenance that is required by the instructions to be carried out on a regular basis;
the program complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by continuing airworthiness management organisations before approving proposed maintenance programs

content.p: Obligation

A continuing airworthiness management organisation must ensure that an individual does not approve a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft on its behalf unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.945 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
A continuing airworthiness management organisation commits an offence if:
an individual approves a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft on its behalf; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.945 is not met in relation to the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before approving proposed maintenance programs

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not approve a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.945 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she approves a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.945 is not met in relation to the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
To approve a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft, an individual must:
make a record that:
identifies the maintenance program to which it relates; and
includes a statement to the effect that the maintenance program is approved; and
includes the name and approval certificate reference number of the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft; and
sign and date the record.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation approves a proposed maintenance program, the organisation must retain, for the period during which the approved maintenance program is in effect, a copy of the following documents:
the approved maintenance program;
the record of the approval;
any other documents that support the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Approval of maintenance programs by CASA

section.heading: Application to CASA for approval of maintenance programs

content.p: The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval of a proposed maintenance program for the aircraft.
The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft must apply to CASA for approval of a proposed maintenance program for the aircraft if:

the proposed maintenance program does not comply with the requirements in the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, or for an aeronautical product fitted to the aircraft, that relate to maintenance that is required by the instructions to be carried out on a regular basis; or

the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft is a continuing airworthiness management organisation, but its approval under Subpart 42.G does not permit it to approve proposed maintenance programs under Division 42.J.2 for that type and model of aircraft; or
the aircraft is authorised to operate under an Australian air transport AOC.
An application to CASA for approval of a proposed maintenance program must:
be in writing; and
include a copy of the program; and

if the program does not comply with the requirements in the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, or for an aeronautical product fitted to the aircraft, that relate to maintenance that is required by the instructions to be carried out on a regular basis—include the technical justification for the non-compliance.

section.heading: Approval of maintenance programs by CASA

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft if CASA is satisfied that the program:
complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
adequately provides for the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.

division.heading: Approval of variations of approved maintenance programs by continuing airworthiness management organisations

section.heading: Circumstances in which continuing airworthiness management organisations may approve proposed variations

content.p: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may approve a proposed variation of the approved maintenance program for the aircraft if the organisation’s approval under Subpart 42.G permits it to approve proposed variations of maintenance programs under this Division for that type and model of aircraft.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation approves a proposed variation of an approved maintenance program for an aircraft, the organisation must ensure that the program is approved on behalf of the organisation by an individual:
who is a maintenance program approval employee of the organisation; and
whose authorisation as a maintenance program approval employee permits the employee to approve a maintenance program for the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

Note 1: The continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of the approved maintenance program for the aircraft—see subregulation 42.1015(1).

Note 2: In some circumstances, a continuing airworthiness management organisation for an aircraft must apply to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of the approved maintenance program for the aircraft—see subregulation 42.1015(2).

section.heading: Requirements to be met for approval of variations of maintenance programs

content.p: The following are the requirements for the approval of a variation of a proposed maintenance program for an aircraft by the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft:

the program, as varied by the proposed variation, would comply with the requirements in the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, and for aeronautical products fitted to the aircraft, that relate to maintenance that is required by the instructions to be carried out on a regular basis;
the approved maintenance program for the aircraft, as varied by the proposed variation, would comply with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by continuing airworthiness management organisations before approving proposed variations

content.p: Obligation

A continuing airworthiness management organisation must ensure that an individual does not approve a proposed variation to an approved maintenance program for an aircraft on its behalf unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.990 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
A continuing airworthiness management organisation commits an offence if:
an individual approves a proposed variation to an approved maintenance program for an aircraft on its behalf; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.990 is not met in relation to the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements to be met by individuals before approving proposed variations

content.p: Obligation
An individual must not approve a proposed variation to an approved maintenance program for an aircraft unless the requirements mentioned in regulation 42.990 are met.
Offence for breach of obligation
An individual commits an offence if:
he or she approves a proposed variation of an approved maintenance program for an aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in regulation 42.990 is not met in relation to the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
To approve a proposed variation of an approved maintenance program for an aircraft, an individual must:
make a record that:
identifies the maintenance program to which it relates; and
includes details of the variation to which it relates; and
includes a statement to the effect that the variation is approved; and
includes the name and approval certificate reference number of the continuing airworthiness management organisation for the aircraft; and
