sign and date the record.

If a continuing airworthiness management organisation approves a proposed variation to an approved maintenance program, the organisation must retain, for the period during which the approved maintenance program is in effect, a copy of the following documents:
the approved variation;
the record of the approval;
any other documents that support the approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Approval of variations of approved maintenance programs by CASA

section.heading: Application to CASA for approval of variations of approved maintenance programs

content.p: The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of the approved maintenance program for the aircraft.
The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft must apply to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of the approved maintenance program for the aircraft if:

the program, as varied by the proposed variation, would not comply with the requirements in the instructions for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft, or for an aeronautical product fitted to the aircraft, that relate to maintenance that is required by the instructions to be carried out on a regular basis; or

the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for the aircraft is a continuing airworthiness management organisation, but its approval under Subpart 42.G does not permit it to approve variations of maintenance programs under Division 42.J.4.
An application to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of an approved maintenance program for an aircraft must:
be in writing; and
include the following:
a copy of the variation;
the technical justification for the variation.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a proposed variation of an approved maintenance program for an aircraft if CASA is satisfied that the program, as varied by the proposed variation:
would comply with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards; and
would adequately provide for the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
Subpart 42.K—Directions to vary approved maintenance programs
This Subpart:
empowers CASA to give directions to vary approved maintenance programs and approved reliability programs; and
requires the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft to comply with a direction.

section.heading: CASA may direct variations of approved maintenance programs

content.p: CASA may direct the person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft to vary the approved maintenance program for the aircraft:
to include a particular requirement for maintenance in the program; or
to vary a requirement for maintenance in the program.
CASA may give the direction only if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary to do so to ensure that the program will adequately provide for the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
The person must comply with the direction within the time specified in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.L—Approval of reliability programs and variations of approved reliability programs
This Subpart sets out the requirements for:
approval of reliability programs for aircraft to which regulation 42.155 applies; and
approval of variations of approved reliability programs.

section.heading: Application for approval of reliability programs

content.p: The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft to which regulation 42.155 applies may apply, in writing, to CASA for approval of a proposed reliability program for the aircraft.
The application must include a copy of the program.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve the program if CASA is satisfied that the program complies with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.

division.heading: Approval of variations of approved reliability programs

section.heading: Application for approval of variations of approved reliability programs

content.p: The person responsible for continuing airworthiness for an aircraft for which there is an approved reliability program may apply, in writing, to CASA for approval of a proposed variation of the program.
The application must include a copy of the variation.

section.heading: Approval of variations of approved reliability programs

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve the variation if CASA is satisfied that the program, as varied by the proposed variation, would comply with the requirements specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards.
Note 1: See Part 11 for other matters relating to applications and decisions.
Note 2: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
Subpart 42.M—Requirements for pilots
This Subpart sets out requirements for pilots.

If an aircraft’s flight manual requires a pre-flight inspection of the aircraft to be carried out before the aircraft is operated for a flight, the pilot in command of the aircraft must ensure that a pre-flight inspection of the aircraft is carried out before the aircraft is operated for the flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: For the definition of flight manual, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Recording information in flight technical log—all aircraft

content.p: Defects and exceeding operating limits

(1) The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight (the first flight) must ensure that, before the aircraft is next operated for flight, the following information is recorded in the flight technical log for the aircraft:
details of any defect of which the pilot becomes aware during the operation of the aircraft, including:
any abnormal instrument indication; and
any abnormal behaviour by the aircraft;
any instance of the exceeding of an operating limit specified in the aircraft’s flight manual during the first flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: For paragraph (b), for the definition of flight manual, see Part 1 of the Dictionary.
Utilisation information mentioned in regulation 42.190

If the flight technical log for an aircraft is capable of containing the information mentioned in regulation 42.190 for each flight for the aircraft, the pilot in command of the aircraft for a flight must record that information for the flight in the log before the aircraft is next operated for flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Strict liability applies to paragraph (1)(b).
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.N—Record-keeping requirements
This Subpart sets out requirements for records made under this Part.

section.heading: Requirements for making records made under Part

content.p: If a person is required to record information under this Part, or to ensure that information is recorded, the person must ensure that the record:
is written in a legible form in English; and
will remain legible for the time for which the record is required, by this Part, to be kept.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Requirements for keeping records made under Part

content.p: If a person is required to record information under this Part, or to ensure that information is recorded, the person must ensure that the record is kept:
in a system that allows the record to be retrieved; and
in a manner that protects the record from being lost, damaged or accidentally altered.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Change to records made under Part

content.p: If a person makes a change to a record made under this Part, the person must make the change in a manner:
that retains the original record; and
that identifies himself or herself; and
that includes the date the change is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 42.O—Copying or disclosing cockpit voice recording information
This Subpart sets out the authorisation of persons for paragraph 32AP(3A)(a) of the Act.

section.heading: Authorisation of persons for paragraph 32AP(3A)(a) of Act

content.p: For paragraph 32AP(3A)(a) of the Act, the following persons are authorised:
a person who:
(i) is a staff member within the meaning of the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003; and
has had training with respect to the replay and analysis of cockpit voice recordings; and
has been briefed on the requirements of Part IIIB of the Act;
a person who:
is to check on behalf of an approved maintenance organisation whether equipment used to make a cockpit voice recording is functioning and reliable; and
has had training from the organisation with respect to the replay and analysis of cockpit voice recordings; and
has been briefed by the organisation on the requirements of Part IIIB of the Act.

The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

The Legislation Act 2003 provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.
If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

Subpart 45.A—Preliminary
This Part applies in relation to the operation of an Australian aircraft required to be registered under Division 47.C.1.
However, this Part does not apply to a Part 103 aircraft (other than a sailplane).
In these Regulations:
aircraft registration identification plate, for an aircraft, means a plate displaying the aircraft’s markings.
Australian nationality mark means the capital letters “VH”.
character means a letter, a digit or a hyphen.
exhibition means an air show or a film or television production.

section.heading: Meaning of markings and set of markings

content.p: (1) Markings, for an aircraft, are the Australian nationality mark and the aircraft’s registration mark, in that order, connected by a hyphen.
However, if the aircraft is a registered sailplane operating in Australian territory:
the aircraft’s markings need not include the Australian nationality mark; and
if the first letter of the aircraft’s registration mark is “G”—the aircraft’s markings need not include that first letter.
(3) A set of markings, for an aircraft, is an instance of the aircraft’s markings.

section.heading: References to aircraft operating for an exhibition

content.p: In this Part, a reference to an aircraft operating for an exhibition includes a reference to the aircraft:
flying in the exhibition, or in a practice or test flight for the exhibition; or
flying between locations where the aircraft is participating in the exhibition or in the practice or test flight; or
flying between a location where the aircraft is participating in the exhibition, or in the practice or test flight, and the aircraft’s base of operations.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 45

content.p: For subsection 38(1) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
Note: The Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument: see subsection 38(1) of the Act.

section.heading: Registration holder to provide copies of approvals under this Part to registered operator

content.p: This regulation applies if:
the registration holder of an aircraft holds an approval under this Part for the aircraft; and
the registration holder is not the registered operator of the aircraft.
The registration holder contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated; and
the registration holder has not provided a copy of the approval to the registered operator of the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 45.B—Aircraft markings
The Part 45 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the display of markings on aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 45 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
when markings must be displayed;
the number of sets of markings that must be displayed;
the location of sets of markings on aircraft;
the characters to be used in each set of markings, including height requirements.
Aircraft must comply with Part 45 Manual of Standards if operated
The registration holder and the registered operator of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated; and
(b) a requirement (the prescribed requirement) prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.050 applies to the aircraft; and
the prescribed requirement is not met.
Exception—operating with dealer’s mark
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the aircraft is operating with a dealer’s mark in accordance with Subpart 47.H.
Exception—approvals
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the registration holder of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 45.065 to display markings other than in accordance with the prescribed requirement; and
the requirements specified in the approval are complied with.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the registration holder of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 45.070:
to display markings other than in accordance with the prescribed requirement; or
to display no markings;
for the purposes of an exhibition; and
the aircraft is operated for the exhibition during the period of the approval; and
the requirements specified in the approval are complied with.
Exception—certain Commonwealth and State functions
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the aircraft is operated:
in relation to the performance of a function of an authority of the Commonwealth, or an authority or agency of a State; and
in circumstances in which knowledge of the operation may:
reduce the effectiveness of the performance of the function; or
expose a person to the danger of physical harm or death arising from the actions of another person.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) to (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Designs etc. not to modify, obscure or create confusion about sets of markings

content.p: The registration holder and the registered operator of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated; and
a design, mark or symbol on an aircraft modifies, obscures or creates confusion about a set of markings on the aircraft.
Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to:
a Defence Force symbol or call-sign on an aircraft operated by the Defence Force; or
a design, mark or symbol on an aircraft approved in writing by CASA.
CASA must not grant an approval under paragraph (2)(b) if granting the approval would adversely affect the safety of air navigation.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Approval to operate with different markings—aircraft of special configuration

content.p: (1) The registration holder of an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval to display markings on the aircraft other than in accordance with a requirement (the prescribed requirement) prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.050.
CASA must approve the application if CASA is satisfied that, because of the configuration of the aircraft, the prescribed requirement specified in the application cannot be met.
The approval must:
be in writing; and
specify the requirements for the display of markings on the aircraft that must be met.

section.heading: Approval to operate with different or no markings—aircraft operated for an exhibition

content.p: Applications for approval to display different or no markings at an exhibition
The registration holder of an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval, for the purposes of an exhibition:
(a) to display markings on the aircraft other than in accordance with a requirement (the prescribed requirement) prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.050; or
to display no markings on the aircraft.
The application for approval must include the following:
the kind of exhibition, and the name (if any) of the exhibition;
the dates and times during which the aircraft will be operated for the exhibition;
the location of the exhibition, including the relevant flight paths;
a photograph or drawing of the aircraft showing the colour of the aircraft and any marks the applicant intends the aircraft to bear while it is operated for the exhibition.
Requirements for approvals
CASA must approve the application if CASA is satisfied that:
the aircraft will be operated for an exhibition; and
the display of markings in accordance with the prescribed requirement would be inconsistent with the operation of the aircraft for the exhibition; and
if the exhibition is in a foreign country—the display of markings in accordance with an approval, or the display of no markings, would not contravene a law of that country.
The approval must:
be in writing; and
specify the requirements (if any) for the display of markings on the aircraft that must be met while the aircraft is operated for the exhibition; and
state the period of the approval.
Markings must be displayed in cockpit and visible to crew
The registration holder and the registered operator of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the registration holder holds an approval under this regulation in relation to the aircraft and an exhibition; and
the aircraft is operated for the exhibition; and
the Australian nationality mark and the registration mark of the aircraft are not:
displayed in the cockpit; and
clearly visible to the aircraft’s crew.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 45.C—Requirement to display words on certain aircraft
The Part 45 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the display of specified words on the following kinds of aircraft:
aircraft for which a special airworthiness certificate of the kind mentioned in regulation 21.189 is in force;
aircraft for which a special airworthiness certificate of the kind mentioned in regulation 21.185 is in force;
aircraft for which a provisional certificate of airworthiness is in force;
experimental aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 45 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
the words that must be displayed;
the location of the words;
the manner in which the words must be displayed, including the colour and height of the letters used.
The registration holder and the registered operator of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated; and
(b) a requirement (the prescribed requirement) prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.090 applies to the aircraft; and
the prescribed requirement is not met.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the registration holder of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 45.100 to:
display words other than in accordance with the prescribed requirement; or
to display no words;
for the purposes of an exhibition; and
the aircraft is operated for the exhibition during the period of the approval; and
any requirements specified in the approval are complied with.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Approval to operate with different or no words—aircraft operated for an exhibition

content.p: Applications for approval to display different or no words at an exhibition
The registration holder of an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval, for the purposes of an exhibition:
(a) to display words on the aircraft other than in accordance with a requirement (the prescribed requirement) prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.090; or
to display no words on the aircraft.
The application for approval must include the following:
the kind of exhibition, and the name (if any) of the exhibition;
the dates and times during which the aircraft will be operated for the exhibition;
the location of the exhibition, including the relevant flight paths;
a photograph or drawing of the aircraft showing the colour of the aircraft and any marks the applicant intends the aircraft to bear while it is operated for the exhibition.
Requirements for approvals
CASA must approve the application if CASA is satisfied that:
the aircraft will be operated for an exhibition; and
the display of words in accordance with the prescribed requirement would be inconsistent with the operation of the aircraft for the exhibition; and
if the exhibition is in a foreign country—the display of words in accordance with an approval, or the display of no words, would not contravene a law of that country.
The approval must:
be in writing; and
specify the requirements (if any) for the display of words on the aircraft that must be met while the aircraft is operated for the exhibition; and
state the period of the approval.
Prescribed word must be displayed and visible
The registration holder and the registered operator of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the registration holder holds an approval under this regulation in relation to the aircraft and an exhibition; and
the aircraft is operated for the exhibition; and
if a specified word for the aircraft is prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.090—the word is not:
displayed in the cockpit; and
clearly visible to the aircraft’s crew.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 45.D—Aircraft registration identification plate
This Subpart applies to an aircraft if:
the aircraft has a maximum take-off weight of more than 5 700 kg; or
the aircraft is operating outside Australian territory; or
the aircraft does not have a manufacturer’s data plate attached in accordance with regulation 21.820.

section.heading: Plate to be attached to aircraft

content.p: The registration holder and the registered operator of the aircraft each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the aircraft’s markings must be displayed on the aircraft registration identification plate for the aircraft;
the method of displaying the aircraft’s markings must meet the requirements prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
the plate must be attached to the aircraft in a way that ensures that the plate is not likely to be defaced or to become detached from the aircraft;
the plate must be attached at the location on the aircraft prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
the plate must be constructed of the material prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to the requirement mentioned in paragraph (2)(b) if:
the registration holder of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 45.135 to display the aircraft’s markings using a different method; and
the markings are displayed using that method.
Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to the requirement mentioned in paragraph (2)(d) if:
the registration holder of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 45.140 to operate the aircraft with the plate attached in a different place; and
the requirements specified in the approval are complied with.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3) or (4): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person removes the aircraft registration identification plate from an aircraft; and
the removal is not:
for the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Part; or
for the purpose of carrying out maintenance on the aircraft in accordance with these Regulations.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person alters the aircraft registration identification plate of an aircraft; and
the alteration is not for the purpose of ensuring compliance with this Part.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Approval of method of displaying markings

content.p: The registration holder of an aircraft may apply to CASA for approval of a method of displaying the aircraft’s markings on the aircraft registration identification plate for the aircraft.
CASA must approve the application if CASA is satisfied that the method of displaying the aircraft’s markings is similar to marking by etching, stamping or engraving.
The approval must be in writing.

section.heading: Approval for attachment of plate—aircraft of special configuration

content.p: The registration holder of an aircraft (other than a balloon) may apply to CASA for approval to attach the aircraft registration identification plate for the aircraft to the aircraft other than in accordance with paragraph 45.125(2)(d).

CASA must approve the application if CASA is satisfied that, because of the configuration of the aircraft, the requirements prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards for the purposes of paragraph 45.125(2)(d) cannot be met.
The approval must:
be in writing; and
specify the requirements for attaching the plate to the aircraft.

Subpart 47.A—General
This Part sets out:
how aircraft are registered; and
how registration marks are assigned to aircraft.
It also sets out how dealer’s marks are assigned to manufacturers, distributors and dealers of aircraft, and regulates their use.
In this Part:
CDCL has the same meaning as in the International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Rules 2014.

eligible person means one of the following: a resident of Australia who is: 18 years of age or older; and (ii) an Australian citizen or the holder of a permanent visa (within the meaning of the Migration Act 1958); (b) a corporation incorporated under the Corporations Act 2001; (c) a body incorporated under a law (other than the Corporations Act 2001) in force in Australia; the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; an agency of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; a foreign corporation that is lawfully carrying on business in Australia.
a resident of Australia who is:
18 years of age or older; and
(ii) an Australian citizen or the holder of a permanent visa (within the meaning of the Migration Act 1958);
(b) a corporation incorporated under the Corporations Act 2001;
(c) a body incorporated under a law (other than the Corporations Act 2001) in force in Australia;
the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory;
an agency of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory;
a foreign corporation that is lawfully carrying on business in Australia.
IDERA has the same meaning as in the International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Rules 2014.
owner, of an aircraft, includes a part-owner of the aircraft who is appointed under regulation 47.020.
registered operator has the meaning given by regulation 47.100.

Note: The owner of an aircraft who becomes its registration holder must, if he or she is not eligible to be its registered operator, appoint an eligible person as the registered operator: see regulation 47.100.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 47

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 47 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.

section.heading: Requirement for aircraft to be registered

content.p: For paragraph 20AA(1)(b) of the Act, an aircraft is required to be registered unless it is one of the following:
an aircraft that is not intended to be used as an aircraft;
an aircraft that, under Subpart 200.B, is exempt from these Regulations;
an unmanned free balloon;
a permanently tethered balloon;
a kite;
a model aircraft;
a parachute;
a rocket;
an aircraft that is prescribed by an instrument under subregulation (1B) for the purposes of this paragraph;
an aircraft that is registered under the law of a foreign country referred to in subregulation (2);
an aircraft that satisfies all the following conditions:
it has been manufactured in Australia for delivery outside Australia to a foreign operator;
it is registered under the law of a foreign country referred to in subregulation (2);
it displays nationality and registration marks in accordance with the law of that country;
it has no certificate of airworthiness issued, or rendered valid, under the law of that country;
it is flown within Australia only for a purpose mentioned in paragraph 21.197(1)(b) or (c);
a Part 103 aircraft mentioned in subparagraph 103.005(4)(b)(i), (ii), (iva), (v), (vi) or (vii) that is listed with a Part 103 ASAO;
a Part 103 aircraft mentioned in subparagraph 103.005(4)(b)(iii) or (iv);
an RPA (other than a large RPA or an aircraft prescribed for the purposes of subregulation 47.096(2)) that is being operated only:
for the purposes of a test flight; and
in circumstances applicable to the aircraft and the test flight that are prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards for the purposes of subregulation 101.099B(1).
Note: For registration requirements affecting aircraft for which a special flight permit is issued, see subregulation 21.197(3).
For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act and paragraph 47.015(1)(i) of this regulation, CASA may issue an instrument prescribing:
classes of medium RPA, small RPA, very small RPA or micro RPA; or
particular medium RPA, small RPA, very small RPA or micro RPA.
Note 1: An instrument made under paragraph (a) is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.
Note 2: An instrument made under paragraph (b) is not a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AB) of the Act.
For paragraph (1)(j) and subparagraph (1)(k)(ii), the foreign countries are:
the Contracting States; and
any other foreign country with which Australia has an agreement that allows an aircraft registered under the law of that country to be operated in Australia.
Note: For the definition of Contracting State see section 3 of the Act.

section.heading: Appointment of person to act on behalf of owners

content.p: If an aircraft is owned by more than 1 person, and is required to be registered under Division 47.C.1, the owners must, to register the aircraft, appoint one of them to act on their behalf.
Subpart 47.B—The Australian Civil Aircraft Register
CASA must keep a register called the Australian Civil Aircraft Register, or ensure that it is kept, in accordance with this Subpart.
Note: The Australian Civil Aircraft Register is the successor to the Aircraft Register mentioned in regulation 8 of CAR: see regulation 202.221.

section.heading: Access to Australian Civil Aircraft Register

content.p: CASA must make the entries in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register about aircraft registered under Division 47.C.1 available for inspection by members of the public at reasonable times and places, and subject to reasonable conditions.
CASA may comply with subregulation (1) by making the information in those entries accessible on the internet or by another suitable electronic means.
CASA must correct the information recorded in an entry in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register as soon as practicable after becoming aware that the entry is out of date or otherwise incorrect.

Note: An aircraft registration holder who finds out that anything in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register in relation to the aircraft is not correct must tell CASA about the change that should be made to the Register: see regulation 47.115.

If CASA thinks that there may be an error in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register in relation to an aircraft, CASA may ask the aircraft registration holder, in writing, to give CASA information that may show the accuracy of the entry.
Note: Information that must be given to CASA under subregulation (1) may include a copy of a relevant document.
A request under subregulation (1) must:
describe the information; and
specify a period of at least 28 days, starting when the request is given to the registration holder, during which the registration holder must give CASA the information.
Note: CASA may cancel the registration of an aircraft if the registration holder fails to comply with a request for information made under subregulation (1): see regulation 47.132.
A registration holder must comply with a request made under subregulation (2).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence under subregulation (3) is an offence of strict liability.
A notice that, under this Part, must be given to CASA may be delivered, posted, sent by fax or sent by e-mail.
Note: The address, fax number and e-mail address for notices can be found in the advisory circular for this Part or on CASA’s website: www.casa.gov.au.
CASA may refuse to accept a notice that is not legible.

CASA must give, to the registration holder of an aircraft registered under Division 47.C.1, a copy of the information in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register that relates to the holder and the aircraft.
CASA must give the copy of the information within 28 days after:
the end of 3 years after the day on which:
an aircraft is registered; or
if the aircraft’s certificate of registration is transferred—the certificate is transferred; and
the end of each period of 3 years after that day.
Within 28 days after the day when the registration holder is given the copy of the information, the holder must:
if necessary, correct the information on the copy about the aircraft and the holder; and
return the copy to CASA.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3) is an offence of strict liability.
Information given to CASA for subregulation (3) must not be used as evidence of an offence against regulation 47.115.
This regulation is not intended to limit the operation of regulations 47.035 and 47.040.

section.heading: Entries in Register etc not conclusive evidence of title to aircraft

content.p: An entry in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register in relation to an aircraft is not conclusive evidence of the existence of a legal or beneficial property interest in the aircraft.
A certificate of registration for an aircraft is not conclusive evidence of the existence of a legal or beneficial property interest in the aircraft.
Subpart 47.C—Registration of aircraft

division.heading: Registration of aircraft other than certain RPA

content.p: This Division applies to aircraft other than aircraft to which Division 47.C.2 applies.
Note: Division 47.C.2 primarily deals with the registration of medium RPA, small RPA, very small RPA and micro RPA.

section.heading: Applying for registration of unregistered aircraft

content.p: An application to register an unregistered aircraft may be made by the owner or a person who is acting on behalf of, and at the direction or request of, the owner.
The application must be made:
in writing; or
orally (by telephone or in person).

Note: An oral application must be confirmed in writing in accordance with regulation 47.070. If an oral application is not confirmed in writing in accordance with that regulation, the registration lapses: see regulation 47.130.
An application for registration made in writing must:
be made in an approved form; and
include the information set out in regulation 47.065; and
be signed by the person making the application.
An application for registration made in writing must also include a declaration, signed by the person making the application:
that the aircraft will be used as an aircraft; and
if the aircraft has not been registered before—that the aircraft has never been registered; and
if the aircraft has been registered before (whether in Australia or not)—that the aircraft is not, at the time of the application, registered on a foreign civil aircraft register.
For paragraph 47.060(3)(b), and subject to regulation 47.075, the following information must be included in an application for registration of an aircraft:
the owner’s name and address;
if the aircraft is owned by more than 1 person—the name and signature of the owner who is appointed to act on behalf of the owners; and
if the application is made by a person on behalf of the owner—the name and address of the person making the application;
if the owner proposes to appoint another person as the registered operator of the aircraft—the registered operator’s name and postal address, and:
if the registered operator is an individual—his or her home address; or
if the registered operator is a corporation—the corporation’s registered address;
for an aircraft that has a type certificate, type acceptance certificate or provisional type certificate:
the number of the certificate (if applicable); and
the production certificate number (if applicable); and
the manufacturer, and the country and year of manufacture, of the aircraft; and
the aircraft model; and
the aircraft serial number;
Note: For paragraph (d), the aircraft’s manufacturer, model and serial number are those set out on the aircraft’s data plate.
for an aircraft to which paragraph (d) does not apply—the following:
the aircraft manufacturer (if applicable);
the aircraft builder (if applicable);
whether the aircraft is a manned free balloon, an airship, a glider, a power-driven aeroplane, a rotorcraft or an ornithopter;
the country and year of manufacture of the aircraft;
the aircraft model;
the aircraft serial number;
if the aircraft is power-driven—the number of engines and whether they are piston, turbopropeller or jet turbine engines;
the number of seats including seats for the crew;
whether the aircraft is able to be used on land, on water, or on both;
if a registration mark has been reserved for the aircraft, and the reservation has not lapsed—the registration mark;
if the aircraft has been imported:
the name of the country from which the aircraft was imported; and
the aircraft’s registration mark, if any, in that country; and
evidence, provided by the national aviation authority of that country, that the aircraft is not on the aircraft register of that country.
Note: If the application for registration is an oral application, CASA will ask for the information mentioned in this regulation during the oral application.
A person who has applied orally for the registration of an aircraft must give to CASA a written confirmation of the application.
The confirmation:
must be in an approved form; and
must include the information required by regulation 47.065; and
must be received by CASA within 14 days after the day on which the oral application was made.

section.heading: CASA may ask for further information

content.p: If CASA reasonably requires further information to enable it to consider an application for the registration of an aircraft, CASA may ask the applicant, in writing, to give CASA the information.
CASA must describe the information in the request.
CASA may refuse to consider, or cease considering, the application until the applicant complies with the request.
CASA must register an aircraft if the application for the registration of the aircraft is made in accordance with regulation 47.060.
However, if:
(a) the aircraft has been registered before (the old registration); and
the old registration was cancelled; and
the aircraft was subject to an IDERA at the time of the cancellation;
CASA must not register the aircraft unless subregulation (1B) or (1C) applies to the aircraft.
This subregulation applies to the aircraft if:
the old registration was cancelled at the request of:
the authorised party under the IDERA; or
if the aircraft was subject to a CDCL at the time of the cancellation—the certified designee under the CDCL; or

CASA is satisfied, on the basis of written evidence provided by the person who has applied for the registration of the aircraft, that the authorised party under the IDERA, or the certified designee under the CDCL, as the case may be, has consented to CASA registering the aircraft.
This subregulation applies to the aircraft if CASA is satisfied, after reasonable enquiries, that:

for an aircraft that was subject to a CDCL at the time of the cancellation of the old registration—the certified designee under the CDCL and the authorised party under the IDERA have both ceased to exist; or
for an aircraft that was not subject to a CDCL at the time of the cancellation of the old registration—the authorised party under the IDERA has ceased to exist.
If CASA registers an aircraft, CASA must enter the following information about the aircraft in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register:
the registration mark assigned to the aircraft;
whether the aircraft is a manned free balloon, an airship, a glider, a power-driven aeroplane, a rotorcraft or an ornithopter;
its manufacturer, model and serial number;
its country and year of manufacture;
the name and address of the owner;
the name and address of the registered operator;
the day on which it was registered.
If CASA registers an aircraft on the basis of an oral application, CASA must:
issue an interim certificate of registration for the aircraft; and
tell the applicant:
the time and date from which the interim registration is in force; and
a unique number that identifies the registration.
Note 1: An interim certificate includes the information set out in paragraph 47.080(2)(a) and the applicable provisions in paragraphs 47.080(2)(c) to (g).
Note 2: If the oral application is not confirmed in accordance with regulation 47.070, the registration of the aircraft lapses: see regulation 47.130.

If CASA registers an aircraft on the basis of an oral application, the aircraft registration holder must not allow the aircraft to be taken outside Australia before CASA issues the certificate of registration for the aircraft.
Maximum penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: An interim certificate of registration is not covered by the provisions of Annex 7 to the Chicago Convention, so is only valid for flights within Australia.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
An interim certificate of registration for an aircraft ceases to be in force on the earlier of the following:
the day that CASA gives the certificate of registration to the aircraft’s registration holder;
14 days after the day on which CASA registered the aircraft on the basis of an oral application.
If CASA:
registers an aircraft because it has received a written application; or
receives confirmation of an oral application for the registration of an aircraft;
CASA must give a certificate of registration for the aircraft to the aircraft’s owner (the registration holder).
Note: The certificate of registration replaces any interim certificate of registration issued under regulation 47.085.
The registration of an aircraft has effect unless, in accordance with these Regulations, it lapses, is suspended or is cancelled.

division.heading: Registration of medium RPA, small RPA, very small RPA and micro RPA

content.p: This Division applies to the following aircraft:
a medium RPA;
a small RPA;
a very small RPA;
a micro RPA.
However, this Division does not apply to an RPA that is prescribed by an instrument under subregulation (3) for the purposes of this subregulation.
Note: Division 47.C.1 applies to an aircraft to which this Division does not apply—see regulation 47.058.
For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act and subregulation (2) of this regulation, CASA may issue an instrument prescribing:
classes of aircraft; or
particular aircraft.
Note 1: An instrument made under paragraph (a) is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.
Note 2: An instrument made under paragraph (b) is not a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AB) of the Act.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates, or conducts an operation using, an aircraft that is required to be registered under this Division; and
the aircraft is not registered under this Division.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person supervises the operation by another person of an aircraft that is required to be registered under this Division; and
the other person is under 16 years old; and
the aircraft is not registered under this Division.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Application for registration of certain RPA

content.p: A person may apply to CASA to register an aircraft as an RPA.
Note: In addition to this regulation, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for registration under this Division.
However, an individual may apply to register an aircraft as an RPA under this Division only if the individual is at least 16 years old.
Note: The person who applies to register the aircraft will be the registration holder of the aircraft: see the definition of registration holder in Part 1 of the Dictionary.
Payment of unmanned aircraft levy
An application to register an aircraft as an RPA under this Division must be accompanied by the unmanned aircraft levy (if any) for the application.
Waiver or refund of unmanned aircraft levy

CASA may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, waive the payment of unmanned aircraft levy under subregulation (4), or refund levy that has been paid under that subregulation, if CASA is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances justifying the waiver or refund.
The waiver or refund:
may be of the whole or part of the levy; and
may be made by CASA on its own initiative, or on written application in the approved form by the applicant for the registration.

Subject to regulation 11.055, on an application under regulation 47.097, CASA must register an aircraft as an RPA under this Division if CASA is satisfied that the aircraft is required to be registered as provided by regulation 47.015.
If CASA registers an aircraft as an RPA under this Division, CASA must, as soon as practicable:
enter the following information about the aircraft in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register:
the serial number on the aircraft or, if there is no serial number, the registration mark assigned by CASA to the aircraft;
whether the aircraft is registered as an RPA;
the name and address of the registration holder of the aircraft;
the day on which the aircraft was registered;
the manufacturer of the aircraft;
the manufacturer’s model (if any) of the aircraft;
any other information required by the approved form for the application; and
issue a certificate of registration for the aircraft to the registration holder of the aircraft.
The registration of an aircraft under this Division:
begins at the time when the aircraft is registered; and
ends at the end of the period of 12 months beginning from the day when the registration begins, unless sooner cancelled.
Example: If an RPA is registered on 15 October 2022, the registration of the RPA will generally end at the end of 14 October 2023.
Note: For cancellation of a registration, see regulations 47.131C and 47.132.

section.heading: Requirement to produce certificate of registration (or copy)

content.p: A person who operates, or conducts an operation of, an RPA must produce a certificate of registration, or a copy of such a certificate, in relation to the aircraft for inspection on a demand made by a person covered by subregulation (2).
For the purposes of subregulation (1), this subregulation covers the following persons:
an authorised person;
a member or special member of the Australian Federal Police;
a member of a police force or a police service of a State or Territory.
(3) A person (the offender) commits an offence of strict liability if:
the offender operates, or conducts an operation of, an RPA; and
a person makes a demand of the offender under subregulation (1); and
the offender fails to comply with the demand.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.

A person who supervises the operation by another person of an RPA must produce a certificate of registration, or a copy of such a certificate, in relation to the aircraft for inspection on a demand made by a person covered by subregulation (2).
(5) A person (the supervisor) commits an offence of strict liability if:
the supervisor supervises the operation by another person of an RPA; and
the other person is under 16 years old; and
a person makes a demand of the supervisor under subregulation (4); and
the supervisor fails to comply with the demand.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
Subpart 47.D—Registered operator
This Subpart applies in relation to an aircraft required to be registered under Division 47.C.1.
Note: See regulation 47.058.

section.heading: Identity of registered operator of aircraft

content.p: (1) If the registration holder of an aircraft is an eligible person, the holder is the aircraft’s registered operator.
However, the registration holder may appoint another eligible person as the registered operator.
If the registration holder is not an eligible person, the registration holder must appoint an eligible person to be the registered operator.

Note: If the registration holder of an aircraft is not an eligible person, and no eligible person is appointed as the registered operator, CASA must suspend the aircraft’s registration: see regulation 47.131A.
The appointment of a registered operator has effect unless the appointment is cancelled or otherwise ceases to have effect.

Note: Regulation 202.222 provides that a reference in CAR to the holder of a certificate of registration of an aircraft is taken to be a reference to the registered operator of the aircraft. Under CAR, the holder of the certificate of registration is responsible for the maintenance and continuing airworthiness of the aircraft.
Subject to this regulation, the appointment of a registered operator of an aircraft may be cancelled by:
the registration holder of the aircraft; or
the registered operator.
If the registration holder of an aircraft:
appoints a person as the aircraft’s registered operator; or
cancels the appointment of a person as the aircraft’s registered operator;

the registration holder must, within 14 days after the appointment or cancellation, give CASA a notice in an approved form, including the aircraft’s registration mark, manufacturer, model and serial number.

(5AA) If a person cancels the appointment of the person as an aircraft’s registered operator as referred to in paragraph (4A)(b), the person must, within 14 days after the cancellation, give CASA a notice in an approved form, including the aircraft’s registration mark, manufacturer, model and serial number.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person fails to comply with a requirement under subregulation (5) or (5AA).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

If CASA finds out, other than by a notice given in accordance with subregulation (5), that the appointment of the registered operator of an aircraft has ceased to have effect, CASA must, within 5 business days, inform the aircraft’s registration holder in writing.
A notice of the appointment of a registered operator must also include:
the registered operator’s name and postal address, and:
if the registered operator is an individual—his or her home address; or
if the registered operator is a corporation—the address of the corporation’s registered office; and
the date of the appointment of the registered operator; and
evidence that the registered operator accepts the appointment.
A notice of the cancellation of the appointment of a registered operator given under subregulation (5) or (5AA) must include the date of the cancellation.

Note: If the appointment of the registered operator is cancelled and another registered operator is not appointed, the registration holder becomes the aircraft’s registered operator. However, if the registration holder is not an eligible person, CASA must suspend the aircraft’s registration: see regulation 47.131A.
If CASA receives a notice that complies with this regulation, CASA must:
amend the Australian Civil Aircraft Register to show the name and address of the new registered operator; and
in writing, notify the registration holder and the new registered operator about the amendment of the Register.
Subpart 47.E—Transfer of ownership of aircraft
This Subpart applies in relation to an aircraft required to be registered under Division 47.C.1.
Note: See regulation 47.058.

section.heading: Meaning of former owner and new owner

content.p: For this Subpart, if the ownership of an aircraft is transferred, the transferor is the former owner and the transferee is the new owner.
(1) In this regulation, transfer notice means a notice in an approved form that relates to the transfer of ownership of an aircraft and:
shows:
the aircraft’s registration mark, manufacturer, model and serial number; and
the date of the transfer; and
the former owner’s name and address; and
the new owner’s name and address; and
either:
is signed by the former owner; or
is signed by a person acting on behalf of, and at the direction or request of, the former owner.
If a transfer notice is signed by a person acting on behalf of the former owner, it must include evidence of the person’s authority to do so.
This regulation sets out how, if the ownership of an aircraft is transferred, the new owner becomes the aircraft’s registration holder.
In accordance with the timetable mentioned in subregulation (4A), the former owner, or a person acting on behalf of the former owner, must:
give CASA a transfer notice; and
give the new owner:
a copy of the transfer notice; and
the aircraft’s certificate of registration.
The documents mentioned in subregulation (4) must be given to CASA and the new owner:
as soon as practicable after the transfer; and
in any case, within 14 days after the transfer.
Within 28 days after the transfer, the new owner must apply to become the registration holder.
Note: If the aircraft’s new owner does not apply to be the new registration holder within 28 days after the day of the transfer, CASA must suspend the aircraft’s registration: see regulation 47.131.
An application must:
be in an approved form; and
either:
be signed by the new owner; or
if the application is made by a person on behalf of the new owner—include the name, address and signature of the person making the application.
CASA must, if it receives a transfer notice and an application that complies with subregulation (6):
amend the Australian Civil Aircraft Register to show the new owner as the registration holder; and
give a certificate of registration to the new owner.
Note 1: The new owner, as the registration holder, is also the registered operator of the aircraft unless the new owner appoints another person as the registered operator: see regulation 47.100.
Note 2: If the new owner is not an eligible person, the new owner must appoint an eligible person as the registered operator: see subregulation 47.100(3).
Subregulation (7) has effect subject to subregulation (9).
CASA must not take any action under subregulation (7) in relation to an aircraft unless CASA is satisfied, on the basis of written evidence provided by the former owner, that:
in the case of an aircraft that is subject to an IDERA, and is not subject to a CDCL—the authorised party under the IDERA has consented to the action being taken; or
in the case of an aircraft that is subject to a CDCL—the certified designee under the CDCL has consented to the action being taken.
Subpart 47.F—Administration of Australian Civil Aircraft Register

section.heading: Notice of error in information in Register

content.p: If an aircraft registration holder finds out that anything in the Australian Civil Aircraft Register in relation to the aircraft is no longer correct, the holder must tell CASA in writing, within 14 days after finding out, about the change that should be made.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.
If the aircraft was registered following an oral application, the registration lapses if:
CASA does not receive a written confirmation of the application in accordance with regulation 47.070; or
within 14 days after the day the oral application was made, CASA has not received a written confirmation that includes all the information mentioned in regulation 47.065; or
CASA receives a document purporting to be a written confirmation that includes information that differs in a significant way from the corresponding information given orally to CASA.

section.heading: Suspension and cancellation of registration following a transfer of ownership

content.p: This regulation applies if:
the ownership of an aircraft registered under Division 47.C.1 is transferred; and
the new owner does not, within 28 days after the day of the transfer, make an application that complies with subregulation 47.110(6) to be the aircraft’s registration holder.
CASA must, by written notice given to the new owner, suspend the aircraft’s registration.
The suspension remains in force until the first-occurring of the following:
CASA issues a new certificate of registration to the new owner;
CASA cancels the registration.

If the new owner does not, within 3 months after the day the aircraft’s registration was suspended, make an application that complies with subregulation 47.110(6) to be the aircraft’s registration holder, CASA must, by written notice given to the new owner, cancel the registration.

section.heading: Suspension and cancellation of registration if registered operator is not an eligible person

content.p: If CASA becomes aware that the registered operator of an aircraft is not an eligible person, CASA must, by written notice given to the registration holder of the aircraft, suspend the aircraft’s registration.
Note: Subregulation (1) will not apply if the registration holder of the aircraft is an eligible person: see subregulation 47.100(1).
The suspension:
takes effect on the day the notice is given to the registration holder; and
ends at the earlier of the following times:
when the Australian Civil Aircraft Register is amended, in accordance with subregulation 47.100(8), to show the name and address of a new registered operator;
when CASA cancels the registration.

If the registration holder does not, within 3 months after the day the aircraft’s registration was suspended under this regulation, give a notice under subregulation 47.100(5) appointing an eligible person as the aircraft’s registered operator, CASA must, by written notice given to the registration holder, cancel the registration.
The cancellation takes effect on the day the notice is given to the registration holder.

section.heading: Cancellation of registration at holder’s request—limitations

content.p: CASA must not cancel, under Subpart 11.D, the registration of an aircraft registered under Division 47.C.1 if:
in the case of an aircraft that is subject to an IDERA, and is not subject to a CDCL—the person who requests the cancellation is not the authorised party under the IDERA; or
in the case of an aircraft that is subject to a CDCL—the person who requests the cancellation is not the certified designee under the CDCL.
CASA must, by written notice given to the registration holder of an RPA registered under Division 47.C.2, cancel the registration of the aircraft if:

CASA is satisfied that the aircraft has been modified to such an extent that, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards for the purposes of subregulation 101.099A(1), the aircraft is no longer an aircraft to which the registration applies; or
CASA is satisfied that the cancellation of the registration is necessary to maintain the accuracy of the Register.
Note: For review of a decision to cancel a registration, see regulation 201.004.

CASA may, by written notice given to the registration holder of an RPA registered under Division 47.C.2, cancel the registration of the RPA if another certificate of registration for the RPA is issued to another person.

section.heading: Cancellation of registration on other grounds

content.p: CASA must, by written notice given to the registration holder of an aircraft, cancel the registration of the aircraft if CASA becomes aware that the aircraft:
is registered under the law of another country; or
is no longer to be used as an aircraft; or
has been stolen or destroyed.

CASA may, by written notice given to the registration holder of an aircraft, cancel the registration of the aircraft if the registration holder does not comply with a request under subregulation 47.040(1).

(3) CASA must, by written notice given to the registration holder of an aircraft, cancel the registration of the aircraft if CASA is required, under the International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Rules 2014, to de-register the aircraft.
A cancellation under this regulation takes effect on the day the notice is given to the registration holder.
Subpart 47.G—Reservation, assignment and change of registration marks
This Subpart applies in relation to an aircraft required to be registered under Division 47.C.1.
Note: See regulation 47.058.
In this Subpart:
aircraft includes an aircraft that: has not yet been built; or is being built.
has not yet been built; or
is being built.
The owner of an aircraft may ask CASA, in writing, to reserve a particular registration mark for the aircraft, whether or not the aircraft is registered.
The request must be in an approved form and identify the aircraft.
On receiving a request, CASA must reserve the registration mark for the aircraft unless, under regulation 47.155, the mark must not be reserved for an aircraft.
Note: About registration marks generally: see Part 45.
The reservation lapses if, 12 months after the day on which the registration mark was reserved, the aircraft is not registered and using the reserved mark.
(5) In subregulation (1), owner includes a person acting on behalf of, and at the direction or request of, the owner.
If a person applies for the registration of an aircraft, and:
CASA has not reserved a registration mark for the aircraft under regulation 47.145; or
the reservation of a registration mark for the aircraft has lapsed;
CASA must assign a registration mark to the aircraft before registering the aircraft.

section.heading: Marks that must not be reserved or assigned

content.p: The following registration marks must not be reserved for, or assigned to, an aircraft:
the registration mark of an Australian aircraft;
a registration mark that has been reserved for an aircraft under regulation 47.145;
a mark that has been assigned to a dealer;
a mark that might be confused with any 5-letter combination used in Part II of the International Code of Signals;
a mark that might be confused with any 3-letter combination beginning with Q used in the Q Code;
a mark that might be confused with the distress signal SOS;
a mark that might be confused with an urgency or safety signal.
Examples: Of urgency or safety signals
XXX, PAN and TTT.

section.heading: Assigning reserved registration mark to unregistered aircraft

content.p: If the owner of an unregistered aircraft:
reserves a registration mark for the aircraft; and
makes an application that complies with regulation 47.060 for registration of the aircraft;
CASA must, when it registers the aircraft, give the applicant a certificate of registration showing the reserved mark.
(1) If the registration holder of a registered aircraft has reserved a registration mark (the reserved mark) for the aircraft:
the holder; or
if the registered operator has the written consent of the registration holder—the registered operator;
may apply to CASA to change the aircraft’s existing mark to the reserved mark.
The application must:
be received by CASA at least 14 days before the day on which the existing mark is proposed to be changed; and
be in an approved form and include the following:
the aircraft’s existing mark;
the aircraft’s manufacturer, model and serial number;
the reserved mark;
the date on which the existing mark is proposed to be changed;
if the application is made by a person on behalf of the registration holder or registered operator—the name and address of the person making the application.
If CASA approves the application, CASA must:
as soon as practicable, notify the applicant, in writing, of the approval; and

on the date specified in the application in accordance with subparagraph (2)(b)(iv), amend the Australian Civil Aircraft Register to show the reserved mark as the registration mark assigned to the aircraft; and
as soon as practicable after making the amendment, give the applicant a certificate of registration showing the reserved mark.
The change of registration mark takes effect on the day the Australian Civil Aircraft Register is amended.
Subpart 47.H—Dealer’s marks
This Subpart applies in relation to an aircraft required to be registered under Division 47.C.1.
Note: See regulation 47.058.
In this Subpart:
aircraft dealer includes a manufacturer or distributor of aircraft.
dealer’s plate means a plate made by an aircraft dealer under regulation 47.205.
This regulation sets out the way in which an aircraft dealer may be assigned 1 or more marks for use on aircraft manufactured, or being distributed or dealt with, by the dealer.
An aircraft dealer may apply to be assigned a mark only if the dealer is an eligible person.
The application must be made in an approved form and must include:
the dealer’s name and address; and
a declaration that the dealer is an eligible person; and
evidence that the dealer is engaged in the manufacture, sales or distribution of aircraft in Australia; and
a request for a particular number of marks and a statement explaining why the dealer needs that number of marks; and
if the application is made by a person on behalf of the dealer—the name and address of the person making the application.
If the application complies with subregulation (3), CASA must assign to the dealer:
the number of marks requested by the dealer; or
if CASA thinks that the dealer has applied for more marks than is reasonably required to undertake the dealer’s business—a lesser number of marks.

section.heading: What marks may be assigned to dealers

content.p: A mark that is assigned to an aircraft dealer must be a mark that could be assigned to an aircraft as a registration mark.
CASA must keep a record of dealer’s marks that have been assigned to aircraft dealers.
The information in the record must include:
the mark; and
the aircraft dealer’s name and address.

section.heading: How long assignment to dealer remains in effect

content.p: The assignment of a dealer’s mark to an aircraft dealer has effect unless CASA revokes the assignment.
Note: For revocation of the assignment of a dealer’s mark: see regulation 47.225.

section.heading: Certificate of assignment of dealer’s mark

content.p: If CASA assigns a dealer’s mark to an aircraft dealer, CASA must give to the dealer a certificate stating that the mark is assigned to the dealer.
Each such certificate must be for 1 dealer’s mark only.
If CASA assigns a dealer’s mark to an aircraft dealer, the dealer may make 1 dealer’s plate bearing that mark.
The plate must:
be a piece of stainless steel (or similar fireproof material) at least 100 mm by 160 mm and at least 1 mm thick; and
be engraved with the following in sans serif capital letters:
‘VH-’ and the mark in letters at least 25 mm high;
‘CIVIL AVIATION SAFETY AUTHORITY’ and ‘DEALER’S PLATE CASR 1998’ in letters at least 8 mm high;
set out as shown in the following diagram, in which the letters ‘ABC’ represent the mark:
An aircraft dealer to whom a dealer’s mark is assigned must use the mark only on an aircraft that:
is not currently registered in any country; and
was manufactured, or is being distributed or dealt with, by the dealer.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.

If title to, or possession of, an unregistered aircraft on which a dealer’s mark is being used passes to another person, the dealer must ensure that the plate is removed from the aircraft before the other person operates the aircraft.
Maximum penalty: 30 penalty units.
The aircraft dealer must keep records showing:
the manufacturer, model and serial number of each aircraft on which the mark was used; and
the periods during which it was used on that aircraft.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.
The aircraft dealer must keep the records for 12 months after the end of the period during which the mark was used on an aircraft.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1), (2), (3) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.
An unregistered aircraft on which a dealer’s mark is being used is taken to be registered during any period in which it is being operated in Australia if:
the aircraft carries the corresponding dealer’s plate; and
the possession of the aircraft remains with the dealer.
Note: Flying an unregistered aircraft may be an offence: see subsection 20AA(1) of the Act.

section.heading: Annual report to CASA on aircraft using dealer’s marks

content.p: An aircraft dealer to whom a dealer’s mark has been assigned must, within 1 month after the end of each reporting period, give CASA a report showing the manufacturer, model and serial number of each aircraft on which the mark was used during that period.
Maximum penalty: 30 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
In subregulation (1):
reporting period means:
the period of 12 months beginning on the day on which the mark was assigned to the dealer; or
each consecutive period of 12 months at the end of which the mark is still assigned to the dealer; or

a period of less than 12 months beginning on the day on which the mark was assigned to the dealer, or an anniversary of that day, and ending on the day on which the assignment of the mark is revoked or otherwise ceases.

section.heading: Revocation of assignment of dealer’s mark etc

content.p: CASA must revoke the assignment of a dealer’s mark to a person if the person:
ceases to be an aircraft dealer, or an eligible person; or
fails to comply with this Subpart.
If CASA revokes such an assignment, it must tell the person in writing that it has done so.
The person must return the certificate of assignment of the mark to CASA within 14 days after receiving the notice of the revocation.
Maximum penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (3) is an offence of strict liability.
