Note: Subpart 61.E sets out certain limitations that apply to all pilot licences, and ratings and endorsements on pilot licences.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of flight activity endorsements—medical certificates

content.p: This regulation applies to the holder of any of the following endorsements:
an aerobatics flight activity endorsement;
an aerobatics (1 500) flight activity endorsement;
an aerobatics (1 000) flight activity endorsement;
an aerobatics (500) flight activity endorsement;
an aerobatics (unlimited) flight activity endorsement;
a formation aerobatics flight activity endorsement;
a spinning flight activity endorsement.
The holder is authorised to conduct an aerobatic or spinning manoeuvre only if the holder:
holds a current class 1 or 2 medical certificate; or
is accompanied by another pilot who:
holds a current class 1 or 2 medical certificate; and
occupies a flight control seat in the aircraft; and
is authorised, under this Part, to conduct the manoeuvre.

section.heading: Requirements for grant of flight activity endorsements

content.p: An applicant for an endorsement mentioned in column 1 of an item in table 61.1145 must:
hold each rating or endorsement (if any) mentioned in column 3 of the item; and
have completed flight training for the endorsement.

Note 1: For paragraph (a), paragraph (a) is satisfied, in relation to a required licence, rating or endorsement, if the applicant holds a certificate of validation of an overseas flight crew licence, rating or endorsement that is equivalent to the licence, rating or endorsement: see item 36 of Part 2 of the Dictionary.
Note 2: For paragraph (b), for the requirements for flight training, see Division 61.B.2.
Subpart 61.T—Pilot instructor ratings

division.heading: Privileges and requirements for grant of flight instructor ratings

content.p: Subject to Subpart 61.E and regulations 61.1170 to 61.1180, a flight instructor is authorised:
to conduct flight training for:
pilot licences; and
ratings on pilot licences, other than:
(A) cruise relief flight engineer type ratings; and
(B) flight examiner ratings; and
endorsements on pilot licences, other than flight examiner endorsements; and
to grant endorsements to holders of pilot licences, other than:
flight examiner endorsements; and
training endorsements mentioned in Part 1 or 2 of table 61.1235; and
endorsements for which a flight test is required; and
to conduct training in multi-crew cooperation; and
to conduct differences training for variants of type ratings; and
to conduct training to meet the general competency requirement in regulation 61.385; and
to conduct flight reviews required by this Part for ratings on pilot licences, other than:
flight examiner ratings; and
cruise relief flight engineer type ratings; and
under Subdivision 61.A.3.1 (Student pilots), to approve a person to pilot an aircraft, including for a solo flight; and
to conduct dual flight checks for a student pilot; and
to approve a person mentioned in regulation 61.125 (Conducting flight activities without rating or endorsement) to pilot an aircraft for the purpose of receiving flight training; and
to approve a person mentioned in regulation 61.120 to transmit on an aviation safety radio frequency; and
to assess the standard of knowledge of an applicant for a pilot licence, or a rating on a pilot licence, in any items mentioned in the applicant’s knowledge deficiency report.
Note: Subpart 61.E sets out certain limitations that apply to all pilot licences, and ratings and endorsements on pilot licences.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of flight instructor ratings—general

content.p: The holder of a flight instructor rating is authorised to exercise the privileges of the rating in an aircraft of a particular category only if the holder has:
completed the aeronautical experience; and
passed the flight test;
required under regulation 61.1185 for the grant of the rating in an aircraft of that category.

The holder of a flight instructor rating is authorised to exercise the privileges of the rating in a flight simulation training device that represents an aircraft of a particular category only if the holder has:
completed the aeronautical experience; and
passed the flight test;
required under regulation 61.1185 for the grant of the rating in an aircraft of that category.

A flight instructor is authorised to conduct flight training for a pilot licence, a rating on a pilot licence or an endorsement on an operational rating only if the instructor is engaged to conduct the flight training by a Part 141 or 142 operator that is authorised to conduct flight training for the licence, rating or endorsement.
A flight instructor is authorised to conduct flight training in an aircraft only if the instructor holds a medical certificate.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of flight instructor ratings—endorsements

content.p: A flight instructor is authorised to conduct flight training mentioned in column 2 of an item in table 61.1235 only if the instructor also holds the endorsement mentioned in column 1 of the item.
A flight instructor is authorised to conduct differences training for a variant of an aircraft type only if the instructor also holds the type rating training endorsement for the aircraft type.

A flight instructor is authorised to conduct training to meet the general competency requirement in regulation 61.385 for a kind of aircraft only if the instructor also holds a training endorsement that authorises the instructor to conduct flight training in the aircraft.

A flight instructor is authorised to grant an endorsement, other than a recreational pilot licence endorsement, only if the instructor also holds a training endorsement required to provide flight training for the endorsement.
A flight instructor is authorised to grant a recreational pilot licence endorsement only if the instructor also holds a grade 1 or 2 training endorsement.
A flight instructor is authorised to approve a student pilot to conduct a solo flight in an aircraft of a particular category only if the instructor also holds:
for the student pilot’s first solo flight in an aircraft of that category—a grade 1 or 2 training endorsement for that aircraft category; or
in any other case—a grade 1, 2 or 3 training endorsement for that aircraft category.
A flight instructor is authorised to conduct a flight review for a rating on a pilot licence only if the instructor also holds:
a grade 1 training endorsement; or
a grade 2 training endorsement; or
the training endorsement required to conduct flight training for the rating.

A flight instructor is authorised to make an assessment of a knowledge deficiency report for an applicant for a flight crew licence or rating only if the instructor also holds a grade 2 training endorsement.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of flight instructor ratings—instructor proficiency check

content.p: The holder of a flight instructor rating is authorised to exercise the privileges of the rating only if the holder has a valid instructor proficiency check.
For subregulation (1), the holder is taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check during the following periods:
the period from when the holder passes the flight test for the rating to the end of the 12th month after the month in which the holder passes the flight test;
if:
the holder passes the flight test for a training endorsement; and
the flight test is conducted more than 6 months after the holder passes the flight test for the rating;
the period from when the holder passes the flight test for the endorsement to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder passes the flight test for the endorsement;

if the holder successfully completes an operator proficiency check that covers operations under the rating and that is conducted by a flight examiner who holds a flight instructor rating flight test endorsement—the period from when the holder successfully completes the check to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder successfully completes the check;
if:
the holder is successfully participating in an operator’s training and checking system for an operation under the rating; and
the operator holds an approval under regulation 61.040 for the system for this subregulation;
the period during which the holder is successfully participating in the system;

if the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check—the period from when the holder successfully completes the check to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder successfully completes the check;
if:
(i) the holder is taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check under any of paragraphs (a) to (e) (the existing check); and
within 3 months before the validity of the existing check expires, the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check;
the period from when the validity of the existing check expires to the end of the 24th month after the validity of the existing check expires.
However, if, at any time, the holder attempts, but does not successfully complete, an instructor proficiency check, the holder is no longer taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check.
For paragraphs (2)(e) and (f), the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check if:
the instructor proficiency check is conducted in an aircraft or an approved flight simulation training device for the proficiency check; and

a person mentioned in subregulation (5) assesses the holder’s competency to conduct flight training as meeting the standards mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for a flight instructor rating; and
the person endorses the holder’s licence document to the effect that the holder has completed the instructor proficiency check on the date stated.
For paragraph (4)(b), the persons are as follows:
CASA;
a flight examiner;
the holder of an approval under regulation 61.040 to conduct the proficiency check.

section.heading: Requirements for grant of flight instructor ratings

content.p: An applicant for a flight instructor rating must:
hold a private pilot licence, commercial pilot licence or air transport pilot licence; and
meet the requirements for the grant of at least one training endorsement.

Note: Paragraph (a) is satisfied if the applicant holds a certificate of validation of an overseas flight crew licence that is equivalent to a private pilot licence, commercial pilot licence or air transport pilot licence: see item 36 of Part 2 of the Dictionary.
The applicant must also have:
passed the aeronautical knowledge examination for the flight instructor rating; and
completed flight training for the rating; and
passed the flight test mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for the flight instructor rating; and
met the following aeronautical experience requirements in an aircraft of the same category as the aircraft used for the flight test:
if the aircraft used for the flight test is a helicopter:
(A) at least 250 hours flight time as a pilot; and
(B) at least 100 hours flight time as pilot in command;
in any other case:
(A) at least 200 hours flight time as a pilot; and
(B) at least 100 hours flight time as pilot in command.
Note 1: For paragraph (a), for the conduct of aeronautical knowledge examinations, see Division 61.B.3.
Note 2: For paragraph (b), for the requirements for flight training, see Division 61.B.2.
Note 3: For paragraph (c), for the conduct of flight tests, see Division 61.B.4.
Note 4: For paragraph (d), for the determination of a person’s flight time and other aeronautical experience, see Division 61.A.2.
The applicant is taken to meet the requirements mentioned in paragraphs (2)(c) and (d) if the applicant:
holds:
a commercial pilot licence with a helicopter category rating; and
a low-level rating and a helicopter low-level endorsement; and
one of the following combinations:
(A) a night VFR rating and a helicopter night VFR endorsement;
(B) an instrument rating and a single-engine helicopter instrument endorsement;
(C) an instrument rating and a multi-engine helicopter instrument endorsement; and
completed his or her flight training for the licence in an integrated training course; and
has passed the flight test mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for the flight instructor rating in a helicopter.
The applicant is taken to meet the requirements mentioned in subparagraph (2)(d)(ii) if the applicant has:

completed an integrated training course for the grant of a commercial pilot licence with the aircraft category rating for the same category of aircraft as used for the flight test for the applicant’s flight instructor rating; and
met the requirements for the grant of the licence with that aircraft category rating.
The applicant must also:
have completed an approved course of training in principles and methods of instruction; or
hold a Certificate IV in Training and Assessment; or
hold a tertiary qualification in teaching.

An applicant to whom subregulation (3) or (3A) does not apply must meet the aeronautical experience requirements mentioned in paragraph (2)(d) before starting the flight training mentioned in paragraph (2)(b).

division.heading: Privileges and requirements for grant of simulator instructor ratings

content.p: Subject to Subpart 61.E and regulations 61.1195 to 61.1205, a simulator instructor is authorised:
to conduct flight training in a flight simulation training device or tethered helicopter for the grant of:
pilot licences; and
ratings on pilot licences, other than:
(A) cruise relief flight engineer type ratings; and
(B) flight examiner ratings; and
endorsements on pilot licences, other than flight examiner endorsements; and
to grant endorsements to holders of pilot licences, other than:
flight examiner endorsements; and
training endorsements mentioned in Part 1 or 2 of table 61.1235; and
recreational pilot licence endorsements; and
endorsements for which a flight test is required; and
to conduct training in multi-crew cooperation; and
to conduct differences training for variants of type ratings; and
to conduct training to meet the general competency requirement in regulation 61.385; and
to conduct flight reviews required by this Part for ratings on pilot licences, other than:
flight examiner ratings; and
cruise relief flight engineer type ratings; and
to approve a person mentioned in regulation 61.120 to transmit on an aviation safety radio frequency; and
to assess the standard of knowledge of an applicant for a pilot licence, or a rating on a pilot licence, in any items listed in the applicant’s knowledge deficiency report.
Note: Subpart 61.E sets out certain limitations that apply to all pilot licences, and ratings and endorsements on pilot licences.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of simulator instructor ratings—general

content.p: The holder of a simulator instructor rating is authorised to exercise the privileges of the rating in a flight simulation training device that represents an aircraft of a particular category only if the instructor has passed the flight test required under regulation 61.1210 for the rating in a flight simulation training device that represents an aircraft of that category.

A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct flight training for a pilot licence, a rating on a pilot licence or an endorsement on an operational rating only if the instructor is engaged to conduct the flight training by a Part 141 or 142 operator that is authorised to conduct the flight training.

A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct flight training for the grant of an endorsement mentioned in column 1 of an item in Part 2 or 3 of table 61.1235 only if the instructor has conducted at least 50 hours of flight training in the activity covered by the endorsement.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of simulator instructor ratings—endorsements

content.p: A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct flight training mentioned in column 2 of an item in table 61.1235 only if the instructor also holds the endorsement mentioned in column 1 of the item.
A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct differences training for a variant of an aircraft type only if the instructor also holds the type rating training endorsement for the aircraft type.

A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct training to meet the general competency requirement in regulation 61.385 for a kind of aircraft only if the instructor also holds a training endorsement that authorises the instructor to conduct flight training in the aircraft.
A simulator instructor is authorised to grant an endorsement only if the instructor also holds the training endorsement required to provide flight training for the endorsement.
A simulator instructor is authorised to conduct a flight review for a rating on a pilot licence only if the instructor also holds:
a grade 1 training endorsement; or
a grade 2 training endorsement; or
the training endorsement required to provide flight training for the rating.

A simulator instructor is authorised to make an assessment of a knowledge deficiency report for an applicant for a flight crew licence or rating only if the instructor also holds a grade 2 training endorsement.

section.heading: Limitations on exercise of privileges of simulator instructor ratings—instructor proficiency check

content.p: The holder of a simulator instructor rating is authorised to exercise the privileges of the rating only if the holder has a valid instructor proficiency check.
For subregulation (1), the holder is taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check during the following periods:
the period from when the holder passes the flight test for the rating to the end of the 12th month after the month in which the holder passes the flight test;
if:
the holder passes the flight test for a training endorsement; and
the flight test is conducted more than 6 months after the holder passes the flight test for the rating;
the period from when the holder passes the flight test for the endorsement to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder passes the flight test for the endorsement;

if the holder successfully completes an operator proficiency check that covers operations under the rating and that is conducted by a flight examiner who holds a pilot instructor rating flight test endorsement—the period from when the holder successfully completes the check to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder successfully completes the check;
if:
the holder is successfully participating in an operator’s training and checking system for an operation under the rating; and
the operator holds an approval under regulation 61.040 for the system for this subregulation;
the period during which the holder is successfully participating in the system;

if the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check—the period from when the holder successfully completes the check to the end of the 24th month after the month in which the holder successfully completes the check;
if:
(i) the holder is taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check under any of paragraphs (a) to (e) (the existing check); and
within 3 months before the validity of the existing check expires, the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check;
the period from when the validity of the existing check expires to the end of the 24th month after the validity of the existing check expires.
However, if, at any time, the holder attempts, but does not successfully complete, an instructor proficiency check, the holder is no longer taken to have a valid instructor proficiency check.
For paragraphs (2)(e) and (f), the holder successfully completes an instructor proficiency check if:
the instructor proficiency check is conducted in an approved flight simulation training device for the proficiency check; and

a person mentioned in subregulation (5) assesses the holder’s competency to conduct flight training as meeting the standards mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for a simulator instructor rating; and
the person endorses the holder’s licence document to the effect that the holder has completed the instructor proficiency check on the date stated.
For paragraph (4)(b), the persons are as follows:
CASA;
a flight examiner;
the holder of an approval under regulation 61.040 to conduct the proficiency check.

section.heading: Requirements for grant of simulator instructor ratings

content.p: An applicant for a simulator instructor rating must:
hold a commercial pilot licence or air transport pilot licence; and
meet the requirements for the grant of at least one training endorsement.

Note: Paragraph (a) is satisfied if the applicant holds a certificate of validation of an overseas flight crew licence that is equivalent to a commercial pilot licence or air transport pilot licence: see item 36 of Part 2 of the Dictionary.
The applicant must also have:
passed the aeronautical knowledge examination for the simulator instructor rating; and
completed flight training for the rating; and
passed the flight test mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for the simulator instructor rating.
Note 1: For paragraph (a), for the conduct of aeronautical knowledge examinations, see Division 61.B.3.
Note 2: For paragraph (b), for the requirements for flight training, see Division 61.B.2.
Note 3: For paragraph (c), for the conduct of flight tests, see Division 61.B.4.
The applicant must also:
have completed an approved course of training in principles and methods of instruction; or
hold a Certificate IV in Training and Assessment; or
hold a tertiary qualification in teaching.
Despite paragraph 61.245(1)(a), the flight test must be conducted in an approved flight simulation training device for the flight test.
A pilot instructor commits an offence if:
the instructor conducts:
flight training for an aircraft class rating, pilot type rating or cruise relief co-pilot type rating; or
differences training;
in an aircraft; and
regulation 61.205 prohibits the conduct of the training in the aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A pilot instructor commits an offence if:
the instructor conducts a flight review for the holder of a pilot licence; and
the holder successfully completes the flight review; and
the instructor does not, within 14 days after the day the flight review is successfully completed:
endorse the holder’s licence document in accordance with subregulation (2); and
give CASA a written notice that complies with subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subparagraph (1)(c)(i), the following details must be endorsed on the licence document:
a statement to the effect that the holder has successfully completed the flight review;
the date on which the flight review was successfully completed;
the rating for which the flight review was conducted.
For subparagraph (1)(c)(ii), the notice must state the following:
the holder’s name and ARN;
that the holder has successfully completed the flight review;
the date on which the flight review was successfully completed;
the rating for which the flight review was conducted;
if the flight review was conducted in an aircraft—the aircraft’s nationality and registration marks;
if the flight review was conducted in a flight simulator—the identifying number for the flight simulator stated on its flight simulator qualification certificate.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A flight instructor commits an offence if:
the instructor approves a person to pilot an aircraft as a student pilot; and
the approval is to pilot the aircraft in a way that is not authorised by the following provisions:
paragraph 61.112(1)(c) or (2)(c) (Flying as a student pilot);
regulation 61.113 (General requirements for student pilots);
regulation 61.114 (Solo flights—medical certificate requirements for student pilots);
regulation 61.115 (Solo flights—recent experience requirements for student pilots).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A flight instructor commits an offence if:
(a) the instructor approves a person (the student) to conduct a solo flight as a student pilot; and
the instructor is not satisfied that the student:
has been briefed appropriately for the flight; and
is capable of conducting the flight safely; and
meets the requirement mentioned in subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subparagraph (2)(b)(iii), the requirement is that:
the student has been assessed by CASA or an examiner as meeting the general English language proficiency standard mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards; or
the student has completed an approved course of training in English language proficiency.
A flight instructor commits an offence if:
(a) the instructor approves a person (the student) to conduct a solo flight of a kind mentioned in subregulation (5) as a student pilot for the first time; and
the instructor is not satisfied that the student:
has completed the training specified by the authorising Part 141 or 142 operator for the conduct of a solo flight of that kind by a student pilot; and
has been assessed by the Part 141 or 142 operator as competent to conduct the solo flight; and
if the solo flight is a cross-country flight and the student is undertaking flight training:
for a private pilot licence, or a commercial pilot licence, with the aeroplane category rating; or
as part of an integrated training course for a private pilot licence, or a commercial pilot licence, with the helicopter category rating;
the student has not completed at least 2 hours of dual instrument time, 1 hour of which is conducted during dual instrument flight time; and
if the solo flight is a night flight—the student has not completed at least 2 hours of dual instrument time, 1 hour of which is conducted during dual instrument flight time.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (4), the kinds of solo flight are as follows:
a circuit training flight;
a flight between an aerodrome and the flight training area for the aerodrome;
a cross-country flight;
a night flight.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
In this regulation:
authorising Part 141 or 142 operator, in relation to an instructor approving a solo flight, means the Part 141 or 142 operator who authorised the instructor to approve the solo flight.

section.heading: Obligations of pilot instructors—approval to operate aircraft radio

content.p: A pilot instructor commits an offence if:

(a) the instructor approves a person who does not hold a flight crew licence, or who holds a recreational pilot licence but does not hold a flight radio endorsement, (the student) to transmit on an aviation safety radio frequency; and
the student does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the requirement is that:
the student has been assessed by CASA or an examiner as meeting the general English language proficiency standard mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards; or
the student has completed an approved course of training in English language proficiency.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Obligations of pilot instructors—records of activities conducted independently of Part 141 or 142 operator

content.p: A pilot instructor commits an offence if:
the instructor conducts a flight review or a session of flight training for a flight crew endorsement, other than an endorsement on an operational rating; and
the training is not conducted on behalf of a Part 141 or 142 operator; and
a record of the training is not made within 7 days after the session.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A pilot instructor commits an offence if the instructor does not retain a record made under subregulation (1) for at least 7 years after the day the record is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
