section.heading: Application of Part 91—Australian aircraft in Australian territory

content.p: This Part applies in relation to the operation of an Australian aircraft in Australian territory.

section.heading: Application of Part 91—Australian aircraft in foreign countries

content.p: This Part applies in relation to the operation of an Australian aircraft in a foreign country.
However, if a law of the foreign country applies to the operation of the aircraft in that country, the law of the foreign country prevails to the extent of any inconsistency.

For the purposes of subregulation (2), a provision of a law of a foreign country is taken not to be inconsistent with a provision of this Part to the extent that the provisions are capable of operating concurrently.

section.heading: Application of Part 91—Australian aircraft over the high seas

content.p: This Part applies in relation to the operation of an Australian aircraft over the high seas.
Annex 2 of the Chicago Convention also applies in relation to the operation of Australian aircraft over the high seas.
However, a provision of Annex 2 of the Chicago Convention prevails to the extent of any inconsistency with a provision mentioned in subregulation (1).

For the purposes of subregulation (3), a provision of Annex 2 of the Chicago Convention is taken not to be inconsistent with a provision mentioned in subregulation (1) to the extent that the provisions are capable of operating concurrently.
This Part (other than Division 91.C.3 and Subparts 91.P and 91.T) applies in relation to the operation of a foreign registered aircraft in Australian territory.
However, this Part does not apply in relation to:
a foreign registered aircraft that is operated in Australian territory under a foreign air transport AOC; or
a foreign registered aircraft that is operated in Australian territory under a New Zealand AOC with ANZA privileges that is in force for Australia.
A provision of this Part applies in relation to the operation of a state aircraft of a foreign country in Australian territory if the provision is expressed to so apply.

section.heading: Application of Part 91—aircraft to which Part 101, 103 or 131 applies

content.p: This Part does not apply in relation to the operation of an aircraft if any provision of Part 101 applies to the operation.
The following provisions of this Part do not apply to the operation of a Part 103 aircraft:
regulation 91.105;
regulations 91.110 and 91.115;
regulation 91.145;
regulation 91.190;
regulation 91.267;
regulations 91.425 and 91.430;
regulations 91.545 and 91.550;
regulation 91.560;
regulations 91.570 and 91.575;
regulation 91.585;
regulations 91.590 to 91.615;
regulations 91.720 and 91.725;
regulations 91.780 and 91.785;
Subpart 91.K;
regulation 91.915.

If Part 103 does not apply to the operation of a touring motor glider because of the operation of subregulation 103.005(2A), then, despite subregulation (2) of this regulation, the provisions mentioned in subregulation (2) of this regulation apply to the operation of the touring motor glider.
The following provisions of this Part do not apply to the operation of a Part 131 aircraft:
Division 91.C.3;
regulation 91.190;
Divisions 91.D.2 and 91.D.3;
regulation 91.255;
regulation 91.265;
regulation 91.267;
Subdivisions 91.D.4.2 and 91.D.4.3;
regulation 91.335;
regulation 91.355;
Subdivision 91.D.4.6 (other than regulation 91.360);
regulation 91.455;
regulation 91.480;
regulation 91.510;
regulation 91.515;
Division 91.D.7 (other than regulations 91.520, 91.525, 91.600 and 91.620);
regulation 91.630;
regulation 91.725;
Subpart 91.F;
Subpart 91.J;
Subpart 91.K;
Subpart 91.P.

content.p: A provision of Part 91 listed in column 1 of an item in the following table does not apply to an operation of an aircraft if a provision of Part 105, 121, 133, 135 or 138 listed in column 2 of that item applies to the operation.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 91

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.
If a provision of this Part, or of the Part 91 Manual of Standards, refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, a person may apply to CASA, in writing, for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, the approval must be granted.
Subregulation 11.055(1B) applies to the granting of an approval under this regulation.

For the purposes of regulations 91.200, 91.320, 91.510, 91.600, 91.655 and 91.745, the operator of an aircraft is taken to hold an approval under this regulation for an activity if the activity is authorised under:
the operator’s AOC or another civil aviation authorisation held by the operator; or
if the operator is required under these Regulations to have an exposition or operations manual—the exposition or operations manual.

For the purposes of regulations 91.860, 91.865, 91.870, 91.875, 91.885 and 91.920, the operator of an aircraft is taken to hold an approval under this regulation for an activity if the activity is authorised under another civil aviation authorisation held by the operator.

section.heading: Approvals by authorised persons for Subpart 91.T

content.p: If a provision of Subpart 91.T refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, a person may apply to an authorised person, in writing, for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, the approval must be granted.
Subregulation 11.055(1B) applies to the granting of an approval under this regulation.
Subpart 91.C—General

section.heading: Aircraft not to be operated in manner that creates a hazard

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the aircraft is operated in a manner that creates a hazard to another aircraft, a person or property.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Unauthorised travel or placing of cargo on aircraft

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
travels on an aircraft for a flight; and
at the time of the travel, does not have the consent of the operator of the aircraft, or the pilot in command of the aircraft for the flight, to travel on the aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
places cargo on an aircraft for a flight; and
at the time of placing the cargo on the aircraft, does not have the consent of the operator of the aircraft, or the pilot in command of the aircraft for the flight, to place cargo on the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the conduct of an NVIS flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for an NVIS flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 133.265 or 138.350 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the aircraft is not flown in accordance with the airspeed limits for the flight prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: This Division does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 133.030 or 138.210 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
This regulation applies in relation to the operation of an aircraft during the following period:
from the earlier of:
the time the aircraft’s doors are closed before take-off; and
the time the flight begins;
to the later of:
the time the aircraft’s doors are opened after landing; and
the time the flight ends.
The pilot in command of the aircraft contravenes this subregulation if the pilot in command does not comply with either or both of the following:
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft;
any conditions specified in the aircraft’s certificate of airworthiness or special flight permit.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: This Division does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Division 121.C.3, 133.C.3 or 135.C.3 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.

To avoid doubt, if a document is required to be carried on a flight of an aircraft under this Division, that requirement is taken to be satisfied if an electronic copy of the document is carried on the flight.
Note: Electronic copies may not satisfy the requirements of the law of a foreign country for flights that begin or end at an aerodrome outside Australian territory.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft begins the flight, a document mentioned in subregulation (2) is not carried on the aircraft.
The documents are as follows:
for each flight crew member:
the member’s medical certificate; and
the member’s flight crew licence or certificate of validation;
for each flight crew member, either:
a photographic identification document issued by a Commonwealth, State or Territory authority or agency; or
the member’s passport;
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft;
if the aircraft is fitted with computerised navigation equipment—the operating instructions for the equipment;
any minimum equipment list for the aircraft.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
aerobatic manoeuvres will be conducted during the flight; and
carriage of the documents on the aircraft would present a risk to the safety of the aircraft or persons on board the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Carriage of documents for certain flights

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to a flight of an aircraft other than:
a VFR flight conducted by day and within 50 nautical miles of the aircraft’s point of departure; or
a flight conducted:
within the flying training area for an aerodrome; and
if the flying training area for the aerodrome is not adjacent to the aerodrome—along the flight path between the flying training area and the aerodrome.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a document mentioned in subregulation (3) is not carried on the aircraft.
The documents are as follows:
the authorised aeronautical information for the flight;
the flight technical log or maintenance release for the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Carriage of documents—flights that begin or end outside Australian territory

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to a flight of an aircraft that begins or ends at an aerodrome outside Australian territory.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a document mentioned in subregulation (3) is not carried on the aircraft.
The documents are as follows:
the aircraft’s certificate of airworthiness;
the aircraft’s certificate of registration;
the journey log for the flight mentioned in regulation 91.120;
a list including the name, place of embarkation and place of destination of each passenger on the aircraft;
if the aircraft is carrying cargo (other than passenger baggage)—a manifest and detailed declaration of the cargo;
if the aircraft has a radio station licence that is an apparatus licence or a class licence—a copy of the licence;

if the operator or pilot in command of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 91.045 or holds another civil aviation authorisation that is relevant to the flight—a copy of the approval or authorisation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Journey logs—flights that begin or end outside Australian territory

content.p: This regulation applies to a flight of an aircraft that begins or ends at an aerodrome outside Australian territory.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the Part 91 Manual of Standards prescribes requirements relating to maintaining a journey log for the flight; and
the requirements are not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

division.heading: Reporting and recording defects and incidents etc.

content.p: Note: This Division is reserved for future use.

division.heading: Search and rescue services and emergency and survival equipment

content.p: Note: This Division is reserved for future use.

section.heading: Operating an Australian aircraft outside Australia

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an Australian aircraft for a flight in a foreign country each contravene this subregulation if:
a requirement of a law of the foreign country applies in relation to the flight; and
the aircraft is operated in a way that does not comply with the requirement.
The operator and the pilot in command of an Australian aircraft for a flight over the high seas each contravene this subregulation if:
a requirement of Annex 2 of the Chicago Convention applies in relation to the flight; and
the aircraft is operated in a way that does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Requirements to be met before Australian aircraft may fly

content.p: The pilot in command of an Australian aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a requirement in subregulation (2) is not met; and
the flight begins.
The requirements are the following:
if the aircraft is required to be registered—the aircraft must be registered;
the aircraft must have a certificate of airworthiness or special flight permit;
the aircraft must meet the requirements prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards (display of nationality marks, registration marks and aircraft registration identification plates);
if Part 42 does not apply to the aircraft:
a maintenance release, or other document approved for use under these Regulations as an alternative to a maintenance release, must be in force for the aircraft; and
the flight must comply with any condition that is set out or referred to in the maintenance release or other document approved for use as an alternative to the maintenance release;
each flight crew member required under these Regulations for the flight must be on board the aircraft.
Note: CASA or an authorised person may direct that these requirements do not apply to an aircraft with a special flight permit: see regulation 21.197.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft begins the flight with inoperative equipment; and
the equipment:
is required to be fitted to, or carried on, the aircraft by the certification basis for the aircraft or by or under these Regulations; and
is accessible, and likely to be used, by a person during the flight; and
is not placarded as inoperative.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if, during a flight of an aircraft:
the person manipulates the flight controls of the aircraft; and
any of the following apply:
for an Australian aircraft other than a Part 103 aircraft or a Part 131 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft under Part 61;
for a foreign registered aircraft—the person is not qualified to pilot the aircraft under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator;
for a Part 103 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft by a Part 103 ASAO;
for a Part 131 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft by a Part 131 pilot authorisation.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the pilot in command permits a person to manipulate the flight controls of the aircraft; and
any of the following apply:
for an Australian aircraft other than a Part 103 aircraft or a Part 131 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft under Part 61;
for a foreign registered aircraft—the person is not qualified to pilot the aircraft under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator;
for a Part 103 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft by a Part 103 ASAO;
for a Part 131 aircraft—the person is not authorised to pilot the aircraft by a Part 131 pilot authorisation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
carries or otherwise possesses a firearm on an aircraft; and
(b) the aircraft is not a prescribed aircraft within the meaning of the Aviation Transport Security Act 2004; and
neither the operator nor the pilot in command of the aircraft has consented to the person carrying or otherwise possessing the firearm on the aircraft.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person is authorised (however described) under another provision of these Regulations or another law of the Commonwealth to carry or otherwise possess the firearm on the aircraft.
Note 1: For other provisions of these Regulations that deal with firearms and aircraft, see Part 138.
Note 2: For other laws of the Commonwealth that deal with firearms and aircraft, see:
(a) Division 3 of Part 4 of the Aviation Transport Security Act 2004; and
(b) section 23 of the Crimes (Aviation) Act 1991.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person discharges a firearm while on an aircraft.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person is authorised (however described) under another provision of these Regulations or another law of the Commonwealth to discharge the firearm on the aircraft.
Note 1: For other provisions of these Regulations that deal with firearms and aircraft, see Part 138.
Note 2: For other laws of the Commonwealth that deal with firearms and aircraft, see:
(a) Division 3 of Part 4 of the Aviation Transport Security Act 2004; and
(b) section 23 of the Crimes (Aviation) Act 1991.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command permits a person to operate a portable electronic device during the flight; and
the pilot in command does not determine that the operation of the device during the flight will not affect the safety of the aircraft.
A person on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, the person operates a portable electronic device; and
the person has been directed by the pilot in command, or instructed by a cabin crew member, not to operate the portable electronic device during the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Operation of portable electronic devices by crew members

content.p: A crew member for a flight of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the crew member operates a portable electronic device at a time during the flight; and
operating the device at that time is likely to distract the crew member from performing the crew member’s duties for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person conducts an air display in Australian territory; and
the person does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct the air display.
The operator and pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the flight is in an air display in Australian territory; and
the person conducting the air display does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct the air display.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the pilot in command conducts aerobatic manoeuvres in IMC.
Note: For the requirement for a pilot to hold flight activity endorsements to conduct aerobatic manoeuvres, see regulation 61.380 and table 61.1145.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the pilot in command conducts aerobatic manoeuvres:
over a populous area; or
at an air display; or
at night; and
the pilot in command does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct the aerobatic manoeuvres:
for a flight over a populous area—over the populous area; or
for a flight at an air display—at the air display; or
for a flight at night—at night.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, a thing is dropped from the aircraft.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.425 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Picking up or setting down people or things during flight

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a person or thing is picked up or set down by the aircraft during the flight; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.410 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The requirement is that:
the pilot in command must hold an approval under regulation 91.045 for the person or thing to be picked up or set down during the flight; or
another provision of these Regulations must permit the person or thing to be picked up or set down during the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Persons not to be carried in certain parts of aircraft

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
during the flight, a person is carried on or in:
a part of the aircraft that is not designed to carry crew members or passengers; or
a thing attached to the aircraft; and
neither the operator nor the pilot in command of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 91.045 to carry the person on or in that part of the aircraft or that thing during the flight.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.410 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to the temporary carriage of a crew member in a part of the aircraft that is not designed to accommodate crew members or passengers if:
the carriage of the crew member in that part of the aircraft is for the purpose of doing anything for the safety of the aircraft or any person or cargo carried in it; or
both:
goods or stores are carried in that part of the aircraft; and
there is a proper means of access for crew members to the goods or stores.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards are met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) or (2A): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flying in formation; and
the pilot in command has not pre-arranged with each pilot in command of the other aircraft making up the formation to fly as part of the formation.
Note: For the requirement for a pilot to hold flight activity endorsements to fly in formation, see regulation 61.380 and table 61.1145.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the requirements prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation are met in relation to the flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flown in formation at night; and
the pilot in command does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to fly in formation at night.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flown in formation in IMC; and
the pilot in command does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to fly in formation in IMC.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (1A): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a thing is towed by the aircraft; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that:
the pilot in command must hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to tow the thing during the flight; or
another provision of these Regulations must permit the thing to be towed by the aircraft during the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 91.D—Operational procedures

section.heading: Authority and responsibilities of pilot in command

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to the operation of an aircraft during the following period:
from the earlier of:
the time the aircraft’s doors are closed before take-off; and
the time the flight begins;
to the later of:
the time the aircraft’s doors are opened after landing; and
the time the flight ends.
The pilot in command of the aircraft:
has final authority over:
the aircraft; and
the maintenance of discipline by all persons on the aircraft; and
must ensure:
the safety of persons on the aircraft; and
the safety of cargo on the aircraft; and
the safe operation of the aircraft during the flight.

section.heading: Actions and directions by operator or pilot in command

content.p: The operator or pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight may do a thing mentioned in subregulation (2) if the operator or pilot in command believes it is necessary for the safety of:
the aircraft; or
a person on the aircraft; or
a person or property on the ground or water.
The things are as follows:
direct a person to do something while the person is on the aircraft;
direct a person not to do something, or to limit the doing of something, while the person is on the aircraft;
direct a person to leave the aircraft before the flight begins;
with such assistance and by the use of such force as is reasonable and necessary:
remove a person or a thing from the aircraft before the flight begins; or
restrain a person for the duration of the flight or part of the flight; or
seize a thing on the aircraft for the duration of the flight or part of the flight; or
place a person on the aircraft in custody; or
detain a person or a thing, until the person or thing can be released into the control of an appropriate authority.
Note: Under regulation 91.225, crew members of an aircraft have a limited power of arrest.
A person on an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator or pilot in command of the aircraft gives the person a direction mentioned in paragraph (2)(a), (b) or (c); and
the person does not comply with the direction.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A crew member of an aircraft for a flight may, without warrant, arrest a person on the aircraft if:

the crew member believes, on reasonable grounds, that the person is committing, is attempting to commit, is about to commit, has committed or has attempted to commit, an offence against the Act or these Regulations in relation to the aircraft; and
the purpose of the arrest is to ensure the safety of the aircraft or of its passengers, crew or cargo or otherwise for the purposes of the Act or these Regulations; and
if the crew member is not the pilot in command of the aircraft—the pilot in command has authorised the crew member to arrest the person without warrant.
The pilot in command of the aircraft must ensure that, as soon as practicable after the end of the flight, a person arrested under subregulation (1) is delivered into the custody of:
if the flight ends in Australia—a constable; or
if the flight ends in a foreign country—a person in that country who is equivalent to a constable.
Note: See also sections 3ZC (use of force in making arrest) and 3ZD (persons to be informed of grounds of arrest) of the Crimes Act 1914.
(1) The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to flight preparation and weather assessments (the flight preparation (weather assessments) requirements).
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a flight preparation (weather assessments) requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
(1) The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to flight preparation and alternate aerodromes (the flight preparation (alternate aerodromes) requirements).
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a flight preparation (alternate aerodromes) requirement is not met for the flight.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.170 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
(1) The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements (the flight notification requirements) relating to flight notifications.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a flight notification requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Matters to be checked before take-off

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft takes off for the flight, a check prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards has not been carried out.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements in relation to the use by an aircraft of:
a class of airspace or a portion of a class of airspace; or
a controlled aerodrome; or
a control area; or
a control zone; or
a prohibited area; or
a restricted area; or
a danger area.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Air traffic control clearances and instructions

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
air traffic control gives the pilot in command an air traffic control clearance or air traffic control instructions; and
the pilot in command does not comply with the clearance or instructions.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
it is not practicable to seek authorisation for the non-compliance before it occurs; and
the non-compliance is necessary for the safety of the aircraft or the persons on the aircraft; and
the pilot in command informs air traffic control about the non-compliance as soon as practicable after the pilot in command is unable to comply with the clearance or instructions.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Unauthorised entry into prohibited or restricted areas

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft:
is in a prohibited area; or
(ii) is in a restricted area in contravention of a condition relating to the declaration of the area as a restricted area under regulation 7 of the Airspace Regulations 2007; and
the pilot in command does not comply with subregulation (2) as soon as the pilot becomes aware that the aircraft is in the prohibited area or restricted area.
The pilot must:

if the aircraft is fitted with, or carries, a means for the pilot in command to communicate with Air Traffic Services during the flight—inform Air Traffic Services, or the controlling authority (specified in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight) for the prohibited or restricted area, that the aircraft is in the area; and
for an aircraft (other than a Part 131 aircraft)—fly the aircraft out of the area; and
for a Part 131 aircraft:
fly the aircraft out of the area; or
if it is not possible to fly the aircraft out of the area—land the aircraft and inform the authority controlling the area as soon as is practicable.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight the aircraft enters an air defence identification zone published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight; and
a procedure published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight for that zone is not complied with for the flight.

Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to a Part 131 aircraft if the pilot in command of the aircraft lands the aircraft and informs the authority controlling the area as soon as is practicable after entering the air defence identification zone.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Minimum height rules—populous areas and public gatherings

content.p: This regulation applies if an aircraft is flown over a populous area or a public gathering.
Note: This regulation does not apply to certain medical transport operations in a rotorcraft and certain aerial work operations: see regulations 133.167 and 138.275.
The pilot in command of an aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aeroplane is flown below 1,000 ft above the highest feature or obstacle within a horizontal radius of 600 m of the point on the ground or water immediately below the aeroplane; and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (4) applies.
The pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
(a) the rotorcraft is flown below 1,000 ft above the highest feature or obstacle within a horizontal radius of 300 m of the point on the ground or water immediately below the rotorcraft; and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (4) applies.
The circumstances are the following:
the aircraft is taking off or landing in circumstances prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards;
the aircraft is engaged in a missed approach;
the aircraft:
is not carrying passengers; and
is engaged in a practice emergency procedure at an aerodrome;
the aircraft is performing training circuits at an aerodrome;
the pilot in command holds an approval for the purposes of regulation 91.180 (air displays in Australian territory);
for a rotorcraft—the rotorcraft is hovering, air transiting, air taxiing or ground taxiing at an aerodrome;
for a rotorcraft, seaplane or amphibian—the aircraft is flying within an access lane:
that is for use by aircraft taking off from, or landing at, a particular place; and
details of which are published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight;
for a single-engine seaplane or a single-engine amphibian:
the aeroplane is operating over water and within safe gliding distance of open water suitable for a forced landing; and
the aeroplane is not flown below 1,000 ft above the highest feature or obstacle within a horizontal radius of 300 m of the point on the water immediately below the aeroplane;
the aircraft is engaged in a procedure to determine the suitability of an aerodrome for a landing.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies if an aircraft is flown other than over a populous area or a public gathering.
Note: This regulation does not apply to certain medical transport operations in a rotorcraft and certain aerial work operations: see regulations 133.167 and 138.275.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
(a) the aircraft is flown below 500 ft above the highest feature or obstacle within a horizontal radius of 300 m of the point on the ground or water immediately below the aircraft; and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (3) applies.
The circumstances are the following:
the aircraft is taking off or landing in circumstances prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards;
the aircraft is engaged in a missed approach;
the aircraft:
is not carrying passengers; and
is engaged in a practice emergency procedure at an aerodrome;
the aircraft:
is not carrying passengers; and
is engaged in a practice forced landing procedure with the consent of the person or authority having control over the land or water above which the procedure is carried out;
the aircraft:
is being operated by a Part 141 operator to conduct low-flying flight training or by a Part 142 operator to conduct a low-flying activity; and

is being flown over an area that, with the consent of the person or authority with control of the area, has been determined by the operator to be a suitable flight training area for the training and has been surveyed by the pilot in command for obstacles before the flight; and
is not carrying passengers;
the aircraft is performing training circuits at an aerodrome;
the pilot holds an approval for the purposes of regulation 91.180 (air displays in Australian territory);
all of the following apply:
the pilot in command of the aircraft is authorised under Part 61, or holds an approval under regulation 91.045, to fly the aircraft below the height mentioned in paragraph (2)(a);
the pilot in command of the aircraft conducts a risk assessment of the area to be flown over;
the point on the ground or water vertically below the aircraft is not within 150 m of a person, vessel, vehicle or structure or of livestock;
for a rotorcraft—the rotorcraft is hovering, air transiting, air taxiing or ground taxiing at an aerodrome;
for a rotorcraft, seaplane or amphibian—the aircraft is flying within an access lane:
that is for use by aircraft taking off from, or landing at, a particular place; and
details of which are published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight;
the aircraft is engaged in a procedure to determine the suitability of an aerodrome for a landing.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Aircraft to be flown under VFR or IFR

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight, other than a Part 103 aircraft or a Part 131 aircraft, contravenes this subregulation if, at any time during the flight, the aircraft is not flown under the VFR or IFR.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if any part of the flight takes place other than by day and under the VFR.
The pilot in command of a Part 131 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if any part of the flight takes place other than under the VFR.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of an aircraft for a VFR flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight on a track, the aircraft is flown at a cruising level that is not a specified VFR cruising level for the track.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the aircraft is in uncontrolled airspace and any of the following apply:
the aircraft is below 3,000 ft above mean sea level;
the aircraft is at or above 3,000 ft above mean sea level but below 1,500 ft AGL;
it is not practicable for the pilot in command to fly the aircraft at a specified VFR cruising level for the track;
the aircraft is a glider in soaring flight.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the aircraft is in controlled airspace; and

air traffic control has given the pilot in command an air traffic control instruction, or an air traffic control clearance, to fly the aircraft other than at a specified VFR cruising level for the track.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) or (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight at night contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
(a) the aircraft is flown along a route or route segment at a height lower than the minimum height mentioned in subregulation (2); and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (3) applies.
Note: This regulation does not apply to certain medical transport operations in a rotorcraft and certain aerial work operations: see regulations 133.167 and 138.275.
The minimum height is the lowest height of the following for the route or route segment:
the published lowest safe altitude for the route or route segment (if any);
the minimum sector altitude published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight (if any);
the lowest safe altitude for the route or route segment;
1,000 ft above the highest obstacle on the ground or water within 10 nautical miles ahead of, and to either side of, the aircraft at that point on the route or route segment;
the lowest altitude for the route or route segment calculated in accordance with a method prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
The circumstances are the following:
the aircraft is taking off or landing;
the aircraft is within 3 nautical miles of the aerodrome from which the aircraft has taken off, or at which the aircraft will land;
the aircraft is being flown in accordance with an air traffic control clearance.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the aircraft is not flown in accordance with a requirement of the VMC criteria for the aircraft and the airspace in which the flight is conducted.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to a flight of an aircraft if:
air traffic control has authorised the pilot in command of the aircraft to conduct the flight under the special VFR; and
the pilot in command complies with the special VFR.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: VFR flights—aircraft not to exceed certain speeds

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the aircraft is flown at a transonic or supersonic speed.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: VFR flights—flights in class A airspace

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a VFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flown in class A airspace; and
the pilot in command does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct a VFR flight in class A airspace.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of an aircraft for an IFR flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight on a track, the aircraft is flown at a cruising level that is not a specified IFR cruising level for the track.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the aircraft is in uncontrolled airspace; and
it is not practicable for the pilot in command to fly the aircraft at a specified IFR cruising level for the track.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if air traffic control has:
given the pilot in command an air traffic control instruction to fly the aircraft at the cruising level; or
given the pilot in command an air traffic control clearance to fly the aircraft at the cruising level.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) or (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: IFR flights at non-specified cruising levels—notifying Air Traffic Services

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight on a track:
the aircraft is flown at a cruising level that is not a specified IFR cruising level for the track; and
before the aircraft is flown at that cruising level, the pilot in command does not notify Air Traffic Services of the cruising level.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: IFR flights at non-specified cruising levels—avoiding collisions with aircraft conducting VFR flights

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight on a track:
the aircraft is flown at a cruising level that is not a specified IFR cruising level for the track; and
there is a risk of collision between the aircraft and another aircraft that:
is conducting a VFR flight on a track; and
is flying at a specified VFR cruising level for the track; and
the pilot in command does not give way to the other aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
(1) The pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flown along a route or route segment at a height lower than the minimum height mentioned in subregulation (2); and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (3) applies.
Note: This regulation does not apply to certain medical transport operations in a rotorcraft and certain aerial work operations: see regulations 133.167 and 138.275.
The minimum height is the lowest of the following for the route or route segment:
the published lowest safe altitude for the route or route segment (if any);
the minimum sector altitude published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight (if any);
the lowest safe altitude for the route or route segment.
(3) The circumstances are the following:
the aircraft is taking off or landing;
the aircraft is being flown in accordance with:
requirements relating to visual approach or departure procedures published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight; or
an authorised instrument departure procedure or an authorised instrument approach procedure; or
an air traffic control clearance;
the aircraft is being flown in VMC by day.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe the following:
(a) requirements (the take-off minima requirements) relating to take-off minima for an aerodrome;
(b) requirements (the landing minima requirements) relating to landing minima for an aerodrome.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft conducts a take-off at an aerodrome; and
a take-off minima requirement for the aerodrome is not met for the flight.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft conducts a landing at an aerodrome; and
a landing minima requirement for the aerodrome is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe circumstances in which an aircraft flown under the IFR must not make an approach to land at an aerodrome.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for an IFR flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft makes an approach to land at an aerodrome; and
the approach to land is made in circumstances mentioned in subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Taking off and landing in low visibility

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft conducts a low-visibility operation at an aerodrome; and
when the operation begins:

if the operator is required under these Regulations to have an exposition or an operations manual—the operator does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct the low-visibility operation; or
if subparagraph (i) does not apply—the pilot in command does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 to conduct the low-visibility operation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if, while the aircraft is operating at an aerodrome:
the aircraft does not operate in the specified aircraft performance category for the aircraft at the aerodrome; and
the operator:
does not hold an approval under regulation 91.045 for the aircraft to operate in a lower aircraft performance category for the aircraft at the aerodrome; or

holds an approval under regulation 91.045 for the aircraft to operate in a lower aircraft performance category for the aircraft at the aerodrome but does not comply with subregulation (3) of this regulation.
The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator holds an approval under regulation 91.045 for the aircraft to operate in a lower aircraft performance category for the aircraft at the aerodrome; and
the aircraft does not operate in that lower aircraft performance category.
The operator must give details to the flight crew of:
the approval; and
the conditions (if any) imposed by CASA on the approval.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A flight crew member must, during a flight, maintain vigilance, so far as weather conditions permit, to see and avoid other aircraft.
The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if, during a flight:
there is a risk of collision between the aircraft and another aircraft; and
a circumstance mentioned in column 1 of an item in the following table exists; and
the pilot in command contravenes the right of way rule mentioned in column 2 of that item.

tr.td: An aircraft is in an emergency and compelled to land
Any other aircraft must give way to the aircraft that is compelled to land
Any other aircraft (whether in flight or operating on the ground or water) must give way to the aircraft that is landing
Two heavier-than-air aircraft are conducting an approach to land at an aerodrome
An aircraft is overtaking another aircraft
The aircraft that is overtaking must give way to the aircraft being overtaken
Aircraft mentioned in column 2 are in the same vicinity
Two aircraft are on converging headings at approximately the same altitude
The aircraft that has the other aircraft on its right must give way to the other aircraft

content.p: Subregulation (1) does not apply if it is necessary, in order to avoid a collision with an aircraft, not to comply with the right of way rule.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Aircraft with right of way to maintain heading and speed
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
there is a risk of collision with another aircraft; and
the aircraft has right of way over the other aircraft (in accordance with regulation 91.330); and
the aircraft’s heading and speed is not maintained until there is no longer a risk of collision.
Overtaking aircraft to keep clear and to right

The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft is overtaking another aircraft (whether in the course of climbing, descending or in level flight), the pilot does not:
keep the aircraft out of the way of the other aircraft, even if the other aircraft alters course while being overtaken; and
fly the aircraft so that it passes to the right of the other aircraft and remains on the right until clear of the other aircraft.
Aircraft approaching head on to alter heading to right
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft and another aircraft are approaching in the air head on or approximately so; and
there is a risk of collision; and
the aircraft’s heading is not altered to the right.
Aircraft giving way not to create collision risk
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is required to give way to another aircraft:
by a right of way rule in regulation 91.330; or
by an additional right of way rule in subregulation (1), (2) or (3) of this regulation; or
by an additional right of way rule in regulation 91.340; and
the aircraft is flown so that it passes ahead of the other aircraft, or directly over or under it, so closely that there is a risk of collision.
Exceptions
Subregulation (1), (2), (3) or (4) does not apply if it is necessary, in order to avoid a collision with an aircraft, to not comply with the subregulation.
Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply if:
the aircraft is a glider engaged in ridge or hill soaring; and
the pilot flies the aircraft so that it passes between the ridge or hill and the other aircraft.

Subregulation (4) does not apply if, as a result of a command of the aircraft’s airborne collision avoidance system, the pilot was manoeuvring the aircraft to the extent necessary to ensure the safety of the aircraft.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5), (5A) or (6): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Right of way rules for take-off and landing

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during take-off or landing, the aircraft is flown in a manner that creates a risk of collision with:
another aircraft; or
a person, vessel, vehicle or structure.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies in relation to a requirement of the International Regulations to the extent that the requirement is not inconsistent with a requirement of regulation 91.355.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is operating on water; and
the aircraft is not operated in accordance with the International Regulations.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is in level flight, or is manoeuvring near the surface of water; and
the aircraft does not, as far as possible:
keep clear of a vessel; or
avoid impeding the navigation of a vessel.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is on water; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the aircraft must give way to, and keep well clear of, an aircraft or vessel converging on its right;
the aircraft must alter its heading to the right, and keep well clear, of an aircraft or vessel that is approaching head-on or approximately head-on;
the aircraft, if overtaking a vessel or another aircraft, must:
give way to the vessel or aircraft being overtaken; and
alter its heading to keep well clear of the vessel or aircraft being overtaken.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if it is necessary, to avoid a collision with an aircraft or vessel, to not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

subDivision.heading: Avoiding collisions at or in the vicinity of aerodromes

section.heading: Meaning of in the vicinity of a non-controlled aerodrome

content.p: (1) An aircraft is in the vicinity of a non-controlled aerodrome if it is:
in uncontrolled airspace; and
within 10 nautical miles of the aerodrome; and
at a height above the aerodrome that could result in conflict with operations at the aerodrome.

For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), if an aerodrome reference point for the aerodrome is published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight, the distance must be measured from that point.

section.heading: Taxiing or towing on movement area of aerodrome

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is taxiing or towing an aircraft on the movement area of an aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the aircraft and any tow vehicle must give way, in accordance with subregulation (3), to an aircraft that is landing or on its final approach to land;
the aircraft and any tow vehicle must give way, in accordance with subregulation (3), to an aircraft that is taking off or preparing for take-off;
the aircraft and any tow vehicle must keep well clear of an aircraft it is overtaking;
the aircraft and any tow vehicle must give way to an aircraft on the right if both aircraft are on a converging course;
the aircraft and any tow vehicle must stop, or alter course to the right, so as to remain clear of an aircraft approaching head on or approximately so.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) or (2)(b):
for a runway that has a marked runway hold position for the aircraft—the aircraft giving way and any tow vehicle must hold at that position; and
for a runway that does not have a marked runway hold position—the aircraft giving way and any tow vehicle must not encroach upon a graded runway strip.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if it is necessary, to avoid a collision with an aircraft and any tow vehicle, to not comply with the requirement.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the aircraft and any tow vehicle are being operated in accordance with an air traffic control clearance or air traffic control instructions.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (4) or (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Take-off or landing at non-controlled aerodrome—all aircraft

content.p: (1) This regulation applies to an aircraft (the subject aircraft) at a non-controlled aerodrome at which a take-off or landing of the aircraft can only occur from or to a runway.
Rules for take-off
The pilot in command of the subject aircraft (other than a glider being towed by a glider tug) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the subject aircraft commences to take-off from a runway; and
before taking off, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
if another aircraft is taking off before the subject aircraft from the same runway:
the other aircraft must have crossed the upwind end of the runway; or
the other aircraft must have commenced a turn; or
the runway must be longer than 1,800 m and the other aircraft must have become airborne and be at least 1,800 m beyond the proposed point of lift-off of the subject aircraft; or

the other aircraft and the subject aircraft must both have a maximum take-off weight below 2,000 kg, and the other aircraft must be airborne and at least 600 m beyond the proposed point of lift-off of the subject aircraft;
if another aircraft is landing on the same runway before the subject aircraft—the other aircraft must have vacated the runway;

if another aircraft is landing before the subject aircraft and is using a crossing runway—the other aircraft must have crossed, or must have stopped short of, the runway the subject aircraft is taking off from.
Rules for landing
The pilot in command of the subject aircraft (other than a glider) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the subject aircraft continues an approach to land at an aerodrome beyond the threshold of the runway; and
before landing, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (5) is not met.
Note: Regulation 91.055 prohibits an aircraft (including a glider) being operated in a manner that creates a hazard to another aircraft, a person or property.
The requirements are the following:
if another aircraft is taking off using the same runway before the subject aircraft:
the other aircraft must be airborne and must have commenced a turn; or

the other aircraft must be beyond the point on the runway at which the subject aircraft could be expected to complete its landing roll, and there must be sufficient distance for the subject aircraft to manoeuvre safely in the event of a missed approach;
if another aircraft is landing on the same runway before the subject aircraft—the other aircraft must have vacated the runway or must be taxiing away from the runway;

if another aircraft is landing before the subject aircraft and is using a crossing runway—the other aircraft must have crossed, or must have stopped short of, the runway the subject aircraft is landing on.
Application of rules where gliders or glider tugs operate
At an aerodrome where gliders or glider tugs operate to a common circuit pattern from a parallel strip outside the runway strip:
subregulations (2) and (4) apply to an aircraft taking off or landing, respectively, on either the runway or the parallel strip as if the runway and the strip were a single runway; but
aircraft taxiing or stationary on either the runway or the parallel strip are taken not to affect operations on the other.
Exception
Subregulation (2) or (4) does not apply if:
the aircraft is taking off or landing at an aerodrome where gliders or glider tugs operate to a contra-circuit pattern on both a runway and a parallel strip outside the runway strip; and
simultaneous operations on the runway and the parallel strip are permitted.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (7): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operating on manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of non-controlled aerodrome—general requirements

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated on the manoeuvring area of, or in the vicinity of, a non-controlled aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the pilot must keep a lookout for other aircraft that are being operated on the manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of the aerodrome to avoid a collision;
the pilot must ensure that the aircraft does not cause a danger to other aircraft on the manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of the aerodrome;
if the pilot is flying the aircraft in the vicinity of the aerodrome—the pilot must join, or avoid, the circuit pattern for the aerodrome;
if the aircraft is an aeroplane—the pilot must not:
take-off from a part of the aerodrome that is outside the aerodrome landing area; or
land the aircraft on a part of the aerodrome that is outside the aerodrome landing area.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Operating on manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of non-controlled aerodrome—landing and taking off into the wind

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated on the manoeuvring area of, or in the vicinity of, a non-controlled aerodrome; and
the pilot does not, to the extent practicable, land and take off into the wind.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft allow the aircraft to land or take off downwind or crosswind; and
the pilot is satisfied that traffic conditions at the aerodrome enable such a landing or take-off to be carried out safely.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operating on manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of non-controlled aerodrome—requirements that apply after joining the circuit pattern

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft (other than a rotorcraft) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated on the manoeuvring area of, or in the vicinity of, a non-controlled aerodrome; and
after joining the circuit pattern for a landing or while flying in the circuit pattern after take-off, the pilot does not:
comply with instructions in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight to the effect that all turns be made in a particular direction; or
if there are no relevant instructions in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight—make all turns to the left.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to the pilot in command of an aircraft if:
the aircraft is a seaplane or amphibian and the pilot in command contravenes the subregulation only to the extent necessary:
to avoid an obstacle; or
to avoid undue noise over a populous area without compromising the aircraft’s safety; or
for a single-engine seaplane or amphibian—to enable the aircraft to land on water if its engine fails; or
the aircraft is a glider (other than a glider with an engine operating) and the pilot in command contravenes the subregulation only to the extent necessary to enable the aircraft to land safely.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operating on manoeuvring area, or in the vicinity, of non-controlled aerodrome—requirements related to maintaining the same track after take-off

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft (other than a rotorcraft, a glider or a powered parachute) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated on the manoeuvring area of, or in the vicinity of, a non-controlled aerodrome; and
the pilot does not, after take-off, maintain the same track from the take-off until the aircraft is 500 ft AGL.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to the pilot in command of a seaplane or amphibian if the pilot in command contravenes the subregulation only to the extent necessary:
to avoid an obstacle; or
to avoid undue noise over a populated area without compromising the aircraft’s safety; or
for a single engine seaplane or amphibian—to enable the aircraft to land on water if its engine fails.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to the pilot in command of an aircraft if a change to the track is necessary to avoid the terrain.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) or (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft approaches a non-controlled aerodrome to land using a straight-in approach; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
before starting the approach, the pilot in command must determine:
the wind direction at the aerodrome; and
the runways in use at the aerodrome;
the aircraft must give way to any other aircraft flying in the circuit pattern for the aerodrome;

for an approach other than an approach covered by subregulation (2A)—all manoeuvring must be carried out, to establish the aircraft on the final approach, at least 3 nautical miles from the threshold of the runway intended to be used for the landing.
An approach is covered by this subregulation if:
the approach is carried out in IMC using an instrument approach procedure; or
the approach is by a Part 103 aircraft prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Communicating at certified, registered, military or designated non-controlled aerodromes

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated on the manoeuvring area of, or in the vicinity of:
a certified aerodrome; or
a registered aerodrome; or
a military aerodrome; or
an aerodrome prescribed as a designated non-controlled aerodrome by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for this subparagraph; and
the aerodrome is a non-controlled aerodrome; and
if the aircraft is not carrying an operative radio—the requirement in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that either subregulation (3) or (4) is satisfied.
This subregulation is satisfied if:
the flight is conducted during the day in VMC; and
the flight is conducted in company with another aircraft; and
the other aircraft is carrying an operative radio; and
the pilot in command of the other aircraft is:
if the aircraft is an Australian aircraft—authorised to operate the radio under Part 61; or
if the aircraft is a foreign registered aircraft—authorised to operate the radio under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator; or
if the aircraft is a Part 103 aircraft—authorised to operate the radio by a Part 103 ASAO.
This subregulation is satisfied if:
either:
the radio becomes inoperative during the flight; or
the purpose of the flight is to take the radio to a place where it can be repaired; and
if the aircraft is flying in the vicinity of the aerodrome—each of the following is switched on:
the aircraft’s landing lights (if any);
the aircraft’s anti-collision lights (if any);
the aircraft’s secondary surveillance radar transponder (if any); and
if the aircraft is arriving at the aerodrome—the aircraft joins the circuit pattern for the aerodrome on the cross-wind or down-wind leg of the circuit pattern.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Aircraft in aerodrome traffic at controlled aerodromes

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is part of aerodrome traffic at a controlled aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
a continuous watch for instructions given visually by Air Traffic Services for the aerodrome using standard visual signals must be maintained;

if a continuous listening watch on the frequency specified in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight for communications with Air Traffic Services for the aerodrome can be maintained—the continuous listening watch must be maintained;
authorisation to conduct a manoeuvre preparatory to, or associated with, taxiing, landing or take-off must be obtained from Air Traffic Services for the aerodrome before the manoeuvre is conducted.
The pilot in command of an aircraft (other than a Part 131 aircraft) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is part of aerodrome traffic at a controlled aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (4) is not met.
The requirements are the following:

if the aircraft takes off from the aerodrome and a change to the aircraft’s track is not necessary to avoid the terrain—the aircraft must maintain the same track from the take-off until the aircraft is 500 ft AGL;
if the aircraft joins the circuit pattern for the aerodrome for a landing—the aircraft must, after joining the circuit pattern, make all turns in the direction of the circuit pattern;

if the aircraft takes off from the aerodrome—the aircraft must, after taking off, make all turns in the direction of the circuit pattern while the pilot is flying in the circuit pattern for the aerodrome.
Subregulation (3) does not apply if:
Air Traffic Services for the aerodrome instructed or permitted the pilot to engage in the conduct that would otherwise result in the contravention of that subregulation; or
the aircraft is being flown in accordance with an authorised instrument departure procedure or an authorised instrument approach procedure.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

division.heading: Taking off, landing and ground operations

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft takes off from, or lands at, a place; and
the place does not meet the requirement in subregulation (2).
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.205 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The requirement is that:
the place is one of the following:
a certified aerodrome;
a registered aerodrome;
an aerodrome for which an arrangement under section 20 of the Act is in force;
a place that is suitable for the landing and taking-off of aircraft; and
the aircraft can land at, or take off from, the place safely having regard to all the circumstances of the proposed landing or take-off (including the prevailing weather conditions).
(3) For the purposes of the definition of aerodrome in the Act, a place mentioned in subparagraph (2)(a)(iv) is authorised to be used as an aerodrome.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person taxis an aircraft; and
any of the following apply:
for an aeroplane that is an Australian aircraft other than a Part 103 aircraft—the person is not authorised under Part 61 or 64 to taxi the aeroplane;
