for a rotorcraft that is an Australian aircraft other than a Part 103 aircraft—the person is not authorised under Part 61 to taxi the rotorcraft;

for an aeroplane that is a foreign registered aircraft—the person is not qualified to taxi the aeroplane under the law of the aeroplane’s State of registry or the State of the operator, nor authorised under Part 64;
for a rotorcraft that is a foreign registered aircraft—the person is not qualified to pilot the rotorcraft under the law of the rotorcraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator;
for a Part 103 aircraft—the person is not authorised by a Part 103 ASAO to taxi the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Parked aircraft not to create hazard

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if the person parks an aircraft in a place where the aircraft is a hazard to the movement of other aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Safety when aeroplane operating on ground

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person starts the engine of an aeroplane, or causes the engine to be started, while the aeroplane is on the ground; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the person who starts the engine or causes the engine to be started must be:
if the aeroplane is an Australian aircraft—a person authorised to pilot the aeroplane under Part 61 or a person authorised to taxi the aeroplane under Part 64; or
if the aeroplane is a foreign registered aircraft—a person qualified to pilot or taxi the aeroplane under the law of the aeroplane’s State of registry or the State of the operator; or
a person of a kind prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards; and
if subparagraph (a)(iii) applies—the aeroplane must be secured from moving.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the person starting the engine of the aeroplane is hand-starting the propeller of the aeroplane; and
assistance is not readily available; and
adequate provision is made to prevent the aeroplane moving forward; and
no person is on board the aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person operates an aeroplane on the ground, or causes an aeroplane to be operated on the ground; and

the person permits another person to board the aeroplane or to remain on the aeroplane while a pilot seat of the aeroplane is not occupied by a person who is competent to apply the brakes and control the engine.
(5) For the purposes of paragraph (4)(b), a person is competent to apply the brakes and control the engine of an aeroplane if:
the person has been given instructions on how, and assessed as competent, to apply the brakes and control the engine (including how to shut the engine down) by another person; or
the person is authorised under Part 61 or Part 64 to taxi the aeroplane; or
if the aeroplane is a foreign registered aircraft—the person is qualified to pilot or taxi the aeroplane under the law of the aeroplane’s State of registry or the State of the operator.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Safety when rotorcraft operating on ground

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person operates a rotorcraft on the ground; and
the rotorcraft is being operated other than for maintenance or maintenance training; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
that the person is:
if the rotorcraft is an Australian aircraft—authorised under Part 61 to pilot the rotorcraft; or
if the rotorcraft is a foreign registered aircraft—authorised to pilot the rotorcraft by the rotorcraft’s State of registry; or
a person of a kind prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards; and
if subparagraph (a)(iii) applies—the rotorcraft must be secured from moving.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to fuel for aircraft, including (but not limited to) the following:
matters that must be considered when determining whether an aircraft has sufficient fuel to complete a flight safely;
the amounts of fuel that must be carried on board an aircraft for a flight;
procedures for monitoring amounts of fuel during a flight;
procedures to be followed if fuel reaches specified amounts during a flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Division 121.D.6, 133.D.6 or 135.D.6 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the aircraft is not carrying sufficient oil to complete the flight safely.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The operator and pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, before the flight begins, the operator or pilot in command does not ensure that the aircraft has been fuelled with fuel that is not contaminated, degraded or inappropriate.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person supplies fuel for fuelling an aircraft (other than a Part 131 aircraft); and
the fuel is contaminated, degraded or inappropriate fuel for the aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person fuels an aircraft; and
the fuel is contaminated, degraded or inappropriate fuel for the aircraft.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
an aircraft is being fuelled; and
the person creates a fire hazard within 15 m of the aircraft or the equipment used to fuel the aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
a fire hazard exists within 15 m of an aircraft or the aircraft’s fuelling equipment; and
the person fuels the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person who fuels an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
at all times during the fuelling, at least the number of fire extinguishers mentioned in subregulation (2A):
must be on the fuelling equipment or positioned at a distance of not less than 6 m and not more than 15 m from the fuelling point; and
must be readily available for use by the person;
each fire extinguisher:
must be of a type and capacity suitable for extinguishing fuel and electrical fires; and
for a fuelling operation in Australian territory—must comply with Australian/New Zealand Standard AS/NZS 1841, as in force from time to time.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(a) the number of fire extinguishers is:
for an aircraft other than a Part 131 aircraft—2; and
for a Part 131 aircraft—one.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is fuelling an aircraft; and
the aircraft and the equipment used to fuel the aircraft are not electrically bonded.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Equipment or electronic devices operating near aircraft

content.p: Operation of equipment or electronic device near aircraft during fuelling
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
an aircraft is being fuelled; and
the person operates equipment or an electronic device within 15 m of a critical fuelling point for the aircraft.
Fuelling aircraft while equipment or electronic device is operated near aircraft
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
equipment or an electronic device is being operated within 15 m of a critical fuelling point for the fuelling of an aircraft; and
the person fuels the aircraft.
Exceptions
Subregulations (1) and (2) do not apply if:
the equipment or electronic device being operated:
is part of the aircraft or the aircraft’s fuelling equipment; or
is designed for use during fuelling operations; or
performs an aircraft servicing function and is safe for use within 15 m of a critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft; or
complies with an industry standard about the safe use of equipment or electronic devices within 15 m of a critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft; or
the equipment being operated is an auxiliary power unit of the aircraft and the following requirements are met:
the operation of the auxiliary power unit starts before the person begins fuelling the aircraft;
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft permit the auxiliary power unit to be operated during fuelling; or
the electronic device being operated:
(i) is hazardous to the process of fuelling the aircraft only because it is designed to produce radio emissions (within the meaning of the Radiocommunications Act 1992); and
is operated at least 6 m from each critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft; or
for a turbine-engine aircraft—the electronic device being operated is a low-risk electronic device and is operated in accordance with regulation 91.490.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Use of device inside cabin of aircraft
A person on a turbine-engine aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the person operates a low-risk electronic device inside the cabin of the aircraft while the aircraft is being fuelled; and
the pilot in command of the aircraft has not given the person permission to operate the device while the aircraft is being fuelled.
The pilot in command of a turbine-engine aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command gives permission to a person to operate a low-risk electronic device inside the cabin of the aircraft while the aircraft is being fuelled; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met.
The requirement is that, during fuelling, each cabin door within 3 m of a critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft must be closed.
Use of device outside cabin of aircraft
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person operates a low-risk electronic device outside the cabin of a turbine-engine aircraft while the aircraft is being fuelled; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (5) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the device must be operated at a distance of greater than 3 m from each critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft;
the device may also be operated at a distance of 3 m or less from a critical fuelling point for the fuelling of the aircraft if the person operating the device:
is employed or engaged by the operator of the aircraft; and

has successfully completed training and has been assessed by the operator as competent to comply with the requirements of this Division in relation to operating the device in those areas and to avoid the risks associated with being distracted when operating the device.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Only turbine-engine aircraft to be hot fuelled

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is hot fuelled for the flight; and
the aircraft is not a turbine-engine aircraft.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.300 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is hot fuelled for the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.300 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The requirements are that, at the time of the hot fuelling:
it must be safe to hot fuel; and
if the aircraft is a turbine-engine propeller-driven aeroplane:
an aeroplane propeller must not be within 2.5 m of the fuelling point used for the hot fuelling; and

a person using the fuelling point must be separated from the propeller by a part of the aeroplane’s structure (such as a wing) and must not be able to move directly into the propeller’s arc from the fuelling point; and
doors on the fuelling side of the aircraft must be closed; and
at least one door on the non-fuelling side of the aircraft must be open; and
a system of fuelling must not be used that allows fuel to be exposed to the atmosphere; and
there must be a means available to the person fuelling the aircraft to quickly cut off the fuel supply at its point of entry into the aircraft’s fuel tank; and
the person in charge of the aircraft, or the person at the aircraft’s controls, must maintain communication with the person fuelling the aircraft by means of:
an electronic communication system; or
visual contact and an agreed system of signals.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is hot fuelled for the flight; and
the following are not set out in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft:
procedures for the hot fuelling of the aircraft;
the circumstances in which the aircraft can be hot fuelled;
the procedures to be followed if an emergency occurs during hot fuelling.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.300 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a requirement of a procedure mentioned in subparagraph (1)(b)(i) or (iii) is not met in relation to the fuelling of the aircraft for the flight; or
the aircraft is fuelled in a circumstance that is not mentioned in subparagraph (1)(b)(ii).
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is hot fuelled; and
before the hot fuelling begins, a person who is directly involved with the hot fuelling has not been briefed about compliance with the procedures and circumstances mentioned in paragraph (1)(b).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Fuelling aircraft—persons on aircraft, boarding or disembarking

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being fuelled for the flight with a highly volatile fuel; and
the fuelling begins or continues when a person who is not a crew member of the aircraft is:
on the aircraft; or
boarding the aircraft; or
disembarking from the aircraft.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being fuelled with fuel other than a highly volatile fuel; and
the fuelling begins or continues when a person who is not a crew member of the aircraft is:
on the aircraft; or
boarding the aircraft; or
disembarking from the aircraft; and
neither the operator of the aircraft nor the pilot in command holds an approval under regulation 91.045 to fuel the aircraft in those circumstances.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.240, 133.195, 135.220 or 138.302 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
Subregulation (1) or (2) does not apply in relation to the replacement of fuel cylinders on a Part 131 aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2A): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Fuelling aircraft if fuel vapour detected

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being fuelled for the flight; and
a person who is not a crew member of the aircraft is:
on the aircraft; or
boarding the aircraft; or
disembarking from the aircraft; and
fuel vapour is detected in the aircraft; and
the aircraft continues to be fuelled.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

division.heading: Safety of persons on aircraft and cargo requirements

section.heading: Crew members to be fit for duty

content.p: A crew member of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the crew member is, or is likely to be, unfit to perform a duty:
that is a required duty for the crew member to perform during the flight; and
that is related to the safety of the aircraft or of the persons on the aircraft or cargo on the aircraft; and
the crew member begins to carry out the crew member’s duties for the flight.
A crew member of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the crew member carries out a duty for the flight; and
either:
the crew member consumes alcohol at any time during the period of 8 hours ending when the flight begins; or

if a test of a body sample of the crew member to determine the level of alcohol in the sample was taken at the time of carrying out the duty—the test would reveal that the permitted level for alcohol (within the meaning of Part 99) is exceeded.
A crew member of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the crew member consumes alcohol while on board the aircraft.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator believes on reasonable grounds that a crew member is unfit to perform a duty on the flight; and
the duty relates to the safety of the aircraft or of the persons on the aircraft or cargo on the aircraft; and
the operator assigns the crew member to duty for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Strict liability applies to paragraphs (4)(b) and (c).
Without limiting subregulation (1) or (4), a crew member is taken to be, or is taken to be likely to be, unfit to perform a duty if:
the crew member is fatigued to the extent that the crew member’s ability to safely perform the duty is reduced or likely to be reduced; or
the crew member’s ability to safely perform the duty is impaired, or likely to be impaired, because the crew member has consumed, used or absorbed a psychoactive substance.

section.heading: Offensive or disorderly behaviour on aircraft

content.p: A person on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the person behaves in an offensive or disorderly manner; and
as a result of that behaviour, the safety of the aircraft or persons on the aircraft is endangered.

The operator or a crew member of an aircraft for a flight may refuse to allow a person to board the aircraft if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person is likely to behave in an offensive or disorderly manner that is likely to endanger the safety of the aircraft or persons on the aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1) or (2), a person is taken to behave in an offensive or disorderly manner if the person:
assaults, intimidates or threatens another person (whether the assault, intimidation or threat is verbal or physical, and whether or not a weapon or object is used); or
intentionally damages or destroys property.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person on an aircraft (other than a Part 103 aircraft) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the person smokes:
during take-off or landing; or
during a period when the pilot in command has directed the person not to smoke.
Note: Section 35 of the Air Navigation Regulations 2026 prohibits smoking anywhere on an aircraft if the aircraft is engaged in certain operations.
A person on an aircraft (other than a Part 103 aircraft) for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the person smokes in the aircraft’s toilet.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the pilot in command is taken to have directed a person on an aircraft not to smoke if:
a permanent “no smoking” sign is displayed in the aircraft’s cabin; or
the pilot has switched on an illuminated “no smoking” sign in the aircraft’s cabin.
A person on a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the person smokes on the aircraft.
For the purposes of this regulation, smoking is taken to include the use of electronic cigarettes.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3A).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a crew member (other than a flight crew member) is carried on the flight; and
before the flight begins, the pilot in command has not implemented procedures for:
the protection of such crew members during turbulence or during a period when turbulence is expected; or
the limiting or ceasing of crew member duties during turbulence or during a period when turbulence is expected.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
due to the design or configuration of the aircraft, the pilot in command is unable to see all seats (and berths) on the aircraft from the pilot in command’s pilot seat; and
before the aircraft begins the flight, the aircraft is not fitted with a means to communicate with all passengers during all phases of the flight (including emergencies).
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
a person is assigned a seat (or a berth) on the aircraft for the flight; and
the seat or berth is not fitted with a seatbelt or shoulder harness; and
the aircraft begins the flight.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if circumstances prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards apply in relation to the carriage of the person for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the flight must be conducted by at least one pilot who:
for an Australian aircraft—holds a pilot licence and is permitted under regulation 61.385 to conduct the flight; or
for a foreign aircraft—is qualified to pilot the aircraft under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator;
at all times during the flight, such a pilot must occupy a pilot seat, with the seatbelt securely fastened;

during take-off, landing or any other period that the pilot in command directs, each flight crew member required for the flight must occupy the flight crew member’s crew station with the seatbelt and shoulder harness securely fastened;
when occupying a crew station on the flight deck other than a flight crew member’s crew station, the flight crew member must keep the flight crew member’s seatbelt securely fastened.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Seating for crew members other than flight crew members

content.p: A crew member (other than a flight crew member) for a flight of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if, during take-off, landing or any other period that the pilot in command directs, the crew member is not:
occupying the crew member’s crew station; and
wearing, securely fastened, the seatbelts and shoulder harnesses provided at that station.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 138.375 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
a direction is given by the pilot in command during turbulence; and
the crew member occupies a seat other than the crew member’s crew station; and
the crew member is wearing, securely fastened, the seatbelts and shoulder harnesses provided at that seat.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A passenger on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a direction is given to passengers under regulation 91.570 to fasten seatbelts or shoulder harnesses (as the case requires); and
the passenger is responsible for an infant or child carried on the flight; and
the passenger does not ensure that the infant or child is restrained in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a passenger is not given a safety briefing and instructions in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph; and
the aircraft takes off for the flight.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.285, 133.240 or 135.280 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the passenger has been previously carried on the aircraft; and
the passenger has previously been given a safety briefing and instructions in accordance with this regulation; and
in the circumstances it is not reasonably necessary to give the same safety briefing and instructions.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Passengers—safety directions by pilot in command

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, before doing a thing mentioned in subregulation (2), a passenger is not directed to do the following:
to fasten the passenger’s seatbelt or shoulder harness;

if the seat back of the seat (or berth) in which the passenger is sitting is adjustable—to ensure that the seat back is in an upright position or other position permitted by the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft while the aircraft is doing a thing mentioned in subregulation (2);

if there are attachments to or for the seat (including a tray table or footrest)—to stow the attachments or to position them as permitted by the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft while the aircraft is doing a thing mentioned in subregulation (2).
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 105.105 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The things are the following:
taxiing;
taking off;
landing.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command has reason to believe it is necessary, for the safety of passengers, that a passenger’s seatbelt or shoulder harness is fastened; and
the pilot in command does not direct the passenger to fasten the passenger’s seatbelt or shoulder harness.
For subregulations (1) and (3), a direction that seatbelts or shoulder harnesses are to be fastened may be given by the operation of an illuminated sign.
A direction mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) does not apply to a person occupying a seat (or berth) on an aircraft if:
the person’s health may suffer a detriment by being restrained by a seatbelt; and
the pilot in command agrees that the person is otherwise safely restrained.
A direction mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) does not apply to a person occupying a seat (or berth) on an aircraft if:
the person is ill or incapacitated; and
the pilot in command agrees to the passenger not adjusting their seat (or berth); and
the person is otherwise safely restrained and will not affect the safety of other passengers.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulations (5) and (6): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A passenger on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a direction mentioned in regulation 91.570 is given to the passenger; and
the person does not comply with the direction.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Passengers—compliance with safety instructions by cabin crew

content.p: A cabin crew member of an aircraft may, during a flight, give an instruction to a passenger:
relating to the safety of the aircraft; or
relating to the safety of a person on the aircraft.
A passenger on the aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
a cabin crew member gives a passenger an instruction under subregulation (1); and
the passenger does not comply with the instruction.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation does not apply in relation to the following kinds of cargo on an aircraft:
an assistance animal carried in a passenger cabin;
carry-on baggage;
equipment that is required or permitted under these Regulations to be carried on the aircraft without being restrained or stowed;
cargo to be dropped from the aircraft during a dropping operation.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if cargo carried on the flight is not:
restrained using equipment that is approved under regulation 21.305 or 21.305A; or
securely stowed in a place designed and approved for that purpose under Part 21; or

for equipment of a foreign registered aircraft operating in Australian territory—restrained or stowed in accordance with any requirements under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Restraint and stowage of carry-on baggage

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
either:
the aircraft is taking off or landing; or
the pilot in command has directed that carry-on baggage be securely stowed; and
an item of carry-on baggage is not:

securely stowed in a place designed and approved under Part 21 (or in the case of a foreign aircraft, under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator) for that purpose; or
otherwise safely restrained.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.265 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Restraint and stowage of certain aircraft equipment

content.p: The operator and pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
either:
the aircraft is taking off or landing; or
the pilot in command has directed that passenger service equipment or galley equipment be restrained or securely stowed; and
the passenger service equipment or galley equipment is not restrained or securely stowed in a place intended for the purpose.
Note: This regulation does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if regulation 121.265 applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met for the flight.
The requirements are the following:
cargo must not be carried in a place where the cargo may damage, obstruct or cause the failure of:
a control, electrical wiring or a pipeline of the aircraft; or
any other equipment that is essential to the safe operation of the aircraft;
cargo must not be carried in a place where the weight of the cargo exceeds the load limitations for the floor structure or any other load bearing components of that place, as set out:
in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft; or
on a placard on the aircraft;
cargo (other than passenger service equipment or galley equipment in an aisle on a temporary basis while in use) must not obstruct an aisle;
either:
cargo must not obstruct, or restrict access to, an emergency exit; or
the operator or the pilot in command must hold an approval from CASA under regulation 91.045 for cargo to be carried in a manner that obstructs, or restricts access to, the emergency exit.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
more than one flight crew member is required for the flight; and
cargo is carried in a cargo compartment; and
the design of the cargo compartment is such that if a fire were to occur during the flight, a crew member would need to enter the compartment to extinguish the fire; and
the cargo is not loaded in a manner to allow a crew member to reach, at any time during the flight, all parts of the compartment with the contents of a hand-held fire extinguisher.
(2) A flight crew member is required for a flight if the flight crew member is one of the number of flight crew members required for the flight by:
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft; or
if a greater number is required by these Regulations—these Regulations.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
cargo is carried on an unoccupied seat in the aircraft; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the cargo must not weigh more than:
77 kg; or
if the seat manufacturer permits a greater weight for the seat—that weight;
the cargo, and the means of restraint of the cargo, must not interfere with the safe operation of the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies in relation to cargo other than cargo that:
is carry-on baggage that weighs less than 9 kg and is stowed under a seat or in a place designed for that purpose; or
is carried on an unoccupied seat in accordance with regulation 91.610.

The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, cargo is not carried in the aircraft in a place that has a placard bearing the instructions for the carriage of the cargo in that place.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person brings an animal onto an aircraft for a flight; and
the person does not have permission from the pilot in command of the aircraft to do so.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command of the aircraft gives permission for a person to bring an animal onto the aircraft for the flight; and
the pilot in command does not take reasonable steps to ensure that carriage of the animal does not have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.

(3) The operator or the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight may refuse to carry an assistance animal (within the meaning of the Disability Discrimination Act 1992) in the aircraft for the flight if the operator or pilot in command reasonably believes that the carriage of the animal for the flight may have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
(4) Subregulation (3) has effect despite anything in the Disability Discrimination Act 1992.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the carriage of animals on an aircraft for a flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (5); and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (5); and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), (6) or (7).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person transmits on a radio frequency published in the AIP or NOTAMs that is:
used by Air Traffic Services; or

used for communications at a certified aerodrome, a registered aerodrome, a military aerodrome or an aerodrome prescribed as a designated non-controlled aerodrome by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of subparagraph 91.400(1)(a)(iv); or
used in aeronautical emergencies; or
of a kind prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for this subparagraph; and
the person is not authorised or qualified to do so:
for an Australian aircraft (other than a Part 103 aircraft or a Part 131 aircraft)—under Part 61, 64 or 65; or
for a foreign registered aircraft—under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator; or
for a Part 103 aircraft—by a Part 103 ASAO; or
for a Part 131 aircraft—by a Part 131 pilot authorisation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is fitted with, or carries, a radio; and
during the flight, the pilot in command does not make a broadcast or a report relating to the flight that is prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, the aircraft is flown in controlled airspace; and
the pilot in command does not continuously monitor the primary communications medium used by air traffic control while flying in that airspace.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Use of radio outside controlled airspaces—listening watch of radio transmissions

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is fitted with, or carries, a radio; and
the aircraft is flown by a pilot who is qualified, eligible or authorised to use the radio:
for an Australian aircraft (other than a Part 103 aircraft or a Part 131 aircraft)—under Part 61 or 64; or
for a foreign registered aircraft—under a law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator; or
for a Part 103 aircraft—by a Part 103 ASAO; or
for a Part 131 aircraft—by a Part 131 pilot authorisation; and
the aircraft is outside controlled airspace; and
radio transmissions are not continuously monitored by:
the pilot in command of the aircraft for the flight; or
another pilot who occupies a pilot seat during the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Availability of instructions for flight data and combination recorders

content.p: The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft begins the flight:
the aircraft is required to be fitted with a flight data recorder or combination recorder by these Regulations; and
the operator does not have the instructions for the recorder available for immediate provision to the Australian Transport Safety Bureau.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Flight recorders—preserving recordings of immediately reportable matters

content.p: The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is fitted with an operative flight data recorder, operative cockpit voice recorder or operative combination recorder; and
an immediately reportable matter occurs in relation to the aircraft; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that recordings from the flight data recorder, cockpit voice recorder and combination recorder related to the occurrence of the matter, and the recorders, are preserved:

(a) if the Australian Transport Safety Bureau notifies the operator, within 72 hours of the matter being reported to the Australian Transport Safety Bureau under section 18 of the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003:
that the operator is not required to preserve the recordings and recorders—until the time of that notification; or
that the operator is required to preserve the recordings and recorders for a certain period—until the end of that period; or

that the operator is required to preserve the recordings for a certain period but is not required to preserve the recorders—until the end of that period for the recordings, and until the time of that notification for the recorders; or
(b) in any other case—until 72 hours after the matter is reported to the Australian Transport Safety Bureau under section 18 of the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the recordings or recorders are not preserved; and
the operator took reasonable steps in the circumstances to preserve the recordings or recorders.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is flown in RVSM airspace; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that either or both of the following apply:
the operator of the aircraft holds:
for an Australian aircraft—an approval under regulation 91.045; or
for a foreign aircraft—an approval by the national aviation authority of the aircraft’s State of registry or of the State of the operator;
for the aircraft to be flown in RVSM airspace;
the pilot in command has been given an air traffic control clearance or an air traffic control instruction for the aircraft to be flown in the RVSM airspace.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is in RVSM airspace; and
the aircraft becomes unable to operate with RVSM separation; and
the pilot in command does not inform air traffic control as soon as practicable after the aircraft becomes unable to operate with RVSM separation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight, or any part of the flight, is conducted using a navigation specification prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph; and
neither the operator of the aircraft for the flight nor the pilot in command holds:
for an Australian aircraft—an approval under regulation 91.045; or
(ii) for a foreign registered aircraft—an approval by the national aviation authority of the aircraft’s State of registry or of the State of the operator;
to use that navigation specification during the flight or part of the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person displays a signal to an aircraft other than a glider for the purposes of marshalling the aircraft; and
the signal is not a standard visual signal.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person displays a standard visual signal to an aircraft; and
the safety of the aircraft, or of any person or property, is likely to be endangered as a result of the display of the signal.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a standard visual signal is displayed to the aircraft during the flight; and
the pilot in command does not comply with the signal.
Subregulation (3) does not apply if the pilot in command reasonably believes that compliance with the signal is likely to endanger the safety of the aircraft or of any person or property.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (4): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Pilot in command to report hazards to air navigation

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command becomes aware that a hazard to air navigation exists; and
information about the hazard is not published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight; and
the pilot in command does not, as soon as circumstances permit, report the hazard to:
Air Traffic Services; and
if the hazard is on an aerodrome—the operator of the aerodrome.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the pilot believes that the hazard has previously been reported as required by subregulation (1); and
the belief is reasonable in the circumstances.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Pilot in command to report emergencies

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
an emergency occurs that threatens the safety of the aircraft or the persons on the aircraft; and
the aircraft is fitted with, or carries, a means for the pilot in command to communicate with Air Traffic Services; and
it is practicable to inform Air Traffic Services of the emergency; and
the pilot does not inform Air Traffic Services, at the time that it is practicable to do so, of:
the emergency; and
if the aircraft is carrying dangerous goods—the nature and state of the goods.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Multi-engine aircraft—pilot in command to land at nearest suitable aerodrome if emergency occurs

content.p: The pilot in command of a multi-engine aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
an emergency occurs that threatens the safety of the aircraft or the persons on the aircraft; and
the pilot does not land at the aerodrome that is, in the circumstances, the nearest suitable aerodrome for the aircraft to land at.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Pilot in command to report contraventions relating to emergencies

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
during the flight, an emergency occurs that threatens the safety of the aircraft or the persons on the aircraft; and
the emergency requires the pilot flying the aircraft to take action that involves a contravention of a provision of these Regulations; and

neither the operator nor the pilot in command give CASA written notice, in the approved form, of the contravention and the circumstances of the contravention, within 2 business days after the day the emergency occurs.

The pilot in command is not excused from giving notice under subregulation (1) on the ground that the giving of the notice, or the information in the notice, might tend to incriminate the pilot in command or expose the pilot in command to a penalty.

(3) The following are not admissible in evidence against the pilot in command in criminal proceedings other than proceedings for an offence against subsection 136.1(1) or (4), 137.1(1) or 137.2(1) of the Criminal Code:
the information in the notice;
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of giving the notice.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements to be met if an aircraft is intercepted by another aircraft during a flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is intercepted by another aircraft during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the person has made an aviation distress signal; and
the reason for making the signal no longer exists; and
the state of the aircraft’s radio and the location of the aircraft are such that the signal is able to be cancelled; and
the person does not cancel the signal as soon as circumstances permit.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Flight in icing conditions—adherence of frost, ice or snow

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft begins the flight, frost, ice or snow is adhering to any of the aircraft’s wings, flaps, control surfaces, rotors, propellers, horizontal stabilisers or vertical stabilisers.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the aircraft begins a flight:
the aircraft has frost, ice or snow adhering to the top of the aircraft’s fuselage; and
either:
the aircraft has rear-mounted engines; or
the adherence of the frost, ice or snow to the top of the aircraft’s fuselage is a hazard to the safe operation of the aircraft for the flight.

Subregulation (1) or (2) does not apply if the take-off for the flight is conducted in accordance with the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft that relate to taking off under the conditions mentioned in that subregulation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Flight in icing conditions—requirements for flight

content.p: This regulation applies to a flight of an aircraft if:
when the flight begins, icing conditions are known or suspected for the flight path along which the aircraft will be flown; or
both:
during the flight, the aircraft flies into icing conditions; and
the pilot in command does not, as soon as practicable, change the aircraft’s flight path to try and avoid the icing conditions.

The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight began, the aircraft was not type certificated as complying with the airworthiness standards relating to flight in icing conditions.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

subDivision.heading: Causing or simulating instrument failure etc.

section.heading: Causing or simulating failure of flight instruments

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the failure of an instrument of any of the following kinds is caused or simulated:
an attitude indicator;
a gyrocompass or an equivalent instrument;
an airspeed indicator;
an altimeter; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the flight must be conducted for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only crew members that are required for the training, checking or testing are carried on the flight;

a person who is authorised to pilot the aircraft under Part 61, by a Part 103 ASAO or by a Part 131 pilot authorisation (or in the case of a foreign aircraft, under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator):
must occupy a pilot seat fitted with a fully functioning set of flight controls; and
if the flight is in IMC or at night—must have a clear view of an operative instrument of the same kind as the instrument subjected to failure or simulated failure.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the pilot in command is carrying out:
a maintenance test flight; or
a procedure to diagnose or isolate a failure of an instrument or system.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, IMC are simulated; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
(a) a pilot (the safety pilot) must:
occupy a pilot seat fitted with fully functioning flight controls; and
have adequate vision forward and to each side of the aircraft;
(b) a pilot (the second pilot) flying the aircraft under simulated IMC must occupy a pilot seat fitted with fully functioning flight controls;
the safety pilot must be authorised or qualified to pilot the aircraft:
for an Australian aircraft—under Part 61; or
for a foreign registered aircraft—under the law of the aircraft’s State of registry or the State of the operator.
Note: If the flight manual for an aircraft requires that it be flown by 2 pilots, Part 61 requires both pilots to have a type rating for the aircraft.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
In this regulation:
permitted person, in relation to an aircraft, means:
a crew member of the aircraft; or
a person authorised by the operator of the aircraft to conduct an audit of the operation involved, or to supervise it; or
an authorised officer carrying out an examination, inspection or test of the work of the aircraft’s crew under these Regulations.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a person other than a permitted person is carried on the aircraft; and
the pilot in command permits any of the following:
flight training for a flight crew member who does not hold a class rating or type rating for the aircraft;
the simulation (other than verbally) of an emergency or abnormal situation that may affect the handling characteristics of the aircraft;
training below 500 ft AGL (other than training for take-off and landing);

training mentioned in Part 61 for a low-level rating, an aerial application rating, an aerobatic endorsement or a spinning endorsement, or training for an equivalent qualification under a law of a foreign country.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a person other than the following is carried on the aircraft:
a permitted person;
a member of the aircraft’s maintenance personnel who is required, as part of the member’s duties, to be on the aircraft; and

the pilot in command permits a test of the aircraft, or any of its instruments, indicators, items of equipment or systems (other than a test of the aircraft during the course of checks associated with the normal operation of the aircraft).
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
for a flight for which the activity mentioned in subparagraph (2)(b)(i) is permitted—more than 4 permitted persons, including the pilot, are on the aircraft; or
for a flight for which the activity mentioned in subparagraph (2)(b)(ii) or (iv) is permitted—more than 3 permitted persons, including the pilot, are on the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2), (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

subDivision.heading: Causing or simulating engine failure etc. for aeroplanes

section.heading: Aeroplane flights in IMC or at night—engine not to be shut down

content.p: The pilot in command of an aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is in IMC or at night; and
an engine of the aeroplane is shut down during the flight.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Single-engine aeroplane—VFR flights by day—engine not to be shut down

content.p: The pilot in command of a single-engine aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is a VFR flight by day; and
the engine of the aeroplane is shut down during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the flight must be conducted for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only flight crew members are carried on the flight;
the pilot in command must hold a flight instructor rating, flight examiner rating or other authorisation under these Regulations that authorises the activity of shutting down an engine;
while the engine is shut down, the aeroplane must remain within gliding distance of a safe forced landing area.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Single-engine aeroplane—simulating engine failure in IMC or at night

content.p: The pilot in command of a single-engine aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is:
in IMC; or
at night; and
a failure of the aeroplane’s engine is simulated during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the flight must be conducted for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only flight crew members are carried on the flight;
the pilot in command must hold a flight instructor rating, flight examiner rating or other authorisation under these Regulations that authorises the activity of simulating an engine failure;
for a simulation at night:
the simulation must commence above 1,000 ft AGL; and
while the engine failure is being simulated, the aeroplane must remain within gliding distance of a lighted runway available for landing;
for a simulation in IMC:
the simulation must commence above the lowest safe altitude for the route or route segment of the flight; and
VMC conditions must exist below that altitude.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of a multi-engine aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
an engine failure is simulated; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that one of the following must apply to the aeroplane:
the aeroplane must be type certificated to carry not more than 9 passengers, or must have a maximum take-off weight of not more than 8,618 kg;
for an aeroplane that is type certificated to carry more than 9 passengers but not more than 19 passengers:
there must be no flight simulator for the type of aeroplane in Australia; or
if subparagraph (i) does not apply—the operator must hold an approval from CASA under regulation 91.045 to simulate the failure of the engine;
for an aircraft that is type certificated to carry more than 19 passengers:
there must be no flight simulator for the type of aeroplane in Australia; and
there must be no flight simulator approved by a recognised national aviation authority in a foreign country for the type of aeroplane; and
if subparagraphs (i) and (ii) do not apply—the operator must hold an approval from CASA under regulation 91.045 to simulate the failure of the engine;
the aeroplane must be conducting a flight of the following kind in accordance with the requirements in Subpart 91.T for the kind of flight:
a test flight of an aircraft for which a provisional certificate of airworthiness is in force;
if a special flight permit allows the aeroplane to simulate a failure of the engine—a flight under the special flight permit;
if an experimental certificate allows the aeroplane to simulate a failure of the engine—a flight under the experimental certificate.
An application for an approval mentioned in subparagraph (2)(b)(ii) or (2)(c)(iii) must include a safety risk management plan.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Multi-engine aeroplane—simulating engine failures in IMC or at night

content.p: The pilot in command of a multi-engine aeroplane for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is:
in IMC; or
at night; and
a failure of one of the aeroplane’s engines is simulated during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the pilot in command must hold a flight instructor rating, flight examiner rating or other authorisation under these Regulations that authorises the activity of simulating an engine failure;
the flight must be conducted for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only flight crew members are carried on the flight;
the pilot in command must brief the pilot under instruction before the simulation and must supervise the simulation;
for an aeroplane flown in IMC that is not conducting an approach to land mentioned in paragraph (f)—the aeroplane must be at or above the minimum height mentioned in subregulation 91.305(2);
for an aeroplane conducting an asymmetric instrument approach and missed approach:
the simulation must be initiated above the initial approach altitude; and
the flight must be conducted with visual reference to the terrain when below a height of 1,000 ft above the relevant minima according to the aeronautical chart in use for the approach;
for an aeroplane flown at night in VMC—the aeroplane must be flown:

if the aeroplane is not conducting an approach to land or within the circling area of an aerodrome—above the minimum height mentioned in subregulation 91.305(2) or 91.277(2) (as the case requires); or
if the aeroplane is conducting an approach to land and is not within the circling area of an aerodrome—in accordance with an authorised instrument approach procedure; or

within the circling area of an aerodrome (as determined in accordance with the method specified in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight for determining the circling area for the aerodrome);
for an aeroplane flown at night in VMC—the simulation must be initiated at or above circuit height and not below 1,000 ft AGL;
the simulation must be carried out in accordance with procedures specified in:
the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aeroplane (if any); or

if procedures are not specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aeroplane, and the operator of the aeroplane is required to have an exposition by these Regulations—the exposition; or

if procedures are not specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aeroplane, and the operator of the aeroplane is not required to have an exposition by these Regulations—the operator’s operations manual.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

subDivision.heading: Causing or simulating engine failure etc. for rotorcraft

section.heading: Single-engine rotorcraft—engine not to be shut down

content.p: The pilot in command of a single-engine rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the engine is shut down.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Single-engine rotorcraft—engine failure not to be simulated and autorotation of main rotor system not to be initiated in IMC

content.p: The pilot in command of a single-engine rotorcraft for a flight in IMC contravenes this subregulation if:
a failure of the rotorcraft’s engine is simulated during the flight; or
an autorotation of the rotorcraft’s main rotor system is initiated.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Single-engine rotorcraft—simulating engine failure or initiating autorotation of main rotor system at night

content.p: The pilot in command of a single-engine rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is at night; and
during the flight, a failure of the rotorcraft’s engine is simulated or an autorotation of the rotorcraft’s main rotor system is initiated; and
the rotorcraft is not:
taxiing or hovering below the hover height for the surface specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the rotorcraft; or
at a height at or above 1,000 ft AGL; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:

the pilot in command must hold a flight instructor rating, flight examiner rating or other authorisation under these Regulations that authorises the activity of simulating an engine failure or initiating an autorotation of the main rotor system (as the case requires);
the flight must be carried out for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only flight crew members are carried on the flight;
the pilot in command must brief the pilot under instruction before the simulation or autorotation and must supervise the simulation or autorotation;
the simulation or autorotation must be carried out in VMC; and
power termination of the autorotation must be initiated so that full power is available before the rotorcraft goes below 100 ft AGL;
the autorotation must be terminated using a power recovery termination or a baulked approach and climb out;
the simulation or autorotation must be conducted at an aerodrome with omnidirectional runway lighting.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Multi-engine rotorcraft—engine not to be shut down at certain altitudes in IMC or at night

content.p: The pilot in command of a multi-engine rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is:
in IMC; or
at night; and
an engine of the rotorcraft is shut down during the flight; and
the rotorcraft is not at or above the lowest safe altitude for a route or route segment for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Multi-engine rotorcraft—simulating engine failure in IMC or at night

content.p: The pilot in command of a multi-engine rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the flight is:
in IMC; or
at night; and
a failure of one of the rotorcraft’s engines is simulated during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:

the pilot in command must hold a flight instructor rating, flight examiner rating or other authorisation under these Regulations that authorises the activity of simulating an engine failure in a multi-engine rotorcraft;
the flight must be for the purpose of pilot training, checking or testing;
only flight crew members are carried on the flight;
the pilot in command must brief the pilot under instruction before the simulation and must supervise the simulation;
for a rotorcraft flown in IMC—the rotorcraft must be established at or above the lowest safe altitude for a route or route segment for the flight;
for a rotorcraft flown at night in VMC:

the rotorcraft must be flown within the circling area of an aerodrome (as determined in accordance with the method specified in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight determining the circling area for the aerodrome); and
in the climb during take-off, the simulation must be initiated before the take-off decision point, or above 500 ft AGL; and
after the climb during take-off, the simulation must be initiated at or above 1,000 ft AGL;
the simulation must be carried out in accordance with:
procedures specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the rotorcraft (if any); or

if procedures are not specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the rotorcraft, and the operator of the rotorcraft is required by these Regulations to have an exposition—the exposition; or

if procedures are not specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the rotorcraft, and the operator of the rotorcraft is not required by these Regulations to have an exposition—the operator’s operations manual.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A passenger on an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the passenger consumes alcohol; and
either:
a crew member has not provided the alcohol to the passenger; or
if there is no crew member other than the pilot in command on the aircraft—the pilot in command has not permitted the passenger to consume the alcohol.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A crew member of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the crew member provides alcohol to a passenger on the aircraft; and

there are reasonable grounds to believe the passenger is affected by one or more psychoactive substances to an extent that the passenger’s behaviour may present a hazard to the aircraft or to a person on the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Prohibiting person affected by psychoactive substances from boarding

content.p: The operator, or a crew member, of an aircraft for a flight may prohibit a person from boarding the aircraft if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person is affected by a psychoactive substance to an extent that may present a hazard to the aircraft or to a person on the aircraft.
Subpart 91.F—Performance
Note: This Subpart does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Subpart 121.F, 133.F, 135.F or 138.F applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to take-off performance for a flight of an aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements that relate to one or more of the following:
the aircraft’s configuration;
the operation of any equipment for the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft takes off;
characteristics of the route flown by the aircraft;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft lands.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to landing performance for a flight of an aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to one or more of the following:
the aircraft’s configuration;
the operation of any equipment for the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft lands;
safety factor percentages to be applied.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 91.J—Weight and balance
Note: This Subpart does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Subpart 121.J, 133.J, 135.J or 138.J applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins the aircraft is loaded in a way that contravenes the aircraft’s weight and balance limits.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the aircraft ceases to be operated in accordance with the aircraft’s weight and balance limits.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 91.K—Equipment
Note: This Subpart does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Subpart 121.K, 133.K or 135.K applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
The Part 91 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
the fitment and non-fitment of equipment to an aircraft; and
the carrying of equipment on an aircraft; and
equipment that is fitted to, or carried on, an aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 91.P—Cabin crew
Note: This Subpart does not apply to the operation of an aircraft if Subpart 121.P, 133.P or 135.P applies to the operation: see regulation 91.035.
Subject to subregulations (2) and (3), a cabin crew member must be carried on a flight of an aircraft if 20 or more passengers are carried on the flight.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the flight involves a parachuting activity to which Part 105 applies.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the flight crew for the flight includes at least 2 pilots; and
no more than 22 passengers are carried on the flight; and
no more than 19 of the passengers are adults or children.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
under regulation 91.820, a cabin crew member must be carried on the flight; and

when the aircraft begins the flight, the number of cabin crew members for the flight is not at least equal to the sum of one cabin crew member for each 50, or part of 50, passengers carried on the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Cabin crew—knowledge of emergency and safety equipment and procedures

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to a flight of an aircraft if, under regulation 91.820, a cabin crew member must be carried on the flight.
The operator, a cabin crew member, and the pilot in command, of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the cabin crew member is not competent to:
operate and use emergency and safety equipment on the aircraft that is relevant to the cabin crew member’s duties; and
implement emergency evacuation procedures for the aircraft; and
the cabin crew member begins to carry out cabin crew member duties for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 91.T—Operations under certain special certificates of airworthiness and special flight permits

section.heading: Aircraft with more than one certificate of airworthiness—application of Subpart 91.T

content.p: If a certificate of airworthiness in more than one category has been issued for an aircraft, this Subpart applies in relation to the operation of the aircraft only for the category in relation to which the aircraft is being operated.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
a special certificate of airworthiness in the restricted category has been issued for the aircraft; and
the aircraft begins a flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met for the flight.
The requirements are as follows:
the certificate of airworthiness must be in force;
