breaches a condition of the tester’s approval given under regulation 99.445; or
does not comply with the requirements of this Part in performing functions or exercising powers under this Part.
CASA may do any or all of the following in respect of the breach:
impose a further condition of approval;
suspend the approved tester’s authorisation under regulation 99.450;
revoke the tester’s authorisation under regulation 99.450.
If:
(a) CASA takes an action mentioned in paragraph (2)(a) or (b) because of a breach of a condition (the first breach); and
CASA later becomes satisfied that the approved tester is not complying with a condition of the approval under regulation 99.445;
CASA may revoke the tester’s authorisation even if the period for fulfilling any condition, or the period of any suspension for the first breach, has not ended.

If CASA imposes on an approved tester a further condition of approval under paragraph 99.485(2)(a), CASA must give the tester notice in writing of the imposition of the condition, the terms of the condition and the date from which the condition takes effect.

If CASA suspends the approved tester’s authorisation under paragraph 99.485(2)(b), CASA must give the tester notice in writing of the suspension, the date that the suspension takes effect and the period of the suspension.
If CASA revokes the approved tester’s authorisation under paragraph 99.485(2)(c), CASA must give the tester notice in writing of the revocation and the date from which the revocation takes effect.
The date under this regulation must not be a date before the day the notice is given.
A notice under this regulation must also include a statement setting out the reason that the condition was imposed or that the authorisation was suspended or revoked, as the case may be.

If a provision of these Regulations requires CASA to give a notice to an approved tester, the requirement is met if CASA gives that notice to the person who, as CASA’s delegate, approved the tester as an approved tester.

Subpart 101.A—Preliminary

This Part sets out the requirements for the operation of unmanned aircraft (including model aircraft), and (to the extent that the operation of rockets and fireworks affects or may affect the safety of air navigation) the operation of rockets and the use of certain fireworks.
Nothing in this Part applies to the operation of a manned balloon or a hot air balloon.
Subparts 101.C to 101.I do not apply to the operation of:

a control-line model aircraft (that is, a model aircraft that is constrained to fly in a circle, and is controlled in attitude and altitude, by means of inextensible wires attached to a handle held by the person operating the model); or
a model aircraft indoors; or
an unmanned airship indoors; or
a small balloon within 100 metres of a structure and not above the top of the structure; or
an unmanned tethered balloon that remains below 400 feet AGL; or
a firework rocket not capable of rising more than 400 feet AGL.
Note: Subpart 101.B applies to the operation of all unmanned aircraft (including model aircraft) and rockets, including firework rockets.
For paragraph (3)(c), a flight does not take place indoors if the building in which it takes place has the roof, or 1 or more walls, removed.
This Part applies to a rocket-powered unmanned aircraft, and to the operation of such an aircraft, unless the contrary intention appears.

section.heading: Exemption from certain provisions of CAR

content.p: Parts 4, 4A, 4B, 4C, 5, 9, 10 and 14 of CAR do not apply to an aircraft to which this Part applies, nor to a micro RPA.
An RPA is a remotely piloted aircraft, other than the following:
a balloon;
a kite;
a model aircraft.
The defined terms listed in the following table have the meaning indicated in the table.

tr.td: an RPA with a gross weight of not more than 250 g.
an RPA with a gross weight of more than 250 g, but not more than 2 kg.
an RPA with a gross weight of more than 2 kg, but not more than 25 kg.
(a) an RPA with a gross weight of more than 25 kg, but not more than 150 kg; or (b) a remotely piloted airship with an envelope capacity of not more than 100 m3.

(a) a remotely piloted aeroplane with a gross weight of more than 150 kg; or (b) a remotely piloted powered parachute with a gross weight of more than 150 kg; or (c) a remotely piloted rotorcraft with a gross weight of more than 150 kg; or (d) a remotely piloted powered-lift aircraft with a gross weight of more than 150 kg; or (e) a remotely piloted airship with an envelope capacity of more than 100 m3.

content.p: Note: For the meaning of excluded RPA, see regulation 101.237.
(1) A model aircraft is an aircraft (other than a balloon or a kite) that does not carry a person:
if the aircraft:
is being operated for the purpose of sport or recreation; and
has a gross weight of not more than 150 kg; or
if the aircraft has a gross weight of not more than 7 kg, and is being operated in connection with the educational, training or research purposes of:
(i) a school in relation to which there is an approved authority under the Australian Education Act 2013; or
(ii) a higher education provider within the meaning of the Higher Education Support Act 2003.

However, paragraph (1)(b) does not apply in relation to education, training or research conducted by or on behalf of an entity other than a school or higher education provider mentioned in subparagraph (1)(b)(i) or (ii).
Note: A model aircraft is not an RPA (see the definition of RPA in regulation 101.021).
The defined term listed in the following table has the meaning indicated in the table.

tr.td: a model aircraft that has a take-off weight (excluding fuel) of more than 25 kilograms.

content.p: For this Part, an area is a populous area in relation to the operation of an unmanned aircraft if the area has a sufficient density of population for some aspect of the operation, or some event that might happen during the operation (in particular, a fault in, or failure of, the aircraft) to pose an unreasonable risk to the life, safety or property of somebody who is in the area but is not connected with the operation.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 101

content.p: For subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
If a provision in this Part refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, the person may apply to CASA for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant the approval if:
for an approval relating to a training course:
the course covers the units of competency (if any) prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards for the course; and
the course meets the standards (if any) prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards for the course; or
for an approval relating to any other thing for which requirements are prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards—the prescribed requirements are met.

section.heading: Approval of areas for operation of unmanned aircraft or rockets

content.p: A person may apply to CASA for the approval of an area as an area for the operation of:
unmanned aircraft generally, or a particular class of unmanned aircraft; or
rockets.
For paragraph (1)(a), the classes of unmanned aircraft are the following:
tethered balloons and kites;
unmanned free balloons;
RPA;
model aircraft.

In considering whether to approve an area for any of those purposes, CASA must take into account the likely effect on the safety of air navigation of the operation of unmanned aircraft in, or the launching of rockets in or over, the area.
An approval has effect from the time written notice of it is given to the applicant, or a later day or day and time stated in the approval.
An approval may be expressed to have effect for a particular period (including a period of less than 1 day), or indefinitely.
CASA may impose conditions on the approval in the interests of the safety of air navigation.
If CASA approves an area under subregulation (1), it must publish details of the approval (including any condition) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart.

CASA may revoke the approval of an area, or change the conditions that apply to such an approval, in the interests of the safety of air navigation, but must publish details of any revocation or change in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart.
CASA must also give written notice of the revocation or change:
to the person who applied for the approval of the area; or
if that person applied for that approval as an officer of an organisation concerned with unmanned aircraft or rockets, and no longer holds that office—to the person who now holds the office.
In the case of an approval of an area as an area for the operation of model aircraft:
subregulation (7) does not apply; and
subregulation (8) does not require the publication of any details of a revocation or change in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart.

section.heading: Requirements in this Part to give information to CASA

content.p: If a provision of this Part requires a person to give information to CASA about the operation, launching or release of an unmanned aircraft or rocket, then, unless the provision says otherwise, the person may do so by giving the information to:
if the person is an approved aviation administration organisation—the Australian NOTAM Office; or
an appropriate approved aviation administration organisation.
However, subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to the release of small balloons, or in relation to a firework display.
The information need not be given in writing unless:
CASA or the authority to which it is given asks for it to be given in writing in the particular case; or
another provision of these Regulations requires it to be given in writing.

If a person gives the information to an authority mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b), then, subject to subregulation (6), the person is taken, for all purposes, to have complied with the requirement to give the information.

If in a particular case CASA or the authority to which the information is given reasonably requires extra information about the operation, launching or release, CASA or the authority may ask the person for the extra information.

If CASA or an authority asks for more information under subregulation (5), the person is not taken to have complied with the requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) to give the information until the person gives to CASA or the authority the extra information.

If a day is not a working day for the office of CASA or an authority to which notice of an event is given or an application made, that day does not count for the purpose of working out how many working days’ notice of the event has been given, or how many working days before an event the application has been made.
In subregulation (7):
working day, in relation to an office of CASA or an authority, means a day on which that office is open for business.
Subpart 101.AB—Authorisations for sections 20AA and 20AB of the Act

section.heading: Flying without a certificate of airworthiness

content.p: For the purposes of paragraph 20AA(3)(b) of the Act, a flight of an RPA (other than a large RPA) is authorised without a certificate of airworthiness.
Note: For requirements in relation to large RPA, see regulation 101.255.

section.heading: Performance of duties during flight time—balloons, kites and model aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies to an Australian aircraft that is an unmanned aircraft if it is:
a balloon; or
a kite; or
a model aircraft.

For the purposes of paragraph 20AB(1)(b) of the Act, a person performing a duty that is essential to the operation of the aircraft during flight time is authorised to do so without a civil aviation authorisation mentioned in paragraph 20AB(1)(a) of the Act.

section.heading: Performance of duties during flight time—remotely piloted aircraft

content.p: For the purposes of paragraph 20AB(1)(b) of the Act, a person performing a duty that is essential to the operation of an RPA during flight time is authorised to do so without a civil aviation authorisation mentioned in paragraph 20AB(1)(a) of the Act.
Operating excluded RPA and micro RPA
Subregulation (1) applies to a person operating an RPA only if:
the RPA is an excluded RPA or a micro RPA; and
the operation is of a kind mentioned in subregulation 101.374B(4) (which covers supervised operation by a person under the age of 16).

Note: These Regulations allow a person to operate an RPA other than an excluded RPA or micro RPA only if the person holds a remote pilot licence. A person is allowed to operate an excluded RPA or micro RPA if the person is accredited or holds a remote pilot licence, or in the circumstance mentioned in paragraph (2)(b) of this regulation. See regulation 101.252 and subregulations 101.374B(1) and (4).
Subpart 101.B—General prohibition on unsafe operation
This Subpart applies to the operation of all unmanned aircraft and rockets that are not aircraft, whether or not any of Subparts C to I applies.
A person must not operate an unmanned aircraft in a way that creates a hazard to another aircraft, another person, or property.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person must not launch a rocket that is not an aircraft in a way that creates a hazard to an aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person must not launch a rocket that:
is not an aircraft; and
(b) is not a high power rocket within the meaning of the Space (Launches and Returns) Act 2018; and
is not a space object or part of a space object within the meaning of that Act;
in a way that creates a hazard to another person or to property.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: Hazards from high power rockets and space objects are regulated under the Space (Launches and Returns) Act 2018.
An offence against subregulation (1), (2) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

It is not a defence to a charge of contravening subregulation (1), (2) or (3) that the relevant unmanned aircraft was being operated, or the relevant rocket was launched, in a way that complied with the operations manual of an approved aviation administration organisation.
In subregulations (2) and (3):
rocket includes a firework rocket.
Subpart 101.C—Provisions applicable to unmanned aircraft generally
This Subpart applies to the operation of unmanned aircraft of all kinds, except operation mentioned in subregulation 101.005(3).
Note: Rockets that are not aircraft are dealt with separately in Subpart 101.H.

section.heading: Operation in prohibited or restricted area

content.p: A person may operate an unmanned aircraft in or over a prohibited area, or in or over a restricted area, only with the permission of, and in accordance with any conditions imposed by, the authority controlling the area.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: Details of prohibited and restricted areas are published in the AIP or NOTAMS.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
In subregulation (1):
authority controlling the area means:
(a) in the case of a prohibited area—the Secretary of the Department administered by the Minister administering section 1 of the Defence Act 1903; and
in the case of a restricted area—the authority mentioned in AIP (as issued from time to time) as the controlling authority for the area.
For subregulation (1):
the authority controlling the area must give a written statement of any condition so imposed to the person who applied for the permission; and
unless the authority gives the statement to the person, the person is not bound by the condition.

section.heading: Operation in prescribed area—requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of unmanned aircraft in an area prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates an unmanned aircraft in an area prescribed under subregulation (1); and
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1) in relation to the operation; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Operation in controlled airspace above 400 ft AGL

content.p: A person may operate an unmanned aircraft above 400 feet AGL in controlled airspace only:
in an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of unmanned aircraft of the same kind as the aircraft, and in accordance with any conditions of the approval; and
in accordance with an air traffic control clearance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operation in controlled airspace—requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of unmanned aircraft in controlled airspace.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates an unmanned aircraft in controlled airspace; and
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1) in relation to the operation; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Operation must generally be within visual line of sight

content.p: Unmanned aircraft must be operated within visual line of sight
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates an unmanned aircraft; and
the aircraft is not operated within the person’s visual line of sight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Exception—CASA approval
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the person holds an approval under regulation 101.029 to operate the unmanned aircraft beyond the person’s visual line of sight; and
the conditions (if any) imposed on the approval are complied with.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Meaning of operated within visual line of sight

(3) An unmanned aircraft is being operated within the visual line of sight of the person operating the aircraft if the person can continually see, orient and navigate the aircraft to meet the person’s separation and collision avoidance responsibilities, with or without corrective lenses, but without the use of binoculars, a telescope or other similar device.
A person may operate an unmanned aircraft at an altitude above 400 feet AGL within 3 nautical miles of an aerodrome only if:
the operation is permitted by another provision of this Part; or
permission has been given for the operation under regulation 101.080.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
A person may operate an unmanned aircraft over an area mentioned in paragraph (3)(a) or (b) only if:
the operation is permitted by another provision of this Part; or
permission has been given for the operation under regulation 101.080.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
The areas for subregulation (2) are:
a movement area or runway of an aerodrome; and
the approach or departure path of a runway of an aerodrome.
A person must not operate an unmanned aircraft in such a manner as to create an obstruction to an aircraft taking off from, or approaching for landing at, a landing area or a runway of an aerodrome.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1), (2) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Permission for operation of unmanned aircraft near aerodrome

content.p: The authority from which permission must be obtained for the purposes of regulation 101.075 is:
if the aerodrome concerned is a controlled aerodrome—the air traffic control service for the aerodrome; or
in the case of any other aerodrome—CASA.

A person applies for permission under this regulation by giving to the relevant authority mentioned in subregulation (1) the information required by table 101.080, so far as relevant to the proposed operation.

tr.th: Table 101.080 Details of operation of unmanned aircraft to be given to CASA or ATC
Table 101.080 Details of operation of unmanned aircraft to be given to CASA or ATC

tr.td: In all cases: (a) the name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will operate the aircraft or (if the aircraft concerned is an unmanned free balloon) release the balloon (or, if several people will be involved, the name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will coordinate the operation); and (b) the date and time the operation or release is to begin and how long it is to last; and (c) where it is to be carried out; and (d) if more than 1 unmanned aircraft is to be operated at a time, how many unmanned aircraft are to be operated at that time

In the case of the operation of a tethered balloon or a kite: (a) a brief description of the balloon or kite, including its predominant colour; and (b) the height to which it is to be operated; and (c) its mass
In the case of the release of an unmanned free balloon: (a) how many balloons are to be released; and (b) the estimated size and mass of the balloon’s payload

In the case of the release of a medium or heavy balloon: (a) the balloon’s flight identification or its project code name; and (b) the balloon’s classification, or a description of the balloon; and (c) the balloon’s SSR code or NDB frequency, and its Morse identification; and (d) the expected horizontal direction of the balloon’s ascent, and the balloon’s expected rate of climb; and (e) the balloon’s float level (given as pressure altitude); and
(f) when the balloon is expected to reach 60 000 feet pressure altitude, and the location over which it is expected to do so; and
(g) when the flight is expected to end, and where the balloon and its payload are expected to fall

content.p: Note: For free balloon and heavy balloon, see regulation 101.145. For tethered balloon, see regulation 101.105.
If more than 1 aircraft is to be operated at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such aircraft.
Regulation 101.035 does not authorise a person who or that applies for permission under this regulation to make the application to a body mentioned in paragraph 101.035(1)(a) or (b).
If the authority grants the permission, it may impose conditions on the permission in the interests of the safety of air navigation.
A person must not contravene a condition imposed under subregulation (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (6) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate an unmanned aircraft above 400 feet AGL only:
in an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of unmanned aircraft of the same class as the aircraft concerned, and in accordance with any conditions of the approval; or
as otherwise permitted by this Part.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person must not cause a thing to be dropped or discharged from an unmanned aircraft in a way that creates a hazard to another aircraft, a person, or property.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate an unmanned aircraft:
in or into cloud; or
at night; or
in conditions other than VMC;
only if permitted by another provision of this Part, or in accordance with an air traffic control direction.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person holds an approval under regulation 101.029 for the purposes of this subregulation.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (1A): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Autonomous aircraft—launch or release without approval prohibited

content.p: This regulation:
(a) applies to an unmanned aircraft (an autonomous aircraft) that does not allow pilot intervention during all stages of the flight of the aircraft; but
does not apply to balloons, kites or model aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person causes an autonomous aircraft to be launched or released.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulation (2) does not apply if:
the person holds an approval under regulation 101.029 to launch or release the autonomous aircraft; and
the conditions (if any) imposed on the approval are complied with.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Identification of certain RPA—requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the identification of RPA required to be registered under Division 47.C.2.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates, or conducts an operation using, an RPA required to be registered under Division 47.C.2; and
the person is subject to a requirement prescribed for the purposes of subregulation (1) in relation to that operation or conduct; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Foreign registered RPA and model aircraft—requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of, or the conduct of operations using, RPA or model aircraft registered under a law of a foreign country.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates, or conducts an operation using, an RPA, or a model aircraft, within Australian territory; and
the person is subject to a requirement prescribed under subregulation (1) in relation to that operation or conduct; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Payment of unmanned aircraft levy

(1) An application under Chapter 13 of the Part 101 (Unmanned Aircraft and Rockets) Manual of Standards 2019 for permission to operate, or to conduct operations using, an RPA registered under a law of a foreign country must be accompanied by the unmanned aircraft levy (if any) for the application.
Waiver or refund of unmanned aircraft levy

CASA may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, waive the payment of unmanned aircraft levy under subregulation (1), or refund levy that has been paid under that subregulation, if CASA is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances justifying the waiver or refund.
The waiver or refund:
may be of the whole or part of the levy; and
may be made by CASA on its own initiative, or on written application in the approved form by the applicant for the registration.

section.heading: Modifications of certain RPA—requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the modification of an RPA registered under Division 47.C.2, including the extent to which modifications may be made to such an aircraft before the aircraft is considered to be no longer the aircraft to which the aircraft’s registration applies.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the RPA is registered under Division 47.C.2; and
the aircraft is modified after it is registered under that Division; and
the person operates the modified aircraft, or conducts an operation using the modified aircraft; and
the person is subject to a requirement prescribed for the purposes of subregulation (1) in relation to that operation or conduct; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Test flights of certain RPA—circumstances and requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards

content.p: Circumstances in which aircraft may be operated for test flights while not registered for the flights

The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe the circumstances in which an RPA that is not required to be registered under Division 47.C.1, and is not registered under Division 47.C.2, may be operated for the purposes of a test flight.

For the purposes of subregulation (1), circumstances in which an aircraft may be operated for the purposes of a test flight may be prescribed only if the circumstances are relevant to the development, manufacture, repair or maintenance of the aircraft or of equipment associated with the aircraft.
Requirements for aircraft operated for test flights while not registered for the flights
The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of an aircraft mentioned in subregulation (1) for the purposes of a test flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates, or conducts an operation using, an RPA for the purposes of a test flight; and
the person is subject to a requirement prescribed for the purposes of subregulation (3) in relation to that operation or conduct; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 101.D—Tethered balloons and kites
This Subpart applies to the operation of tethered balloons and kites.
Note: This Subpart does not apply to:
the shielded operation (that is, operation within 100 metres of a structure and not above the top of the structure) of a small balloon; or
the operation of an unmanned tethered balloon or kite below 400 feet AGL.
See subregulation 101.005(3).
In this Subpart:
tethered balloon means an unmanned balloon that is attached to the ground, or an object on the ground, by a cable.
For this Subpart, the height of a tethered balloon is taken to be the height above ground or water level of the topmost part of its envelope.

section.heading: Tethered balloons and kites that may be operated outside approved areas

content.p: A person may operate a tethered balloon or a kite above 400 feet AGL outside an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of unmanned balloons or kites (as the case requires) only if:
the mass of the balloon or kite is no more than 15 kilograms; and
the horizontal visibility at the time is at least 5 kilometres; and
the person gives to CASA the information required by table 101.110 about the proposed operation at least 1 working day before it is due to start.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note 1: A person can comply with this requirement by telling:
if the person is an approved aviation administration organisation—the Australian NOTAM Office; or
the appropriate approved aviation administration organisation.
See regulation 101.035.
Note 2: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
If more than 1 tethered balloon or kite is to be operated at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such balloon or kite.

The date and time the operation is to begin, and how long it is to last
Where it is to be carried out

The height to which it is to be operated
If more than 1 tethered balloon or kite is to be operated at a time, how many tethered balloons or kites are to be operated at the time

content.p: A person may operate a tethered balloon only if:
each mooring line has coloured streamers attached at intervals of no more than 15 metres along it, with the first streamer no more than 150 feet AGL; and
the streamers would be visible in normal daylight for at least 1.5 kilometres.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operation of tethered balloon or kite under cloud

content.p: A person may operate a tethered balloon or kite under cloud only if he or she keeps the balloon or kite at least 500 feet (measured vertically) below the cloud.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: For tethered balloon, see regulation 101.105.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Tethered balloon to be lit at night

content.p: A person may operate a tethered balloon at night at or above 400 feet AGL only if it is lit so as to be visible in VMC from at least 4 kilometres away.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
The lighting required by subregulation (1) may be inside the balloon, on its outside, or on the ground.
A person may operate a tethered balloon only if it is fitted with a device that will cause it to deflate rapidly and completely if it escapes from its mooring.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: What to do if tethered balloon escapes

content.p: If a tethered balloon escapes from its mooring, and the deflation device does not cause it to deflate, the person operating it must tell Airservices Australia as soon as possible:
where the balloon was launched; and
what time it broke free; and
the direction it was headed when last seen.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subpart 101.E—Unmanned free balloons
This Subpart applies to the operation of an unmanned free balloon.
There are 4 kinds of unmanned free balloon. These are defined (in order of ascending size) in the following 4 subregulations.
(2) A small balloon is an unmanned free balloon that:
has a diameter of 2 metres or less at launch; and
either:
is not carrying a payload; or
is carrying a payload with a combined mass of 50 g or less.
(3) A light balloon is an unmanned free balloon that:
carries a payload to which all of the following apply:
the payload does not include a heavy package;
the payload has a combined mass of more than 50 g but less than 4 kg;
if a rope or other device has been used for the suspension of the payload—an impact force of less than 230 N is required to separate the suspended payload from the balloon; or
has a diameter of greater than 2 metres at launch and either:
is not carrying a payload; or
is carrying a payload with a combined mass of 50 g or less.
(4) A medium balloon is an unmanned free balloon that carries a payload to which all of the following apply:
the payload includes at least 2 packages but no heavy packages;
the payload has a combined mass of at least 4 kg but less than 6 kg;
if a rope or other device has been used for the suspension of the payload—an impact force of less than 230 N is required to separate the suspended payload from the balloon.
(5) A heavy balloon is an unmanned free balloon that carries a payload to which any of the following apply:
the payload includes a heavy package;
the combined mass of the payload is at least 6 kg;
if a rope or other device has been used for the suspension of the payload—an impact force of 230 N or more is required to separate the suspended payload from the balloon.
(6) A heavy package means a package that:
weighs at least 3 kg; or
(b) weighs at least 2 kg and has an area density of more than 13 g per cm2.
For paragraph (6)(b), the area density of a package is worked out by dividing the total mass in grams of the package by the area in square centimetres of its smallest surface.
In this Subpart:
approved area means an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation or release of unmanned free balloons.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(7).
A person may release a small balloon only if the person has first complied with any requirements as to approval or notice set out in table 101.155-1.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if no more than 100 balloons are to be released at once.

a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
Note 2: CASA will tell the NOTAM Office about the release.

section.heading: Light balloons that may be released outside approved areas

content.p: A person may release a light balloon outside an approved area only if the person gives to CASA the information required by table 101.160 at least 1 working day before the proposed release.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note 1: A person can comply with this requirement by telling:
if the person is an approved aviation administration organisation—the Australian NOTAM Office; or
the appropriate approved aviation administration organisation.
See regulation 101.035.
Note 2: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
If more than 1 balloon is to be released at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such balloon.

tr.td: The name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will release the balloon (or, if several people will be involved, the name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will coordinate the release)
The date and time the release is to begin

The estimated size and mass of the balloon’s payload

content.p: Subregulation (1) does not require the Bureau of Meteorology to give notice of the proposed release of a light balloon if:
the release is part of the Bureau’s normal meteorological procedures; and
the release location has been notified in AIP or NOTAM.

section.heading: Release of medium and heavy balloons outside approved areas

content.p: Subject to subregulation (3), a person may release a medium or heavy balloon outside an approved area only if the person gives to CASA the information required by table 101.165 at least 2 working days before the proposed release.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note 1: A person can comply with this requirement by telling:
if the person is an approved aviation administration organisation—the Australian NOTAM Office; or
the appropriate approved aviation administration organisation.
See regulation 101.035.
Note 2: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
If more than 1 balloon is to be operated at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such balloon.
