content.p: Subregulation (1) does not require the Bureau of Meteorology to give notice of the proposed release of a medium balloon if:
the release is part of the Bureau’s normal meteorological procedures; and
the release location has been notified in AIP or NOTAM.

Subject to subregulation (5), the person must also confirm the details of the proposed release to the air traffic control service that has responsibility for the airspace within which the balloon will be released no later than the earlier of:
6 hours before the expected release time; or
the time the balloon begins to be inflated.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subregulation (4) does not require the Bureau of Meteorology to confirm the details of the release of a medium balloon with an air traffic control service if:
the release is part of the Bureau’s normal meteorological procedures; and
the release location has been notified in AIP or NOTAM.

section.heading: Medium and heavy balloons not to be flown low

content.p: A person who is operating a medium or heavy balloon must not allow it to go below 3 000 feet AGL while it is over a populous area.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Medium and heavy balloons to be flown in clear sky

content.p: Subject to subregulations (3) and (4), a person must not operate a medium or heavy balloon below 60 000 feet pressure altitude if, at the altitude at which the balloon is being operated, the horizontal visibility is less than 8 kilometres.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

Subject to subregulations (3) and (4), a person who is operating a medium or heavy balloon must not allow it to remain at an altitude below 60 000 feet pressure altitude at which cloud, fog or mist obscures more than half the sky.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subregulations (1) and (2) do not apply to operation outside controlled airspace if CASA approves the operation and the operation is carried out in accordance with the approval.
Those subregulations also do not apply to operation in controlled airspace in accordance with an air traffic control clearance.

section.heading: How payload must be supported—medium and heavy balloons

content.p: A person may operate a medium or heavy balloon only if the means by which the payload is attached to the balloon can support at least 10 times the mass of the payload.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Equipment that must be carried—medium and heavy balloons

content.p: A person may operate a medium or heavy balloon only if:
the balloon is fitted with at least 2 independent ways (either automatic or remotely-operated) of releasing its payload; and
if the balloon is not a zero-pressure balloon, it has at least 2 independent ways of ending the flight of the balloon envelope; and
either:
the balloon envelope carries a radar reflector, or radar-reflective material, that will return an echo to a surface radar operating in the frequency range 200 megahertz to 2 700 megahertz; or
the balloon is fitted with a device to allow it to be continuously tracked by the operator beyond the range of ground-based radar; and

if the balloon is operated in an area in which ground-based secondary surveillance radar is in use, it is fitted with an SSR transponder (with altitude-reporting capability) that either operates continuously or can be turned on by the operator if an air traffic control service so requires.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

A person may operate a medium or heavy balloon below 60 000 feet pressure altitude at night only if both the balloon and its payload are lit (whether or not they become separated during the operation) so as to be visible, under the prevailing conditions, for at least 4 kilometres in all directions.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), a balloon is being operated at night if the sun is below the balloon’s horizon.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

A person may operate an unmanned free balloon that carries a trailing antenna that requires a force of more than 230 newtons to break it only if the antenna has coloured streamers or pennants attached to it every 15 metres.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
A person may operate an unmanned free balloon that carries a payload only if the payload has fixed to it a durable identification plate carrying sufficient information:
to identify the payload; and
to enable somebody who finds the payload to contact the person who released the balloon.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Subregulation (2) does not apply to a light or medium balloon operated by the Bureau of Meteorology.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate a heavy balloon (being a heavy balloon that has its payload suspended more than 15 metres below the envelope) above 60 000 feet pressure altitude by day only if:
the payload’s suspension is coloured in alternate bands of conspicuous colours, or has coloured pennants attached to it; or
the balloon has a conspicuous payload-recovery parachute suspended under the envelope, or the balloon is suspended beneath a conspicuous open parachute.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), a balloon is being operated by day if the sun is above the balloon’s horizon.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate a heavy balloon above 60 000 feet pressure altitude at night only if it is lit so as to be visible in VMC from at least 4 kilometres away.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), a balloon is being operated at night if the sun is below the balloon’s horizon.
The lighting required by subregulation (1) may be inside the balloon, on its outside, or on the ground.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Obligation to stay in communication with ATC—medium and heavy balloons

content.p: The operator of a medium or heavy balloon must establish and maintain communication with the relevant air traffic control service from the time the balloon begins to be inflated until the flight ends.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
The operator must tell the relevant air traffic control service at least 1 hour before the balloon is launched.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Tracking of flight—medium and heavy balloons

content.p: The operator of a medium or heavy balloon must track its flight continuously.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
While the balloon is below 60 000 feet pressure altitude, if it cannot be tracked visually from the ground or by radar, the operator must ensure that a tracking aircraft accompanies it continuously.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
The operator of a medium or heavy balloon must report the progress of the balloon’s flight to the relevant air traffic control service as follows:
the operator must tell the service immediately when the balloon is released;
the operator must tell the service when the balloon leaves each 10 000-foot level up to 60 000 feet (pressure altitude);
the operator must report the balloon’s position to the relevant air traffic control service periodically, as follows:
when required to do so by the service;
while the balloon is below 60 000 feet pressure altitude—every 10 minutes;
while the balloon is at or above 60 000 feet pressure altitude—every 2 hours;
if the operator loses the balloon’s position, the operator must tell the service immediately that tracking has been lost and the balloon’s last known position;
after having re-established tracking of the balloon, the operator must tell the service immediately that tracking has been re-established and the balloon’s position at that time.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

If the balloon is being accompanied by a tracking aircraft, the operator must ensure that the crew of the aircraft maintains continuous 2-way communication with the relevant air traffic control service.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

A reference in this regulation to the relevant air traffic control service is to be read, at a particular time, as a reference to the air traffic control service that is responsible for the airspace in which the balloon is located at the time.

section.heading: Ending flight and recovery—medium and heavy balloons

content.p: The operator of a medium or heavy balloon must give to the relevant air traffic control service at least 1 hour’s notice of the time the flight is planned to end, and when doing so must also give to the air traffic control service the following information:
the balloon’s current position and altitude;
the estimated time at which, and the estimated location over which, the balloon will pass through 60 000 feet pressure altitude during its descent;
the estimated time when, and place where, the payload will fall.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The operator may command the balloon to end its flight only:
in an emergency; or
if cleared to do so by the relevant air traffic control service.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

If the operator commands the balloon to end its flight when not cleared by air traffic control to do so, the operator must tell the relevant air traffic control service immediately, and when doing so must also give to it the following information:
the balloon’s current position and altitude;
the estimated time when and place where the payload will fall.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The operator must tell the relevant air traffic control service as soon as possible after the balloon’s payload falls.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1), (2), (3) or (4) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

A reference in this regulation to the relevant air traffic control service is to be read, at a particular time, as a reference to the air traffic control service that is responsible for the airspace in which the balloon is located at the time.

section.heading: Direction by ATC to end flight in certain circumstances

content.p: If a balloon is in controlled airspace and an air traffic control service considers that it poses a hazard to other aircraft, or to people or property on the ground, that service may direct the balloon’s operator to end the balloon’s flight immediately.
The operator must comply with the direction by ending the balloon’s flight by the fastest possible method.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subpart 101.F—Remotely piloted aircraft
This Subpart applies to the operation of the following:
very small RPA;
small RPA;
medium RPA;
large RPA.
Note 1: This Subpart does not apply to model aircraft, as they are not RPA—see the definitions of RPA in regulation 101.021 and model aircraft in regulation 101.023.
Note 2: This Subpart also does not apply to micro RPA—see the definition of micro RPA in regulation 101.022.
In this Subpart:
approved area means an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of RPA.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAMS or on an aeronautical chart: see subregulation 101.030(7).
(1) This regulation sets out what is an excluded RPA.
Note: A remote pilot licence is not required to operate an excluded RPA. An accreditation is sufficient—see regulation 101.252 and Subpart 101.FA.
(3) A very small RPA is an excluded RPA if it is being operated in standard RPA operating conditions.
(4) A small RPA is an excluded RPA if it is being operated:
by or on behalf of the owner of the RPA; and
over land owned or occupied by the owner of the RPA; and
in standard RPA operating conditions; and
for the purposes of one or more of the following:
aerial spotting;
aerial photography;
agricultural operations;
aerial communications retransmission;
the carriage of cargo;
any other activity that is similar to an activity mentioned in the subparagraphs above; and
for which no remuneration is received by the operator or the owner of the RPA, the owner or occupier of the land or any person on whose behalf the activity is being conducted.
(6) A small RPA is an excluded RPA if it is being operated in standard RPA operating conditions by:
a person for the sole purpose of meeting the experience requirement mentioned in paragraph 101.295(2)(c) for the grant of a remote pilot licence; or
the holder of a remote pilot licence for the sole purpose of getting practical experience and gaining competency in the operation of an RPA of a category that is specified in the licence.

Note: For paragraph (b), for example, if a remote pilot licence states that the holder is authorised to operate a small RPA with a gross weight of not more than 7 kg that is an aeroplane, a small RPA with a gross weight of 10 kg that is an aeroplane may be an excluded RPA when operated by that holder. However, a small RPA (of any weight) that is a helicopter cannot be an excluded RPA when operated by that holder, because an aeroplane is not of the same category of RPA as a helicopter (see the definition of category in Part 1 of the Dictionary).
(7) A medium RPA is an excluded RPA if it is being operated:
by or on behalf of the owner of the RPA; and
by a person who holds a remote pilot licence that authorises the person to operate the RPA; and
over land owned or occupied by the owner of the RPA; and
in standard RPA operating conditions; and
for the purposes of one or more of the following:
aerial spotting;
aerial photography;
agricultural operations;
aerial communications retransmission;
the carriage of cargo;
any other activity that is similar to an activity mentioned in the subparagraphs above; and
for which no remuneration is received by the operator or owner of the RPA, the owner or occupier of the land or any person on whose behalf the activity is being conducted.
(8) An RPA is an excluded RPA if it is being operated:

by a person solely for the purpose of the person receiving training from an RPA operator who holds a certificate under Division 101.F.4 that authorises the operator to conduct operations using the RPA; and
in accordance with the operator’s documented training procedures.

section.heading: Meaning of standard RPA operating conditions

content.p: An RPA is operated in standard RPA operating conditions if, at all times during the operation:
the RPA is operated in Australian territory; and
the RPA is operated within the visual line of sight of the person operating the RPA; and
the RPA is operated at or below 400 ft AGL by day; and
the RPA is not operated within 30 m of a person who is not directly associated with the operation of the RPA; and
the RPA is not operated:
in a prohibited area; or
in a restricted area that is classified as RA3; or
in a restricted area that is classified as RA2 or RA1 otherwise than in accordance with regulation 101.065; or
over a populous area; or
within 3 nautical miles of the movement area of a controlled aerodrome; and
the RPA is not operated over an area where a fire, police or other public safety or emergency operation is being conducted without the approval of a person in charge of the operation; and
the person operating the RPA operates only that RPA.
(1) Subject to subregulations (2) and (3), a person must not operate an RPA within 30 metres of a person (the second person) who is not directly associated with the operation of the RPA.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the second person is standing behind the RPA while the RPA is taking off.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the RPA is a very small RPA, small RPA or medium RPA; and
the second person has consented to the RPA operating within 30 m of him or her; and
the RPA is operated no closer than 15 m of him or her.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the RPA is an airship; and
the airship approaches no closer to the second person than 10 m horizontally and 30 ft vertically.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person holds an approval under regulation 101.029 for the purposes of this subregulation.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2) to (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Where very small, small and medium RPA may be operated

content.p: A person may operate a very small RPA, a small RPA or a medium RPA outside an approved area only if:
where the RPA is operated above 400 feet AGL, the operator has CASA’s approval to do so; and
the RPA stays clear of populous areas.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note 2: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
Note 3: This Subpart only applies to the operation of certain RPA: see regulation 101.235.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Certain RPA—requirement for remote pilot licence

content.p: This regulation does not apply in relation to the operation of an excluded RPA.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates an RPA; and
the person does not hold a remote pilot licence that authorises the person to operate the RPA.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
(3) A person (the offender) commits an offence of strict liability if:
the offender operates an RPA; and
one of the following persons demands the offender to produce, for inspection by the person, a remote pilot licence that authorises the offender to operate the RPA:
an authorised person;
a member or special member of the Australian Federal Police;
a member of a police force or a police service of a State or Territory; and
the offender fails to comply with the demand.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
Subregulation 302(1) of CAR does not apply in relation to a remote pilot licence.
A person may operate a large RPA only if either a special certificate of airworthiness (restricted category), or an experimental certificate, has been issued for it under Subpart 21.H of Part 21.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: For large RPA, see regulation 101.022.
Note 2: A large RPA is required to carry a manufacturer’s data plate and an aircraft registration identification plate—see respectively regulation 21.820 and Subpart 45.D of Part 45.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subdivision 2 of Division 2 of Part 4A of CAR applies to large RPA.
Note: That is, a large RPA must be maintained as a Class B aircraft.

A person who carries out maintenance on a large RPA must comply with any directions given in writing by CASA in relation to the maintenance of the RPA, or the maintenance of RPA of a class that includes the RPA.

section.heading: Large RPA—persons permitted to carry out maintenance

content.p: For subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, and despite anything in regulation 42ZC of CAR 1988, a person may carry out maintenance on:
a large RPA that is an Australian aircraft; or
an aircraft component for such an RPA; or
aircraft material for such an RPA;
if the person:
holds an airworthiness authority that authorises the maintenance; or
carries out the maintenance under the supervision of a person who holds such an authority.

section.heading: Certain RPA—requirement for RPA operator’s certificate

content.p: This regulation does not apply in relation to the operation of an excluded RPA.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person conducts operations using RPA; and
the person does not hold a certificate as an RPA operator under Division 101.F.4 that authorises the person to conduct the operations.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Certain RPA—requirement to keep records or give information to CASA

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may require a person who operates, or proposes to operate, RPA to do either or both of the following:
keep records, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards;
give information to CASA, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Approval of operation of large RPA

content.p: A person may operate a large RPA only with CASA’s approval.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for approval to operate a large RPA.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant the approval if:
the person is certified as an operator of large RPA; and
the operation would not contravene any condition of the certification.
Note 1: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
Note 2: For certification as an operator of RPA, see Division 101.F.4.
Without limiting regulations 11.056 and 11.067, CASA may impose conditions on an approval:
prohibiting the operation of the relevant RPA at night or in conditions other than VMC; or
restricting the extent to which the RPA may be operated at night or in conditions other than VMC; or
requiring the RPA to stay within a specified area, or
requiring the operator to make specified broadcasts.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: RPA not to be operated over populous areas

content.p: In this regulation:
certificated RPA means an RPA for which a certificate of airworthiness has been issued.
A person must not operate an RPA that is not a certificated RPA over a populous area at a height less than the height from which, if any of its components fails, it would be able to clear the area.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note 1: For populous area, see regulation 101.025. For RPA, see regulation 101.022.
Note 2: For the kinds of RPA operation to which this Subpart applies, see regulation 101.235.

Without the approval of CASA, a person must not operate a certificated RPA over a populous area at a height less than the height from which, if any of its components fails, it would be able to clear the area.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (2) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
In considering whether to give an approval under subregulation (3), CASA must take into account:
the degree of redundancy in the RPA’s critical systems; and
any fail-safe design characteristics of the RPA; and
the security of its communications and navigation systems.

Before giving an approval under subregulation (3), CASA must be satisfied that the person who intends to operate the RPA will take proper precautions to prevent the proposed flight being dangerous to people and property.
A person may operate an RPA (other than a very small RPA) in controlled airspace only if he or she:
holds a relevant qualification; and
maintains a listening watch on a specified frequency or frequencies; and
makes broadcasts on a specified frequency or frequencies at the specified interval giving the specified information.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: This Subpart only applies to the operation of certain RPA: see regulation 101.235.
In this regulation:
relevant qualification means any of the following qualifications:
an aeronautical radio operator certificate;
a flight crew licence;
an ATC licence;
a military qualification equivalent to a licence mentioned in paragraph (b) or (c);
a flight service licence.
specified frequency for particular airspace means a frequency specified from time to time in AIP or by ATC as a frequency for use in the airspace.
specified information for particular airspace means information specified from time to time in AIP or by ATC as information that must be broadcast in the airspace.
specified interval for particular airspace means the interval specified from time to time in AIP or by ATC as the interval at which broadcasts must be made while in that airspace.
CASA may direct that a particular person must not operate an RPA unless the person:
holds a relevant qualification; and
maintains a listening watch on a frequency or frequencies specified in the direction; and
makes broadcasts:
on a frequency or frequencies; and
at intervals; and
giving information—
specified in the direction.
The person must comply with the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
CASA may direct, in regard to a particular RPA or type of RPA, that a person must not operate the RPA, or an RPA of that type, unless he or she:
holds a relevant qualification; and
maintains a listening watch on a frequency or frequencies specified in the direction; and
makes broadcasts:
on a frequency or frequencies; and
at intervals; and
giving information—
specified in the direction.
The person must comply with the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

For subregulations (3) and (5), CASA may specify that a frequency is to be a frequency prescribed by the Part 91 Manual of Standards for the purposes of subregulation 91.255(1) or paragraph 91.630(1)(b).
An offence against subregulation (1), (4) or (6) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for a remote pilot licence.
(1A) An individual may apply to CASA, in writing, for a licence (a remote pilot licence) to operate an RPA.
Note: For the kinds of RPA to which this Subpart applies, see regulation 101.235.
An application for a remote pilot licence must include the following information:
details of any flight crew licence, ATC licence or flight service licence that the applicant holds (including details of ratings, endorsements and qualifications);
details of any military qualification the applicant holds that is equivalent to a licence mentioned in paragraph (a);
details of any aeronautical experience that the applicant has;
details of any of the following examinations the applicant has passed (other than any examination passed in the course of gaining a licence mentioned in paragraph (a)):
an aeronautical examination (within the meaning of Part 61);
an aviation licence theory examination before 1 September 2014 that is taken to be an equivalent requirement for the grant of a flight crew licence under regulation 202.274;
if the applicant does not hold a licence mentioned in paragraph (a), details of any aeronautical radio operator certificate that the applicant holds;
details of the applicant’s experience in operating RPA;
evidence of the completion of any training course in RPA operation that the applicant has undertaken.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant a remote pilot licence to the applicant if he or she:
has passed:
an aeronautical knowledge examination (within the meaning of Part 61) for a flight crew licence under Part 61; or
an aviation licence theory examination before 1 September 2014 that is taken to be an equivalent requirement for the grant of a flight crew licence under regulation 202.274; or
the theory component of an RPL training course; or
the theory component of a course conducted in a foreign country which CASA is satisfied is equivalent to the theory component of an RPL training course; and
has completed:
an RPL training course in the manual or automated operation of a category of RPA that he or she proposes to operate; or
before 1 June 2017, a training course in the operation of a category of RPA that he or she proposes to operate, conducted by the RPA’s manufacturer or an agent of the manufacturer; or
a flight test conducted by CASA for the purposes of this subparagraph; and
has at least 5 hours experience in operating an RPA under standard RPA operating conditions.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to grant, or cancelling, suspending or varying, a licence; or
a decision imposing a condition on a licence.
See also section 31 of the Act.
A person who holds or has held:
a flight crew licence; or
a military qualification equivalent to a flight crew licence; or
an ATC licence, or a military qualification equivalent to an ATC licence;
is taken to satisfy the condition in paragraph (2)(a).
Without limiting regulations 11.056 and 11.067, a condition may:
allow the person to operate RPA of only specified kinds; or
limit the areas where he or she may operate RPA; or
allow him or her to operate RPA only in VMC.

It is a condition of a remote pilot licence that the licence holder must not operate an RPA above 400 ft AGL in controlled airspace, or within 3 nautical miles of the movement area of a controlled aerodrome, unless he or she holds at least one of the following qualifications:
an aeronautical radio operator certificate;
a flight crew licence;
an ATC licence;
a military qualification equivalent to a licence mentioned in paragraph (b) or (c);
a flight service licence.
It is a condition of a remote pilot licence that an RPA must be operated within the visual line of sight of the licence holder unless he or she:
has passed:
an aeronautical knowledge examination (within the meaning of Part 61) for the grant of an instrument rating under Part 61; or
an aviation licence theory examination before 1 September 2014 that is taken to be an equivalent requirement for the grant of an instrument rating under regulation 202.274; or
an approved examination; and
either:
holds both a certificate as an RPA operator under Division 101.F.4 and an approval under regulation 101.029 to operate the RPA beyond the person’s visual line of sight; or

is a member of an RPA operator’s personnel and the RPA operator holds both a certificate as an RPA operator under Division 101.F.4 and an approval under regulation 101.029 for the operator’s personnel to operate RPA beyond their visual line of sight.
It is a condition of a remote pilot licence that the licence holder must not operate more than 1 RPA at a time unless:
he or she holds an approval under regulation 101.029 to operate more than 1 RPA at a time; and
the conditions (if any) imposed on the approval are complied with.
The holder of a remote pilot licence commits an offence of strict liability if the holder contravenes a condition mentioned in subregulation (3), (4) or (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Notice to holder of remote pilot licence to show cause

content.p: Show cause notice—variation, cancellation or suspension

CASA may give a show cause notice to the holder of a remote pilot licence if there are reasonable grounds for believing that there are facts or circumstances that would justify the variation, suspension or cancellation of the licence under regulation 101.320.
A show cause notice must:
tell the holder of the licence of the facts and circumstances that, in CASA’s opinion, would justify the variation, suspension or cancellation of the licence under regulation 101.320; and
invite the holder of the licence to show in writing, within a reasonable time stated in the notice, why the licence should not be varied, suspended or cancelled.
Immediate suspension if serious risk to the safety of air navigation
The remote pilot licence is suspended from the time the show cause notice is given to the holder, if:
CASA reasonably considers that there may be a serious risk to the safety of air navigation if the licence were not suspended; and
the show cause notice states that the licence is suspended for that reason.
CASA may at any time revoke the suspension.
If the licence is suspended under subregulation (3):
the holder is taken not to be the holder of a remote pilot licence during the period of suspension; and
the licence is not in force while suspended; and

if CASA has not dealt with the suspension under regulation 101.320 within 90 days after the day the licence is suspended, the suspension lapses at the end of that period (if it is not earlier revoked under subregulation (5) of this regulation or subregulation 101.320(2)).
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.

section.heading: Variation, suspension or cancellation of remote pilot licence

content.p: CASA may vary, suspend or cancel a remote pilot licence by written notice to the holder of the licence, if:
CASA has given to the holder a show cause notice under regulation 101.315 in relation to it; and
CASA has taken into account any representations made, within the period stated in the notice, by or on behalf of the holder; and
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the holder:
has operated an RPA in contravention of these Regulations, an instrument under these Regulations or a condition of the licence; or
has operated an RPA negligently or carelessly; or
in operating an RPA, has recklessly endangered human life or property; or
at the time of the grant of the licence did not meet, or now no longer meets, the criteria for eligibility under regulation 11.055 as they applied at the time of the grant.
Note: For subparagraph (iv), in determining whether the criteria for eligibility were or are met, CASA may take into account the matters mentioned in subregulation 11.055(4).
Notice of decision
If CASA has given a show cause notice under regulation 101.315 to the holder of a remote pilot licence:

in the event that CASA decides to vary, suspend or cancel the licence—CASA must give the holder notice of the decision, including (in the case of a decision to suspend the licence) notice of the period of suspension; and
in the event that CASA decides not to vary, suspend or cancel the licence—CASA must, in writing:
give the holder notice accordingly; and
if the licence was suspended under subregulation 101.315(3)—revoke the suspension.
Effect of suspension
If a remote pilot licence is suspended under this regulation:
the holder is taken not to be the holder of a remote pilot licence during the period of suspension; and
the licence is not in force during the period of suspension stated in the notice under paragraph (2)(a).
Note 1: CASA may also impose a condition on the licence, or vary an existing condition of the licence—see regulation 11.067.
Note 2: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for certification as an RPA operator.

section.heading: Application for certification as RPA operator

content.p: A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for certification as an RPA operator.
Note: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
An application for certification as an RPA operator must include:
details of:
the applicant’s structure and organisation; and

its staff and their qualifications and experience (including, in particular, the names, qualifications, experience, duties and functions of the persons who are to be the applicant’s chief remote pilot and maintenance controller); and
its facilities and equipment; and
its practices and procedures; and
a general description of the proposed operations, including the type or types of RPA to be used; and
if the applicant proposes to conduct an RPL training course—details of the proposed training.
The application must be accompanied by a copy of each of the applicant’s manuals relevant to the operation of RPA.

section.heading: Eligibility for certification as RPA operator

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must certify an applicant as an RPA operator if the applicant is eligible to be certified as an RPA operator in accordance with this regulation.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to grant, or cancelling, suspending or varying, a certificate; or
a decision imposing a condition on a certificate.
See also section 31 of the Act.
A person is eligible to be certified as an RPA operator if:
the person has an organisation and structure that is appropriate for safe operation of RPA; and
the person has enough qualified and experienced personnel to undertake the proposed operations safely; and
the person has facilities and equipment appropriate to carry out the proposed operations using RPA of the type to be used; and
the person has suitable documented practices and procedures to do so, including practices and procedures for the maintenance of the operator’s RPASs; and
the person has nominated suitable persons to be its chief remote pilot and maintenance controller.
A body that is not a legal person is not eligible to be certified as an RPA operator.
Two or more persons cannot be certified jointly as an RPA operator.
It is a condition of the certification of a person as an RPA operator that the person:
maintains within its organisation a position of chief remote pilot having at least the functions and duties set out in regulation 101.342; and
employs as its chief remote pilot a person who holds a remote pilot licence under Division 101.F.3 and who is competent to carry out those duties and perform those functions; and
either:
maintains a position within its organisation of maintenance controller, with the functions and duties set out in an advisory circular issued by CASA from time to time; or
has an arrangement with another qualified and competent person to carry out those functions and duties; and

if it maintains within its organisation a position of maintenance controller—employs as its maintenance controller a person who is competent to carry out the duties and perform the functions of a maintenance controller; and
complies with the operator’s documented practices and procedures.
Without limiting regulations 11.056 and 11.067, a condition may:
allow the person to operate RPA of only specified kinds; or
allow the person to operate RPA only for specified purposes; or
limit the areas where the person may operate RPA; or
allow the person to operate RPA only in VMC; or
limit the number of RPA that an RPA operator may operate.

section.heading: Functions and duties of chief remote pilot

content.p: For paragraph 101.340(1)(a), the functions and duties of a chief remote pilot are as follows:
ensuring the operator’s RPA operations are conducted in accordance with the civil aviation legislation;
maintaining a record of the qualifications held by each person operating RPA for the operator;
monitoring the operational standards and proficiency of each person operating RPA for the operator;
maintaining a complete and up-to-date reference library of operational documents required by CASA under subregulation 101.335(1) for the types of operations conducted by the operator.

section.heading: Notice to certified RPA operator to show cause

content.p: Show cause notice—variation, cancellation or suspension

CASA may give a show cause notice to a certified RPA operator if there are reasonable grounds for believing that there are facts or circumstances that would justify the variation, suspension or cancellation of the certification under regulation 101.365.
A show cause notice must:
tell the operator of the facts and circumstances that, in CASA’s opinion, would justify the variation, suspension or cancellation of the certification under regulation 101.365; and
invite the operator to show in writing, within a reasonable time stated in the notice, why the certification should not be varied, suspended or cancelled.
Immediate suspension if serious risk to the safety of air navigation
The certification is suspended from the time the show cause notice is given to the operator, if:
CASA reasonably considers that there may be a serious risk to the safety of air navigation if the certification were not suspended; and
the show cause notice states that the certification is suspended for that reason.
CASA may at any time revoke the suspension.
If the certification of a person as an RPA operator is suspended under subregulation (3):
the operator is taken not to be a certified RPA operator during the period of suspension; and
the certification is not in force while suspended; and

if CASA has not dealt with the suspension under regulation 101.365 within 90 days after the day the certification is suspended, the suspension lapses at the end of that period (if it is not earlier revoked under subregulation (5) of this regulation or subregulation 101.365(2)).
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.

section.heading: Variation, suspension or cancellation of RPA operator’s certification

content.p: CASA may vary, suspend or cancel a certified RPA operator’s certification by written notice to the operator, if:
CASA has given to the operator a show cause notice under regulation 101.360 in relation to it; and
CASA has taken into account any representations made, within the period stated in the notice, by or on behalf of the operator; and
there are reasonable grounds for believing that:
the operator has operated an RPA in contravention of these Regulations, an instrument under these Regulations or a condition of the certification; or
a person engaged or employed by the operator has operated an RPA negligently or carelessly; or
a person engaged or employed by the operator, in operating an RPA, has recklessly endangered human life or property; or
at the time the operator was certified the operator did not meet, or now no longer meets, the criteria for eligibility under regulation 11.055 as they applied at the time of certification.
Note: For subparagraph (iv), in determining whether the criteria for eligibility were or are met, CASA may take into account the matters mentioned in subregulation 11.055(4).
Notice of decision
If CASA has given a show cause notice under regulation 101.360 to a certified RPA operator:

in the event that CASA decides to vary, suspend or cancel the certification—CASA must give the operator notice of the decision, including (in the case of a decision to suspend the certification) notice of the period of suspension; and
in the event that CASA decides not to vary, suspend or cancel the certification—CASA must, in writing:
give the operator notice accordingly; and
if the certification was suspended under subregulation 101.360(3)—revoke the suspension.
Effect of suspension
If the certification of a person as an RPA operator is suspended under this regulation:
the operator is taken not to be a certified RPA operator during the period of suspension; and
the certification is not in force during the period of suspension stated in the notice under paragraph (2)(a).
Note 1: CASA may also impose a condition on the certification, or vary an existing condition of the certification—see regulation 11.067.
Note 2: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.

section.heading: Compliance with RPA operator’s practices and procedures

content.p: A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person:
is a member of an RPA operator’s personnel; and
is subject to a requirement under the RPA operator’s documented practices and procedures; and
does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

division.heading: Operation of certain RPA for hire or reward

content.p: This Division applies in relation to the first operation of a very small RPA, a small RPA or a medium RPA while the RPA is an excluded RPA under any of the following provisions:
subregulation 101.237(3) (a very small RPA being operated in standard RPA operating conditions);
subregulation 101.237(4) (a small RPA being operated in certain circumstances);
subregulation 101.237(7) (a medium RPA being operated in certain circumstances).

(2) The first operation of an RPA while it is an excluded RPA under a provision mentioned in subregulation (1) is its first operation, while it is such an excluded RPA, in each period during which it is registered under Subpart 47.C.

Before the first operation of an RPA to which this Division applies (whether by the registration holder for the RPA or another person), the registration holder must notify CASA of the operation, in writing, in a form and manner approved by CASA.
A registration holder for an RPA commits an offence of strict liability if:
the registration holder is subject to the requirement under subregulation (1) in relation to the RPA; and
the registration holder fails to comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulations (1) and (2) do not apply if the registration holder, or another person, is certified under Division 101.F.4 to conduct the operation.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subregulation—see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Notification of changes in relation to operating very small RPA for hire or reward etc.

content.p: If:
a person has given CASA a notice under regulation 101.372; and
a change, event or other matter of a kind prescribed by the Part 101 Manual of Standards occurs;
the person must notify CASA of the change, event or matter within 21 business days of the change, event or matter occurring.
The notification must be given in the form, and in the manner or way, approved by CASA.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
CASA may establish and maintain a database of information that relates to notifications given under regulations 101.372 and 101.373.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the database may contain the following information in relation to each notification:
the name of the person who gave the notification;
the person’s contact details;
the locations at which the operations will take place;
the types of RPA covered by the notification.
The database may be made publicly available.
The database may be kept and made publicly available in electronic form.
Subpart 101.FA—Excluded RPA and micro RPA accreditation
This Subpart applies to the operation of excluded RPA and micro RPA.
Note 1: See the definition of excluded RPA in regulation 101.237.
Note 2: This Subpart does not apply to model aircraft, as they are not RPA—see the definitions of RPA in regulation 101.021 and model aircraft in regulation 101.023.

section.heading: Excluded RPA and micro RPA—requirement for accreditation or remote pilot licence

content.p: Excluded RPA and micro RPA
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person operates an excluded RPA or a micro RPA; and
the person holds neither of the following:
an accreditation authorising the person to operate excluded RPA and micro RPA;
a remote pilot licence.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
General exception—excluded RPA operated by child under adult supervision
(4) Subregulation (1) does not apply to a person under 16 years old (the child) operating an excluded RPA or a micro RPA if:
(a) when the aircraft is being operated, the child is being supervised by another person (the supervisor); and
the supervisor is at least 18 years old; and
the supervisor holds:
an accreditation authorising the supervisor to operate excluded RPA and micro RPA; or
a remote pilot licence.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in this subregulation—see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Excluded RPA and micro RPA—requirement to produce accreditation or remote pilot licence

content.p: General requirement

A person who operates an excluded RPA or micro RPA must produce an accreditation or licence covered by subregulation (2) that authorises the person to do so, or a copy of such an accreditation or licence, for inspection on a demand made by a person covered by subregulation (3).
Accreditations and licences covered
The following accreditations and licences are covered by this subregulation:
an accreditation authorising the operation of excluded RPA and micro RPA;
a remote pilot licence.
Persons who may demand production of accreditations and licences
The following persons are covered by this subregulation:
an authorised person;
a member or special member of the Australian Federal Police;
a member of a police force or a police service of a State or Territory.
Offence for failing to comply with demand
(4) A person (the offender) commits an offence of strict liability if:
the offender operates an excluded RPA or micro RPA; and
a person makes a demand of the offender under subregulation (1); and
the offender fails to comply with the demand.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
Operation permissible without an accreditation or licence
Subregulations (1) to (4) do not apply to a person operating an excluded RPA or micro RPA if:
such operation by the person without an accreditation or licence covered by subregulation (2) of this regulation does not constitute an offence under regulation 101.374B; or
subregulation (4) applies in relation to such operation.
Supervised operations

A person who supervises the operation by another person of an excluded RPA or micro RPA must produce an accreditation or licence covered by subregulation (2) for that RPA, or a copy of such accreditation or licence, for inspection on a demand made by a person covered by subregulation (3).
(7) A person (the supervisor) commits an offence of strict liability if:
the supervisor supervises the operation by another person of an excluded RPA or micro RPA; and
the other person is under 16 years old; and
a person makes a demand of the supervisor under subregulation (6); and
the supervisor fails to comply with the demand.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.

division.heading: Grant of accreditation to operate excluded RPA and micro RPA

content.p: Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for accreditation under this Division.
An individual may apply to CASA, in writing, for accreditation authorising the holder to operate excluded RPA and micro RPA.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must give an applicant under regulation 101.374D the accreditation applied for if the applicant is eligible for that accreditation under this regulation.
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal. See also section 31 of the Act.
The applicant is eligible for the accreditation mentioned in regulation 101.374D if the applicant:
is at least 16 years old; and
has completed an online training course provided by CASA for that accreditation, to the standard required by CASA, in accordance with any conditions for completing the course required by CASA; and

has achieved a standard required by CASA in an examination (including an online examination) for that accreditation, administered by CASA, in accordance with any conditions for undertaking that examination required by CASA.
However, the applicant is not eligible for the accreditation:
if an accreditation formerly held by the applicant has been cancelled within the 12 months before the date of the application; or
while an accreditation currently held by the applicant is suspended under regulation 101.374H or 101.374J.
An applicant may undertake a course or an examination mentioned in subsection (2) only if the applicant is at least 16 years old at that time.
Two or more persons cannot jointly hold the accreditation.
The accreditation authorises the holder to operate excluded RPA and micro RPA as stated in the accreditation.
Note: Any conditions imposed on the accreditation under regulation 11.056 must also be set out in, or attached to, the accreditation.

section.heading: Accreditation—conduct of online courses and examinations

content.p: The Part 101 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements in relation to the following:
the completion of an online training course under paragraph 101.374E(2)(b) (including conditions relating to cheating in such a course);
the conduct of an online examination under paragraph 101.374E(2)(c) (including conditions relating to cheating in such an examination);
the disclosure and use of information or documents which form part of, or are related to, such a training course or examination.
A person commits an offence if:
the person completes, or attempts to complete:
an online training course under paragraph 101.374E(2)(b); or
an online examination under paragraph 101.374E(2)(c); and
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1) of this regulation in relation to completing the course or examination; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person discloses or uses information or a document which forms part of, or is related to:
an online training course under paragraph 101.374E(2)(b); or
an online examination under paragraph 101.374E(2)(c); and
the person is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1) of this regulation in relation to disclosing or using the information or document; and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An accreditation ceases at the start of the earlier of the following days (unless sooner cancelled):
if the person holding the accreditation is granted a remote pilot licence—the day after the licence is granted;
the day after the end of the period of 3 years beginning on the day the accreditation comes into effect.
Note 1: For when an accreditation comes into effect, see regulation 11.065.
Note 2: For cancellation, see regulation 101.374J.

section.heading: Notice to accreditation holder to show cause

content.p: Show cause notice—cancellation or suspension

(1) CASA may give a show cause notice to a person who holds an accreditation (the accreditation holder) if there are reasonable grounds for believing that there are facts or circumstances that would justify the suspension or cancellation of the accreditation under regulation 101.374J.
A show cause notice must:
tell the accreditation holder of the facts and circumstances that, in CASA’s opinion, would justify the suspension or cancellation of the accreditation; and
invite the accreditation holder to show in writing, within a reasonable time stated in the notice, why the accreditation should not be suspended or cancelled.
Immediate suspension if serious risk to the safety of air navigation
The accreditation is suspended from the time the show cause notice is given to the accreditation holder, if:
CASA reasonably considers that there may be a serious risk to the safety of air navigation if the accreditation were not suspended; and
the show cause notice states that the accreditation is suspended for that reason.
CASA may at any time revoke the suspension.
If the accreditation is suspended under subregulation (3):
the accreditation holder is taken not to be the holder of an accreditation during the period of suspension; and
the accreditation is not in force while suspended; and
the period of the accreditation under paragraph 101.374G(b) continues to run; and

if CASA has not dealt with the suspension under regulation 101.374J within 90 days after the day the accreditation is suspended, the suspension lapses at the end of that period (if it is not earlier revoked under subregulation (4) of this regulation or subregulation 101.374J(2)).
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
Suspension or cancellation of accreditation
CASA may suspend or cancel an accreditation by written notice to the accreditation holder, if:
CASA has given the accreditation holder a show cause notice under regulation 101.374H; and
CASA has taken into account any representations made, within the period stated in the notice, by or on behalf of the accreditation holder; and
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accreditation holder:
has operated an RPA in contravention of these Regulations, an instrument under these Regulations or a condition of the accreditation; or
has operated an RPA negligently or carelessly; or
in operating an RPA, has recklessly endangered human life or property; or
at the time the accreditation was given did not meet, or now no longer meets, the criteria for eligibility under regulation 11.055 as they applied at the time the accreditation was given.
Note: For subparagraph (iv), in determining whether the criteria for eligibility were or are met, CASA may take into account the matters mentioned in subregulation 11.055(4).
Notice of decision
If CASA has given a show cause notice under regulation 101.374H to an accreditation holder:

in the event that CASA decides to suspend or cancel the accreditation—CASA must give the accreditation holder notice of the decision, including (in the case of a decision to suspend the accreditation) notice of the period of suspension; and
in the event that CASA decides not to suspend or cancel the accreditation—CASA must, in writing:
give the accreditation holder notice accordingly; and
if the accreditation was suspended under subregulation 101.374H(3)—revoke the suspension.
Effect of suspension
If an accreditation is suspended under this regulation:
the accreditation holder is taken not to be the holder of an accreditation during the period of suspension; and
the accreditation is not in force during the period of suspension stated in the notice under paragraph (2)(a); and
the period of the accreditation under paragraph 101.374G(b) continues to run.
Note 1: CASA may also impose a condition on the accreditation, or vary a condition of the accreditation—see regulation 11.067.
Note 2: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
Subpart 101.G—Model aircraft
This Subpart applies to the operation of model aircraft weighing more than 250 g (except operation mentioned in paragraph 101.005(3)(a) or (b)).
Note 1: For model aircraft, see regulation 101.023.
Note 2: This Subpart does not apply to:

a control-line model aircraft (that is, a model aircraft that is constrained to fly in a circle, and is controlled in attitude and altitude, by means of inextensible wires attached to a handle held by the person operating the model); or
a model aircraft flown indoors.
See subregulation 101.005(3).
In this Subpart:
approved area means an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of model aircraft.

section.heading: Visibility for operation of model aircraft

content.p: A person may operate a model aircraft only if the visibility at the time is good enough for the person operating the model to be able to see it continuously.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate a model aircraft at night only in accordance with the written procedures of an approved aviation administration organisation.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Keeping model aircraft away from people

content.p: A person must not operate a model aircraft over a populous area at a height less than the height from which, if any of its components fails, it would be able to clear the area.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: For populous area, see regulation 101.025.

Subject to subregulations (3) and (4), somebody who is operating a powered model aircraft must ensure that, while the model aircraft is in flight, or is landing or taking off, it stays at least 30 metres away from anyone not directly associated with the operation of model aircraft.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulation (2) is not contravened if somebody stands behind the model aircraft while it is taking off.
Subregulation (2) is also not contravened if, as part of a model flying competition, a model aircraft is flown within 30 metres of somebody who is judging the competition.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Operation of model aircraft outside approved areas

content.p: A person may operate a model aircraft outside an approved area above 400 feet AGL only if he or she:
keeps it in sight; and
keeps it clear of populous areas.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note 1: For populous area, see regulation 101.025.
Note 2: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may operate a giant model aircraft only in accordance with:
the rules and procedures of an approved aviation administration organisation; or
an approval given by CASA.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: For giant model aircraft, see regulation 101.024.
CASA may impose a condition on the operation of a giant model aircraft if the condition is reasonably necessary in the circumstances in the interests of aviation safety.
The operator of a giant model aircraft must comply with any condition imposed under subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may conduct a model aircraft flying display only in compliance with subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person complies with this subregulation if the display is conducted:
in an approved area; and
in accordance with the rules and procedures of an approved aviation administration organisation.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
A person complies with this subregulation if the display is conducted in accordance with the following conditions and any other conditions imposed by CASA under subregulation (4):
at least 21 days before the display, somebody is nominated as the organiser of the display;
at least 21 days before the display, he or she gives to CASA the following information:
his or her name, address, email address and telephone number;
the proposed program of flying;
where the display will be held, and how big the intended flying field is;
how many spectators are expected, and where they will be;
he or she ensures that:
having regard to the events making up the display, proper precautions are taken for the safety of the participants and spectators; and
the operators participating in the display are competent to carry out each proposed manoeuvre safely.
CASA may impose a condition on the conduct of a model flying display if in the circumstances the condition is reasonably necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
Subpart 101.H—Rockets
This Subpart applies to the operation of rockets of all kinds, except rockets mentioned in paragraph 101.005(3)(f).
Note 1: That is, this Subpart does not apply to a firework rocket not capable of rising more than 400 feet AGL. See paragraph 101.005(3)(f).
Note 2: Rocket in this Subpart does not include a rocket-powered aircraft—see regulation 101.425.

section.heading: Application of State and Territory laws about rockets

content.p: If a law of a State or Territory deals with the operation or use of rockets, and is not inconsistent with this Subpart, nothing in this Subpart affects the operation of the law.
For subregulation (1), a law of a State or Territory is not inconsistent with this Subpart if it is possible to comply with both this Subpart and the State or Territory law at once.
In this Subpart:
approved area means an area approved under regulation 101.030 as an area for the operation of rockets.
model rocket means a rocket that:
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(7).
weighs no more than 1 500 grams; and
carries no more than 125 grams of propellant; and
produces no more than 320 newton-seconds of impulse; and
is made of balsa, wood, paper or plastics or a combination of those materials, but contains no metal as structural parts.
rocket does not include a rocket-powered or rocket-assisted aircraft.

section.heading: Launching rocket in or over prohibited or restricted area

content.p: A person may launch a rocket (including a model rocket) in or over a prohibited area, or in or over a restricted area, only with the permission of, and in accordance with any conditions imposed by, the authority controlling the area.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: Details of prohibited and restricted areas are published in the AIP or NOTAMS.
In subregulation (1):
authority controlling the area means:
(a) in the case of a prohibited area—the Secretary of the Department administered by the Minister administering section 1 of the Defence Act 1903; and
in the case of a restricted area—the authority mentioned in AIP (as issued from time to time) as the controlling authority for the area.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may launch a rocket (including a model rocket) to higher than 400 feet AGL in controlled airspace only:
in an approved area; or
in accordance with an air traffic control clearance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(5).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may launch a rocket that is not a small model rocket to higher than 400 feet AGL within 3 nautical miles of an aerodrome only if:
doing so is permitted by another provision of this Part; or
permission has been given for the operation under regulation 101.445.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note 1: For model rocket, see regulation 101.425.
Note 2: Some special provisions apply to model rockets—see regulation 101.470.
In subregulation (1):
small model rocket means a model rocket that weighs less than 500 grams and either:
uses no more than 25 grams of propellant; or
produces no more than 20 newton-seconds of impulse.
A person may launch a rocket (including both a small model rocket and any other model rocket) from or over an area mentioned in paragraph (4)(a) or (b) only if:
doing so is permitted by another provision of this Part; or
permission has been given for the operation under regulation 101.445.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
The areas for subregulation (3) are:
a movement area or runway of an aerodrome; and
the approach or departure path of a runway of an aerodrome.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (3) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Getting permission for launch of rocket near aerodrome

content.p: The authority that must give permission for regulation 101.440 is:
if the aerodrome concerned is a controlled aerodrome—the air traffic control service for the aerodrome; or
in the case of any other aerodrome—CASA.

A person applies for permission under this regulation by giving to the relevant authority mentioned in subregulation (1) the information required by table 101.445, so far as relevant to the proposed launch:

tr.th: Table 101.445 Details of launching of rocket to be given to CASA
Table 101.445 Details of launching of rocket to be given to CASA

tr.td: The name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will launch the rocket (or, if several people will be involved, the name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will coordinate the launching)
The date and time the rocket is to be launched
Where it is to be carried out
The size and mass of the rocket
The estimated greatest altitude or flight level that the rocket will reach
If more than 1 rocket is to be launched at a time, how many rockets are to be launched at the time

content.p: If more than 1 rocket is to be launched at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such launch.
Regulation 101.035 does not authorise a person who or that applies for permission under this regulation to make the application to a body mentioned in paragraph 101.035(1)(a) or (b).
An authority mentioned in subregulation (1) may impose conditions on a permission in the interests of the safety of air navigation.
A person must not contravene a condition imposed under subregulation (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (6) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Rockets other than model rockets must be launched in approved area

content.p: A person may launch a rocket that is not a model rocket, or permit such a rocket to be launched, only in an approved area.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(7).

A person may launch a rocket that is not a model rocket, or permit such a rocket to be launched, only if the person gives the details listed in the table following subregulation 101.445(2) to CASA at least 1 working day before the intended time of the launch.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: A person can comply with this requirement by telling:
if the person is an approved aviation administration organisation—the Australian NOTAM Office; or
the appropriate approved aviation administration organisation.
See regulation 101.035.
If more than 1 rocket is to be launched at a time, such a requirement is a requirement to give the information about each such rocket.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person may launch a rocket that is not a model rocket to higher than 400 feet AGL only:
in an approved area; or
as permitted by another provision of this Part.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: CASA must publish details of the approval of an area (including any conditions) in NOTAM or on an aeronautical chart—see subregulation 101.030(7).
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Dropping or discharging of things from rockets

content.p: A person must not cause anything to be dropped or discharged from a rocket in a way that creates a hazard to an aircraft.
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Weather and day limitations—rockets other than model rockets

content.p: A person may launch a rocket that is not a model rocket:
in or into cloud; or
at night; or
in conditions other than VMC;
only as permitted by another provision of this Part, or in accordance with an air traffic control clearance.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: For model rocket, see regulation 101.425.
However, subregulation (1) does not prevent rockets being operated as part of a firework display.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
A person must not launch a model rocket into cloud.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Note: For model rocket, see regulation 101.425.
A person must not launch a model rocket to higher than 400 feet AGL within 5 nautical miles of an aerodrome.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (2) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subject to subregulations (1) and (2) and Subpart 101.B, a person may launch a model rocket outside an approved area, or at night.
Subpart 101.I—Firework displays
This Subpart regulates the conduct of certain firework displays, to the extent necessary to prevent them being a hazard to the safety of air navigation.

section.heading: Application of State and Territory laws about fireworks

content.p: If a law of a State or Territory deals with the use of fireworks, and is not inconsistent with this Subpart, nothing in this Subpart affects the operation of the law.
For subregulation (1), a law of a State or Territory is not inconsistent with this Subpart if it is possible to comply with both this Subpart and the State or Territory law at once.

section.heading: Meaning of operate a firework display

content.p: For this Subpart, a person operates a firework display if the person places the fireworks for the display, or fires them off.

section.heading: Certain projectiles prohibited in firework displays

content.p: A person may use, in a firework display, a projectile that is capable of reaching more than 400 feet AGL only if CASA so approves.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Firework displays not permitted near aerodromes

content.p: A person may operate a firework display in or over an area mentioned in paragraph (2)(a) or (b) only if subregulation (3) or (4) applies to the display.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
The areas for subregulation (1) are:
a movement area or runway of an aerodrome; and
the approach or departure path of a runway of an aerodrome.
This subregulation applies to a firework display if:
permission for the display has been given by:
if the aerodrome is a controlled aerodrome—the air traffic control service for the aerodrome; and
in the case of any other aerodrome—CASA; and
the person who proposes to operate the display has, before doing so, given to CASA the details required by table 101.500.
This subregulation applies to a firework display if the fireworks are set off on or near domestic premises by or for somebody who lives there.

section.heading: Notice to CASA of certain firework displays

content.p: A person may operate a firework display at a place within 3 nautical miles of an aerodrome only if the person has given at least 2 working days’ notice to CASA.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
However, subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the fireworks are set off on or near domestic premises by or for somebody who lives there; and
either:
if a law of a State or Territory allows fireworks to be set off in that place only on a particular day or days—the fireworks are set off on such a day; or
if there is no such law in that place—the fireworks are set off on a day on which fireworks are customarily set off on domestic premises in that place.
When the person tells CASA, the person must also give to CASA the information required by table 101.500.

tr.th: Table 101.500 Details of firework display to be given to CASA
Table 101.500 Details of firework display to be given to CASA

tr.td: The name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will operate the display (or, if several people will be involved in its operation, the name, address, email address and telephone number of the person who will coordinate it)
The date the display is to begin, the starting time, and how long it is to last
Where it is to be given
How many projectiles capable of reaching more than 400 feet AGL are to be used in the display
A general description of the pyrotechnic characteristics of each such projectile
The estimated highest altitude that any projectile can reach
The maximum burst radius of the pyrotechnics in a projectile

content.p: CASA may impose a condition on the operation of a firework display if the condition is reasonably necessary in the circumstances in the interests of the safety of air navigation.
A person operating a display must comply with any condition imposed under subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) or (5) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
