Subpart 103.A—Preliminary
This Part (other than Subpart 103.Z) applies to Part 103 aircraft.
Despite subregulation (1), this Part does not apply to the operation of a Part 103 aircraft if Part 132, 133, 135 or 137 applies to the operation.
Despite subregulation (1), this Part does not apply to the operation of a touring motor glider if:
the touring motor glider is registered; and
the touring motor glider is being operated solely under Part 91 during a flight; and
either:
the pilot in command for the flight is exercising the privileges of a pilot licence with an aeroplane category rating; or
the pilot in command for the flight holds an approval under regulation 61.040 for paragraph 61.1515(1)(b).
Subpart 103.Z applies in relation to the towing of a Part 103 aircraft by an aircraft that is not a Part 103 aircraft.
Meaning of Part 103 aircraft
(4) An aircraft is a Part 103 aircraft if:
the aircraft is not registered; and
the aircraft is any of the following:
a powered parachute;
a gyroglider;
a hang glider or powered hang glider;
a paraglider or powered paraglider;
a touring motor glider;
a rotorcraft prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph;
a weight-shift-controlled aeroplane prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph;
any other aeroplane prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph.
(5) A sailplane is a Part 103 aircraft.

Note: This subregulation applies to all sailplanes, including sailplanes registered under Part 47 and sailplanes that are foreign registered aircraft. Sailplanes are required to be registered under Part 47, unless an exception in subregulation 47.015(1) applies.
(6) Despite subregulations (4) and (5), neither of the following aircraft are Part 103 aircraft:
an RPA;
a model aircraft.
In these Regulations:

Part 103 activity means any of the following: operating a Part 103 aircraft; maintaining, or ensuring the airworthiness of, a Part 103 aircraft or aeronautical products for Part 103 aircraft; providing training in an activity covered by paragraph (a) or (b). carrying on a business or undertaking involving the provision of services or equipment for undertaking an activity covered by paragraph (a) or (b); the towing of a Part 103 aircraft by another Part 103 aircraft; an activity prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards.
operating a Part 103 aircraft;
maintaining, or ensuring the airworthiness of, a Part 103 aircraft or aeronautical products for Part 103 aircraft;
providing training in an activity covered by paragraph (a) or (b).
carrying on a business or undertaking involving the provision of services or equipment for undertaking an activity covered by paragraph (a) or (b);
the towing of a Part 103 aircraft by another Part 103 aircraft;
an activity prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards.
Part 103 ASAO means an ASAO whose approved function is or includes administering a Part 103 activity.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 103

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.
If a provision of this Part, or of the Part 103 Manual of Standards, refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, a person may apply to CASA, in writing, for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, the approval must be granted.
Subregulation 11.055(1B) applies to the granting of an approval under this regulation.
Subpart 103.B—Aircraft listing, certification and markings

A Part 103 aircraft is listed with a Part 103 ASAO for the purposes of this regulation if the aircraft is listed with the Part 103 ASAO in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
Certain Part 103 aircraft must be listed
The owner of a Part 103 aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is an aircraft other than a sailplane, hang glider, powered hang glider, paraglider, powered paraglider or registered touring motor glider; and
the aircraft has an empty weight of more than 70 kg; and
a person operates the aircraft; and
the aircraft is not listed with a Part 103 ASAO.
Other Part 103 aircraft may be listed
If paragraphs (2)(a) and (b) do not apply to a Part 103 aircraft, the aircraft may be listed with a Part 103 ASAO.
Listing with more than one ASAO prohibited
The owner of a Part 103 aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
a person operates the aircraft; and
the aircraft is listed with more than one Part 103 ASAO at the same time.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Flying without a certificate of airworthiness—airworthiness standards for certain kinds of Part 103 aircraft

content.p: The Part 103 Manual of Standards may make provision in relation to one or more of the following:
airworthiness standards for specified kinds of Part 103 aircraft;
for Part 103 ASAOs whose approved functions include administering Part 103 aircraft:
the kinds of aircraft for which the Part 103 ASAO may set airworthiness standards; and
procedures for setting such standards;
procedures for accepting a Part 103 aircraft that meets the standards referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);
procedures for issuing a statement of acceptance to the owner of an aircraft accepted in accordance with the procedures mentioned in paragraph (c).

For the purposes of paragraph 20AA(3)(b) of the Act, a flight in a Part 103 aircraft is authorised without a certificate of airworthiness if a Part 103 ASAO has issued a statement of acceptance to the owner of the aircraft in accordance with the procedures mentioned in paragraph (1)(d) of this regulation.

section.heading: Display of markings—aircraft other than sailplanes

content.p: Part 45 does not apply to a Part 103 aircraft that is not a sailplane.
If the approved functions of a Part 103 ASAO include administering a Part 103 activity in relation to Part 103 aircraft that are not sailplanes, the exposition for the Part 103 ASAO must:
include requirements relating to the display of markings (within the ordinary meaning of the term) on the aircraft; and
prohibit the operation of the aircraft if the aircraft does not meet the requirements mentioned in paragraph (a).
Note: An ASAO, and the holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO, must not contravene the ASAO’s exposition: see regulations 149.345 and 149.410.
Without limiting subregulation (2), the exposition must include requirements relating to the following:
when markings must be displayed;
the number of sets of markings that must be displayed;
the location of sets of markings on aircraft;
the characters to be used in each set of markings, including height, width and font requirements.
Subpart 103.C—General obligations
Part 103 activity must be authorised
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a Part 103 activity; and
the person does not hold an authorisation from a Part 103 ASAO authorising the person to undertake the activity.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the person holds an approval under regulation 103.020 to undertake the activity; or
the person is otherwise authorised under these Regulations to undertake the activity.
Part 103 activity must be undertaken in accordance with authorisation
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
undertakes a Part 103 activity; and
holds an authorisation from a Part 103 ASAO authorising the person to undertake the activity; and
undertakes the activity in a way that contravenes the authorisation.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Subpart 103.D—Operational procedures

section.heading: Minimum height rules—other than over populous areas or public gatherings

content.p: This regulation applies if a Part 103 aircraft is flown other than over a populous area or a public gathering.
Note: For minimum height rules if an aircraft is flown over a populous area or a public gathering, see regulation 91.265.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
the aircraft is flown below 500 ft above the highest feature or obstacle within a horizontal radius of 300 m of the point on the ground or water immediately below the aircraft; and
none of the circumstances mentioned in subregulation (3) applies.
The circumstances are the following:
the aircraft is taking off, operating or landing in circumstances prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
the aircraft is engaged in a missed approach;
the aircraft is a glider engaged in ridge or hill soaring;
the aircraft:
is not carrying passengers; and
is engaged in a practice emergency procedure at an aerodrome;
the aircraft:
is not carrying passengers; and
is engaged in a practice forced landing procedure with the consent of the person or authority having control over the land or water above which the procedure is carried out;
the aircraft is performing training circuits at an aerodrome in circumstances prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
the pilot holds an approval for the purposes of regulation 91.180 (air displays in Australian territory);
all of the following apply:
the pilot in command of the aircraft holds an approval under regulation 103.020 to fly the aircraft below the height mentioned in paragraph (2)(a);
the pilot in command of the aircraft conducts a risk assessment of the area to be flown over;
the point on the ground or water vertically below the aircraft is not within 150 m of a person, vessel, vehicle or structure;
for a rotorcraft—the rotorcraft is hovering, air transiting, air taxiing or ground taxiing at an aerodrome;
for a rotorcraft, seaplane or amphibian—the aircraft is flying within an access lane:
that is for use by aircraft taking off from, or landing at, a particular place; and
details of which are published in the authorised aeronautical information for the flight;
the aircraft is engaged in a procedure to determine the suitability of an aerodrome for a landing.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Safety when aircraft operating on ground

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person starts the engine of a Part 103 aircraft, or causes the engine to be started, while the aircraft is on the ground; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the person who starts the engine or causes the engine to be started must be:
authorised by a Part 103 ASAO to pilot or maintain the aircraft; or
a person of a kind prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph; and
if subparagraph (a)(ii) applies—the aircraft must be secured from moving; and
if the aircraft is hand-started—the requirements relating to hand-starting prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person operates a Part 103 aircraft on the ground, or causes a Part 103 aircraft to be operated on the ground; and

the person permits another person to board the aircraft or to remain on the aircraft while a pilot seat of the aircraft is not occupied by a person who is competent to apply the brakes and control the engine.
For the purposes of paragraph (3)(b), a person is competent to apply the brakes and control the engine of an aircraft if:

the person has been given instructions on how, and assessed as competent, to apply the brakes and control the engine (including how to shut the engine down) by another person who is authorised by a Part 103 ASAO to pilot or maintain the aircraft; or
the person is authorised by a Part 103 ASAO to maintain the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An exposition for a Part 103 ASAO must include requirements in relation to the carriage of passengers on Part 103 aircraft.
Note: An ASAO, and the holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO, must not contravene the ASAO’s exposition: see regulations 149.345 and 149.410.
Carriage of infants
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met for the flight.
The requirement is that an infant must not be carried on the flight except in the circumstances prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
Restraint of adults and children
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (4) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
if the aircraft is fitted with any seats—at all times during the flight:
the pilot in command must occupy a pilot seat, with the seatbelt, and the shoulder harness (if any), securely fastened; and
any other adult carried on the flight must occupy a seat, with the seatbelt, and the shoulder harness (if any), securely fastened;
if the aircraft is not fitted with any seats—at all times during the flight each adult on the flight must be wearing a harness or restraint that is securely fastened;
in any case—any child carried on the flight must be restrained in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
Subregulation (4) does not apply in relation to a person if regulation 105.105 imposes requirements in relation to restraint of the person.
Note: Regulation 105.105 is about restraint of persons carried on an aircraft being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
This regulation does not apply in relation to an animal carried in a passenger cabin.
Note: For the carriage of animals, see regulation 91.620.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
cargo is carried on the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met for the flight.
The requirements are the following:
cargo must not be carried in a place where the cargo may damage, obstruct or cause the failure of any part of the aircraft, or any equipment, that is essential to the safe operation of the aircraft;
cargo carried on the aircraft must be:
securely stowed in accordance with the aircraft flight manual instructions; or
otherwise safely restrained;
cargo must be carried in accordance with any requirements relating to the carriage of cargo:
in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft; or
on a placard on the aircraft;
if cargo is carried on an unoccupied seat in the aircraft:
the cargo must not weigh more than the weight limitation for that seating position; and
the cargo, and the means of restraint of the cargo, must not interfere with the safe operation of the aircraft;
any other requirement relating to the restraint or stowage of cargo prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, IMC are simulated; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the aircraft must be of a kind prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
(b) a pilot (the safety pilot) must:
occupy a pilot seat fitted with fully functioning flight controls; and
have adequate vision forward and to each side of the aircraft;
(c) a pilot (the second pilot) flying the aircraft under simulated IMC must occupy a pilot seat fitted with fully functioning flight controls;
the safety pilot must be authorised by a Part 103 ASAO to pilot the aircraft.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
In this regulation:
permitted person, in relation to an aircraft, means a person who is carried on the aircraft for the purpose of:
giving or receiving flying training; or
practising for the issue of an authorisation by a Part 103 ASAO; or
being assessed for the issue of an authorisation by a Part 103 ASAO.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a person other than a permitted person is carried on the aircraft; and
the pilot in command permits the simulation (other than verbally) of an emergency or abnormal situation that may affect the handling characteristics of the aircraft.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight:
a person other than the following is carried on the aircraft:
a permitted person;
a person prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph; and

the pilot in command permits a test of the aircraft, or any of its instruments, indicators, items of equipment or systems (other than a test of the aircraft during the course of checks associated with the normal operation of the aircraft).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person on a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the person consumes alcohol; or
the person provides alcohol to another person on the aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Additional requirements in relation to Part 103 activities

content.p: The Part 103 Manual of Standards may prescribe additional requirements in relation to undertaking a Part 103 activity.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 103 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
flights over populous areas, prohibited areas, restricted areas or water;
flights in specified classes of airspace;
flights at or above specified altitudes;
the operation of a Part 103 aircraft at, or within a prescribed distance from, an aerodrome;
the conduct of aerobatic manoeuvres during flights;
the dropping of things from a Part 103 aircraft during flights;
the towing of a Part 103 aircraft by another Part 103 aircraft;
the conduct of training in operating a Part 103 aircraft;
placards that must be displayed in a Part 103 aircraft;
documents that must be carried on a Part 103 aircraft for a flight;
documents or authorisations that must be in force when a Part 103 aircraft begins a flight.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) in relation to a Part 103 activity; and
the requirement is not met in undertaking the Part 103 activity.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 103.K—Equipment
The Part 103 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
the fitment and non-fitment of equipment to a Part 103 aircraft; and
the carrying of equipment on a Part 103 aircraft; and
equipment that is fitted to, or carried on, a Part 103 aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 103.M—Airworthiness requirements
Parts 4 and 4A of CAR do not apply to a Part 103 aircraft unless:
the aircraft is listed with a Part 103 ASAO; and
a standard certificate of airworthiness is in force in relation to the aircraft.
Parts 4B, 4C and 4D of CAR do not apply to a Part 103 aircraft unless:
a standard certificate of airworthiness is in force in relation to the aircraft; and
the aircraft is:
a sailplane; or
listed with a Part 103 ASAO.

section.heading: Requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards

content.p: The Part 103 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the maintenance, or ensuring the airworthiness of, a Part 103 aircraft or aeronautical products for Part 103 aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For the purposes of subsection 20AB(2) of the Act, a person is permitted to carry out maintenance:
on a Part 103 aircraft; or
on an aeronautical product for a Part 103 aircraft;
if the person holds an authorisation from a Part 103 ASAO authorising the person to carry out the maintenance.
Note: See also regulation 103.040.

(1) This regulation applies if the approved functions of a Part 103 ASAO include administering the activity mentioned in paragraph (b) of the definition of Part 103 activity (maintaining, or ensuring the airworthiness of, a Part 103 aircraft or aeronautical products for Part 103 aircraft).
The exposition for the Part 103 ASAO must include requirements relating to undertaking the activity.
Note: An ASAO, and the holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO, must not contravene the ASAO’s exposition: see regulations 149.345 and 149.410.

section.heading: Aircraft data plate—aircraft to which Part 21 does not apply

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to an aircraft data plate attached, or to be attached, to a Part 103 aircraft that is administered by a Part 103 ASAO (other than a data plate attached in accordance with Division 21.Q.2).
The exposition for the Part 103 ASAO must include requirements relating to the procedures to be used for attaching an aircraft data plate to the aircraft.
Note: An ASAO, and the holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO, must not contravene the ASAO’s exposition: see regulations 149.345 and 149.410.

The owner of a Part 103 aircraft contravenes this subregulation if an aircraft data plate attached to the aircraft does not meet the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person removes or engages in conduct that results in the alteration of any of the information on an aircraft data plate attached to a Part 103 aircraft; and
the person does not hold an approval under regulation 103.020 to do so.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Reporting of defects
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
is the owner or operator of a Part 103 aircraft that is administered by a Part 103 ASAO; and
knows there is a major defect in the aircraft; and

does not report the defect, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph, to the Part 103 ASAO within 3 business days after becoming aware of the defect.
Note: Part 4B of CAR contains additional requirements in relation to the reporting of defects in sailplanes.
A Part 103 ASAO contravenes this subregulation if the Part 103 ASAO:
receives a report under subregulation (1); and
does not, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph, provide a copy of the report to the following:
CASA;
each other Part 103 ASAO prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph;
the manufacturer of the aircraft.
Recording of defects
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
is the owner or operator of a Part 103 aircraft that is administered by a Part 103 ASAO; and
knows there is a major defect in the aircraft; and
does not record the defect, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 103 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is administered by a Part 103 ASAO; and
a major defect in the aircraft has been recorded in accordance with subregulation (3); and
when the flight begins, a person authorised by the Part 103 ASAO has not signed a release to service for the aircraft in relation to the defect.
Offences
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 103.Z—Towing of Part 103 aircraft by other aircraft

section.heading: Towing of Part 103 aircraft by other aircraft

content.p: The Part 103 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements in relation to the towing of a Part 103 aircraft by an aircraft that is not a Part 103 aircraft.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

Subpart 105.A—Preliminary
This Part does not apply in relation to:
parachutes that are not personnel parachutes; or
parachute descents that are not from aircraft; or
emergency parachute descents.
In these Regulations:
emergency parachute has the meaning given by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
major defect means:
for an emergency parachute—a defect of any part of the emergency parachute that may affect the safe operation of the parachute or cause the parachute to become a danger to persons or property;
for a reserve parachute—a defect of any part of the reserve parachute assembly that may affect the safe operation of the parachute or cause the parachute to become a danger to persons or property.
parachute does not include a parasail or a powered parachute.
parachute operator means a person who carries on a business or undertaking involving the provision of services or equipment for undertaking parachute descents.

parachuting activity means any of the following: a parachute descent; packing a parachute; maintaining a parachute; assembling a parachute; supervising a parachute descent; operating an aircraft to facilitate a parachute descent; providing training in an activity covered by paragraphs (a) to (f); carrying on a business or undertaking involving the provision of services or equipment for undertaking a parachute descent; an activity prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
a parachute descent;
packing a parachute;
maintaining a parachute;
assembling a parachute;
supervising a parachute descent;
operating an aircraft to facilitate a parachute descent;
providing training in an activity covered by paragraphs (a) to (f);
carrying on a business or undertaking involving the provision of services or equipment for undertaking a parachute descent;
an activity prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
Part 105 ASAO means an ASAO whose approved function is or includes administering a parachuting activity.
reserve parachute has the meaning given by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
reserve parachute assembly has the meaning given by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
tandem parachutist means a person undertaking a parachute descent in which the person’s harness is attached to the harness of another person who is in control of the descent.
trainee parachutist has the meaning given by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 105

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument: see subsection 98(5AA) of the Act.
Subpart 105.C—General
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person undertakes a parachute descent in a way that creates a hazard to an aircraft, another person or property.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Persons must not create hazards to aircraft operated to facilitate parachute descents

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if the person does an act that creates a hazard to an aircraft that is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.

division.heading: Reporting and recording defects, incidents etc.

section.heading: Reserve parachutes and emergency parachutes—reporting of major defects by maintainers

content.p: This regulation applies to a person if the person holds an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO to carry out maintenance on:
reserve parachutes; or
emergency parachutes.
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
carries out maintenance on a reserve parachute or emergency parachute; and
knows there is a major defect in the parachute; and
does not report the defect to the Part 105 ASAO within 3 business days after becoming aware of the defect.
The report must:
be made in writing; and
be made in a form approved by the Part 105 ASAO; and
contain the following information:
the make and type of the parachute;
the serial number of the parachute;
the name and address of the owner of the parachute;
a description of the defect;
how the defect may affect the safety of the parachute or cause the parachute to become a danger to persons or property.
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if the ASAO:
receives a report under subregulation (2); and
does not provide a copy of the report to the following within 3 business days of receiving the report:
CASA;
the manufacturer of the parachute;
all other Part 105 ASAOs.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Reserve parachutes—reporting of major defects by parachutists

content.p: This regulation applies to a person if the person holds an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO to undertake a parachute descent.
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
knows there is a major defect in the reserve parachute; and
knows that the major defect has not been reported to the Part 105 ASAO; and
does not report the defect to the Part 105 ASAO within 3 business days after becoming aware of the defect.
The report must:
be made in writing; and
be made in a form approved by the Part 105 ASAO; and
contain the following information:
the make and type of the parachute;
the serial number of the parachute;
the name and address of the owner of the parachute;
a description of the defect;
how the defect may affect the safety of the parachute or cause the parachute to become a danger to persons or property.
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if the ASAO:
receives a report under subregulation (2); and
does not provide a copy of the report to the following within 3 business days of receiving the report:
CASA;
the manufacturer of the reserve parachute;
all other Part 105 ASAOs.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

division.heading: Search and rescue services and emergency and survival equipment

section.heading: Reserve parachute and emergency parachute equipment requirements

content.p: Reserve parachutes
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a parachute descent; and
the person is not equipped with a reserve parachute that meets the requirements in subregulation (3).
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person provides a reserve parachute to another person for the purposes of the other person undertaking a parachute descent; and
the reserve parachute does not meet the requirements in subregulation (3).
The requirements are as follows:
the reserve parachute assembly must meet the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards;
the reserve parachute assembly must have been maintained in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
Emergency parachutes
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person provides an emergency parachute to another person for carriage on board an aircraft prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards; and
the emergency parachute does not meet the requirements in subregulation (5).
The requirements are as follows:
the emergency parachute must meet the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards;
the emergency parachute must have been maintained in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Defective reserve parachutes and defective emergency parachutes

content.p: Defective reserve parachutes
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a parachute descent; and
the person is equipped with a defective reserve parachute.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person is a tandem parachutist or a trainee parachutist.
Defective reserve parachutes and defective emergency parachutes

A person contravenes this subregulation if the person provides a defective reserve parachute or a defective emergency parachute to another person for the purposes of the other person undertaking a parachute descent.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Defective reserve parachute
(5) For the purposes of this regulation, a defective reserve parachute means a reserve parachute:
that is covered by a report under regulation 105.045 or 105.050; or
that is covered by an airworthiness directive; or
whose assembly does not meet a requirement prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of paragraph 105.055(3)(a); or

for which the manufacturer of the parachute has issued a notice stating that action must be taken in relation to the parachute to ensure the safety of air navigation and that action has not been taken.
Defective emergency parachute
(6) For the purposes of this regulation, a defective emergency parachute means an emergency parachute:
that is covered by a report under regulation 105.045; or
that is covered by an airworthiness directive; or
that does not meet a requirement prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of paragraph 105.055(5)(a); or

for which the manufacturer of the parachute has issued a notice stating that action must be taken in relation to the parachute to ensure the safety of air navigation and that action has not been taken.
Parachuting activity must be authorised
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
undertakes a parachuting activity; and
does not hold an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO authorising the person to undertake the activity.
Parachuting activity must be undertaken in accordance with authorisation
A person contravenes this subregulation if the person:
undertakes a parachuting activity; and
holds an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO authorising the person to undertake the activity; and
undertakes the activity in a way that contravenes the authorisation.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Additional obligations applying to parachute operators

content.p: A parachute operator must take reasonable steps to ensure that each person employed or otherwise engaged by the operator to provide services or equipment for undertaking parachute descents:
is aware of the obligations imposed on persons under this Part; and
complies with any written procedures of the operator relating to the safe provision of those services or that equipment.
A parachute operator must take reasonable steps to ensure that a person to whom the operator provides services or equipment for undertaking parachute descents:
is aware of the obligations imposed on the person under this Part; and
complies with any written procedures of the operator relating to the safe conduct of parachute descents.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies in relation to a person undertaking a parachute descent other than as a tandem parachutist.
(2) A person (the parachutist) contravenes this subregulation if:
the parachutist undertakes a parachute descent; but

before the parachutist exits the aircraft to begin the parachute descent, the pilot in command of the aircraft, or a person nominated by the pilot, has not given permission for the parachutist to do so.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: General requirements for aircraft used for parachute descents

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
the aircraft is not one of the following:
a Part 103 aircraft;
an aeroplane;
a helicopter;
a powered-lift aircraft;
a manned free balloon.
The pilot in command of a Part 103 aircraft contravenes this subregulation if the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist.
The pilot in command of an aircraft (other than a Part 103 aircraft) contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist; and
the pilot does not meet the pilot training requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
The pilot in command of a multi-engine aeroplane or a single-engine turbine-powered aeroplane contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist; and
the pilot does not meet the flight time required by subregulation (5).
The flight time required by this subregulation is:
if the aircraft is a multi-engine aeroplane:
at least 10 hours of experience as pilot in command of the type of aircraft being operated; or
at least 100 hours of experience as pilot in command, or as pilot in command under supervision, of a multi-engine aeroplane; or
if the aircraft is a single-engine turbine-powered aeroplane:
at least 10 hours of experience as pilot in command of the type of aircraft being operated; or
at least 100 hours of experience as pilot in command, or as pilot in command under supervision, of a multi-engine aeroplane or a single-engine turbine-powered aeroplane.
The pilot in command of a powered-lift aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist; and
the pilot does not meet the flight time requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), (3), (4) or (6).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
In this regulation:
flight time has the same meaning as in Part 61.
multi-engine aeroplane has the same meaning as in Part 61.

section.heading: Requirements for aircraft used for descents by trainee parachutists and tandem parachutists

content.p: This regulation applies if an aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft each contravene this subregulation if the aircraft does not meet a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3).
The requirements are as follows:
a standard certificate of airworthiness must be in force for the aircraft;
if the certificate of airworthiness is granted subject to a condition or requirement—the condition or requirement must be complied with;
there must be either:
a certificate of release to service for the most recent maintenance carried out on the aircraft; or
a maintenance release for the aircraft;
the aircraft and each of the aircraft’s engines must have been maintained in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a parachute descent over a populous area; and
the person causes a thing to be dropped:
from the aircraft before the descent; or
during the descent; and
the thing is dropped otherwise than in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Dropping things other than over populous areas

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a parachute descent other than over a populous area; and
the person causes a thing to be dropped:
from the aircraft before the descent; or
during the descent; and
either or both of the following apply:
the thing is dropped otherwise than in accordance with an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO to cause the thing to be dropped;
the thing is dropped otherwise than in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person undertakes a parachute descent; and
the person causes a thing to be dropped:
from the aircraft before the descent; or
during the descent; and
the thing creates a hazard to another aircraft, a person or property.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 105.D—Operational requirements

section.heading: Additional requirements in relation to parachuting activities

content.p: The Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe additional requirements in relation to undertaking parachuting activities.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
commencing parachute descents;
the making of broadcasts by pilots in command of aircraft being operated to facilitate parachute descents;
entering cloud during parachute descents;
descents through different classes of airspace or in restricted areas;
descents that involve landings near public gatherings;
descents that involve landings in populous areas;
packing, inspecting, maintaining, assembling, repairing, modifying or altering reserve parachutes, reserve parachute assemblies or emergency parachutes;
the safe management of parachuting drop zones.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Restraint of persons other than flight crew members

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
a person is carried on the aircraft who is not a flight crew member; and
the person is not provided with any of the following restraint devices:
a seatbelt;
a shoulder harness;
a single-point or dual-point restraint that is an approved restraint device.
The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
a person is carried on the aircraft who is not a flight crew member; and
the person:
is provided with a restraint device mentioned in paragraph (1)(c); but
is not provided with instructions for the use of the device.
The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
a person is carried on the aircraft who is not a flight crew member; and
the person is provided with a restraint device mentioned in paragraph (1)(c); and
before doing any of the following, the requirement mentioned in subregulation (4) is not met:
taxiing;
taking off;
landing.
The requirement is that the person must be directed to fasten the person’s restraint device.
The pilot in command of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
a person is carried on the aircraft who is not a flight crew member; and
the person is provided with a restraint device mentioned in paragraph (1)(c); and
the pilot in command has reason to believe it is necessary, for the safety of the person, that the person’s restraint device is fastened; and
the pilot in command does not direct the person to fasten the person’s restraint device.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2), (3) or (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
(7) For the purposes of this regulation, a restraint device is an approved restraint device if it is approved by CASA under regulation 21.305.

section.heading: Persons other than flight crew members—compliance with safety directions

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
a person is carried on an aircraft being operated to facilitate a parachute descent; and
the person is not a flight crew member; and
a direction mentioned in subregulation 105.105(4) or paragraph 105.105(5)(e) is given to the person; and
the person does not comply with the direction.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Restrictions on aircraft occupants for descents by trainee parachutists and tandem parachutists

content.p: This regulation applies if an aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent by either or both of the following:
a trainee parachutist;
a tandem parachutist.
The pilot in command of the aircraft contravenes this subregulation if a person is carried on the aircraft and the person is not:
undertaking a parachute descent from the aircraft; or
a crew member; or
an officer, or delegate of CASA, who is on board the aircraft to carry out the officer’s or delegate’s duties; or
performing a duty in accordance with the exposition of a Part 105 ASAO; or
authorised by a Part 105 ASAO to be carried on the flight for training purposes.
Subregulation (2) does not apply if:
the aircraft is a manned free balloon; and
the pilot in command holds an authorisation from a Part 105 ASAO to carry the person on board the balloon.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Subpart 105.G—Personnel fatigue management

section.heading: Management of fatigue in relation to persons exercising certain parachute descent duties

content.p: The Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements in relation to managing the risk of fatigue in persons who exercise a duty in relation to the operation of aircraft being operated to facilitate parachute descents.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 105.J—Weight and balance

section.heading: Loading of aircraft used for parachute descents

content.p: The Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements in relation to the loading of aircraft being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to one or more of the following:
aircraft loading procedures that must be followed;
aircraft loading system requirements;
the making and retention of aircraft loading records.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 105.K—Instruments, indicators, equipment and systems

section.heading: Requirements relating to radio equipment and oxygen equipment

content.p: The Part 105 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to one or more of the following:
radio equipment that must be carried on aircraft that are being operated to facilitate parachute descents;
oxygen equipment that must be carried on aircraft that are being operated to facilitate parachute descents;
the circumstances in which equipment mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b) must be used.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 105.N—Flight crew

section.heading: Pilot requirements for parachute descents—Part 103 aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies if a Part 103 aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
The pilot in command of the aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot does not satisfy the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph; or
the aircraft does not satisfy the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies if an aeroplane (other than a Part 103 aircraft) is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
The pilot in command of the aeroplane contravenes this subregulation if none of the following apply:
the pilot holds an air transport pilot licence with an aeroplane category rating;
the pilot holds a commercial pilot licence with an aeroplane category rating;
the pilot has both:
a private pilot licence with an aeroplane category rating; and
the aeronautical experience mentioned in regulation 61.610.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies if a helicopter (other than a Part 103 aircraft) is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
The pilot in command of the helicopter contravenes this subregulation if none of the following apply:
the pilot holds an air transport pilot licence with a helicopter category rating;
the pilot holds a commercial pilot licence with a helicopter category rating;
the pilot has both:
a private pilot licence with a helicopter category rating; and
the aeronautical experience mentioned in regulation 61.610 in a helicopter.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Pilot requirements for parachute descents—powered-lift aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies if a powered-lift aircraft is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
The pilot in command of the aircraft contravenes this subregulation if none of the following apply:
the pilot holds an air transport pilot licence with a powered-lift aircraft category rating;
the pilot holds a commercial pilot licence with a powered-lift aircraft category rating;
the pilot has both:
a private pilot licence with a powered-lift aircraft category rating; and
the aeronautical experience mentioned in regulation 61.610 in a powered-lift aircraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Pilot requirements for parachute descents—manned free balloons

content.p: This regulation applies if a manned free balloon is being operated to facilitate a parachute descent.
The pilot in command of the balloon contravenes this subregulation if none of the following apply:
the pilot holds a commercial pilot (balloon) licence;
the pilot has both:
an authorisation from a Part 131 ASAO that authorises the pilot to operate a manned free balloon; and
at least 75 hours of experience as pilot in command of a manned free balloon;
the pilot meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 105 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

part.heading: Commercial sport and recreational aviation operations

content.p: Note: This Part heading is reserved for future use.
Contents of Part 117
117.005 What this Part is about
117.010 Misrepresentations about holding certain civil aviation authorisations
117.015 Safety-related surveys or questionnaires—holders of certain civil aviation authorisations
117.020 Owner or registered operator to provide information about aircraft
117.025 Owner or registered operator to provide traffic reports
117.030 Protection of information
This Part provides for offences for:
misrepresentations about holding certain civil aviation authorisations; and
not completing safety-related surveys or questionnaires; and
not providing statistical information about aircraft; and
not providing traffic reports.

section.heading: Misrepresentations about holding certain civil aviation authorisations

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person represents to another person, in any way, that the person is willing to conduct an activity using an aircraft; and
the person does not hold a particular civil aviation authorisation authorising the person to conduct the activity using the aircraft; and
under the Act or these Regulations, it is an offence for a person to conduct the activity using the aircraft if the person does not hold the civil aviation authorisation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For the definition of civil aviation authorisation, see section 3 of the Act.

section.heading: Safety-related surveys or questionnaires—holders of certain civil aviation authorisations

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to a person mentioned in subregulation (2), direct the person to:
complete a safety-related survey or questionnaire by accurately answering all mandatory questions in the survey or questionnaire; and
submit the completed survey or questionnaire to CASA within the time stated in the notice.
For subregulation (1), the persons are the following:
the holder of an AOC;
a Part 141 operator who conducts flight training in aircraft;
a person who gave a notice to CASA under regulation 101.372 (Notice to operate very small RPA for hire or reward);
the holder of a certificate as an RPA operator under Division 101.F.4;
the holder of an aerial work certificate;
the holder of an approval under regulation 131.035 to conduct a specialised balloon operation.
The person may, before the end of the time stated in the notice, apply in writing to CASA for an extension.
(4) CASA may, by written notice given to the person (the notice of extension), grant the extension.
The person commits an offence if the person does not comply with the direction within:
if CASA grants an extension under subregulation (4)—the time stated in the notice of extension; or
if paragraph (a) does not apply—the time stated in the notice under subregulation (1).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Owner or registered operator to provide information about aircraft

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to the owner of an aircraft or the registered operator of the aircraft if the owner is not the registered operator of the aircraft, direct the person to:
(a) collect specified statistical and other information relating to the aircraft, including information in relation to any of the following:
operations of the aircraft;
passengers or cargo carried by the aircraft;
crew members of the aircraft;
modifications, repairs, damage or defects in the aircraft; and
provide the information to CASA within the time stated in the notice.
The person may, before the end of the time stated in the notice, apply in writing to CASA for an extension.
CASA may, by written notice given to the person, grant the extension.
If CASA gives a person a direction under this regulation, the person must comply with the direction:
if CASA grants an extension under subregulation (3)—within the time stated in the notice of extension; or
otherwise—within the time stated in the notice under subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Owner or registered operator to provide traffic reports

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to the owner of an aircraft engaged in air transport operations or the registered operator of the aircraft if the owner is not the registered operator of the aircraft, direct the person to:
prepare traffic reports; and
provide the traffic reports to CASA within the time stated in the notice.
The person may, before the end of the time stated in the notice, apply in writing to CASA for an extension.
CASA may, by written notice given to the person, grant the extension.
If CASA gives a person a direction under this regulation, the person must comply with the direction:
if CASA grants an extension under subregulation (3)—within the time stated in the notice of extension; or
otherwise—within the time stated in the notice under subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
When this regulation applies
This regulation does not apply in relation to personal information.
Note: For disclosure of personal information, see regulation 201.016.
Information must not be disclosed except in certain circumstances
A person to whom information has been disclosed under regulation 117.020 or 117.025 must not disclose the information.
Subregulation (2) does not apply if:
the disclosure is for the purposes of these Regulations or the Act; or
the disclosure is authorised or required by a law of the Commonwealth; or
the disclosure is in connection with compliance with a requirement of the Chicago Convention; or
the disclosure is with the consent of the person to whom the information disclosed relates.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
