Also, subregulation (2) does not apply if the rotorcraft is carrying sufficient fuel to allow it to hold near the planned destination aerodrome until the end of 30 minutes after the visibility and cloud ceiling height is expected to be at or above the specified landing minima for the rotorcraft for the aerodrome.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3) or (4): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Minimum height rules for medical transport operations

content.p: Regulation 91.265, 91.267, 91.277 or 91.305 does not apply to a pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight that is a medical transport operation if:
circumstances prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph apply to the rotorcraft and the operation; or
requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph are complied with in relation to the flight.

section.heading: Procedures to determine information about aerodromes

content.p: A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures to determine the kinds of information mentioned in subregulation (2) for a flight of the rotorcraft in relation to the following:
the departure aerodrome;
the planned destination aerodrome;
if a destination alternate aerodrome is required for the flight by the flight preparation (alternate aerodromes) requirements—the destination alternate aerodrome;

(b) procedures for the pilot in command to plan a take-off from, or a landing at, an aerodrome, including a procedure to determine the kinds of information mentioned in subregulation (2) in relation to the aerodrome.
The kinds of information are the following:
final approach and take-off area dimensions, directions, slopes, surface types and ground or water types for the aerodrome;
touch down and lift-off area dimensions, limitations and location;
the location of taxiways and turning nodes (if any);
the aerodrome’s elevation;
the location on the aerodrome of the aerodrome reference point (if any);
the location of the aerodrome’s windsocks (if any);
the aids to navigation and communication facilities available at the aerodrome (if any);
the limitations (if any) on the use of the aerodrome;
the special procedures (if any) in use at the aerodrome, in flight or on the ground or water;
a contact person capable of providing information about the condition of the aerodrome;
the special procedures and restrictions (if any) that the operator requires the flight crew of the rotorcraft to use at the aerodrome, including:
engine failure procedures; and
obstacle clearance procedures.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures to ensure the safety of persons in the vicinity of the rotorcraft when any of the following circumstances apply:
a person is embarking or disembarking the rotorcraft;
the rotorcraft is being loaded or unloaded;
the rotorcraft is being operated at an aerodrome;
procedures to determine the minimum distance that a person, animal or thing must be kept from the following to ensure the safety of the person, animal or thing:
the rotorcraft while it is on the ground at an aerodrome with its rotors turning;
the movement area of an aerodrome while the rotorcraft is landing or taking off;
a hazard created by the downwash of the rotorcraft at an aerodrome.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures to ensure that a flight of the rotorcraft is conducted in accordance with the requirements mentioned in subregulation 133.190(1).

The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the rotorcraft is not carrying sufficient oil to complete the flight safely.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to fuel for rotorcraft, including (but not limited to) the following:
matters that must be considered when determining whether a rotorcraft has sufficient fuel to complete a flight safely;
the amounts of fuel that must be carried on board a rotorcraft for a flight;
procedures for monitoring amounts of fuel during a flight;
procedures to be followed if fuel reaches specified amounts during a flight.
The pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures to ensure the rotorcraft is fuelled safely;

procedures relating to the safety of passengers for a flight of the rotorcraft who are embarking or disembarking, or on board, the rotorcraft during fuelling, including the normal, emergency and communication procedures to be followed by the following persons:
any crew members for the flight other than flight crew members;
any flight crew members for the flight who are on duty in the cockpit;
any of the operator’s personnel who carry out a ground support duty for the flight;
if the operator permits a person to operate low-risk electronic devices inside the cabin of the rotorcraft while the rotorcraft is being fuelled:
a statement that radio frequency emissions from those devices will not affect systems on the rotorcraft; or
procedures to ensure that, before an engine of the rotorcraft is started, any effects of radio frequency emissions from those devices have been corrected.
This Division applies in relation to the operation of a rotorcraft for a passenger transport operation.
This Division (other than regulations 133.215, 133.225 and 133.235) also applies in relation to the operation of a rotorcraft for a medical transport operation.

section.heading: Simulation of emergency or abnormal situations

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, an emergency or abnormal situation is simulated.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must state whether the operator will, or will not, carry a restricted person on a flight of the rotorcraft.
Note: For other requirements for the carriage of restricted persons who are deportees, removees and other persons in custody, see Division 4.5 of the Aviation Transport Security Regulations 2005.
If a rotorcraft operator’s exposition states that the operator will carry a restricted person on a flight of the rotorcraft, the exposition must also include the following:
procedures for carrying a restricted person on the rotorcraft;
procedures to inform each crew member for the flight about the carriage of a restricted person for the flight.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for the following:
securely stowing carry-on baggage;
determining the maximum weight and size of baggage that can be taken on the rotorcraft as carry-on baggage;
determining the locations on the rotorcraft where carry-on baggage can be stowed;
giving instructions to passengers about securely stowing carry-on baggage at the following times:
before take-off;
before landing;
any other time that the pilot in command directs.
The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, an emergency exit is obstructed.
For the purposes of subregulation (1), an emergency exit is not obstructed only because a seat adjacent to the exit, or a seat in a row of seats adjacent to the exit, is occupied by a passenger.
(3) Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the flight is a medical transport operation; and
the emergency exit is obstructed by a stretcher fit-out that is described or identified in a supplemental type certificate for the rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Passengers in seats adjacent to emergency exits

content.p: The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, during the flight, the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that the pilot in command of the rotorcraft for the flight must be satisfied that each person occupying a seat adjacent to an emergency exit:
is a suitable person; or
is accompanied or assisted, for the flight, by a suitable person who can access the emergency exit.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins:
a suitable person is occupying a seat adjacent to an emergency exit; and
the suitable person has not agreed to assist the rotorcraft’s crew with the evacuation of the rotorcraft in an emergency.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins:
a person other than a suitable person is occupying a seat adjacent to an emergency exit; and
a suitable person is, for the flight, accompanying or assisting the person; and
the suitable person has not agreed to assist the rotorcraft’s crew with the evacuation of the rotorcraft in an emergency.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Carriage of passengers with reduced mobility

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, a passenger with reduced mobility occupies a seat where the passenger could:
hinder the crew in their safety duties; or
obstruct access to emergency equipment; or
hinder the evacuation of the rotorcraft in an emergency.
Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to a passenger with reduced mobility if:
the passenger is accompanied or assisted, for the flight, by a suitable person who is seated adjacent to an emergency exit; and
the suitable person is accompanying or assisting only that passenger for the flight; and
the suitable person has agreed to assist the rotorcraft’s crew with the evacuation of the rotorcraft in an emergency.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for informing crew members for a flight about any passenger with reduced mobility who is to be carried on the flight.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a procedure mentioned in subregulation (3) is not complied with for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
This regulation applies to a rotorcraft with a maximum operational passenger seat configuration of more than 2.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a safety briefing card for the rotorcraft is not available to each passenger on the rotorcraft.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a safety briefing card does not meet the requirements mentioned in subregulation (4).
The requirements are the following:
the safety briefing card must include any information prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards;
the only other information that may be included in the safety briefing card is the following:
information that is relevant to the type and model of rotorcraft;
information that is relevant to the safety of the rotorcraft and its passengers.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if a passenger is not given a safety briefing, instructions or demonstrations in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this regulation.
(2) Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to a medical patient on a flight that is a medical transport operation.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if a safety briefing, instruction or demonstration required to be given to a passenger under this regulation includes:
information that is not relevant to the type and model of the rotorcraft; or
information that is not relevant to the safety of the rotorcraft and its passengers.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a passenger with reduced mobility will be carried on the flight; and

before the rotorcraft takes off for the flight, the passenger, or a person accompanying or assisting the passenger, is not asked by a crew member for the flight about the best way of helping the passenger if an emergency evacuation of the rotorcraft is necessary.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Safety briefing in the event of an emergency

content.p: A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for briefing passengers on what to do if an emergency occurs during a flight of the rotorcraft.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to a medical patient on a flight that is a medical transport operation.
This regulation applies to a rotorcraft that conducts a flight:
for which airborne weather radar equipment is required, under Subpart 133.K, to be fitted to the rotorcraft; or
whilst the rotorcraft is fitted with airborne weather radar equipment (whether or not the airborne weather radar equipment is required, under Subpart 133.K, to be fitted for the flight).
The rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for using the equipment during a flight mentioned in subregulation (1);
procedures for conducting a flight mentioned in subregulation (1) without the equipment, for use if the equipment is inoperative.

section.heading: Head-up displays, enhanced vision systems and synthetic vision systems

content.p: This regulation applies to a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the rotorcraft is fitted with any of the following systems:
a head-up display;
an enhanced vision system;
a synthetic vision system; and
the flight is:
an IFR flight; or
a VFR flight at night.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for using each system that is fitted to the rotorcraft during a flight mentioned in paragraph (1)(b);
procedures for conducting a flight mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) without an element of the system, for use if the element is inoperative.
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for the use of a system mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) for a flight of a rotorcraft.
The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
a system mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) is used during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) for that system is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the flight is in or through an area prescribed as a remote area by the Part 91 Manual of Standards; or
the rotorcraft is required, under Subpart 133.K, to carry a life raft for the flight.
If a rotorcraft is, or will be, used to conduct a flight to which this regulation applies, the operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for determining the survival equipment required for the area in or through which the flight will be conducted;

(b) for a flight mentioned in paragraph (1)(b)—procedures for determining the pyrotechnic signalling devices required to ensure the distress signals, set out in Appendix 1 to Annex 2, Rules of the Air, to the Chicago Convention, can be made.
This regulation applies to a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the rotorcraft is fitted with a night vision imaging system; and
the flight is:
an IFR flight; or
a VFR flight at night.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for using a night vision imaging system during a flight to which subregulation (1) applies;
procedures for conducting such a flight without an element of a night vision imaging system, for use if the element is inoperative.
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for the use of a night vision imaging system for a flight of a rotorcraft.
The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
a night vision imaging system is used during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for identifying items of moveable equipment that must be stowed securely on board the rotorcraft at the following times during a flight:
while the rotorcraft is taking off;
while the rotorcraft is landing;
any other time that the pilot in command directs;
procedures for stowing the items.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following in relation to a flight of the rotorcraft:
procedures for the inspection of the rotorcraft by the pilot in command before a flight if frost or freezing conditions exist;
if de-icing and anti-icing measures are required for the flight—procedures for carrying out these measures before the flight;
procedures for using de-icing and anti-icing equipment (where fitted) during the flight.

section.heading: Procedures relating to portable electronic devices

content.p: A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for the operation of portable electronic devices for a flight of the rotorcraft.

section.heading: Procedures relating to carriage of animals

content.p: A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for the carriage of animals for a flight of the rotorcraft.
This regulation applies to a rotorcraft that conducts a flight to or from an aerodrome in a polar region.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include procedures for the following:
monitoring and dealing with fuel freezing;
ensuring communication capability for the duration of an operation that includes a flight mentioned in subregulation (1);
training the rotorcraft’s flight crew in polar operations;
mitigating crew member and passenger exposure to cosmic radiation during solar flare activity;

if the rotorcraft is not flown over water during a flight mentioned in subregulation (1)—ensuring that each person on the rotorcraft wears a serviceable, cold-weather, anti-exposure suit that is appropriate for the temperatures in which the flight is conducted;

if the rotorcraft is flown over water during a flight mentioned in subregulation (1)—ensuring that each person on the rotorcraft wears an immersion suit that is appropriate for the temperatures in which the flight is conducted.

section.heading: External load operations involving winching a person

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
an external load operation involving winching a person is conducted during the flight; and
a requirement prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 133.F—Performance
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to take-off performance for a flight of a rotorcraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements that relate to one or more of the following:
the kinds of operations to be carried out during the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the rotorcraft takes off;
characteristics of the route flown by the rotorcraft;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the rotorcraft lands.
The pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to landing performance for a flight of a rotorcraft.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to one or more of the following:
the rotorcraft’s configuration;
the operation of any equipment for the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the rotorcraft lands;
safety factor percentages to be applied.
The pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during any stage of the flight, the rotorcraft is not flown in a performance class.
Subregulation (1) does not apply in relation to a stage of a flight if:
the flight is a medical transport operation; and
the stage of the flight is conducted at a medical transport operating site; and
the operator’s exposition includes risk assessment and management procedures that must be complied with if the rotorcraft is not flown in a performance class during such a stage; and
the procedures are complied with for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Rotorcraft permitted to fly in performance class 1 or 2, or performance class 2 with exposure

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during any stage of the flight:
the rotorcraft is flown in performance class 1 or 2, or performance class 2 with exposure; and
the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that the rotorcraft must be a rotorcraft of a kind prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Flight in performance class 2 with exposure

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the rotorcraft is flown in performance class 2 with exposure during the take-off, take-off and initial climb, approach and landing, or baulked landing stage of the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are the following:
the rotorcraft must be flown in accordance with any requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph;
the operator must hold an approval under regulation 133.015 for the rotorcraft to be flown in performance class 2 with exposure during that stage of the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Flight in performance class 1 for certain rotorcraft

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the rotorcraft has a maximum operational passenger seat configuration of more than 19; and
the rotorcraft is flown in a performance class other than performance class 1 during a stage of the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Flight in performance class 1 or 2, or performance class 2 with exposure for certain rotorcraft

content.p: This regulation applies to a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the rotorcraft has a maximum operational passenger seat configuration of more than 9 and not more than 19; or
the flight is a medical transport operation; or
all of the following apply:
the rotorcraft has a maximum operational passenger seat configuration of not more than 19;
the flight is a passenger transport operation;
the flight is conducted under the IFR or at night.
The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met for the flight.
The requirements are the following:

during the take-off, take-off and initial climb, the approach and landing, or baulked landing, stage of the flight, the rotorcraft must be flown in performance class 1 or 2, or performance class 2 with exposure;
during any other stage of the flight, the rotorcraft must be flown in performance class 1.
Subregulation (2) does not apply in relation to the take-off, take-off and initial climb, the approach and landing, or baulked landing stage of a flight, if:
the flight is a medical transport operation; and
the stage is conducted from or at a place as part of the medical transport operation; and
the operator holds an approval under regulation 133.015 in relation to the place and the rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (4): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Flight in performance class 3 over populous areas

content.p: The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight over a populous area each contravene this subregulation if:
during a stage of the flight, the rotorcraft is flown in performance class 3; and
a suitable forced landing area is not available to the rotorcraft; and
the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards are not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 133.J—Weight and balance

The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the rotorcraft is loaded in a way that contravenes the rotorcraft’s weight and balance limits.

The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, the rotorcraft ceases to be loaded in accordance with the rotorcraft’s weight and balance limits.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
procedures for loading the rotorcraft for a flight to comply with regulation 133.345;
procedures for working out the following weights for a flight of the rotorcraft:
the total weight of the crew members and the carry-on baggage of the crew members;
the total weight of the passengers and the carry-on baggage of the passengers;
the total weight of the cargo (other than carry-on baggage);
the total weight of the usable fuel to be carried;
procedures to ensure that a last-minute change to a load does not cause the rotorcraft to exceed its weight and balance limits;
procedures for offloading passengers or cargo to ensure that the rotorcraft does not exceed its weight and balance limits.

The operator and the pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the weight and balance documents for the flight do not comply with subregulation (2).
The weight and balance documents must include the following:
the weight and balance of the rotorcraft and the information used to calculate the weight and balance;
the name of the person who prepared the weight and balance documents;
confirmation by the person responsible for planning and supervising the loading of the rotorcraft that the rotorcraft has been loaded in accordance with:
the procedures set out in the operator’s exposition for loading the rotorcraft; and
the weight and balance documents;
if the person mentioned in paragraph (c) is not the pilot in command or the co-pilot—confirmation of the acceptance of the weight and balance documents by the pilot in command or the co-pilot;
any other information that the pilot in command needs to ensure that the loading of the rotorcraft is in accordance with the weight and balance limits for the rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 133.K—Equipment
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
the fitment and non-fitment of equipment to a rotorcraft; and
the carrying of equipment on a rotorcraft; and
equipment that is fitted to, or carried on, a rotorcraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 133.N—Flight crew
General
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are as follows:
the composition of the rotorcraft’s flight crew for the flight must comply with the rotorcraft’s flight manual;
if the rotorcraft has a maximum operational passenger seat configuration of more than 9—the flight crew must include 2 pilots;
if the flight is a kind of operation for which the operator’s exposition requires the carriage of additional flight crew members—the flight crew must include the additional flight crew members;
each flight crew member must be qualified under regulation 133.385 or 133.390 to carry out the duties assigned to the flight crew member by the operator for the flight;
if the flight is a VFR flight at night that is a passenger transport operation or a medical transport operation—at least one of the flight crew members must hold an instrument rating;
the pilot in command and the co-pilot (if any) for the flight must have the recent experience for the flight required by Division 133.N.4;
each flight crew member must meet the training and checking requirements for the flight crew member and the flight mentioned in subregulation (4);

if the operator’s exposition includes requirements, in accordance with regulation 133.400, in relation to knowledge that the pilot in command must have relating to the route of, and aerodromes for, the flight—the pilot in command must meet the requirements;
each flight crew member for whom, under the operator’s exposition, differences training for the rotorcraft is required, must have successfully completed the differences training.
For the purposes of paragraph (2)(c), the rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the kinds of operation (if any) for which additional flight crew members must be carried.
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by a flight crew member for a flight.
New or inexperienced crew members
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the requirements that must be met for new or inexperienced crew members to be assigned to duty for a flight of the rotorcraft.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as a flight crew member for the flight; and
the person has not been assessed by the operator, in accordance with the operator’s training and checking system, as competent to perform the duties assigned to the person for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training and checking to be conducted by certain persons

content.p: The operator of a rotorcraft contravenes this subregulation if:
a flight crew member of the operator’s personnel undertakes training or a check that is required under this Part; and
the training or check is conducted other than in accordance with subregulation (2).
The training or check must be conducted by:
an individual who:
is engaged by the operator (whether by contract or other arrangement) to conduct the training or check; and
meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards; or
a Part 142 operator with whom the operator has a contract for the Part 142 operator to conduct the training or check for the operator.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Assignment to duty of pilot in command

content.p: The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, none of the pilots assigned as flight crew members for the flight is assigned to duty as the pilot in command of the rotorcraft for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A pilot is qualified as pilot in command for a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the pilot meets the minimum flying experience requirements specified, in accordance with subregulation (2), in the rotorcraft operator’s exposition for the rotorcraft; and
for a flight described in an item of column 1 of the following table—the pilot has completed, in a rotorcraft of that kind, the flight hours mentioned in column 2 of the item; and
for a flight that is a multi-crew operation—the pilot has successfully completed command training that complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards; and
the pilot is:
if the rotorcraft is an Australian aircraft—authorised to pilot the rotorcraft during the flight as pilot in command under Part 61; or
if the rotorcraft is a foreign registered aircraft—authorised to pilot the rotorcraft during the flight as pilot in command by the rotorcraft’s State of registry.

tr.th: Flight hours required to qualify as pilot in command
Flight hours required to qualify as pilot in command
Flight hours required to qualify as pilot in command

tr.td: 5 hours as pilot in command, or pilot in command under supervision, at night

Either: (a) 5 hours as pilot in command, or pilot in command under supervision, by day in a rotorcraft of that kind; or (b) if the pilot has 5 hours of aeronautical experience in another kind of single-engine rotorcraft—3 hours as pilot in command, or pilot in command under supervision, by day in a rotorcraft of the kind referred to in paragraph (a)
10 hours as pilot in command, or pilot in command under supervision, by day
15 hours as pilot in command under supervision under the IFR
Flight that is a multi-crew operation
Either: (a) 20 hours as pilot in command; or (b) 20 hours as pilot in command under supervision in a multi-crew operation

content.p: For the purposes of paragraph (1)(a), the rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include minimum flying experience requirements for all rotorcraft operated by the operator for Australian air transport operations.
To avoid doubt, more than one item of column 2 of the table in subregulation (1) may apply to a particular hour of flight time.
(1) A pilot is qualified as co-pilot for a flight of a rotorcraft if:
the pilot is:
if the rotorcraft is an Australian aircraft—authorised to pilot the rotorcraft during the flight as co-pilot under Part 61; or
if the rotorcraft is a foreign registered aircraft—authorised to pilot the rotorcraft during the flight as co-pilot by the rotorcraft’s State of registry; and
the pilot has completed supervised line flying on a rotorcraft of that aircraft type rating as co-pilot for the number of sectors or flight hours mentioned in the operator’s exposition.
A pilot is qualified as co-pilot for a flight of a rotorcraft if the pilot is qualified under regulation 133.385 as pilot in command of the rotorcraft for the flight.

section.heading: Pilot in command in non-command pilot’s seat

content.p: Operator
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator requires the pilot in command of the rotorcraft for the flight to do any of the following in the non-command pilot’s seat:
operate the rotorcraft as pilot in command;
carry out the duties of co-pilot;
carry out training or examining duties; and

the pilot in command does not hold a valid proficiency check, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards, for the operator and the rotorcraft for a pilot who will be required to operate the rotorcraft in the non-command pilot’s seat.
Pilot in command
The pilot in command of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot in command operates the rotorcraft in the non-command pilot’s seat; and

the pilot in command does not hold a valid proficiency check, in accordance with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards, for the operator and the rotorcraft for a pilot who will be required to operate the rotorcraft in the non-command pilot’s seat.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include requirements in relation to the knowledge that a pilot in command of the rotorcraft for a flight must have of:
the route of the flight; and
the departure aerodrome and the planned destination aerodrome for the flight; and
any alternate aerodrome required for the flight by the flight preparation (alternate aerodromes) requirements; and

if the flight is to an unfamiliar aerodrome—any procedures included in the operator’s exposition under regulation 133.170 or 133.175 that relate to managing the safety of operations to an unfamiliar aerodrome.
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.

division.heading: Operation of rotorcraft of different types

content.p: This Division applies to the operator of a rotorcraft if the operator operates rotorcraft of more than one type for Part 133 operations.

section.heading: Assignment of flight crew to different multi-engine rotorcraft

content.p: A rotorcraft operator’s exposition must include the following:
a description of the circumstances in which the operator may assign a flight crew member to duty on 2 or more different multi-engine rotorcraft;
the combinations of different rotorcraft that a single flight crew member may be assigned to duty on by the operator;

the flying experience, checks and training that a flight crew member must gain or complete, while the flight crew member is employed by the operator, before being assigned to duty on 2 or more different multi-engine rotorcraft;

procedures to ensure that, if a flight crew member is assigned to duty on 2 or more different multi-engine rotorcraft within one tour of duty, the flight crew member has adequate time between flights on the different rotorcraft for the flight crew member to prepare for duty.

section.heading: Recent experience requirements—90 days before flight

content.p: Operator
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a pilot to duty as pilot in command or co-pilot of the rotorcraft for the flight; and
the pilot does not have:
if the flight is a flight by day—the recent experience required for the flight by subregulation (3); or
if the flight is a flight at night—the recent experience required for the flight by subregulation (4).
Pilot
A pilot of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot operates the rotorcraft as pilot in command or co-pilot for the flight; and
the pilot does not have:
if the flight is a flight by day—the recent experience required for the flight by subregulation (3); or
if the flight is a flight at night—the recent experience required for the flight by subregulation (4).
Requirements for flights by day
The recent experience required for a flight by day is that, within 90 days before the flight:
the pilot must have carried out, in a rotorcraft of that kind or an approved flight simulator for the rotorcraft:
at least 3 take-offs followed by climbs to at least 500 ft AGL while controlling the rotorcraft or simulator; and
at least 3 landings while controlling the rotorcraft or simulator; or
the pilot must have passed a flight test for the grant of a pilot licence or a rating on a pilot licence in a rotorcraft of that kind or an approved flight simulator for the rotorcraft; or
the pilot must have successfully completed a proficiency check for the rotorcraft that complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards.
Note: For other recent experience requirements, see Part 61.
Requirements for flights at night
The recent experience required for a flight at night is that, within 90 days before the flight:
the pilot must have carried out, at night in a rotorcraft of that kind or under night time conditions in an approved flight simulator for the rotorcraft:
at least 3 take-offs followed by climbs to at least 500 ft AGL while controlling the rotorcraft or simulator; and
at least 3 landings while controlling the rotorcraft or simulator; or
the pilot must have passed a flight test for the grant of a pilot licence or a rating on a pilot licence in a rotorcraft of that kind or an approved flight simulator for the rotorcraft; or
the pilot must have successfully completed a proficiency check for the rotorcraft that complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 133.P—Crew other than flight crew
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins:
under subregulation (2), a cabin crew member must be carried on the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met for the flight.
A cabin crew member must be carried on the flight if circumstances prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards exist for the flight.
The requirements are the following:
the number of cabin crew for the flight must be at least the number prescribed by the Part 133 Manual of Standards;
each cabin crew member must meet the training and checking requirements for the cabin crew member and the flight mentioned in subregulation (4).
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by a cabin crew member for a flight of a rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as a cabin crew member for a flight; and
the person has not been assessed by the operator, in accordance with the operator’s exposition, as competent to perform the duties assigned to the person for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a cabin crew member for the flight has not turned 18.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as a cabin crew member for the flight; and
the person does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
The requirement is that the person must meet the ICAO level 4, 5 or 6 aviation English language proficiency standards mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Assignment to duty as senior cabin crew member

content.p: The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins:
there is more than one cabin crew member for the flight; and
none of the cabin crew members is assigned to duty as the senior cabin crew member for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training and checking requirements for senior cabin crew member

content.p: The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a cabin crew member to duty as the senior cabin crew member for a flight; and
the cabin crew member has not successfully completed the training and checking requirements for a senior cabin crew member set out in the operator’s exposition.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
an air crew member is carried on the flight; and
the air crew member does not meet the training and checking requirements for the air crew member and the flight mentioned in subregulation (2).
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by an air crew member for a flight of a rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as an air crew member for a flight; and
the person has not been assessed by the operator, in accordance with the operator’s exposition, as competent to perform the duties assigned to the person for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as an air crew member for the flight; and
the person does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
The requirement is that the person must meet the ICAO level 4, 5 or 6 aviation English language proficiency standards mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a medical transport specialist is carried on the flight; and
the medical transport specialist does not meet the training and checking requirements for the medical transport specialist and the flight mentioned in subregulation (2).
The Part 133 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by a medical transport specialist for a flight of a rotorcraft.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator of a rotorcraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as a medical transport specialist for a flight; and
the person has not been assessed by the operator, in accordance with the operator’s exposition, as competent to perform the duties assigned to the person for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
