ensuring that training and checking of flight crew conducted by the operator is conducted in accordance with the operator’s training and checking manual;
if the operator has a contract with a Part 142 operator for the Part 142 operator to conduct training or checking for the operator’s flight crew:
ensuring that each person who conducts the training or checking for the Part 142 operator is authorised under Part 61 to conduct the training or checking; and
ensuring that the training or checking is conducted in accordance with the aerial work operator’s training and checking manual; and
telling the Part 142 operator, in writing, of any change in the aerial work operator’s training and checking manual.
This regulation applies to an aerial work operator that is required by regulation 138.140 to have a safety management system.
The operator’s safety manager must have:
sufficient relevant experience in carrying out, or managing other persons in carrying out, air operations; and

sufficient relevant safety management experience to capably lead, manage and set standards to enable the operator to safely implement its safety management system in accordance with its operations manual; and
a satisfactory record in the conduct or management of air operations; and

sufficient safety and regulatory knowledge to enable the operator to conduct the operator’s aerial work operations safely and in accordance with its operations manual and the civil aviation legislation.
This regulation applies to an aerial work operator that is required by regulation 138.140 to have a safety management system.
The operator’s safety manager must manage the operator’s safety management system.
Without limiting subregulation (2), the responsibilities of the safety manager include:
managing the operation of the safety management system including managing corrective, remedial and preventative action in relation to the system; and
regularly reporting to the chief executive officer on the effectiveness of the safety management system; and
managing the maintenance and continuous improvement of the safety management system.

section.heading: Additional qualification and experience requirements for key personnel

content.p: This regulation applies to:
an applicant for an aerial work certificate; or
an aerial work operator.

CASA may, by written notice given to the applicant or operator, direct that any of the key personnel of the applicant or operator must have stated additional qualifications or experience to those otherwise required under this Subpart.

If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to a person who is, or is proposed to be, any of the key personnel of the applicant or operator, direct the person:
to undertake a stated examination; or
to be interviewed by CASA; or
to complete a stated training course.
In deciding whether to give a direction under this regulation, CASA must have regard to, but is not limited to considering, the following:
the need to ensure that the applicant or operator can conduct safe aerial work operations in accordance with its operations manual and the civil aviation legislation;
the nature and complexity of the operations;
the leadership, management and standards-setting skills required by the person for the operations;
how recently the person has used the person’s aviation skills;
whether the person is able to exercise the privileges of each civil aviation authorisation held by the person.

section.heading: Operators who are required to have a training and checking system

content.p: An aerial work operator who conducts one or more of the following must have a training and checking system:
operations transporting marine pilots;
operations in:
multi-engine transport category rotorcraft with a maximum take-off weight of more than 3,175 kg; or
multi-engine aeroplanes with a maximum take-off weight of more than 5,700 kg; or
turbine-engine aeroplanes (other than turbine-engine propeller-driven aeroplanes);
operations prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.

Despite subregulation (1), an aerial work operator is not required to have a training and checking system for an aerial work operation conducted in an aeroplane or a rotorcraft if circumstances prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards apply to the aeroplane or rotorcraft and the operation.
The training and checking system must meet the requirements of regulations 138.130 and 138.135.
This regulation applies to an operator of an aeroplane or a rotorcraft if the operator is required, under regulation 138.125, to have a training and checking system.
Despite subregulation (1), this regulation does not apply in relation to the following:
for an operator that is also a Part 141 operator—training that is authorised Part 141 flight training for the operator;
for an operator that is also a Part 142 operator—training or checking that is an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator.
The operator’s training and checking for flight crew, including recurrent training and line checking, must include the matters mentioned in subregulation (4).
The training and checking system must include the following:
a description of how the training and checking is conducted by or for the operator;
an auditable system for maintaining records of the results of the training and checking;
procedures that ensure that each of the operator’s flight crew:
completes training and checking in accordance with the training and checking system; and
is supervised effectively during training and checking;
a description of:
the operator’s requirement for conversion training for flight crew; and
how the operator manages conversion training for flight crew;
a description of the operator’s requirement for differences training for flight crew;
any additional training required to familiarise a flight crew member with their duties;
a description of how the operator assesses the competence of a flight crew member to perform the duties assigned to the member for a flight;
the remedial training requirements for flight crew;
if the operator has a contract with a person for the person to conduct training or checking of flight crew for the operator:
details of the person; and
details of the training or checking covered by the contract; and
details of how the operator ensures that the person is complying with the operator’s training and checking system;
for each kind of aeroplane or rotorcraft operated by the operator:

the number of flight hours of supervised line flying as pilot in command a pilot must complete on that kind of aeroplane or rotorcraft to be qualified as pilot in command for the aeroplane or rotorcraft; and
the number of flight hours of supervised line flying as co-pilot a pilot must complete on that kind of aeroplane or rotorcraft to be qualified as a co-pilot for the aeroplane or rotorcraft.
Without limiting paragraph (4)(a), the description must include the following:
details of the training resources used in the training and checking;
details of the persons conducting the training and checking;
for each position in the operator’s organisation the holder of which has managerial or operational responsibilities under the system:
selection criteria for the position; and
the responsibilities of the position; and
details of the training, assessment and certification of competence that must be completed before the position-holder begins carrying out the position-holder’s responsibilities;
for each kind of training conducted by or for the operator—the minimum number of check pilots and the minimum crew qualifications required by the operator for the training (if any);
for each kind of training conducted by or for the operator—a course outline, detailed syllabus, standards to be met and record forms;
the requirements that a person conducting conversion training, other than flying training and training conducted in a flight simulator, must meet;
training checklists (if any) and the circumstances when use of a training checklist is permitted;
a description of the normal line operation covered by a line check;
command responsibility during flights for training and checking;
any general restrictions, specifications or safety precautions for training and checking (including in relation to fuel load, ballast and minimum weather conditions);
methods of conducting training and checking sequences including the following:
the standards to be achieved;
training sequences for common faults;
the method of simulating emergencies or malfunctions;
the procedure to be followed when a standard is not met;
details of how the operator will address matters of high risk that are identified by the operator’s safety management system.

section.heading: Requirements for other operational safety-critical personnel

content.p: The training and checking system must include the following in relation to operational safety-critical personnel who are not flight crew:
a description of how training and checking, including recurrent training, for the personnel is conducted by or for the operator;
an auditable system for maintaining records of the results of the training and checking;
the circumstances in which training is required to familiarise a member of the personnel with their duties;
the remedial training requirements for the personnel;
if the operator has a contract with a person for the person to conduct the training or checking for the operator:
details of the person; and
details of the training or checking covered by the contract; and
details of how the operator ensures that the person is complying with the operator’s training and checking system;
if any of the training or checking is conducted by a member of the personnel—a description of the operator’s system for training and assessing such personnel.
Without limiting paragraph (1)(a), the description must include the following:
any general restrictions, specifications or safety precautions for the training and checking;
for each kind of training conducted by or for the operator—a course outline, detailed syllabus, standards to be met and record forms;
the procedure to be followed when a standard is not met.

section.heading: Operators who are required to have a safety management system

content.p: An aerial work operator who conducts one or more of the following must have a safety management system:
aerial work operations transporting marine pilots;
operations in:
multi-engine transport category rotorcraft with a maximum take-off weight of more than 3,175 kg; or
multi-engine aeroplanes with a maximum take-off weight of more than 5,700 kg; or
turbine-engine aeroplanes (other than turbine-engine propeller-driven aeroplanes);
operations prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.

Despite subregulation (1), an aerial work operator is not required to have a safety management system for an aerial work operation conducted in an aeroplane or a rotorcraft if circumstances prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards apply to the aeroplane or rotorcraft and the operation.
The safety management system must meet the requirements of regulation 138.145.
The safety management system must include the following matters:
a statement of the operator’s safety policy and objectives, including details of the following:
the management commitment to, and responsibility for, safety;
the safety accountabilities of managers (including key personnel);
the appointment of safety management personnel;
coordination of an emergency response plan;
safety management system documentation;
a safety risk management process, including:
hazard identification processes; and
safety risk assessment and mitigation processes;
a safety assurance system, including details of processes for:
safety performance monitoring and measurement; and
management of change; and
continuous improvement of the safety management system;
a safety training and promotion system, including details of the following:
safety management system training and education;
safety management system safety communication.

section.heading: Operators who are required to have a crew fatigue management system

content.p: This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The aerial work operator must have a system for managing crew fatigue that meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An operations manual for an aerial work operator must include the following:
the operator’s name (including any operating or trading name), contact details and ABN (if any);
the address of:
the operator’s operational headquarters; and
each of the operator’s main operating bases;
a description and diagram of the operator’s organisational structure showing formal reporting lines, including the formal reporting lines for each of the key personnel;
if the operator is a corporation—a description of the operator’s corporate structure;
for each of the key personnel, the following information:
the qualifications and experience (if any) required by the operator for the position in addition to the qualifications and experience required under Division 138.B.4 for the position;
each matter (if any) for which the holder of the position is responsible in addition to the responsibilities mentioned in Division 138.B.4 for the position;
the name of the person appointed to the position;
the name of each person (if any) authorised to carry out the responsibilities of the position when the position holder is absent from the position or cannot carry out the responsibilities;
a description of how the operator will manage the responsibilities of the position during a circumstance mentioned in subparagraph (iv);
each matter (if any) for which the chief executive officer is responsible and accountable in addition to the matters mentioned in regulation 138.085;
an outline of the aerial work operations conducted by the operator under the operator’s aerial work certificate;
details of each plan, process, procedure, program and system implemented by the operator to safely conduct and manage their aerial work operations in compliance with the civil aviation legislation;
for each registered aircraft operated by the operator under their aerial work certificate—the kind of aircraft;
for each foreign registered aircraft operated by the operator under their aerial work certificate—the kind of aircraft and its nationality;
a description of the arrangements for managing the continuing airworthiness of the aircraft used by the operator under its aerial work certificate;
for operators that are not required to have a safety management system under regulation 138.140—a description of the operator’s safety policy;
a description of the operator’s process for making changes, including:
identifying changes that are significant changes; and
identifying changes that are not significant changes; and
telling CASA and the operator’s personnel of the changes;
a description of anything else required to be approved by CASA under these Regulations in relation to the operations mentioned in paragraph (g);
any other matter required to be included in the operations manual under these Regulations.
Note: The plans, processes, procedures, programs and systems mentioned in paragraph (h) may be set out in one or more operator manuals.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if the operator’s operations manual does not comply with subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Compliance with operations manual by operator

content.p: An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if the operator does not meet a requirement of the operator’s operations manual.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Compliance with operations manual by personnel

content.p: A member of an aerial work operator’s personnel contravenes this subregulation if:
the member is subject to a requirement in relation to an aircraft under the operator’s operations manual; and
the requirement relates to:
the operation of the aircraft; or
the safety of the aircraft, or of a person on board the aircraft or in the vicinity of the aircraft; and
the member does not meet the requirement.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
a member of the aerial work operator’s personnel is subject to a requirement in relation to an aircraft under the operator’s operations manual; and
the requirement relates to:
the operation of the aircraft; or
the safety of the aircraft, or of a person on board the aircraft or in the vicinity of the aircraft; and
the member does not meet the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator’s operations manual relates to a duty or responsibility of a person who is a member of the operator’s personnel; and
the operator does not make the part of the operations manual that relates to the duty or responsibility available to the person before the person first begins carrying out the duty or responsibility.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
a person who is a member of the operator’s personnel undertakes a training activity, obtains a qualification or certificate relating to aerial work operations or gains flying experience; and
the following records are not made within 21 days after the person undertakes the activity, obtains the qualification or certificate or gains the flying experience:
the date the activity was undertaken, the qualification or certificate obtained or the flying experience gained;
if the activity was training or a check, flight test, flight review or assessment of competency—whether the training, check, flight test, flight review or assessment was successfully completed.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator makes a record about a person under regulation 138.170; and
the person requests that the record be made available to the person; and
the operator does not make the record available to the person within 7 days after receiving the request.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
a record is made under regulation 138.170; and
the operator receives a request from another aerial work operator for a copy of the record; and
the operator holds a written authority from the person to whom the record relates to provide a copy of the person’s records to another aerial work operator if requested; and
the operator does not give a copy of the record to the other aerial work operator within 7 days after receiving the request.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Copies of flight crew licences and medical certificates

content.p: An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
a person who is a flight crew member of the operator’s personnel exercises a privilege of the person’s flight crew licence for the operator; and
the operator does not have the following:
a copy of the person’s flight crew licence;
a copy of the person’s medical certificate.

Note: A reference to a flight crew licence or medical certificate includes a certificate of validation of an overseas flight crew licence or overseas medical certificate: see the definitions of flight crew licence and medical certificate in Part 1 of the Dictionary.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is required under regulation 138.170 to make a record about a member of the operator’s personnel, other than a member mentioned in subregulation (2) of this regulation; and
the operator does not keep the record for the period beginning when the record is created and ending 5 years after the member ceases to be a member of the operator’s personnel.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is required under regulation 138.170 to make a record about a member of the operator’s personnel who carries out ground support duties; and
the operator does not keep the record for the period beginning when the record is created and ending 1 year after the member ceases to be a member of the operator’s personnel.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if the operator does not maintain a reference library that complies with subregulation (2).
For subregulation (1), the reference library must:
include the following documents:
all operational documents and material;
the civil aviation legislation that is relevant to the operator’s aerial work operations;
the parts of the AIP that are relevant to the operations;
documents that include information about each kind of aircraft operated, and each kind of aerial work operation conducted, by the operator;
any other material required for the reference library by the operator’s operations manual; and
be readily available to all members of the operator’s personnel; and
be up-to-date and in a readily accessible form; and
include a system for notifying the operator’s personnel of any updates to the documents mentioned in paragraph (a).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Maximum period for use of foreign registered aircraft in Australian territory

content.p: An aerial work operator contravenes this subregulation if, in a period mentioned in subregulation (2), the operator uses a particular foreign registered aircraft to conduct aerial work operations in Australian territory on a consecutive number of days during that period that is more than:
90; or
if the operator holds an approval under regulation 138.025 in relation to the aircraft—the number mentioned in the approval for the aircraft.
The periods are:
the 12 month period from the day the foreign registered aircraft first becomes available to conduct the aerial work operations in Australian territory; and
each subsequent 12 month period.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 138.C—General

section.heading: Permitted categories of aircraft for aerial work operations

content.p: The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
the aircraft is operated for a flight involving an aerial work operation; and
if the operation is covered by subregulation (2)—the aircraft is not type certificated in the normal, commuter or transport category; and
if the operation is not covered by subregulation (2)—the aircraft is not type certificated in the normal, commuter, transport, restricted or utility category.
An operation is covered by this subregulation if the operation is one in which the aircraft carries an aerial work passenger.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate.

The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if the aircraft is operated in a way during the flight that does not meet a requirement or limitation that:
is set out in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft; and
relates to the operation of the aircraft.
Subregulation (2) does not apply to a limitation or requirement if circumstances prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards apply to the aircraft for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.

The requirement is that, before a crew member for the aircraft begins to carry out a duty of the crew member’s position, the operator must make each checklist of normal, abnormal and emergency procedures for the aircraft that is relevant to the duty available to the crew member.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

To avoid doubt, if a document is required to be carried on a flight of an aircraft under this Division, that requirement is taken to be satisfied if an electronic copy of the document is carried on the flight.
Note: Electronic copies may not satisfy the requirements of the law of a foreign country for flights that begin or end at an aerodrome outside Australian territory.

section.heading: Availability of parts of operations manual

content.p: The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if the following parts of the aircraft operator’s operations manual are not available to a crew member for the flight before the flight begins:
a part that is relevant to the duties of the crew member for the flight;
a part that is required for the conduct of the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

division.heading: Reporting and recording defects and incidents etc.

section.heading: Procedures for reporting and recording defects etc.

content.p: An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures for the reporting and recording by a flight crew member for a flight of the aircraft of any of the following that occur during the flight:
an abnormal instrument indication;
abnormal behaviour by the aircraft;
exceedence of an operating limit specified in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft;
a defect in the aircraft.
Note: For other provisions dealing with aircraft defects, see Part 42 and regulation 37 of CAR.

An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures for the reporting and recording by crew members of incidents relating to a flight of an aircraft for an aerial work operation that endanger, or could endanger, the safe operation of the aircraft.

division.heading: Search and rescue services and emergency and survival equipment

content.p: Note: This Division is reserved for future use.
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.
Subpart 138.D—Operational procedures
Note: This Division is reserved for future use.
An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures for complying with the following for a flight of an aircraft involving an aerial work operation:
the flight preparation (weather assessments) requirements;
the flight preparation (alternate aerodromes) requirements.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met for the flight.
The requirements are the following:
the pilot in command of the aircraft must have access to the information mentioned in subregulation (3) before and during the flight;
each person in the operator’s organisation who is responsible for flight planning for the flight must have access to the information mentioned in subregulation (3) before the flight;
each person in the operator’s organisation who is responsible for flight replanning for the flight must have access to the information mentioned in subregulation (3) during the flight;
each person in the operator’s organisation who exercises operational control for the flight must have access to the information mentioned in subregulation (3) before and during the flight.
The information is the following:
authorised weather forecasts and authorised weather reports:
in relation to the flight; and
if a destination alternate aerodrome is required for the flight by the flight planning (alternate aerodromes) requirements—in relation to the destination alternate aerodrome;
NOTAMs for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Regulation 91.265, 91.267, 91.277 or 91.305 does not apply to a pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation if:
circumstances prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph apply to the aircraft and the operation; or
requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph are complied with in relation to the flight.
An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures to ensure the safety of persons in the vicinity of an aircraft when any of the following circumstances apply:
a person is embarking or disembarking the aircraft;
the aircraft is being loaded or unloaded;
the aircraft is on the ground with its engine or engines running;
the aircraft is landing or taking off at an aerodrome that is not a certified aerodrome.

An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures to ensure that a flight of an aircraft operated by the operator is conducted in accordance with the requirements mentioned in subregulation 91.455(1).

The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the aircraft is not carrying sufficient oil to complete the flight safely.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
the aircraft is hot fuelled; and
the following are not set out in the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft or the operator’s operations manual:
procedures for the hot fuelling of the aircraft;
the circumstances in which the aircraft can be hot fuelled;
procedures to be followed if an emergency occurs during hot fuelling;
procedures to ensure a person involved in hot fuelling the aircraft is trained and competent to be involved in hot fuelling the aircraft.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
a requirement of a procedure mentioned in subparagraph (1)(b)(i), (iii) or (iv) is not met in relation to the hot fuelling of the aircraft for the flight; or
the aircraft is hot fuelled in a circumstance that is not mentioned in subparagraph (1)(b)(ii).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the following in relation to an aircraft operated by the operator:
procedures to ensure the aircraft is fuelled safely;
procedures relating to the safety of:
any aerial work passengers; and
crew members other than air crew members, cabin crew members or flight crew members;
who are embarking or disembarking, or on board, the aircraft during fuelling, including the procedures mentioned in subregulation (2);

if the operator permits a person to operate low-risk electronic devices inside the cabin of the aircraft while the aircraft is being fuelled—procedures to ensure that, before an engine of the aircraft is started, any effects of radio frequency emissions from those devices have been corrected.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the procedures must include the normal, emergency and communication procedures to be followed by the following persons:
any air crew members;
any cabin crew members;
any flight crew members who are on duty in the cockpit of the aircraft;
any of the operator’s personnel who carry out a ground support duty for a flight of the aircraft.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is the operator, or the pilot in command, of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation; and
a passenger is carried on the aircraft for the flight; and
any of the following circumstances exist in relation to the flight:
the passenger is not an aerial work passenger;
when the passenger is carried on the aircraft, the operator of the flight does not hold an aerial work certificate authorising the operation;
when the passenger is carried on the aircraft, the operator’s operations manual does not include procedures to ensure the safety of the passenger;
any requirements about carrying the passenger that are prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subparagraph are not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Procedures for carriage of restricted persons

content.p: An aerial work operator’s operations manual must state whether or not the operator will carry restricted persons as part of aerial work operations.

section.heading: Head-up displays, enhanced vision systems and synthetic vision systems

content.p: This regulation applies to an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation if:
the aircraft is fitted with any of the following systems:
a head-up display;
an enhanced vision system;
a synthetic vision system; and
the flight is:
an IFR flight; or
a VFR flight at night.
An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the following:
procedures for using each system mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) that is fitted to an aircraft for a flight mentioned in paragraph (1)(b);
procedures for conducting such a flight without an element of the system, for use if the element is inoperative.
This regulation applies to a flight of an aircraft if:
the flight is in or through an area prescribed as a remote area by the Part 91 Manual of Standards; or
the aircraft is required, under Subpart 138.K, to carry a life raft for the flight.
If an aircraft is, or will be, used to conduct a flight to which this regulation applies, an aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the following:
procedures for determining the survival equipment required for the area in or through which the flight will be conducted;

(b) for a flight mentioned in paragraph (1)(b)—procedures for determining the pyrotechnic signalling devices required to ensure the distress signals, set out in Appendix 1 to Annex 2, Rules of the Air, to the Chicago Convention, can be made.
This regulation applies to a flight of an aircraft if:
the flight involves use of a night vision imaging system; and
the flight is:
an IFR flight; or
a VFR flight at night.
An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the following:
procedures for using a night vision imaging system during a flight to which subregulation (1) applies;
procedures for conducting such a flight without an element of a night vision imaging system, for use if the element is inoperative.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for the use of a night vision imaging system for a flight of an aircraft.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight each contravene this subregulation if:
a night vision imaging system is used during the flight; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
risk criteria that must be met to conduct an aerial work operation; and
risk assessment and mitigation processes to be undertaken before conducting an aerial work operation.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) applies for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Wearing of seatbelts and other restraint devices

content.p: The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the wearing of seatbelts or other restraint devices during aerial work operations.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Procedures in relation to frost etc.

content.p: An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the following:
procedures for the inspection of the aircraft by the pilot in command before a flight for which frost or freezing conditions exist or are forecast;
procedures for carrying out de-icing and anti-icing measures before a flight for which these measures are necessary;
procedures for using de-icing and anti-icing equipment during a flight.

section.heading: Procedures in relation to polar operations

content.p: This regulation applies to an aircraft if it is used to conduct a flight to or from an aerodrome in a polar region.
The aerial work operator’s operations manual must include procedures for the following:
monitoring and dealing with fuel freezing;
ensuring communication capability for the duration of an operation that includes a flight mentioned in subregulation (1);
training the aircraft’s flight crew in polar operations;
ensuring that maintenance personnel who will carry out maintenance on the aircraft in a polar region are appropriately trained;
mitigating crew member and aerial work passenger exposure to cosmic radiation during solar flare activity;

if the aircraft will not be flown over water during a flight mentioned in subregulation (1) and it is reasonably likely a normal or emergency landing will expose persons on the aircraft to the polar environment in a location without support personnel immediately available—ensuring that each person on the aircraft will wear a serviceable, cold-weather, anti-exposure suit;

if the aircraft will be flown over water during a flight mentioned in subregulation (1) and it is reasonably likely that an emergency landing will expose the persons on the aircraft to a landing on or in water—ensuring that each person on the aircraft will wear an immersion suit that is appropriate for the temperatures in which the flight will be conducted;

dealing with emergency landings, or instruments, indicators, equipment or systems becoming inoperative, while the aircraft is away from the base for an operation that includes a flight mentioned in subregulation (1).

section.heading: Certain night operations prohibited unless operation is an emergency service operation or approved by CASA

content.p: This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if:
the operation is an external load operation at night; and
the operation is not conducted as part of an emergency service operation; and
the requirement in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirement is that the operator must hold an approval under regulation 138.025 to conduct the operation at night.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for external load operations

content.p: This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to flights of aircraft involving external load operations.
Without limiting subregulation (2), the Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe classes of external loads.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4) or (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for dispensing operations

content.p: This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to dispensing operations.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements for task specialist operations

content.p: This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to flights of aircraft involving task specialist operations.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if:
either or both of the following apply for the flight:
a person carries or otherwise possesses a firearm on an aircraft;
a person discharges a firearm while on an aircraft; and
a requirement prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies despite regulations 91.160, 91.165 and 91.190.
Subpart 138.F—Performance
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to take-off performance for a flight of an aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (2), the Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements that relate to one or more of the following:
the kinds of operations to be carried out during the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft takes off;
characteristics of the route flown by the aircraft;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft lands.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4) or (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to landing performance for a flight of an aircraft.
Without limiting subregulation (2), the Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to one or more of the following:
the aircraft’s configuration;
the operation of any equipment for the flight;
characteristics of the aerodrome at which the aircraft lands;
safety factor percentages to be applied.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) for the flight; and
the requirement is not met for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4) or (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 138.J—Weight and balance
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate.

The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins, the aircraft is loaded in a way that contravenes the aircraft’s weight and balance limits.

The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if, during the flight, the aircraft ceases to be loaded in accordance with the aircraft’s weight and balance limits.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe the weight and balance documents that are required for flights involving aerial work operations, and requirements in relation to those documents.
The operator and the pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation each contravene this subregulation if, when the flight begins:
weight and balance documents for the flight are required by the Part 138 Manual of Standards; and
either:
there are no weight and balance documents for the flight; or
the weight and balance documents for the flight do not comply with the requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 138.K—Equipment
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
the fitment and non-fitment of equipment to an aircraft; and
the carrying of equipment on an aircraft; and
equipment that is fitted to, or carried on, an aircraft.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 138.N—Flight crew
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are as follows:
the composition of the aircraft’s flight crew for the flight must comply with the aircraft flight manual instructions for the aircraft;
if the aerial work operation is one for which the operator’s operations manual requires the carriage of additional flight crew members—the flight crew must include the additional flight crew members;
each flight crew member must:
if the aircraft is an Australian aircraft—be authorised to pilot the aircraft during the flight under Part 61; or
if the aircraft is a foreign registered aircraft—be authorised to pilot the aircraft during the flight by the aircraft’s State of registry;
each flight crew member must meet the training and checking requirements for the flight crew member and the flight mentioned in subregulation (3).
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by a flight crew member for a flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training for new or inexperienced flight crew members

content.p: An aerial work operator’s operations manual must include the requirements that must be met for new or inexperienced flight crew members to be assigned to duty on the aircraft for an aerial work operation conducted by the operator.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a person to duty as a flight crew member for the flight; and
the person has not been assessed by the operator as competent to perform the duties assigned to the person for the flight in accordance with the operator’s operations manual.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Assignment to duty of pilot in command

content.p: The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, none of the pilots assigned as flight crew members for the flight is assigned to duty as the pilot in command of the aircraft for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This regulation applies to the operator of an aircraft for an aerial work operation whether or not the operator holds an aerial work certificate authorising the operation.
A pilot is qualified as pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation if:
the pilot is:
if the aircraft is an Australian aircraft—authorised under Part 61 to carry out, in relation to the flight, the duties assigned to the pilot by the operator of the flight; or

if the aircraft is a foreign registered aircraft—authorised by the aircraft’s State of registry to carry out, in relation to the flight, the duties assigned to the pilot by the operator of the flight; and
the pilot has the qualifications and experience required by the operator’s operations manual (if any) for the flight; and
the pilot has the qualifications and experience prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards for the flight.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
the pilot performs a duty as pilot in command for the flight; and
the pilot is not qualified under subregulation (1) as pilot in command for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator assigns a pilot to duty as pilot in command of the aircraft for the flight; and
the pilot is not qualified under subregulation (1) as pilot in command for the flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (2A).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training and checking to be conducted by certain persons

content.p: The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
a flight crew member of the operator’s personnel undertakes training or a check mentioned in this Subpart; and
the training or check is conducted other than in accordance with subregulation (2).
The training or check must be conducted by:
an individual who:
is engaged by the operator (whether by contract or other arrangement) to conduct the training or check; and
meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards; or
a Part 142 operator with which the operator has a contract for the Part 142 operator to conduct the training or check for the operator.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 138.P—Air crew members and task specialists
This Division applies in relation to an operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation if an air crew member is carried on the aircraft for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are as follows:
if the aerial work operation is one for which the operator’s operations manual requires the carriage of air crew members—those air crew members must be carried on the flight;
each air crew member must meet the training and checking requirements for the air crew member and the flight mentioned in subregulation (3).
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by an air crew member for a flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training and checking to be conducted by certain persons

content.p: The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
an air crew member of the operator’s personnel undertakes training or a check mentioned in this Subpart; and
the training or check is conducted other than in accordance with subregulation (2).
The training or check must be conducted by an individual:
who is engaged by the operator (whether by contract or other arrangement) to conduct the training or check; and
who meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
This Division applies in relation to an operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation if a task specialist is carried on the aircraft for the flight.
The operator of an aircraft for a flight involving an aerial work operation contravenes this subregulation if, when the flight begins, a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2) is not met.
The requirements are as follows:
if the aerial work operation is one for which the operator’s operations manual requires the carriage of task specialists—those task specialists must be carried on the flight;
each task specialist must meet the training and checking requirements for the task specialist and the flight mentioned in subregulation (3).
The Part 138 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to training and checking that must be completed by a task specialist for a flight.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Training and checking to be conducted by certain persons

content.p: The operator of an aircraft contravenes this subregulation if:
a task specialist of the operator’s personnel undertakes training or a check mentioned in this Subpart; and
the training or check is conducted other than in accordance with subregulation (2).
The training or check must be conducted by an individual:
who is engaged by the operator (whether by contract or other arrangement) to conduct the training or check; and
who meets the requirements prescribed by the Part 138 Manual of Standards.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
