Subpart 139.A—Preliminary
• The operator of an aerodrome may apply to CASA for an aerodrome certificate. An aerodrome that has an aerodrome certificate is a certified aerodrome.
• Certain aerodromes are required to be certified. Generally these are aerodromes with terminal instrument flight procedures. Other aerodromes can opt to become certified.

• The operator of a certified aerodrome must meet certain requirements for operating and maintaining the aerodrome. The Part 139 Manual of Standards has detailed requirements (which may be different for different classes of aerodrome).
• An aerodrome (whether certified or not) that provides a frequency confirmation service or air/ground radio service must also meet certain requirements.

• Some objects, structures or emissions sources can create a hazard to aircraft operations at an aerodrome and more generally. CASA can make determinations that such things are hazards, and must be notified of proposed building or other activity that will potentially create such hazards.
• Providers of aerodrome rescue and firefighting services must be approved by CASA and must comply with operating and technical standards.

Note 1: Aerodrome is defined in section 3 of the Act. For the reference in that definition to an area being authorised under the regulations for use as an aerodrome, see also regulations 91.410 and 121.205.
Note 2: There are requirements relating to aerodromes that are not in this Part. For example:
aerodrome operators may have obligations about drug and alcohol management plans (Part 99), or as aeronautical data originators (Part 175); and
aerodromes may need to meet certain requirements to support operational rules that apply to aircraft operators and pilots (such as in Part 121).

Note 3: Other legislation apart from these Regulations may regulate aspects of aerodromes, such as the Air Navigation Act 1920, the Airports Act 1996, the Air Services Act 1995, the Airspace Act 2007 and regulations made under those Acts.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 139

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
If a provision of this Part refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, a person may apply to CASA, in writing, for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, the approval must be granted.
Subregulation 11.055(1B) applies to the granting of an approval under this regulation.

section.heading: Effect on operation of other laws

content.p: Nothing in this Part affects the operation of the following:
(a) the Airports (Building Control) Regulations 2025;
(b) the Airports (Protection of Airspace) Regulations 2026;
(c) the Airports (Control of On-Airport Activities) Regulations 2026.
Subpart 139.B—Aerodrome certificates
A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for an aerodrome certificate for an aerodrome.
The application must be accompanied by a copy of the applicant’s proposed aerodrome manual for the aerodrome.
Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to an aerodrome certificate.

section.heading: When aerodromes are required to have an aerodrome certificate

content.p: The operator of an aerodrome must hold an aerodrome certificate for the aerodrome if:
there is a terminal instrument flight procedure for the aerodrome; and
the procedure is not only for use in a specialised helicopter operation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant an aerodrome certificate to an applicant if CASA is satisfied that:
the aerodrome facilities and equipment comply with this Part and the Part 139 Manual of Standards; and
the proposed aerodrome manual for the aerodrome complies with the requirements mentioned in regulation 139.045; and
the aerodrome complies with the requirements that apply in relation to the aerodrome under Division 139.C.4 (safety management, emergency preparedness and other systems); and

(d) the applicant would, if the certificate were granted, be able to operate and maintain the aerodrome safely and in accordance with the aerodrome manual for the aerodrome and the civil aviation legislation.

section.heading: Suspension or cancellation of aerodrome certificate by CASA

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to the holder of an aerodrome certificate, suspend or cancel the certificate if CASA reasonably believes that:
the aerodrome facilities and equipment do not comply with this Part or the Part 139 Manual of Standards; or
the aerodrome manual for the aerodrome does not comply with the requirements mentioned in regulation 139.045; or
the aerodrome does not comply with the requirements that apply in relation to the aerodrome under Division 139.C.4 (safety management, emergency preparedness and other systems); or
the holder is not operating or maintaining the aerodrome safely and in accordance with the aerodrome manual for the aerodrome and the civil aviation legislation; or
the holder has failed to operate and maintain the aerodrome with a reasonable degree of care and diligence; or
a condition to which the certificate is subject has been breached; or
the aerodrome facilities and equipment, or the operations or maintenance of the aerodrome, are not of the standard necessary in the interests of the safety of air navigation; or
the holder has failed to comply with regulation 139.135.
Before suspending or cancelling an aerodrome certificate, CASA must:
give to the holder a show cause notice that:
sets out the facts and circumstances that, in the opinion of CASA, would justify the suspension or cancellation; and
invites the holder to show cause, in writing, within 30 days after the date of the notice, why the certificate should not be suspended or cancelled; and
take into account any written submissions that the holder makes to CASA within the time allowed under subparagraph (a)(ii).
Suspension or cancellation under this regulation has effect:
if a time is specified in the notice given by CASA under subregulation (1)—at that time; or
otherwise—at the time the holder is given the written notice under subregulation (1).
Suspension under this regulation ceases to have effect:
if the notice given by CASA under subregulation (1) specifies a time at which the suspension is to cease—at that time; or
otherwise—at the time CASA directs, by written notice to the person who, immediately before the suspension, was the holder of the aerodrome certificate.
If an aerodrome certificate is suspended under this regulation, the certificate is not in force during the period of the suspension.

section.heading: Notification requirement if aerodrome ceases to be certified

content.p: The operator of an aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator holds an aerodrome certificate for the aerodrome; and
the aerodrome ceases to be a certified aerodrome because the aerodrome certificate has been suspended or cancelled under these Regulations or the Act; and
the operator does not, as soon as possible after the cessation, give written notice of the cessation to:
the AIS; and

if the aerodrome has one or more terminal instrument flight procedures—each certified designer (within the meaning of regulation 173.015) responsible for maintaining a terminal instrument flight procedure for the aerodrome.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Subpart 139.C—Operation and maintenance of a certified aerodrome
(1) The operator of a certified aerodrome must have an aerodrome manual for the aerodrome that complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
the information that must be included in an aerodrome manual;
keeping an aerodrome manual up-to-date;
the accessibility of an aerodrome manual.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the operator does not comply with the requirement.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
If the operator of a certified aerodrome amends the aerodrome manual for the aerodrome, the operator must:
give CASA written notice of the amendment and a copy of the amended part of the aerodrome manual clearly identifying the amendment; and
do so within 30 days after the amendment is made.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
(1) The operator of a certified aerodrome must operate the aerodrome in accordance with the procedures set out in the aerodrome’s aerodrome manual.
Note: Section 3 of the Act defines operate, in relation to an aerodrome, to include manage, maintain and improve the aerodrome.
However, subregulation (1) does not apply to the operator if:
the operator does not comply with the procedures set out in the aerodrome’s aerodrome manual; and
the non-compliance is necessary to ensure the safety of aircraft, aircraft operations or individuals using the aerodrome; and
the operator tells CASA of the non-compliance in accordance with regulation 139.060.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Notice of non-compliance with aerodrome manual

content.p: This regulation applies if the operator of a certified aerodrome does not comply with a procedure set out in the aerodrome’s aerodrome manual as mentioned in paragraphs 139.055(2)(a) and (b).
The operator must tell CASA, in writing, of the non-compliance within 30 days after the non-compliance.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to aerodrome facilities and equipment for certified aerodromes.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
the physical characteristics of the movement area of an aerodrome;
visual aids for the movement area and other areas of an aerodrome;
the maintenance of visual aids at an aerodrome;
wind direction indicators at an aerodrome;
visual approach slope indicator systems at an aerodrome;
lighting systems at an aerodrome;
reference code systems at an aerodrome;
the installation, operation or maintenance of aerodrome facilities and equipment;
access to an aerodrome, including requirements relating to fencing for the aerodrome;
design requirements to avoid the creation of hazards from aircraft propulsion systems at an aerodrome.
The operator of a certified aerodrome must ensure that the aerodrome facilities and equipment for the aerodrome comply with the requirements mentioned in subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Planning and carrying out aerodrome works

content.p: The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
planning aerodrome works at a certified aerodrome;
giving notice of planned aerodrome works at a certified aerodrome;
carrying out aerodrome works at a certified aerodrome.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
The operator of a certified aerodrome must ensure that any aerodrome works at the aerodrome are carried out in a way that does not create a hazard to aircraft or cause confusion to pilots.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to aerodrome inspections.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
different kinds of inspections that must be conducted;
aerodrome facilities and equipment that must be inspected as part of inspections;
when inspections must be conducted;
the qualifications and experience of persons conducting inspections;
records of inspections that the operator of an aerodrome must keep;
reports of inspections that the operator of an aerodrome must provide to CASA;
notifications that the operator of an aerodrome must give to CASA in relation to matters identified in inspections.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operator of a certified aerodrome reporting information to an AIS provider.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
information that must be reported;
the form and manner in which information must be reported;
establishing procedures for reporting.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Reporting changes or occurrences at aerodromes

content.p: The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to reporting changes or occurrences at certified aerodromes.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
changes or occurrences at a certified aerodrome that must be reported;
persons to whom changes or occurrences must be reported;
how changes or occurrences must be reported;
information that must be reported;
the form and manner in which information must be reported;
establishing procedures for reporting.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to:
monitoring the airspace around a certified aerodrome for infringements, or potential infringements, of the airspace; and
reporting such infringements, or potential infringements.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
monitoring the obstacle limitation surfaces of an aerodrome;
monitoring other surfaces and obstacles associated with the airspace around an aerodrome;
establishing procedures for monitoring;
kinds of infringements that must be monitored for and reported;
persons to whom infringements must be reported;
how infringements must be reported;
information that must be reported;
the form and manner in which information must be reported;
establishing procedures for reporting.
To avoid doubt, and without limiting subregulation (1) or (2), an infringement of airspace may include a gaseous efflux or other emissions source that affects the airspace.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1); and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

division.heading: Safety management, emergency preparedness and other systems

section.heading: Safety management systems and risk management plans

content.p: The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe:
the circumstances in which a certified aerodrome must have a safety management system; and
requirements relating to safety management systems for aerodromes; and
the circumstances in which a certified aerodrome must have a risk management plan; and
requirements relating to risk management plans for aerodromes.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the Part 139 Manual of Standards requires the aerodrome to have a safety management system; and
any of the following apply:
the aerodrome does not have a safety management system;
a requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) that applies in relation to the safety management system for the aerodrome is not met;
a procedure under the safety management system for the aerodrome is not complied with.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the Part 139 Manual of Standards requires the aerodrome to have a risk management plan; and
either:
the aerodrome does not have a risk management plan; or
a requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(d) that applies in relation to the risk management plan for the aerodrome is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Emergency preparedness and aerodrome emergency plans

content.p: The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe:
requirements relating to emergency preparedness of aerodromes; and
the circumstances in which a certified aerodrome must have an aerodrome emergency plan; and
requirements relating to aerodrome emergency plans for aerodromes.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
maintaining and reviewing aerodrome emergency plans;
conducting emergency exercises to test the adequacy of procedures and facilities provided for in an aerodrome emergency plan;
keeping and retaining records of reviews of an aerodrome emergency plan and exercises conducted to test the plan.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the operator is subject to a requirement relating to emergency preparedness mentioned in paragraph (1)(a); and
the requirement is not met.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the Part 139 Manual of Standards requires the aerodrome to have an aerodrome emergency plan; and
either:
the aerodrome does not have an aerodrome emergency plan; or
a requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(c) that applies in relation to the aerodrome emergency plan for the aerodrome is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe:
a kind of system (other than a safety management system) that an aerodrome must have, including (but not limited to) the following:
a wildlife hazard management system;
an airside vehicle control system;
an aircraft parking control system; and
the circumstances in which a certified aerodrome must have a system of a kind mentioned in paragraph (a); and
requirements relating to that kind of system.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the Part 139 Manual of Standards requires the aerodrome to have a system of a kind mentioned in paragraph (1)(a); and
any of the following apply:
the aerodrome does not have a system of that kind;
a requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(c) that applies in relation to the system for the aerodrome is not met;
a procedure under the system for the aerodrome is not complied with.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Requirement to have personnel
The operator of a certified aerodrome must have personnel who carry out the responsibilities of the following positions for the aerodrome:
accountable manager;
reporting officer;
if aerodrome works are being carried out at the aerodrome—works safety officer;
any other position prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
Without limiting subregulation (1):
the personnel of an operator of a certified aerodrome may include any of the following persons:
an employee of the operator;
a person engaged by the operator (whether by contract or other arrangement) to provide services to the operator;
an employee of a person mentioned in subparagraph (ii); and
more than one person may carry out the responsibilities of a position mentioned in subregulation (1).
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if the operator does not have the personnel for the aerodrome mentioned in subregulation (1).
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 20 penalty units.
Accountable manager
The responsibilities of an accountable manager for a certified aerodrome are:
ensuring that the operator of the aerodrome complies with the civil aviation legislation; and
ensuring that the operator of the aerodrome operates and maintains the aerodrome safely and with a reasonable degree of care and diligence; and
ensuring that the operator of the aerodrome operates and maintains the aerodrome in accordance with the aerodrome manual for the aerodrome.
Reporting officer
The responsibilities of a reporting officer for a certified aerodrome are:
monitoring the serviceability of the aerodrome; and
reporting information to AIS providers as required under regulation 139.080; and
reporting changes or occurrences at the aerodrome as required under regulation 139.085; and
monitoring airspace and reporting as required under regulation 139.090.
Works safety officer
The responsibilities of a works safety officer for a certified aerodrome are ensuring aerodrome safety while aerodrome works are being carried out at the aerodrome.

The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the training, knowledge, qualifications or experience of personnel carrying out the responsibilities of positions mentioned in subregulation 139.110(1).
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
a person who is a member of the operator’s personnel for the aerodrome carries out the responsibilities of a position mentioned in subregulation 139.110(1); and
the person does not meet the requirements relating to the position mentioned in subregulation (1) of this regulation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 20 penalty units.
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to personnel carrying out the responsibilities of positions mentioned in subregulation 139.110(1).
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
a person who is a member of the operator’s personnel for the aerodrome carries out the responsibilities of a position mentioned in subregulation 139.110(1); and
the person does not meet a requirement relating to the position mentioned in subregulation (1) of this regulation.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 20 penalty units.

section.heading: Condition on aerodrome certificate to operate aerodrome ground surveillance system

content.p: Request by ATS provider for condition to be imposed or varied
An ATS provider for a certified aerodrome may request CASA:
to impose a condition on the aerodrome certificate that an aerodrome ground surveillance system must operate in relation to one or more areas of the aerodrome; or
if such a condition has been imposed on the aerodrome certificate—to vary the condition.
A request under paragraph (1)(a) must:
specify the areas of the aerodrome in relation to which the aerodrome ground surveillance system is to operate; and

include a safety assessment demonstrating that the use of an aerodrome ground surveillance system is necessary to ensure the safe control of aircraft and vehicles operating in those areas of the aerodrome.
A request under paragraph (1)(b) must:
if the variation includes a change to the areas of the aerodrome in relation to which an aerodrome ground surveillance system operates—specify the changes to those areas; and

include a safety assessment demonstrating that the requested variation in relation to the use of an aerodrome ground surveillance system is necessary to ensure the safe control of aircraft and vehicles operating in the relevant areas of the aerodrome.
Before making a request under subregulation (1), the ATS provider must consult the operator of the aerodrome in relation to the request.
CASA may impose or vary condition
CASA may, in accordance with regulation 11.067:
impose the condition mentioned in subregulation (1) of this regulation on an aerodrome certificate; or
if such a condition has been imposed on the aerodrome certificate—vary the condition.
Note: For breach of a condition imposed under regulation 11.067, see the offence in regulation 11.077.
The condition may include requirements relating to the aerodrome ground surveillance system to be operated.
The condition, or variation of the condition, may be different from the condition or variation requested by the ATS provider.
Notice of decisions etc.
If CASA decides to impose or vary the condition mentioned in subregulation (1):
CASA must give notice of the decision to both the ATS provider and the holder of the aerodrome certificate; and
the time the condition or variation takes effect must not be less than 6 months after the date of the notice of the decision.
If CASA decides to refuse a request from an ATS provider under subregulation (1), CASA must:
give written notice of the decision, and the reasons for the decision, to the ATS provider; and
do so as soon as practicable.
CASA’s other powers to impose or vary conditions not affected
This regulation does not limit any other power of CASA to impose a condition on an aerodrome certificate or vary a condition of an aerodrome certificate.
Note: See for example the powers in regulations 11.056, 11.067 and 11.068.

section.heading: Requirements for aerodrome ground surveillance systems

content.p: The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to aerodrome ground surveillance systems.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
surveillance and communications equipment that must be installed on vehicles moving in areas of an aerodrome in which an aerodrome ground surveillance system operates;
establishing procedures for vehicle movements in areas of an aerodrome in which an aerodrome ground surveillance system operates.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
it is a condition of the aerodrome certificate that an aerodrome ground surveillance system operate in relation to the aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (1) applies in relation to the aerodrome ground surveillance system; and
the requirement is not met.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 25 penalty units.

section.heading: Access to aerodromes to conduct tests

content.p: (1) The operator of a certified aerodrome must allow CASA to conduct tests of aerodrome facilities and equipment for the aerodrome, or operating procedures at the aerodrome, for the purpose of ensuring the safety of aircraft.

(2) The operator must allow CASA access to any part of the aerodrome, any aerodrome facilities and equipment for the aerodrome or any of the operator’s records relating to the aerodrome for the purposes of subregulation (1).
CASA:
must give reasonable notice of any tests to be conducted to the operator; and
must carry out the tests at a reasonable time.
(4) The operation of regulation 305 of CAR is not limited by subregulation (1) or (2) of this regulation.

section.heading: Requests for data from aerodrome operator

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to the operator of a certified aerodrome, request the operator to provide aircraft movement data of a kind prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe data relating to the following:
the number of aircraft using the aerodrome;
the type of aircraft using the aerodrome.
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
CASA gives the person a request under subregulation (1); and
the person does not comply with the request within the period mentioned in subregulation (4).
The person must comply with the request within:
if paragraph (b) does not apply—28 days after the request is given; or
if CASA specifies a longer period in the request—that period.
Subregulation (3) does not apply if:
the person does not possess the data requested; and
the person has taken all reasonable steps available to the person to obtain the data requested and has been unable to obtain the data.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Requests for data from ATS providers

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to an ATS provider, request the ATS provider to provide aircraft movement data of a kind prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this subregulation.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe data relating to the following:
the number of aircraft using an aerodrome;
the type of aircraft using an aerodrome;
the nature of the operations undertaken by aircraft at an aerodrome;
(d) the flight rules applying to aircraft at an aerodrome.
The ATS provider must comply with the request within:
if paragraph (b) does not apply—28 days after the request is given; or
if CASA specifies a longer period in the request—that period.
Subpart 139.D—Aerodrome radiocommunication services
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe:
the circumstances in which a certified aerodrome must have a frequency confirmation system for the aerodrome; and
requirements relating to frequency confirmation systems for aerodromes.
The operator of an aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the aerodrome has a frequency confirmation system; and
a requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) that applies in relation to the frequency confirmation system for the aerodrome is not met.
The operator of a certified aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
the Part 139 Manual of Standards requires the aerodrome to have a frequency confirmation system; and
the aerodrome does not have a frequency confirmation system.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2) or (3).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Air/ground radio service must be approved

content.p: The operator of an aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
there is an air/ground radio service for the aerodrome; and
the operator does not hold an approval under regulation 139.010 for the air/ground radio service.

CASA may grant an approval mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) only if CASA is satisfied that the service meets the requirements for an air/ground radio service prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to approval of an air/ground radio service.
(4) An air/ground radio service for which there is an approval mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) is a certified air/ground radio service.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.

section.heading: Requirements for operating certified air/ground radio service

content.p: Operator of radio service must hold approval
The operator of an aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
there is a certified air/ground radio service for the aerodrome; and
the service is operated by a person who does not hold an approval under regulation 139.010 to operate the service.

CASA may grant an approval mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) only if CASA is satisfied that the person meets the requirements for operating a certified air/ground radio service prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements
The Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the operation of certified air/ground radio services.
(4) Without limiting subregulation (3), the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe requirements relating to the following:
the facilities to be provided for the operation of a certified air/ground radio service;
when a certified air/ground radio service must be operating for an aerodrome;
documenting operational procedures for a certified air/ground radio service;
information and notifications about a certified air/ground radio service for an aerodrome that the operator of the aerodrome must provide to the NOTAM Office.
The operator of an aerodrome contravenes this subregulation if:
there is a certified air/ground radio service for the aerodrome; and
a requirement mentioned in subregulation (3) applies in relation to the service; and
the requirement is not met.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1) or (5).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Subpart 139.E—Hazards to aircraft operations

section.heading: Notifying CASA of certain proposed objects or structures

content.p: This regulation applies if a person proposes to construct or erect an object or structure that:
will have a height of 100 metres or more above ground level; or
will include an emissions source that generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
The person must, as soon as practicable after forming the intention to construct or erect the proposed object or structure, give written notice to CASA of the following:
the proposal;
the proposed height and location of the object or structure;
if the object or structure includes an emissions source—the details of the velocity and location of the emissions;
the proposed timeframe for constructing or erecting the object or structure;
any other information about the proposal that is prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The kinds of objects or structures that may be prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards under paragraph (1)(c) are not limited by paragraph (1)(a) or (b).
Note: See also Subpart 175.E in relation to requests for data about objects or structures that affect aviation safety.

section.heading: Notifying CASA of activities that create certain emissions sources

content.p: This regulation applies if a person proposes to undertake an activity (other than constructing or erecting an object or structure) that will create an emissions source that:
generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards.
The person must, as soon as practicable after forming the intention to undertake the proposed activity, give written notice to CASA of the following:
the proposal;
the proposed location of the activity;
the proposed timeframe for undertaking the activity;
the details of the emissions source that will be created;
any other information about the proposal that is prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards for the purposes of this paragraph.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
The kinds of emissions sources that may be prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards under paragraph (1)(b) are not limited by paragraph (1)(a).

section.heading: Determination that certain existing objects, structures or emissions sources are a hazard to aircraft operations

content.p: CASA may determine, in writing, that an object or structure that:
has a height of 100 metres or more above ground level; or
includes an emissions source that generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind mentioned in regulation 139.185;
is a hazard to aircraft operations.
CASA may determine, in writing, that an emissions source that:
generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind mentioned in regulation 139.185;
is a hazard to aircraft operations.
If CASA makes a determination under subregulation (1) or (2), CASA must:

publish in the AIP or NOTAMS the particulars of the hazard to which the determination relates, unless the hazard is of a kind that the operator of a certified aerodrome is required to report under Division 139.C.3 (aerodrome inspections, monitoring and reporting); and
if CASA can identify a person who owns, or is in occupation or control of, the object, structure or emissions source—give written notice of the determination to the person.

section.heading: Determination that certain proposed objects, structures or emissions sources are a hazard to aircraft operations

content.p: If there is a proposal to construct or erect an object or structure that:
will have a height of 100 metres or more above ground level; or
will include an emissions source that generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind mentioned in regulation 139.185;
CASA may determine, in writing, that the proposed object or structure will be a hazard to aircraft operations.
If there is a proposal to undertake an activity (other than constructing or erecting an object or structure) that will create an emissions source that:
generates a gaseous efflux with a velocity exceeding 4.3 metres per second at the point of emission; or
is of a kind mentioned in regulation 139.185;
CASA may determine, in writing, that the proposed activity will be a hazard to aircraft operations.
If CASA makes a determination under subregulation (1) or (2), CASA must give written notice of the determination to:
the person proposing to construct or erect the object or structure, or undertake the activity; and
if the approval of an authority is required to construct or erect the object or structure, or undertake the activity—the authority.

section.heading: Kinds of objects, structures or emissions sources that may be hazards

content.p: For the purposes of regulations 139.175 and 139.180, the Part 139 Manual of Standards may prescribe:
kinds of objects or structures that may constitute a hazard to aircraft operations; and
kinds of emissions sources that may constitute a hazard to aircraft operations.
The kinds of objects or structures that may be prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards under subregulation (1) are not limited by paragraph 139.175(1)(a) or (b) or 139.180(1)(a) or (b).
The kinds of emissions sources that may be prescribed by the Part 139 Manual of Standards under subregulation (1) are not limited by paragraph 139.175(2)(a) or 139.180(2)(a).
Note: For powers to remove or mark hazards affecting an aerodrome, see the following:
Division 9 of Part 9 of CAR;
(b) the Civil Aviation (Buildings Control) Regulations 1988;
(c) Part 12 of the Airports Act 1996 and the Airports (Protection of Airspace) Regulations 2026.
Subpart 139.H—Aerodrome rescue and firefighting services

Note: As a signatory to the Chicago Convention, Australia is obliged to require, as part of its domestic law, that certain classes of airport provide rescue and firefighting services of an adequate standard. (See generally section 9.2 of chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention.) To satisfy that obligation, this Subpart requires operators of aerodromes that have scheduled international traffic, or specified levels of domestic passenger traffic, to provide those services, and sets out the standards that apply to such services. Aerodromes that are not obliged to provide an ARFFS may choose to do so, and this Subpart will apply to a service so provided until the operator gives reasonable notice that it will no longer provide such a service.
This Subpart applies to aerodrome rescue and firefighting services.
This Subpart sets out:
how a person receives approval as a provider of an aerodrome rescue and firefighting service; and
the operating and technical standards applicable to such a service.
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Subpart, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for approval as a provider of an aerodrome rescue and firefighting service.
This Subpart does not apply to:
a person who is providing an aerodrome rescue and firefighting service in the course of his or her duties for the Defence Force; or
any aerodrome rescue and firefighting service provided by the Defence Force.
In this Subpart:
airside of an aerodrome has the same meaning as airside of an airport in the Airports Act 1996.
ARFFS means aerodrome rescue and fire-fighting service.
ARFFS operation means an operation undertaken in carrying out a function mentioned in paragraph 139.710(1)(a) or (b).
ARFFS provider for an aerodrome means the person or organisation that provides ARFFS for the aerodrome.
category of an aerodrome means its category worked out by the method set out in section 9.2 of chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention.
ERSA means the part of AIP known as En Route Supplement Australia.
Manual of Standards means the document called ‘Manual of Standards (MOS) – Subpart 139.H’ issued by CASA under regulation 139.712, as in force from time to time.
A reference in this Subpart to an AFC certificate of a particular level is a reference to:
a certificate of that level issued under the Australian Fire Competencies Scheme (that is, the training scheme administered by the Australian Fire Authorities Council); or

a certificate accepted by CASA as indicating that the certificate holder has successfully completed a training program of a standard equivalent to that required for the issue of an AFC certificate of that level.
The functions of an ARFFS for an aerodrome are:
to rescue persons and property from an aircraft that has crashed or caught fire during landing or take-off; and
to control and extinguish, and to protect persons and property threatened by, a fire on the aerodrome, whether or not in an aircraft.

Nothing in subregulation (1) prevents the ARFFS provider for an aerodrome from performing fire control services or rescue services elsewhere than on an aerodrome, but the provider must give priority to operations mentioned in subregulation (1).

section.heading: Person not to provide service without approval

content.p: A person must not provide an ARFFS at an aerodrome unless the person is approved, under Division 139.H.5, to provide the ARFFS.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Subpart that provides for the following matters:
standards and criteria for the establishment and disestablishment of an ARFFS;
standards relating to the procedures, systems and documents required for the provision of an ARFFS;
standards for facilities and equipment used to provide an ARFFS;
standards, including competency standards, minimum qualifications and training standards, for persons engaged in an ARFFS;
any matter required or permitted by these Regulations to be provided for by the Manual of Standards;
any matter necessary or convenient to be provided for the effective operation of this Subpart.

Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument—see subsections 98(5A) and (5B) of the Act. It must be registered in accordance with the Legislation Act 2003 and must be tabled in both Houses of the Parliament within 6 sitting days after its making.
CASA must give a copy of a notice about a Manual of Standards for this Subpart (being a notice referred to in subregulation 11.275(3) or regulation 11.280) to each ARFFS provider.
Note: Subpart 11.J (including regulations 11.275 and 11.280) sets out procedures for the issue, amendment and revocation of a MOS.

If CASA sets out, in the Manual of Standards, a way of complying with a requirement of this Subpart, an ARFFS provider who uses that way is taken to have complied with the requirement unless the contrary is shown.
CASA may take the extent to which an ARFFS provider complies with the Manual into account in deciding whether the service provided by the provider is adequate.

division.heading: Requirements to be complied with by ARFFS provider

content.p: A requirement in this Division for there to be a system or procedure to do something is a requirement that the system or procedure:
must exist; and
must be in use.

section.heading: Definition for Division—applicable standards and requirements

content.p: In this Division:
for an aerodrome to which subregulation (2) applies—the standards and requirements for an aerodrome of its category set out in:
Chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention; and
the Manual of Standards; or
for any other aerodrome—the standards and requirements for an aerodrome of its category set out in the Manual of Standards.
This subregulation applies to:
an aerodrome from or to which an international passenger air service operates; and
any other aerodrome through which more than 350 000 passengers passed on air transport flights during the previous financial year.
In paragraph (2)(a):

(a) an international air service (within the meaning given by subsection 3(1) of the Air Navigation Act 1920) that carries passengers, other than a non-scheduled service (within the meaning given by that subsection); or
(b) a non-scheduled passenger-carrying flight, or program of non-scheduled passenger-carrying flights, carried out under a permission granted under section 15D of the Air Navigation Act 1920; or

a non-scheduled passenger-carrying flight, or program of non-scheduled passenger-carrying flights, in a category in respect of which the Secretary to the Department has determined, under subsection 15A(3) of that Act, that such a permission is not required.
For paragraph (2)(b), the number of passengers that pass through an aerodrome is to be determined according to statistics published by the Department.

Note: Department means the Department administered by the Minister who administers these Regulations (see section 19A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 as it applies because of section 13 of the Legislation Act 2003).

section.heading: Inconsistency between Manual and chapter 9 of Annex 14

content.p: If a requirement of the Manual of Standards, as it applies to a particular aerodrome, is inconsistent with a requirement of chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention, as it applies to that aerodrome, the requirement of the Manual prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

section.heading: Knowledge, equipment and expertise to deal with aviation hazards

content.p: An ARFFS provider must have the knowledge, equipment and expertise to deal with any hazard likely to arise during an aviation accident or incident, including any hazard mentioned in the Manual of Standards.
An ARFFS provider must ensure that the service is available during the period or periods published in ERSA as the period or periods of its availability.

Subregulation (1) does not prevent the level of protection provided during predictable periods of reduced activity at the aerodrome from being reduced, within the limit allowed by Chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention.
An ARFFS must be able to meet the criteria for response time set out in Chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention.
Subregulation (1) applies to an ARFFS whether or not Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention applies to the ARFFS.
An ARFFS provider for an aerodrome to which subregulation 139.755(2) applies must ensure that the necessary buildings and facilities for the service, including the following, are at the aerodrome:
a fire station;
communications facilities;
facilities for the maintenance of vehicles and equipment;
training facilities;
storage facilities;
if there is a body of water within 1 000 metres of a runway threshold—a boat ramp and boat launching facilities.
The ARFFS provider must ensure that those buildings and facilities comply with any applicable requirements (including requirements as to location) in the Manual of Standards.
The ARFFS provider must ensure that there is a facility, in accordance with the requirements of the Manual of Standards, for replenishing the water supply of a fire fighting vehicle.
The ARFFS provider must ensure that there are the appropriate emergency roads on the aerodrome in accordance with the requirements of the Manual of Standards.
An ARFFS provider must ensure that there are, at an aerodrome other than one to which subregulation 139.755(2) applies, the following facilities:
a standby point for an emergency vehicle that will allow the vehicle to achieve the response time required by the Manual of Standards;
storage for a reserve stock of extinguishing agents.
An ARFFS provider must appoint, as officer in charge of ARFFS operations for an aerodrome, a person who is based at the aerodrome and who holds:
for an aerodrome categorised as Category 6 or above—an AFC Advanced Diploma that meets the standards in the Manual of Standards; or
for an aerodrome categorised as Category 5 or below—an AFC Diploma that meets the standards in the Manual of Standards.
In paragraphs (1)(a) and (b):
AFC means Australian Fire Competencies.

section.heading: Notice about times service is available etc

content.p: An ARFFS provider must ensure that notice is published in ERSA of the hours during which the service is available.

If for some reason (such as an emergency on the aerodrome) it becomes temporarily impossible to provide an ARFFS to the standard required by this Subpart, the provider must tell the Australian NOTAM Office:
of the reduction in the service; and
how long it is likely to be before the full service is restored.
The provider must tell CASA in writing of any proposed reduction in the standard of service that:
will last longer than 24 hours; or
reduces the standard of ARFFS provided at the airport concerned to a greater extent than is permissible under Chapter 9 of Annex 14 to the Chicago Convention.

section.heading: Agreements with other fire fighting bodies

content.p: An ARFFS provider may make an arrangement:

(a) for an aerodrome that is a joint user airport (within the meaning of the Airports Act 1996)—with the Defence Force for the provision of the ARFFS provider’s services to the Defence Force for the part of the aerodrome under the control of the Force; or
with a State or Territory, or another person or body, for the services of the provider for firefighting or rescue in the State or Territory beyond the airside of the aerodrome concerned.
If a provider makes such an arrangement, the provider must ensure that it is recorded in writing.
There must be, on the aerodrome, a stock of fire-extinguishing agents of the kind or kinds, and meeting the performance standards, required by the applicable standards and requirements.
The fire-extinguishing agents must be held in at least the quantities required by those standards and requirements.
There must be, on the aerodrome, vehicles and equipment for delivering extinguishing agent onto a fire.
There must be at least as many vehicles, and at least as much equipment, as required by the applicable standards and requirements.
Each vehicle or piece of equipment:
must be capable of delivering extinguishing agent onto a fire at at least the rate required by the applicable standards and requirements; and
must have at least the performance (in other respects) required by those standards and requirements.
The vehicles must carry ancillary equipment in accordance with the applicable standards and requirements.
Each vehicle and piece of equipment must be in good working order.
The vehicles must be of a colour permitted by the applicable standards and requirements.

The provider must keep maintenance instructions for each vehicle and each piece of the equipment, including all the information necessary to permit an appropriately qualified and technically competent person to carry out maintenance, performance monitoring, defect reporting, fault reporting and record-keeping on or for the vehicle or equipment.

There must be, at the aerodrome, enough vehicles and equipment (other than vehicles and equipment for delivering extinguishing agent onto a fire) to provide the service, in accordance with the applicable standards and requirements.
The performance of the vehicles and equipment must be in accordance with the applicable standards and requirements.
The vehicles must carry ancillary equipment in accordance with the applicable standards and requirements.

The provider must keep maintenance instructions for each piece of the provider’s equipment, including all the information necessary to permit a technically competent person to carry out maintenance, performance monitoring, defect reporting, fault reporting and record-keeping on or for the equipment.

section.heading: Vehicles and equipment for firefighting and rescue in difficult environments

content.p: If a significant proportion of aircraft movements at the aerodrome take place over water, swamp or another difficult environment, there must be appropriate vehicles, boats and equipment for firefighting and rescue in that environment within 1 000 metres of the threshold of each runway.
The vehicles, boats and equipment must be in at least the numbers and quantity required by the applicable standards and requirements.
The vehicles and boats must be of a colour required or permitted by the applicable standards and requirements.

An ARFFS provider must not begin to use a piece of operational equipment for the purpose of an ARFFS unless the equipment has been approved by CASA as conforming to specifications and any applicable standards, in accordance with the operator’s aerodrome manual, and any applicable standards or requirements in the Manual of Standards.
At the aerodrome there must be, for the firefighters and rescue personnel:
protective clothing that complies with:
if there is a relevant Australian Standard (as in force immediately before this regulation commences)—that Standard; or
if there is no such Australian Standard—any relevant internationally recognised standard;
in at least the quantity required by the applicable standards and requirements; and
other protective equipment in the quantity required by, and of a kind in accordance with, those standards and requirements.
There must be, on the aerodrome, sufficient communications equipment available to provide communication during an ARFFS operation.
The vehicles used for the service must carry suitable communications equipment.
A person who is required to operate the equipment must hold an aeronautical radio operator certificate.
The equipment must not interfere, when in use, with communications equipment used by the air traffic service at the aerodrome.
The provider must have the necessary equipment and tools, in accordance with the applicable standards and requirements, to test and maintain the equipment used to provide the service.

If the applicable standards and requirements require particular test or maintenance equipment, particular kinds of test or maintenance equipment, or particular numbers or quantities of a particular type of test or maintenance equipment, the provider must have that equipment or that number or quantity of that type of equipment.

section.heading: Commissioning of new vehicles and equipment

content.p: The provider must not put a new vehicle, or a new item of equipment that affects the quality or rate of discharge of extinguishing agent, into service unless:
the vehicle or equipment has been approved by CASA, for conformity to specification and the applicable standards and requirements, in accordance with the provider’s operations manual; and
CASA has acknowledged that the vehicle or equipment meets the applicable standards and requirements; and
any necessary personnel training has been completed.

During any period announced in ERSA as a period during which ARFFS is available at an aerodrome, there must be enough trained personnel available at the aerodrome to operate the equipment and vehicles required to provide the service at full capacity.
Those personnel must be stationed at places that allow the ARFFS to respond to an emergency at least as quickly as required by the applicable standards and requirements.
The people employed as firefighters must meet the medical standard for firefighters set out in the Manual of Standards.
There must be a system of continuing medical checks for the people employed as firefighters that ensures that the ARFFS provider knows whether or not those people continue to meet that standard.

The people employed as firefighters must already be trained to at least AFC Certificate 2 standard, or, if for a particular position the Manual of Standards specifies a higher standard, that higher standard.

Before being used in any operational capacity, those people must also receive, or have received, appropriate training in dealing with hazards specific to aviation accidents and incidents, to the extent that such training is not part of the training required for an AFC Certificate 2.
The people employed as firefighters must receive appropriate training to familiarise them with local conditions.
There must be ongoing training for the people employed as firefighters to ensure that they continue to meet that standard.

If a significant proportion of aircraft movements at the aerodrome take place over water, swamp or another difficult environment, the firefighters must be appropriately trained to carry out their functions in that environment.
There must be an operations manual for the service that complies with the standards set out in the Manual of Standards.

The operations manual must include a chart showing the organisations that provide services to the provider, setting out the roles and responsibilities of those organisations and how those roles and responsibilities affect the Aerodrome Emergency Procedures for the aerodrome concerned.
The operations manual must be kept up to date.
Each of the provider’s employees must have ready access to an up-to-date copy of the operations manual.
The provider must give CASA a copy of the operations manual, and of any changes to it.
There must be an up-to-date copy of the operations manual at each operational station.
The provider must comply with the requirements of the operations manual.
An ARFFS provider may amend its operations manual, but an amendment is of no effect until approved in writing by CASA.
CASA may direct an ARFFS provider to amend its operations manual is a way specified in the direction.
The provider must comply with the direction.

There must be a system to record electronically, in accordance with the standards or requirements set out in the Manual of Standards, any voice communication by radio or telephone in the course of an ARFFS operation.

There must be a system, in accordance with the standards or requirements set out in the Manual of Standards, to record the details of any aircraft accident or incident, or building fire, in relation to which the service is required to take any action.

There must be a plan, in accordance with the standards or requirements set out in the Manual of Standards, of the procedures to be used in the event of an emergency that results, or may result, in the service being interrupted.
The plan must include at least the following:
actions to be taken by firefighters and rescue personnel;
possible alternative arrangements for providing the service (including arrangements for procuring any necessary replacement vehicles or spare parts, or supplies of extinguishing materials);
notification procedures;
procedures for re-establishing normal services.
There must be a system, in accordance with the standards or requirements set out in the Manual of Standards, to collect, index, store and maintain the records relating to the service.
The records must include:
voice records made under regulation 139.860; and
records of accidents or incidents made under regulation 139.865.
A record must be kept for 5 years (or a shorter period specified for the particular kind of record in the Manual) after the date to which it relates.
The provider must, at all times, maintain an appropriate organisation with a sound and effective management structure, having regard to the nature of the service it provides.

section.heading: System for rectification of service failures

content.p: There must be a system, in accordance with the standards or requirements in the Manual of Standards, to rectify any failure that results or may result in an interruption in the service or a reduction in the standard of the service.
There must be a system, in accordance with the standards or requirements set out in the Manual of Standards, to ensure that the service complies with the requirements of this Subpart.
There must be a system, in accordance with the Manual of Standards, to manage changes in:
equipment and procedures; and
what the service does; and
the level or kinds of service provided; and
the way the service is provided.

There must be a safety management system for the service, in accordance with the standards or requirements in the Manual of Standards, including the policies, procedures and practices necessary to provide the service safely.
The provider must tell CASA in writing:
who its managers are; and
its organisational structure; and
how many staff of each class it uses to provide the service.
The provider must tell CASA in writing about any change in a matter mentioned in paragraph (1)(a), (b) or (c) within 14 days after the change.

section.heading: Telling users and CASA about changes

content.p: There must be a procedure, in accordance with the standards and requirements in the Manual of Standards, for an ARFFS provider to give, to aerodrome users, safety-related information about changes, faults or interruptions to the service.
The procedure must comply with CASA’s requirements for reporting information to the Aeronautical Information and Data Service and the Australian NOTAM Office.

If the provider fails, for a period of 24 hours or longer, to provide the service at the standard required by Division 139.H.3, the ARFFS provider for the aerodrome must tell CASA in writing as soon as practicable:
why the service is not being provided at that standard; and
how long it is likely to be before the service can be resumed; and
what action the service provider has taken and will take to resume the service at that standard.

section.heading: Powers of officer in charge or firefighter

content.p: In this regulation:
firefighter, in relation to an ARFFS operation for an aerodrome, means:
somebody employed as a firefighter by the ARFFS provider for the aerodrome; or
a member of a fire brigade, or of a rescue or fire fighting service, who is taking part in the operation in accordance with an arrangement made with such a brigade or service.
officer in charge, in relation to an ARFFS operation for an aerodrome, means:
the person appointed under regulation 139.773 as officer in charge of ARFFS operations at the aerodrome; or
if, in accordance with an arrangement made with a fire brigade, or a rescue or fire fighting service, the person in control of the operation is a member of such a brigade or service—that person.
volunteer, in relation to an ARFFS operation, means somebody who has volunteered to help in the operation under the direction of the officer in charge.
For an ARFFS operation for an aerodrome under this Subpart, the officer in charge may:
give directions that he or she thinks proper to firefighters and volunteers under his or her control; and
take measures that he or she thinks proper.
Without limiting paragraph (2)(b), the officer in charge may do the following things for the purpose of the ARFFS operation:
enter (by force, if necessary), take possession of and deal with in any appropriate way, premises, an aircraft or other property;
close a road or other thoroughfare to traffic;
use a convenient water supply (including shutting off water supply from a main or pipe to obtain greater pressure or supply);
disconnect electricity supply to premises;
remove flammable, explosive or other dangerous material from premises, an aircraft or other property;
order a person to leave premises, an aircraft or other property;
remove from the vicinity of the operation a person or thing the presence of whom or which is interfering, or is likely to interfere, significantly with the operation;
take a fire engine or other fire appliance onto land or premises;
shore up or destroy a wall or building that is insecure or may be dangerous to persons or property;
direct or authorise a firefighter or a volunteer to do something that, under this regulation, the officer may do.

For an ARFFS operation, a firefighter may do something mentioned in paragraph (3)(a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f) or (h) without authorisation under paragraph (3)(j) if there are reasonable grounds for believing that, for the operation:
it is necessary or desirable to do the thing; and
it is not practicable for him or her to get authorisation to do so.
A person is guilty of an offence punishable by a fine of 10 penalty units if he or she fails to comply with:
a direction of the officer in charge under paragraph (3)(f); or
a direction of the kind mentioned in that paragraph, given by a firefighter or volunteer, if:
the firefighter or volunteer has been authorised under paragraph (3)(j) by the officer in charge to give it; or
the conditions in paragraphs (4)(a) and (b) are satisfied in relation to the direction.
In this Division:
show cause notice means a notice under regulation 139.1015.

section.heading: How to apply for approval as ARFFS provider

content.p: An eligible person may apply to CASA for approval as an ARFFS provider.
A person is eligible to apply for approval as an ARFFS provider if:
the person is mentioned in column 2 of an item in table 139.925; and
the application relates to an aerodrome mentioned in column 3 of that item.
The application must be in writing.
The application:
must set out the applicant’s name and address; and
(b) if the applicant is a corporation (within the meaning given by the Corporations Act 2001)—must set out the applicant’s registered address and ACN and the names and addresses of its officers.
In paragraph (3)(b):
officer has the meaning given by section 9 of the Corporations Act 2001.
The applicant must include with the application:
a copy of the applicant’s operations manual, prepared as if the applicant were an approved provider; and
information that will enable CASA to decide whether or not the applicant is of sound financial standing; and
a statement of the intended location and category of the service to be provided.
Note: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.

tr.td: a person who is to provide an ARFFS at a particular aerodrome: (a) in cooperation with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(b) of the Air Services Act 1995; or (b) by arrangement with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(c) of the Air Services Act 1995
a person who is to provide an ARFFS in accordance with an arrangement mentioned in paragraph 216(1)(e) of the Airports Act 1996
the aerodrome specified in the arrangement mentioned in column 2

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055 and subregulation (3), if a person has applied for approval as an ARFFS provider under this Subpart, CASA must grant the approval.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
CASA may approve an application only if CASA approves the applicant’s draft operations manual.
CASA must not approve the draft operations manual unless the draft manual complies with the relevant requirements in the Manual of Standards.

(6) Without limiting regulations 11.056 and 11.067, if the application is made by a person mentioned in column 2 of item 1, 2, 5 or 6 of Table 139.925 in relation to an ARFFS at the corresponding aerodrome, CASA may impose any condition necessary to give effect to an arrangement mentioned in subsection 11(3) of the Air Services Act 1995.
If CASA does not make a decision about an application within 21 days after receiving it, CASA is taken to have refused the application.

However, if CASA makes a request under regulation 11.035 or 11.040, the time between when CASA makes the request, and when the applicant’s officer or officers participates or participate in the interview, or gives CASA the information or copy requested, does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA asks an applicant to make a statutory declaration under regulation 11.047 or subregulation 11.050(3A), the time between when CASA asks the applicant to do so and when the applicant gives CASA the statutory declaration does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA invites an applicant to make a written submission under subregulation 11.050(2), the time between when CASA gives the invitation and when the applicant makes the written submission does not count towards the period.
An approved ARFFS provider may apply to vary its approval.
Regulations 139.965 and 139.970 apply to the application.
Note: Part 11 also contains provisions relating to an application for variation of approval.

section.heading: Suspension or continued suspension of approval by show cause notice

content.p: CASA may state, in a show cause notice, that the approval as an approved ARFFS provider of the ARFFS provider concerned is suspended if CASA reasonably considers that not suspending the approval would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
If a show cause notice states that the approval is suspended:

if the approval is already suspended when the show cause notice is given to the holder—the approval continues to be suspended until CASA revokes the suspension, or the suspension lapses under subregulation (4); or
the approval is suspended from when the notice is given to the approved ARFFS provider concerned.
CASA may revoke the suspension at any time.
If CASA has not cancelled the approval within 90 days after the day the show cause notice is given to the provider, the suspension lapses at the end of that period.
It is grounds for the cancellation of the approval of an approved ARFFS provider if the provider:
has breached a condition of the approval; or
has contravened the Act or these Regulations; or
has otherwise been guilty of conduct that renders the holder’s continued holding of the approval likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.

section.heading: Notice to approved ARFFS provider to show cause

content.p: CASA may give an approved ARFFS provider a show cause notice if there are reasonable grounds for believing that there are facts or circumstances that amount to grounds for the cancellation of the approval.
A show cause notice must:
tell the provider of the facts and circumstances that justify the cancellation of the approval; and
invite the holder to show in writing, within a reasonable period stated in the notice, why the approval should not be cancelled.
For paragraph (2)(b), the period must not be less than 7 days.

section.heading: Cancellation of approval after show cause notice

content.p: CASA may cancel an approval only if:
there exist facts or circumstances that amount to grounds for the cancellation of the approval; and
CASA has given the holder a show cause notice in relation to the grounds for the proposed cancellation; and
CASA has taken into account any written representations made, within the period stated in the notice, by or on behalf of the holder; and
not cancelling the approval would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
If CASA has given a show cause notice to an approved ARFFS provider, and it decides not to cancel the approval, it:
must tell the provider in writing of the decision; and
must, if the approval is suspended, revoke the suspension.

section.heading: Cancellation if holder ceases to provide ARFFS

content.p: CASA must cancel the approval of a person mentioned in column 2 of item 3 or 4 of Table 139.925 if the person ceases to be an ARFFS provider for the aerodrome mentioned in column 3 of the item.
CASA must cancel the approval of a person mentioned in column 2 of item 5 of Table 139.925 if the cooperation or arrangement mentioned in that item ceases.
CASA must cancel the approval of a person mentioned in column 2 of item 6 of Table 139.925 if the arrangement mentioned in that item ceases.
