each direction given to the operator, or obligation imposed on the operator, by CASA under a provision of these Regulations; and
each other provision of civil aviation legislation that applies to the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities covered by the certificate;
each of the operator’s key personnel must comply with:
each provision of this Part that applies to the person; and
each direction given to the person, or obligation imposed on the person, by CASA under a provision of these Regulations; and
each other provision of civil aviation legislation that applies to the activities covered by the certificate;
each of the positions of the operator’s key personnel must be filled;
each of the operator’s personnel must comply with each provision of civil aviation legislation that applies to the activities;
if the operator is an individual—the individual must be the operator’s chief executive officer;
the positions of chief executive officer and quality assurance manager may be occupied by the same person only:
in an unforeseen circumstance; and
for the period mentioned in subregulation (2);
the positions of head of operations and quality assurance manager may be occupied by the same person only:
in an unforeseen circumstance; and
for the period mentioned in subregulation (2).
For subparagraphs (1)(f)(ii) and (g)(ii), the period is:
no more than 7 consecutive days for each unforeseen circumstance; or
if the operator holds an approval under regulation 142.040 for this paragraph in relation to an unforeseen circumstance—the period mentioned in the approval for the unforeseen circumstance.
A Part 142 operator that holds a certificate under this Division commits an offence if the operator does not maintain a reference library that complies with subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), the reference library must:
include the following documents:
all operational documents and material;
the civil aviation legislation that is relevant to the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities covered by the certificate;
the parts of the AIP that are relevant to the activities;
documents that include information about the operation or maintenance of each kind of flight simulation training device operated by the operator to conduct the activities;
any other publications, information or data required for the reference library by the operator’s exposition; and
be readily available to all members of the operator’s personnel; and
be up-to-date and in a readily accessible form.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if the operator does not keep up-to-date records of the distribution of operational documents to members of the operator’s personnel.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Certificate holders—regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply in relation to certain matters

content.p: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply to the following for a Part 142 operator that holds a certificate under this Division:
a change of which CASA is notified under regulation 142.135;
a significant change that is approved by CASA under regulation 142.145;
a change made under a process mentioned in regulation 142.150;
a change that is made as a consequence of a change made to the organisation’s exposition in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 142.155.
Subpart 142.C—Part 142 operators—changes
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if the operator:
makes a change mentioned in subregulation (2); and
does not, before making the change:
amend its exposition to reflect the change; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the amended part of the exposition clearly identifying the change.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(a), the changes are the following:
a change to its name (including any operating or trading name) or contact details;
if the address of the applicant’s operational headquarters is different from its mailing address—a change to the address of its operational headquarters.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—application for approval of significant change

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the operator makes a significant change other than a significant change mentioned in subregulation (2) or (3); and
CASA has not approved the significant change.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:

the operator makes a significant change that is the permanent appointment as any of the operator’s key personnel of a person previously authorised to carry out the responsibilities of the position in a circumstance mentioned in subparagraph 142.340(1)(e)(iv); and
the operator does not apply to CASA for approval of the change, in accordance with subregulation (4), within 7 days after the change is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:

the operator makes a significant change that is the permanent appointment as any of the operator’s key personnel of a person not previously authorised to carry out the responsibilities of the position in a circumstance mentioned in subparagraph 142.340(1)(e)(iv); and
the operator does not apply to CASA for approval of the change, in accordance with subregulation (4), within 3 days after the change is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An application for approval of a significant change must:
be in writing; and
set out the change; and
be accompanied by a copy of the part of the operator’s exposition affected by the change, clearly identifying the change.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

CASA may approve a significant change for a Part 142 operator that holds an AOC that authorises the operator to conduct Part 142 activities only if satisfied that the requirements mentioned in section 28 of the Act and subregulation 142.085(1) will continue to be met.

Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a significant change for a Part 142 operator that holds a certificate under Division 142.B.2 if satisfied that the requirements mentioned in subregulation 142.110(1) will continue to be met.
If CASA approves the significant change, CASA is taken to have also approved the changes to the operator’s exposition covered by the application.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the operator makes a change; and
the change is not made in accordance with the process described in the operator’s exposition for making changes.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—CASA directions relating to exposition or key personnel

content.p: If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may direct a Part 142 operator to change its exposition:
to remove particular information, procedures or instructions from the exposition; or
to include particular information, procedures or instructions in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information, procedures or instructions in the exposition.
CASA may direct a Part 142 operator to remove any of the operator’s key personnel from the person’s position if satisfied that the person is not:
carrying out the responsibilities of the position; or
if the person is the chief executive officer—properly managing matters for which the person is accountable.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
state the time within which the direction must be complied with.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
CASA gives the operator a direction under this regulation; and
the operator does not comply with the direction within the time stated in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 142.D—Part 142 operators—organisation and personnel

Note: For the qualifications for the position of head of aircraft airworthiness and maintenance control, see the qualifications specified in the Part 42 Manual of Standards for the position of continuing airworthiness manager.
A Part 142 operator must maintain an organisational structure that effectively manages its authorised Part 142 activities, taking into account the following:
the nature and complexity of the activities;
the number and kinds of aircraft or flight simulation training devices used to conduct the activities;
the number and location of training bases used by the operator to conduct the activities;
the number of the operator’s personnel;
for Part 142 flight training—the number of course participants undertaking the training;
for contracted training—the number of contracting operators and the number of their personnel for which the Part 142 operator is conducting contracted training;
for contracted checking—the number of contracting operators and the number of their personnel for which the Part 142 operator is conducting contracted checking.

A Part 142 operator commits an offence if any of the operator’s key personnel carries out a responsibility of the person’s position otherwise than in accordance with the operator’s exposition or this Subpart.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—key personnel cannot carry out responsibilities

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the operator becomes aware that any of its key personnel cannot carry out, or is likely to be unable to carry out, the person’s responsibilities for a period of longer than 35 days; and
the operator does not tell CASA of the matter mentioned in paragraph (a) within the time mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the time is:
if there is not another person authorised to carry out the responsibilities for all or part of the period—24 hours after the operator becomes aware of the matter; or
if there is another person authorised to carry out the responsibilities for all or part of the period—3 days after the operator becomes aware of the matter.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—familiarisation training for key personnel

content.p: A Part 142 operator must ensure that before a person appointed as any of the operator’s key personnel begins to carry out the responsibilities of the position, the person has completed any training that is necessary to familiarise the person with the responsibilities.

The chief executive officer of a Part 142 operator must have sufficient relevant experience in organisational, operational, financial and people management of air operations to enable the operator to conduct safe operations in accordance with its exposition and civil aviation legislation.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—chief executive officer: responsibilities and accountabilities

content.p: The chief executive officer of a Part 142 operator is responsible for the following:
ensuring that, for the safe conduct of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities in accordance with the operator’s Part 142 authorisation, exposition and civil aviation legislation, the operator:
has sufficient suitably experienced, qualified and competent personnel; and
has a suitable management structure; and
is adequately financed and resourced;
ensuring that the operator:
sets and maintains standards for the activities in accordance with the operator’s exposition; and
complies with civil aviation legislation;
if the operator conducts the activities in aircraft—ensuring that the operator:
implements and manages the operator’s safety management system; and
has procedures that ensure that all of the operator’s personnel understand the operator’s safety policy; and
has an organisational structure that ensures that the safety manager is independent and not subject to undue influence; and
tells CASA if the operator enters into a leasing, financing or other arrangement for the supply of a turbine-engined aircraft for use in the activities; and
tells CASA if the operator becomes aware that any arrangement mentioned in subparagraph (iv) may:
(A) affect the operator’s safe conduct of the activities; or
(B) contravene a provision of civil aviation legislation or the law of the country in which the aircraft is registered; and
complies with the aviation safety laws of each foreign country (if any) where the operator conducts the activities; and
for each foreign registered aircraft (if any) used in the activities—maintains the aircraft in accordance with the law of the country in which the aircraft is registered;
if the operator conducts the activities only in flight simulation training devices—ensuring that the operator implements and manages the operator’s quality assurance management system;
establishing and regularly reviewing the operator’s safety performance indicators and targets;
ensuring that the operator’s exposition is monitored and managed for continuous improvement;
ensuring that key personnel satisfactorily carry out the responsibilities of their positions in accordance with:
the operator’s exposition; and
civil aviation legislation.
The chief executive officer of a Part 142 operator is accountable to the operator and CASA for ensuring the responsibilities mentioned in subregulation (1) are carried out effectively.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—head of operations: qualifications and experience

content.p: The head of operations of a Part 142 operator must:
meet the requirements mentioned in subregulation (2); or
hold an approval under regulation 142.040 to be the head of operations for the operator.
For paragraph (1)(a), the requirements are that the person must:
hold, and be able to exercise the privileges of, a flight examiner rating; and
hold the pilot licence required by subregulation (3); and
be authorised under Part 61 to pilot a kind of aircraft that is used to conduct a significant proportion of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities; and
have the experience required by subregulation (4); and
have a satisfactory record in the conduct or management of air operations; and
have sufficient safety and regulatory knowledge to enable the operator to conduct the activities safely and in accordance with its exposition and civil aviation legislation.
For paragraph (2)(b), the licence required is:
if any of the activities relate to the operation of an aircraft for a multi-crew operation—an air transport pilot licence; or
in any other case—a commercial pilot licence or an air transport pilot licence.
For paragraph (2)(d), the experience required is:
if the operator holds an approval under regulation 142.040 for this paragraph—the experience mentioned in paragraph (5)(a) or (b); or
if paragraph (a) does not apply—the experience mentioned in paragraphs (5)(a) and (b).
For subregulation (4), the experience is the following:
at least 500 hours flight time on a kind of aircraft used to conduct a significant proportion of the activities;
at least 6 months experience in the conduct or management of air operations conducted under an AOC or equivalent foreign authorisation.
CASA may, by written notice given to a head of operations, or proposed head of operations, of a Part 142 operator, direct the person to undertake an assessment mentioned in subregulation (7).
For subregulation (6), the assessment:
is an assessment conducted by CASA or a person nominated by CASA to demonstrate suitability as head of operations for the operator; and
may include assessment in an aeroplane, rotorcraft, airship or flight simulation training device.
The head of operations of a Part 142 operator must safely manage the authorised Part 142 activities of the operator.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the responsibilities of the head of operations include the following:

monitoring and maintaining, and reporting to the chief executive officer on, the operator’s compliance with the provisions of civil aviation legislation and the operator’s exposition that apply to the activities;
setting and maintaining the operator’s standards for the activities in accordance with the operator’s exposition;
if the activities include flight training or contracted training—ensuring that the training is conducted in accordance with the operator’s training management system;
ensuring that the activities are monitored effectively;
managing the maintenance and continuous improvement of the operator’s fatigue risk management system (if any);
ensuring the proper allocation and deployment of aircraft, flight simulation training devices and personnel for use in the activities;
ensuring that the operator’s personnel are provided with the information and documentation necessary to properly carry out their responsibilities;
if the operator conducts an activity in a flight simulation training device—ensuring that the device is used only in accordance with the operator’s exposition;
if the operator conducts an activity in a flight simulator or flight training device—ensuring that the simulator or device is qualified under Part 60;
if the operator conducts an activity in a synthetic trainer—ensuring that the trainer is approved under Civil Aviation Order 45.0;
if the operator conducts an activity in any other device—ensuring that the device:
meets the qualification standards prescribed by a legislative instrument under regulation 61.045; or
is qualified (however described) by the national aviation authority of a recognised foreign State (within the meaning of regulation 61.010);
ensuring that each instructor who conducts an activity for the operator:
has access to the parts of the operator’s exposition that relate to the instructor’s duties; and
holds a valid standardisation and proficiency check for the operator under regulation 142.325;
ensuring that each examiner who conducts an activity for the operator has access to the parts of the operator’s exposition that relate to the examiner’s duties;
ensuring that each instructor or examiner who conducts an activity for the operator:
is authorised to conduct the activity under Part 61; and
has successfully completed the training set out in the operator’s internal training and checking system manual; and
meets the requirements in the operator’s exposition about training in human factors principles and non-technical skills;
reporting to the chief executive officer on the operator’s compliance with the matters mentioned in paragraph (n);
ensuring that each instructor or examiner who conducts contracted training or contracted checking for the operator has access to the contracting operator’s training and checking manual;

if an instructor attempts but does not successfully complete a standardisation and proficiency check mentioned in the operator’s internal training and checking system manual—telling CASA, in writing, within 14 days after the date of the attempt, of the person’s name, position and ARN;

ensuring that the operator establishes and maintains effective communication, in relation to the activities, with CASA and each contracting operator for which the operator conducts contracted training or contracted checking;

ensuring that written reports are provided to the head of training and checking of each contracting operator in relation to the performance of each person for whom the operator conducts contracted training or contracted checking;
if the operator conducts the activities in aircraft—ensuring that the operator complies with section 28BH of the Act in relation to flight crew.
The safety manager of a Part 142 operator must have:

sufficient relevant safety management experience to capably lead, manage and set standards to enable the operator to safely implement its safety management system in accordance with its exposition; and
a satisfactory record in the conduct or management of air operations; and
sufficient safety and regulatory knowledge to enable the operator to conduct safe authorised Part 142 activities in accordance with its exposition and civil aviation legislation.

Note: A Part 142 operator must have a safety manager if the operator conducts authorised Part 142 activities only in aircraft, or in aircraft and flight simulation training devices: see regulation 142.025, definition of key personnel.
The safety manager of a Part 142 operator must manage the safety management system of the operator.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the responsibilities of the safety manager include:
managing the operation of the safety management system including managing corrective, remedial and preventative action in relation to the system; and
regularly reporting to the chief executive officer on the effectiveness of the safety management system; and
managing the maintenance and continuous improvement of the following systems:
safety management system;
fatigue risk management system (if any).
The quality assurance manager of a Part 142 operator must have:

sufficient relevant quality assurance management experience to capably lead, manage and set standards to enable the operator to safely implement its quality assurance management system in accordance with its exposition; and
sufficient safety and regulatory knowledge to enable the operator to conduct authorised Part 142 activities safely and in accordance with its exposition and civil aviation legislation.

Note: A Part 142 operator must have a quality assurance manager if the operator conducts authorised Part 142 activities only in flight simulation training devices: see regulation 142.025, definition of key personnel.
The quality assurance manager of a Part 142 operator must manage the quality assurance management system of the operator.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the responsibilities of the quality assurance manager include:
managing the operation of the quality assurance management system including managing corrective, remedial and preventative action in relation to the system; and
regularly reporting to the chief executive officer on the effectiveness of the quality assurance management system; and
managing the maintenance and continuous improvement of the quality assurance management system.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—key personnel: additional qualifications and experience requirements

content.p: This regulation applies to:
an applicant for a Part 142 authorisation; and
a Part 142 operator.

CASA may, by written notice given to the applicant or operator, direct that any of the key personnel of the applicant or operator must have stated additional qualifications or experience to those otherwise required under this Subpart.

If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to a person who is, or is proposed to be, any of the key personnel of the applicant or operator, direct the person:
to undertake a stated examination; or
to be interviewed by CASA; or
to complete a stated training course.
In deciding whether to give a direction under this regulation, CASA must have regard to, but is not limited to considering, the following:
the need to ensure that the applicant or operator can conduct safe authorised Part 142 activities in accordance with its exposition and civil aviation legislation;
the nature and complexity of the activities;
the leadership, management and standards-setting skills required by the person for the activities;
how recently the person has used his or her aviation skills;
whether the person is able to exercise the privileges of each civil aviation authorisation held by the person.
Subpart 142.E—Part 142 operators—instructors and examiners

section.heading: Part 142 activities—instructors and examiners must comply with Part 142 authorisation

content.p: An instructor or examiner for a Part 142 operator commits an offence if the instructor or examiner conducts a Part 142 activity otherwise than in accordance with the operator’s Part 142 authorisation.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 activities—instructors and examiners must comply with exposition

content.p: An instructor or examiner for a Part 142 operator commits an offence if the instructor or examiner conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator otherwise than in accordance with the operator’s exposition.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—instructors and examiners must be authorised under Part 61

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
an instructor or examiner for the operator conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator; and
the instructor or examiner is not authorised under Part 61 to conduct the activity.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—instructors and examiners must have access to records

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
an instructor or examiner for the operator conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator; and
the instructor or examiner does not have access to the operator’s records for the persons participating in the activity.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—instructors and examiners must be competent to conduct authorised Part 142 activities in flight simulation training devices

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
an instructor or examiner for the operator conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator in a flight simulation training device; and
the instructor or examiner has not been assessed by the operator as competent to conduct the activity in the device.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—person recommended for flight test

content.p: A Part 142 operator and the operator’s head of operations each commit an offence if:
a person is recommended for a flight test by:
the head of operations; or
a person named in the operator’s exposition as responsible for the Part 142 activity to which the flight test relates; and
the person is not eligible under regulation 61.235 to undertake the test.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 142.F—Part 142 operators—training management system
A Part 142 operator must have a training management system that meets the requirements of regulation 142.255.
The training management system must include the following:
for each kind of Part 142 flight training or contracted training that is an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator—a course outline, detailed syllabus, standards to be met and record forms;
the procedures to be followed when a standard is not met;
an auditable system for maintaining records of the results of the operator’s flight training or contracted training.
Subpart 142.G—Part 142 operators—safety management system

A Part 142 operator that conducts authorised Part 142 activities only in aircraft, or in aircraft and flight simulation training devices, must have a safety management system that meets the requirements of regulation 142.265.
The safety management system must be a systemic approach to managing safety that:
includes the matters mentioned in subregulation (2); and
ensures that the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities are conducted in a planned and systematic manner and identifies and addresses deficiencies in training outcomes; and
if the operator conducts the training in flight simulation training devices:
ensures the correct operation and maintenance of the devices; and
without limiting subparagraph (i), includes the matters mentioned in subregulation 142.275(2); and
integrates human factors principles.
For paragraph (1)(a), the matters are the following:
organisational structures, accountabilities, policies and procedures necessary to manage safety in a systemic way;
a statement of the operator’s safety policy, objectives and planning, including details of the following:
the management commitment to, and responsibility for, safety;
the safety accountabilities of managers (including key personnel);
the appointment of safety management personnel;
how human factors principles are integrated into the safety management system;
a safety management system implementation plan;
relevant third party relationships and interactions;
coordination of an emergency response plan;
safety management system documentation;
a safety risk management system, including:
hazard identification processes; and
risk assessment and mitigation processes;
a safety assurance system, including:
details of processes for:
(A) safety performance monitoring and measurement; and
(B) internal safety investigation; and
(C) management of change; and
(D) continuous improvement of the safety management system; and
if the operator operates an aircraft mentioned in subregulation (3) for the activities—a flight data analysis program that meets the requirements mentioned in subregulation (4);
a safety training and promotion system, including details of the following:
safety management system training and education;
safety management system safety communication.
For subparagraph (2)(d)(ii), the aircraft are the following:
an aeroplane with a maximum certificated take-off weight of more than 27 000 kg;
a rotorcraft with a maximum certificated take-off weight of more than 7 000 kg.
For subparagraph (2)(d)(ii), the requirements are that the flight data analysis program must:
regularly record and analyse the operational flight data of individual and aggregated operations for the purpose of improving the safety of flight operations; and
be provided by:
the operator; or
another appropriate person; and
ensure that, except as mentioned in subregulations (6) and (7):
the identity of a person who is the source of data is protected from disclosure to anyone other than the following:
(A) a person whose duties require the person to analyse operational flight data;
(B) a person who has access to the person’s identity solely for the purpose of analysing operational flight data;
(C) a pilot appointed by the operator to liaise with flight crew in relation to matters arising from the flight data analysis program; and
no punitive action in relation to the data may be taken by the operator against the person.

For subparagraph (4)(b)(ii), the provision of the flight data analysis program by an appropriate person does not in any way compromise the operator’s responsibility to provide, and ensure the effectiveness of, the program.
For paragraph (4)(c), the identity of a person who is the source of data may be disclosed:
with the written consent of the person; or
under a court order.
For paragraph (4)(c), the identity of a person who is the source of data may be disclosed, and the operator may take punitive action against the person, if the operator has evidence that the person:
deliberately contravened a provision of civil aviation legislation or the operator’s exposition; or
persistently engaged in unsafe actions without appropriate safety reasons.
Without limiting paragraph (1)(b), the system must include the following:
a process for auditing the activities;
a process for promoting the continual improvement of the activities;
a process for evaluating the training outcomes from pre-flight test assessments and post-flight test feedback from examiners;
a process for regularly assessing the suitability of the operator’s facilities and resources used for conducting the activities;
a process for recommending changes to the following:
the safety management system;
the training management system;
the internal training and checking system.
Subpart 142.H—Part 142 operators—quality assurance management system

A Part 142 operator that conducts authorised Part 142 activities only in flight simulation training devices must have a quality assurance management system that meets the requirements of regulation 142.275.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—quality assurance management system requirements

content.p: The quality assurance system must:
ensure the correct operation and maintenance of the flight simulation training devices; and
ensure that the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities are conducted in a planned and systematic manner and identifies and addresses deficiencies in training outcomes.
Without limiting paragraph (1)(a), the system must include the following:
quality policy;
management responsibility;
document control;
resource allocation;
quality procedures;
internal audit.
Without limiting paragraph (1)(b), the system must include the following:
a process for auditing the activities;
a process for promoting the continual improvement of the activities;
a process for evaluating the training outcomes from pre-flight test assessments and post-flight test feedback from examiners;
a process for regularly assessing the suitability of the operator’s facilities and resources used for conducting the activities;
a process for recommending changes to the following:
the quality assurance management system;
the training management system;
the internal training and checking system.
Subpart 142.I—Part 142 operators—personnel fatigue management
Subpart 142.J—Part 142 operators—internal training and checking
Note: This Subpart is reserved for future use.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—internal training and checking system

content.p: A Part 142 operator must have an internal training and checking system for its personnel that meets the requirements of regulation 142.315.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—internal training and checking system requirements

content.p: The internal training and checking system must include the following:
a description of the operator’s internal training and checking, including details of how the training and checking is conducted;
a description of the duties and responsibilities assigned to personnel conducting internal training and checking;
procedures that ensure that each of the operator’s personnel:
has an understanding of the operator’s training management system; and
completes internal training and checking as described under paragraph (a); and
is supervised effectively;
command responsibility during flights for internal training and checking;

for each kind of internal training and checking conducted by or for the operator—the minimum number of check pilots and the minimum crew qualifications required by the operator for the training (if any);
any general restrictions, specifications or safety precautions for internal training and checking (including in relation to fuel load, ballast and minimum weather conditions);
methods of conducting internal training and checking including the following:
the standards to be achieved;
training sequences for common faults;
the method of simulating emergencies or malfunctions;
procedures that ensure that an instructor who conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator holds a valid standardisation and proficiency check for the operator under regulation 142.325;

procedures that ensure that an instructor who uses a flight simulation training device to conduct an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator is competent to use the device to conduct the activity.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
an instructor for the operator conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator; and
the instructor does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the requirement is that the instructor must:
hold a valid standardisation and proficiency check for the operator under regulation 142.325; or
be successfully participating in the operator’s internal training and checking system.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—holding valid standardisation and proficiency check for operator

content.p: An instructor for a Part 142 operator holds a valid standardisation and proficiency check for the operator if:
the instructor has successfully completed the operator’s standardisation and proficiency check; and
the check complies with regulation 142.330; and
under subregulation (2) or (3), the check is valid.
A standardisation and proficiency check is valid for the period comprising:
the period beginning on the day on which the check is completed, and ending at the end of the month in which the check is completed; and
the period of 12 months immediately following the month in which the check was completed.
If:
(a) an instructor holds a standardisation and proficiency check that is valid under subregulation (2) (the existing check); and
the instructor successfully completes a new standardisation and proficiency check on a day that is less than 3 months before the day on which the existing check is due to expire;
the new check is valid for 12 months beginning at the end of the day on which the existing check expires.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—standardisation and proficiency check requirements

content.p: A Part 142 operator’s standardisation and proficiency check for an instructor must check the competency of the instructor to conduct the Part 142 activity that the operator has engaged the instructor to conduct.
The check must be carried out by:
the operator’s head of operations; or
a person authorised to conduct the check by the operator’s head of operations.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—instructors and examiners—training in human factors principles and non-technical skills

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
an instructor or examiner for the operator conducts an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator; and
the instructor or examiner does not meet the requirements in the operator’s exposition about training in human factors principles and non-technical skills.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 142.K—Part 142 operators—expositions
An exposition for a Part 142 operator must include the following:
the operator’s name (including any operating or trading name), contact details and ABN (if any);
the address of:
the operator’s operational headquarters; and
each of the operator’s training bases;
a description and diagram of the operator’s organisational structure showing formal reporting lines including the formal reporting lines for each of the key personnel;
if the operator is a corporation—a description of the operator’s corporate structure;
for each of the key personnel, the following information:
the qualifications and experience (if any) required by the operator for the position in addition to the qualifications and experience required under Subpart 142.D for the position;
each matter (if any) for which the holder of the position is responsible in addition to the responsibilities mentioned in Subpart 142.D for the position;
the name of the person appointed to the position;
the name of each person authorised to carry out the responsibilities of the position when the position holder:
(A) is absent from the position; or
(B) cannot carry out the responsibilities;
a description of how the operator will manage the responsibilities of the position during a circumstance mentioned in subparagraph (iv);
each matter (if any) for which the chief executive officer is responsible and accountable in addition to the matters mentioned in regulation 142.180;

if the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities include Part 142 flight training—the name of each instructor appointed by the operator’s head of operations to have responsibility for particular flight training;
a description of the operator’s program for training and assessing personnel in human factors principles and non-technical skills;
details of the responsibilities of the operator’s personnel (other than key personnel) under these Regulations;
a description of the authorised Part 142 activities conducted by the operator including:
for Part 142 flight training or contracted training:
(A) the training plans and syllabuses for the training; and
(B) the areas of operation for the training; and
(C) checklists (if any) and the circumstances when the use of a checklist is permitted; and
minimum qualifications and experience for personnel conducting the activities; and
command responsibility during flights for the activities; and

for contracted training or contracted checking—procedures to ensure that the operator conducts the training or checking in accordance with the contracting operator’s training and checking manual and standard operating procedures (if any);
a description of the procedures by which the operator conducts and manages the activities, including the supervision of instructors and persons participating in activities;
if the operator conducts the activities in aircraft:
for each registered aircraft that is flown into, out of or outside Australian territory in the course of conducting the activities—the kind of aircraft and its registration mark; and
for each foreign registered aircraft—the kind of aircraft and its nationality and registration marks; and
a description of any leasing or other arrangements for the supply of any turbine-engined aircraft; and
a description of the way any turbine-engined aircraft are managed and maintained, and the way continuing airworthiness of the aircraft is assured; and
a description of each flight training area;

if the operator conducts the activities in relation to a flight crew licence or rating of a kind for which a low-flying activity is required—a description of how the operator will determine a suitable flight training area for the activity;
if the operator conducts the activities in flight simulation training devices:
a description of the devices used by the operator in conducting the activities; and
for each device—each purpose mentioned in Part 61 that the device may be used for; and
for flight simulators and flight training devices—a description of the procedures by which the operator ensures the qualification of the simulators and devices under Part 60; and
for synthetic trainers—a description of the procedures by which the operator ensures the approval of the trainers under Civil Aviation Order 45.0; and
for any other device—a description of the procedures by which the operator ensures that the device:
(A) meets the qualification standards prescribed by a legislative instrument under regulation 61.045; or
(B) is qualified (however described) by the national aviation authority of a recognised foreign State (within the meaning of regulation 61.010);
a description of the way the operator manages the risk of fatigue in its personnel, including the operator’s fatigue risk management system manual (if any);
the facilities used by the operator for the activities;
a description of any operations, other than authorised Part 142 activities, conducted, or proposed to be conducted, by the operator;
a description of any aeronautical or aviation-related services provided, or to be provided, by third parties to the operator;
the following manuals:
an operations manual;
a dangerous goods manual (if any);
a training management system manual that describes the operator’s training management system;

if the operator conducts the activities only in aircraft, or in aircraft and flight simulation training devices—a safety management system manual that describes the operator’s safety management system;
if the operator conducts the activities only in flight simulation training devices—a quality assurance management system manual that describes the operator’s quality assurance management system;
an internal training and checking system manual that describes the operator’s internal training and checking system;
a description of the operator’s process for making changes including:
identifying changes that are significant changes; and
identifying changes that are not significant changes; and
telling CASA of the changes;
a description of any other matter required to be approved by CASA under these Regulations in relation to Part 142 activities;
a matter prescribed by a legislative instrument under regulation 142.045 for this paragraph.
A manual mentioned in paragraph (o) or any of subparagraphs (1)(s)(ii) to (vi) may be included as part of the operator’s operations manual.
An exposition for a Part 142 operator may include a list of material required for the operator’s reference library.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—compliance with exposition by operator

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if the operator contravenes a provision of its exposition.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the operator’s exposition relates to a duty or responsibility of a person who is a member of the operator’s personnel; and
the operator does not make the part of the exposition that relates to the duty or responsibility available to the person before the person first begins carrying out the duty or responsibility.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 142.L—Part 142 operators—logs and records
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a person participates in an authorised Part 142 activity conducted by the operator; and
a record of the person’s participation, including a description and assessment of the person’s performance, is not made within 21 days after the activity is conducted.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if the operator does not retain a record made under subregulation (1) for at least 7 years after the record is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if the operator does not make a record made under regulation 142.355 available, on request, to the person to whom the record relates.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a record is made under regulation 142.355; and
the operator receives a request from another Part 142 operator for a copy of the record; and
the operator holds a written authority from the person to whom the record relates to provide a copy of the person’s records to another Part 142 operator if requested; and
the operator does not give a copy of the record to the other Part 142 operator within 7 days after receiving the request.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 142.M—Part 142 operators—miscellaneous offences

section.heading: Part 142 operators—pilot in command for training to be authorised under Part 61

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a person flies an aircraft as pilot in command in the conduct of an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator; and
the person is not authorised under Part 61 to fly the aircraft as pilot in command.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Note: See also subsection 20AB(1) of the Act.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—carriage of passengers prohibited during abnormal operations or low-flying activity

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
during a flight of an aircraft for an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator:
a simulated engine or system failure that affects the aircraft’s performance or handling characteristics is conducted; or
a low-flying activity is conducted; and
a passenger is carried on the flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—authorisation of carriage of passengers

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a person flies an aircraft used in an authorised Part 142 activity for the operator as pilot in command; and
the operator authorises the carriage of a passenger on the flight; and
the person is not authorised under Part 61 to fly the aircraft as pilot in command with a passenger on board.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—integrated training courses: transfer of student from another Part 142 operator

content.p: This regulation applies if:
(a) a person seeks to undertake part of an integrated training course with a Part 142 operator (the current operator); and
(b) the person has previously undertaken part of the course with one or more other Part 142 operators (the previous operators).
The current operator commits an offence if:
the operator provides part of the course to the person; and
the operator does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (2)(b), the requirement is that the current operator must have determined:
what part of the course the person has completed with the previous operators; and

what part of the course the person needs to complete with the current operator to ensure that, taken together, the parts of the course provided by the previous and current operators will meet the standards specified in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for the course.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—completion of training and assessment of competency for certain solo flights

content.p: Student pilots
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a student pilot who is undertaking authorised Part 142 flight training with the operator conducts a solo flight of a kind mentioned in subregulation (2) for the first time; and
the student pilot does not meet the requirements mentioned in subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(a), the kinds of solo flight are the following:
a circuit training flight;
a flight between an aerodrome and the flight training area for the aerodrome;
a cross-country flight;
a flight at night.
For paragraph (1)(b), the requirements are the following:
the student pilot must have completed the training mentioned in the operator’s exposition that relates to the conduct of a solo flight of that kind by a student pilot;
the student pilot must have been assessed by the operator as competent to conduct the solo flight;

if the flight is a flight of a kind mentioned in paragraph (2)(c) or (d)—the student pilot must have completed at least 2 hours of dual instrument time, 1 hour of which is conducted during dual instrument flight time.
Holders of pilot licences
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the holder of a pilot licence who is receiving flight training from the operator for a rating or endorsement on the pilot’s licence conducts a solo flight at night for the first time; and
the flight training is authorised Part 142 training for the operator; and
the holder does not meet the requirements mentioned in subregulation (5).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (4)(c), the requirements are the following:
the holder must have completed the training mentioned in the operator’s exposition that relates to the conduct of a solo flight for flight training for the rating or endorsement;
the holder must have been assessed by the operator as competent to conduct the solo flight.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Note: See also Subdivision 61.A.3.1 and regulation 61.1225.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—appropriate briefing and capability to conduct certain solo flights etc.

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
a person who is undertaking authorised Part 142 flight training with the operator conducts a solo flight for the first time; and
the person does not meet the requirements mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the requirements are the following:
the person must have been briefed appropriately for the flight;
the person must be capable of conducting the flight safely;
if the person is a student pilot—the person must:
have been assessed by CASA or an examiner as meeting the general English language proficiency standard mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards; or
have completed an approved course of training in English language proficiency;
the person must have an ARN.
Strict liability applies to paragraph (1)(a).
Note: See also Subdivision 61.A.3.1 and regulation 61.1225.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—dealings in relation to cancelled, suspended, varied, pending or refused civil aviation authorisations: when approval required

content.p: Requirement for approval
A Part 142 operator commits an offence if:
the operator does an act mentioned in subregulation (2), (4), (6) or (8); and
the operator does not hold an approval under regulation 142.040 to do the act.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Acts in relation to cancelled authorisations
For paragraph (1)(a), the acts are the following:
to use, in any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, an aircraft the operation of which was authorised by a cancelled authorisation;

to employ, in connection with any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, a person who was, at the time of the cancellation, employed in connection with an operation the conduct of which was authorised by a cancelled authorisation;
to conduct an operation, or part of an operation, the conduct of which was authorised by a cancelled authorisation.
Acts in relation to suspended or varied authorisations
Subregulation (4) applies in relation to a suspended or varied authorisation.
For paragraph (1)(a), the acts are the following:
to use, in any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, an aircraft the operation of which:
was, immediately before the suspension or variation, authorised by the authorisation; but
is no longer authorised by the authorisation as suspended or varied;

to employ, in connection with any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, a person who was, at the time of the suspension or variation, employed in connection with an operation the conduct of which:
was, immediately before the suspension or variation, authorised by the authorisation; but
is no longer authorised by the authorisation as suspended or varied;
to conduct an operation, or part of an operation, the conduct of which:
was, immediately before the suspension or variation, authorised by the authorisation; but
is no longer authorised by the authorisation as suspended or varied.
Note: See section 28BB of the Act in relation to varying AOC conditions.
Pending applications for authorisations
Subregulation (6) applies in relation to an application for a civil aviation authorisation that has not been finally determined by CASA.
For paragraph (1)(a), the acts are the following:
to use, in any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, an aircraft the operation of which would be authorised by the authorisation;

to employ, in connection with any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, a person employed, or proposed to be employed, in connection with an operation the conduct of which would be authorised by the authorisation;
to conduct an operation, or part of an operation, the conduct of which would be authorised by the authorisation.
Application for authorisation refused
Subregulation (8) applies in relation to an application for a civil aviation authorisation that has been refused by CASA.
For paragraph (1)(a), the acts are the following:
to use, in any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, an aircraft the use of which would have been authorised by the authorisation;

to employ, in connection with any of the operator’s authorised Part 142 activities, a person employed, or proposed to be employed, in connection with an operation the conduct of which would have been authorised by the authorisation;
to conduct an operation, or part of an operation, the conduct of which would have been authorised by the authorisation.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
In this regulation:
cancelled authorisation means a civil aviation authorisation that has been cancelled otherwise than on application by the holder of the authorisation.
employ includes engage, whether by contract or other arrangement.
suspended authorisation means a civil aviation authorisation that has been suspended otherwise than on application by the holder of the authorisation.
varied authorisation means a civil aviation authorisation that has been varied otherwise than on application by the holder of the authorisation.

section.heading: Part 142 operators—maximum period for use of foreign registered aircraft in Australian territory

content.p: A Part 142 operator commits an offence if, in any 12 month period, the operator uses a foreign registered aircraft to conduct authorised activities in Australian territory for a total of more than the number of days mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), the number of days is:
90; or
if the operator holds an approval under regulation 142.040 for this regulation in relation to the aircraft—the number mentioned in the approval for the aircraft.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
In this regulation:
authorised activity, for a Part 142 operator, means an activity authorised by a civil aviation authorisation held by the operator.

Subpart 143.A—General
This Part:
applies to a person that wants to become, or is, an ATS training provider; and
sets out certain administrative rules applying to CASA in its administration of this Part.
However, this Part does not apply to:
a person who is providing ATS training in the course of his or her duties for the Defence Force; or
any ATS training provided by the Defence Force.
In this Part:
Australian National Training Authority means the Australian National Training Authority established by the Australian National Training Authority Act 1992.

Australian Qualifications Framework means the framework set out in a document called ‘Australian Qualifications Framework Implementation Handbook’ published by the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) Advisory Board in 1998.

Australian Quality Training Framework means the quality arrangements for vocational education and training services set out in the document called ‘Australian Quality Training Framework – Standards for Registered Training Organisations’ published by the Australian National Training Authority in 2001.
Manual of Standards – Part 65 means the document called ‘Manual of Standards (MOS) – Part 65’ issued by CASA under regulation 65.033, as in force from time to time.
Manual of Standards – Part 143 means the document called ‘Manual of Standards (MOS) – Part 143’ issued by CASA under regulation 143.017, as in force from time to time.
training provider means a person who, or entity that, provides vocational education and training.

training recognition authority, in relation to a State or Territory, means a body that has, under a law of the State or Territory, the responsibility for registering training providers in that State or Territory.

section.heading: What is an ATS training provider

content.p: An ATS training provider is a person approved, under Subpart 143.F, to provide the training relating to air traffic services that is covered by the approval.

section.heading: Person not to provide service without approval

content.p: A person must not provide training relating to air traffic services unless the person:
is approved, under Division 143.F.2, to provide the training; or
is an ATS provider within the meaning in Part 172.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part that provides for the following matters:
standards, including procedures, plans, systems and documentation, for the provision of air traffic services training;
standards for facilities and equipment used to provide air traffic services training;
standards, including competency standards and minimum qualifications, for instructors engaged in air traffic services training;
any matter required or permitted by these Regulations to be provided for by the Manual of Standards;
any matter necessary or convenient to be provided for the effective operation of this Part.

Note: A Manual of Standards is a legislative instrument—see subsections 98(5A) and (5B) of the Act. It must be registered in accordance with the Legislation Act 2003 and must be tabled in both Houses of the Parliament within 6 sitting days after its making.
CASA must give a copy of a notice about a Manual of Standards for this Part (being a notice referred to in subregulation 11.275(3) or regulation 11.280) to each ATS training provider.
Note: Subpart 11.J (including regulations 11.275 and 11.280) sets out procedures for the issue, amendment and revocation of a MOS.
Subpart 143.B—Approval as an ATS training provider

section.heading: What an application must be accompanied by

content.p: An application for approval as an ATS training provider must be accompanied by:
a written statement setting out details of the training relating to air traffic services that the applicant proposes to provide; and

a written statement setting out details of the relevant qualifications and experience of the applicant and applicant’s personnel, including the number of suitably qualified personnel who will be involved in providing the training; and
enough information to show that the applicant is a registered training organisation whose registration:
is in force; and
is for training delivery covering the training; and
a written statement describing the arrangements the applicant has made to comply with the requirements of Subparts 143.C and 143.D.

section.heading: When applicant is eligible for approval

content.p: For Subpart 143.F, an applicant is eligible to become an ATS training provider for particular training relating to air traffic services if the applicant:
is any of the following:
the Commonwealth;
AA;
(iii) a person who is to provide air traffic services training services in cooperation with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(b) of the Air Services Act 1995;
(iv) a person who is to provide air traffic services training services by arrangement with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(c) of the Air Services Act 1995; and
is a registered training organisation whose registration:
is in force; and
is for training delivery covering that training; and
is able to comply with the requirements of Subparts 143.C and 143.D or will be able to do so if the applicant is approved.

section.heading: CASA may impose conditions on approvals

content.p: Without limiting regulations 11.056 and 11.067, CASA may impose, on an approval, any condition necessary to give effect to an arrangement mentioned in subsection 11(3) of the Air Services Act 1995.
If an ATS training provider wants to vary its approval, it must apply to CASA, under Subpart 143.F, for that purpose.
The application must contain, or have with it, a copy of the proposed variation.
Subpart 143.C—Requirements to be complied with by ATS training providers
An ATS training provider must ensure that the training relating to air traffic services that it provides:
is of at least the standard required by the Manual of Standards – Part 65; and
complies with the Australian Qualifications Framework.

An ATS training provider must have, and put into effect, a training plan for the training relating to air traffic services covered by its approval that is in accordance with the standards and requirements set out in the Manual of Standards – Part 65.

An ATS training provider must have, at all times, enough suitably qualified personnel to enable it to provide, in accordance with both the Australian Quality Training Framework and the standards and requirements set out in the Manual of Standards – Part 65, the training relating to air traffic services that is covered by its approval.
An ATS training provider must not give to a person responsibility as an instructor or assessor for any training relating to air traffic services that it provides unless the person:
has suitable qualifications and experience in accordance with the Australian Quality Training Framework; and
satisfies the requirements of the Manual of Standards – Part 65 for persons having that responsibility.

An ATS training provider must maintain a set of the reference materials mentioned in regulation 143.080 for use by members of its personnel who have responsibilities as instructors or assessors for any training relating to air traffic services that it provides.
The provider must maintain another set of the reference materials for use by anyone undertaking training relating to air traffic services that it provides.
The provider must keep the reference materials up to date and in a readily accessible form.
The instructors and assessors and anyone undertaking training must have ready access to the reference materials.

section.heading: Material to be included in reference materials

content.p: For regulation 143.075, the reference materials to be maintained by the provider must include the following:
copies of the Act and these Regulations;
copies of Annexes 1, 6, 11 and 12 to the Chicago Convention;
a copy of the AIP;
copies of the Manual of Standards – Part 65 and the Manual of Standards – Part 143;
all manuals and documents specified in the Manual of Standards – Part 65 and Manual of Standards – Part 143.
The provider must keep documents and records of the kinds specified in the Manual of Standards – Part 143.
A document or record must be retained for as long as the Manual specifies for the particular kind of document or record.
The provider must, at CASA’s request, make the documents and records, or copies of them or extracts from them, available for inspection by CASA.

The provider must establish, and put into effect, a system, in accordance with the standards set out in the Manual of Standards – Part 143, for controlling the documents and records required to be kept under regulation 143.085.
The system must include the policies and procedures for making, amending and preserving those documents and records.
Subpart 143.D—Telling CASA about changes

The provider must tell CASA, in writing, of a change of circumstances that materially affects its capacity to provide any training relating to air traffic services that is covered by its approval within 7 days after the change occurs.

The provider must not discontinue any training relating to air traffic services that is covered by its approval, unless it has given CASA at least 28 days written notice that the training is to be discontinued.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if, having regard to the provider’s circumstances:
it was not reasonably practicable for the provider to give to CASA at least 28 days notice; and
the provider gives the notice as soon as reasonably practicable before, on or after the day when the service is discontinued.

If an ATS training provider, for any reason at any time after its approval as an ATS training provider, loses its status as a registered training organisation, it must, within 7 days, tell CASA in writing accordingly.
Subpart 143.E—Miscellaneous
An ATS training provider must not provide any training relating to air traffic services unless:
its approval:
is in force; and
covers that training; and
it is a registered training organisation whose registration:
is in force; and
is for training delivery covering that training.
Subpart 143.F—Administration
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Subpart, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for approval as an ATS training provider.
This Subpart:
sets out certain administrative rules applying to CASA in its administration of this Part; and
includes certain generic provisions applying to anyone who wants to become, or is, an ATS training provider.
Subject to regulation 143.120, a person may apply to CASA, in writing, for approval as an ATS training provider.
Note: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
An application purportedly made by 2 or more persons jointly is not a valid application for any purpose.
An application purportedly made by a partnership is not a valid application for any purpose.

section.heading: Applications by corporations etc—what must be included

content.p: An application from a person other than an individual must set out:
the applicant’s registered address and ACN; and
the names and addresses of its officers.
In paragraph (1)(b):
officer has the meaning given by section 9 of the Corporations Act 2001.

section.heading: CASA may require demonstrations of procedures or equipment

content.p: Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to an approval as an ATS training provider.
Subject to regulation 11.055, if an applicant has applied for approval as an ATS training provider under this Part, CASA must grant the approval.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
If CASA does not make a decision about an application within the period mentioned in subregulation (2) after receiving it, CASA is taken to have refused the application.
The period is 6 months.

However, if CASA makes a request under regulation 11.035, 11.040 or 11.045, the time between when CASA makes the request, and when the applicant conducts the demonstration, comes in for interview, or gives CASA the information or copy requested, does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA asks an applicant to make a statutory declaration under regulation 11.047 or subregulation 11.050(3A), the time between when CASA asks the applicant to do so and when the applicant gives CASA the statutory declaration does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA invites an applicant to make a written submission under subregulation 11.050(2), the time between when CASA gives the invitation and when the applicant makes the written submission does not count towards the period.
In this regulation:
application includes an application to vary an approval under this Division.
In this Division:
show cause notice means a notice under regulation 143.230.

section.heading: Suspension of approval by show cause notice

content.p: CASA may state, in a show cause notice, that an ATS training provider’s approval is suspended if CASA reasonably considers that not suspending the approval would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
If a show cause notice states that the approval is suspended, the approval is suspended from when the notice is given to the provider.
CASA may revoke the suspension at any time.
If CASA has not cancelled the approval under regulation 143.235, within 90 days after the day the show cause notice is given to the provider, the suspension lapses at the end of that period.
It is grounds for the cancellation of an ATS training provider’s approval if the provider:
has breached a condition of the approval; or
has contravened the Act or these Regulations; or
does not meet, or continue to meet, a requirement of this Part for getting the approval; or
has otherwise been guilty of conduct that renders the provider’s continued holding of the approval likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Note: Regulation 201.004 provides for review of certain decisions by the Administrative Review Tribunal.

CASA may give an ATS training provider a show cause notice if there are reasonable grounds for believing that there are facts or circumstances that amount to grounds for the cancellation of the provider’s approval.
A show cause notice must:
tell the provider of the facts and circumstances that justify the cancellation of the approval; and
invite the provider to show in writing, within a reasonable period stated in the notice, why the approval should not be cancelled.
For paragraph (2)(b), the period must not be less than 7 days.

section.heading: Cancellation of approval after show cause notice

content.p: Subject to regulation 143.245, CASA may cancel an ATS training provider’s approval only if:
there exist facts or circumstances that amount to grounds for the cancellation of the approval; and
CASA has given the provider a show cause notice in relation to the grounds for the proposed cancellation; and
CASA has taken into account any written representations made, within the period stated in the notice, by or on behalf of the provider; and
not cancelling the approval would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
If CASA has given a show cause notice to an ATS training provider, and it decides not to cancel the provider’s approval, it:
must tell the provider, in writing, of the decision; and
must, if the approval is suspended, revoke the suspension.

section.heading: Cancellation if cooperation or arrangement ceases

content.p: CASA must cancel the approval of a person mentioned in subparagraph 143.025(aa)(iii) if the cooperation mentioned in that subparagraph ceases.
CASA must cancel the approval of a person mentioned in subparagraph 143.025(aa)(iv) if the arrangement mentioned in that subparagraph ceases.
Note: This Part heading is reserved for future use.
