Subpart 145.A—General
This Part:
sets out matters relating to Part 145 organisations, including:
requirements for approval as a Part 145 organisation; and
requirements that apply to Part 145 organisations; and
empowers CASA to issue a Manual of Standards for this Part.
Note: See Division 202.GE.2.1 for transitional provisions under which Part 145 organisations can be approved to undertake CAR maintenance activities.
In this Part:
accountable manager, for a Part 145 organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for:
ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition, each approval rating that it holds, and these Regulations; and
ensuring that the organisation is able to finance the provision of the maintenance services set out in its exposition; and
ensuring that the organisation has adequate resources available to enable it to provide maintenance services in accordance with its exposition; and
establishing and promoting policies for safety management and quality systems in accordance with the requirements of this Part and Part 42.
approval certificate means a certificate issued under regulation 145.035.
approval rating means a rating for a kind of aircraft, aeronautical product or specialist maintenance specified in the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
exposition, for a Part 145 organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 145.030 in relation to the organisation, including:
if a change to the document is approved by CASA under regulation 145.055—that change; and
if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under regulation 145.060—the updated part of the document; and
if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 145.065—that change.

quality manager, for a Part 145 organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for the quality management system described in the Part 145 Manual of Standards for the organisation.

responsible manager, for a Part 145 organisation, means an individual appointed by the organisation to be responsible to the accountable manager for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to a particular matter.

safety manager, for a Part 145 organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for the safety management system described in the Part 145 Manual of Standards for the organisation.
significant change, in relation to a Part 145 organisation, has the meaning given by subregulation (2).
Note: See the Dictionary for definitions of other terms used in this Part.
(2) A significant change, in relation to a Part 145 organisation, means any of the following changes:
a change to the organisation’s name;
a change to the location of the organisation’s maintenance facility, including the addition of a new maintenance facility;
a change in the personnel holding:
the position of accountable manager in the organisation; or
the position of quality manager in the organisation; or
any of the positions of responsible manager in the organisation; or
the position of safety manager in the organisation;
a change to the maintenance services provided by the organisation, if the change would require a change to the approval ratings mentioned in the organisation’s approval certificate;
a change to the permitted training that it is approved to provide;

a change to the organisation’s facilities, equipment, tools, materials, procedures or certifying employees that could adversely affect the organisation’s ability to provide maintenance services that it is approved to provide.
For subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part that specifies matters affecting the maintenance or airworthiness of aircraft.
In particular, a Manual of Standards may specify the following matters:
maintenance that is specialist maintenance for a Part 145 organisation;
ratings for kinds of aircraft, aeronautical products and specialist maintenance;
requirements for a Part 145 organisation’s exposition;
the privileges that apply to an approval rating;
requirements for a Part 145 organisation, including requirements in relation to the following:
facilities;
managers;
certifying employees;
employee qualifications;
the grant of certification authorisations;
training;
equipment, tools and materials;
aeronautical products;
maintenance data;
writing procedures for carrying out maintenance;
production planning;
the issue of certificates of release to service;
in-house maintenance and in-house release documents;
the fabrication of parts in the course of carrying out maintenance;
records;
defect reporting;
a quality management system, including auditing;
a safety management system;
a procedure for making changes to the organisation that are not significant changes;
requirements for providing permitted training;

requirements for a Part 145 organisation in relation to arranging for the manufacturer of an aircraft or aircraft engine that forms part of a permitted aircraft type to provide training and assessment for the permitted aircraft type to the organisation’s employees.

section.heading: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply in relation to certain matters

content.p: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply to:
a significant change to a Part 145 organisation that is approved by CASA under regulation 145.055; or
a change to a Part 145 organisation of which CASA is notified under regulation 145.060; or
a change to a Part 145 organisation that is made as a consequence of a change made to the organisation’s exposition in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 145.065.
Subpart 145.B—Approval of Part 145 organisations
(1) A person (the applicant) may apply to CASA for approval as a Part 145 organisation.
The application must:
be in writing; and
be signed by a person who is, or proposes to be, the applicant’s accountable manager.
The application must include the following:
a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition;
the approval rating sought by the applicant for:
each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant proposes to provide maintenance services; and
each kind of specialist maintenance that the applicant proposes to provide;
if the applicant intends to provide permitted training for its employees—each aircraft type, aircraft system or subset of an aircraft system for which the applicant intends to provide training.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations, and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant as a Part 145 organisation if CASA is satisfied that:
the applicant has an exposition that complies with the requirements specified in the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has facilities, equipment, materials, maintenance data and tools that are suitable for:
providing maintenance services for the kinds of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant proposes to provide maintenance services; and
providing the specialist maintenance that the applicant proposes to provide; and
providing the permitted training that the applicant proposes to provide for its employees; and
the facilities, equipment, materials, maintenance data and tools mentioned in paragraph (b) comply with the requirements specified in the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for each of the following positions in the organisation:
accountable manager;
quality manager;
safety manager; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for each position of responsible manager in the organisation; and
each individual nominated for a position mentioned in paragraph (d) or (e) is appropriately qualified to hold the position; and
the audit requirements of the applicant’s quality management system will be carried out by a person who is not:
the accountable manager; or
a responsible manager.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
If CASA decides to approve an applicant as a Part 145 organisation, CASA must determine:
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the applicant is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the applicant is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b); and
the permitted training that the applicant is approved to provide for its employees.
In approving the applicant, CASA also approves the applicant’s proposed exposition.
If CASA approves an applicant as a Part 145 organisation, CASA must issue a certificate setting out the matters mentioned in paragraphs 145.030(2)(a) to (c).
The certificate issued by CASA must include an approval certificate reference number determined by CASA.
If CASA approves a significant change to a Part 145 organisation under regulation 145.055, CASA may issue a new approval certificate to the organisation.
A Part 145 organisation may provide:
maintenance services that it is approved to provide; and
permitted training that it is approved to provide for its employees.
A Part 145 organisation may arrange for training and assessment for a permitted aircraft type to be provided by the manufacturer of the aircraft or the aircraft engine.
It is a condition of approval of a Part 145 organisation that:
the organisation must, at all times, comply with the requirements of:
its exposition; and
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the organisation is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the organisation is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in subparagraph (ii) or (iii); and
the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
Part 42 and this Part; and
the organisation must ensure that, at all times, its employees comply with the requirements mentioned in paragraph (a).
Note 1: The approval is also subject to the conditions set out in Part 11.
Note 2: Subpart 11.G empowers CASA to issue directions.
Subpart 145.C—Changes to Part 145 organisations

section.heading: Application for approval of significant changes to organisations

content.p: If a Part 145 organisation proposes to make a significant change, the organisation must apply to CASA for approval of the change.
The application must:
be in writing; and
set out the proposed change; and
include a copy of the part of the exposition consequentially affected by the change, showing the proposed change.
Subject to subregulation (4), the application must be made before the change is made.
If:
the change is of the kind mentioned in paragraph 145.010(2)(c); and
the organisation does not apply, in accordance with subregulation (2), before making the change;
the organisation must apply in accordance with subregulation (2) within 7 days after making the change.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Note 3: Making a significant change without applying for approval in accordance with this regulation will be a breach of condition of an approval—see regulation 145.045.

Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a significant change to a Part 145 organisation if CASA is satisfied that, after making the change, the requirements mentioned in subregulation 145.030(1) will continue to be met.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
In approving the significant change, CASA also approves the consequential changes to the applicant’s exposition.

section.heading: Changes to Part 145 organisations that are not significant changes

content.p: A change that is not a significant change to a Part 145 organisation must be made in accordance with the procedure set out in the organisation’s exposition for making changes to the organisation that are not significant changes.
If such a change is made, the organisation must, within 28 days after making the change:
update its exposition; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the updated part of the exposition.

section.heading: CASA may direct Part 145 organisations to change exposition

content.p: CASA may direct a Part 145 organisation to change its exposition:
to remove particular information from the exposition; or
to include particular information in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information in the exposition.

CASA may give a direction under this regulation only if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary to do so to ensure that the exposition complies with the requirements specified in the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
Note: The Part 145 organisation must comply with the direction—see regulation 145.085.
Subpart 145.D—Requirements and offences for Part 145 organisations
If a Part 145 organisation provides maintenance services, it must provide the services only in accordance with:
its exposition; and
the approval rating for each kind of aircraft or aeronautical product for which the organisation is approved to provide maintenance services; and
the approval rating for each kind of specialist maintenance that the organisation is approved to provide; and
any limitations applying to an approval rating mentioned in paragraph (b) or (c); and
the privileges that apply to the approval rating under the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
If a Part 145 organisation provides permitted training for its employees, it must:
provide only the permitted training that it is approved to provide; and
provide the permitted training only in accordance with its exposition.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

If a Part 145 organisation’s exposition relates to the duties of an employee of the organisation, the organisation must make the part of the organisation’s exposition that relates to those duties available to the employee before the employee begins carrying out the duties.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
If CASA gives a direction to a Part 145 organisation under regulation 145.065, the organisation must comply with the direction within the time mentioned in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

Subpart 147.A—General
This Part:
sets out matters relating to maintenance training organisations, including:
requirements for approval as a maintenance training organisation; and
requirements that apply to maintenance training organisations; and
empowers CASA to issue a Manual of Standards for this Part.
In this Part:
accountable manager, for a maintenance training organisation, means the individual, appointed by the organisation, who is responsible for ensuring that the organisation:
complies with its exposition and these Regulations; and
is able to finance the provision of the kinds of maintenance training set out in its exposition; and
has adequate resources available to enable it to provide maintenance training in accordance with its exposition.
aircraft type has the meaning given by regulation 66.010.
approval certificate means a certificate issued under regulation 147.035.

assessment means an assessment of units of competency for category training, or elements for aircraft type training, by any or all of the following means: examination of theory by means of written questions or oral questions or both; practical testing of the skills acquired in practical training; consideration of evidence for recognition of prior learning. 1 Responses to interview questions. 2 Formal qualifications and other documents evidencing an area of competence. 3 Third party verification. 4 Workplace observation. 5 Sample examination results or sample practical test results. course plan, for a maintenance training organisation and a maintenance training course, means the plan for the maintenance training course set out in the organisation’s exposition. exposition, for a maintenance training organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 147.030 in relation to the organisation, including: if a change to the document is approved under regulation 147.055—that change; and if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under subregulation 147.060—the updated part of the document; and if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 147.065—that change. feedback system, for a quality management system, has the meaning given by the Part 147 Manual of Standards.
examination of theory by means of written questions or oral questions or both;
practical testing of the skills acquired in practical training;
consideration of evidence for recognition of prior learning.
Examples: Evidence that may be assessed for recognition of prior learning
1 Responses to interview questions.
2 Formal qualifications and other documents evidencing an area of competence.
3 Third party verification.
4 Workplace observation.
5 Sample examination results or sample practical test results.
course plan, for a maintenance training organisation and a maintenance training course, means the plan for the maintenance training course set out in the organisation’s exposition.
exposition, for a maintenance training organisation, means the document that is approved by CASA under regulation 147.030 in relation to the organisation, including:
if a change to the document is approved under regulation 147.055—that change; and
if the document is updated and the organisation gives CASA a copy of the updated part of the document under subregulation 147.060—the updated part of the document; and
if the organisation makes a change to the document in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 147.065—that change.
feedback system, for a quality management system, has the meaning given by the Part 147 Manual of Standards.
practical training means training that allows a student who has undertaken training in theory to practise applying the theory.
quality management system, for a maintenance training organisation, means the quality management system described in the Part 147 Manual of Standards.

recognition of prior learning means full or partial credit given in a unit of competency for category training, or in an element for aircraft type training, for prior work experience, training or qualifications attained in Australia or a foreign country.

responsible manager, for a maintenance training organisation, means an individual appointed by the organisation to be responsible to the accountable manager for ensuring that the organisation complies with its exposition and these Regulations in relation to a particular matter.
significant change, in relation to a maintenance training organisation, has the meaning given by subregulation (2).
theory means a theoretical element of aircraft type training or category training.
Note: See the Dictionary for definitions of other terms used in this Part.
(2) A significant change, in relation to a maintenance training organisation, means any of the following changes:
a change to the organisation’s name;
a change to the location of the organisation’s maintenance training facility, including the addition of a new maintenance training facility;
a change in the personnel holding:
the position of accountable manager in the organisation; or
any of the positions of responsible manager in the organisation;
a change to a course or a course plan provided by the organisation, other than a change resulting from a change to Appendix I, II, III or IV to the Part 66 Manual of Standards;
a change to the organisation’s quality management system, other than a change involving the taking of any necessary corrective action under the feedback system;

a change to the organisation’s facilities, personnel, record management system, instructional equipment, maintenance training material or procedures that could adversely affect the organisation’s ability to provide the maintenance training that it is approved to provide.
For subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part that specifies matters affecting the maintenance or airworthiness of aircraft.
In particular, a Manual of Standards may specify the following matters:
the category training a maintenance training organisation may be approved to provide;
the aircraft type training a maintenance training organisation may be approved to provide;
the kinds of assessment a maintenance training organisation may be approved to carry out;
requirements for a maintenance training organisation’s exposition;
requirements for a maintenance training organisation, including requirements in relation to the following:
facilities;
employees, including employee qualifications;
records of instructors and assessors;
course plans;
conduct of assessments;
instructional equipment;
maintenance training material;
records;
training procedures and the quality management system, including auditing;
assessments;
a procedure for making changes to the organisation that are not significant changes.

section.heading: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply in relation to certain matters

content.p: Regulations 11.070 to 11.075 do not apply to:
a significant change to a maintenance training organisation that is approved by CASA under regulation 147.055; or
a change to a maintenance training organisation of which CASA is notified under regulation 147.060; or
a change to a maintenance training organisation that is made as a consequence of a change made to the organisation’s exposition in accordance with a direction given by CASA under regulation 147.065.
Subpart 147.B—Approval of maintenance training organisations
(1) A person (the applicant) may apply to CASA for approval as a maintenance training organisation.
Only a person who is a registered training organisation may apply for approval as a maintenance training organisation to provide category training or carry out assessment of units of competency.
The application must:
be in writing; and
be signed by a person who is, or proposes to be, the applicant’s accountable manager.
The application must include the following:
a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition;
if the applicant is seeking approval to provide category training—the categories of aircraft engineer licence for which the applicant proposes to provide training;
if the applicant is seeking approval to provide aircraft type training—the ratings for which the applicant proposes to provide training;
the kinds of assessment that the applicant proposes to carry out;
whether the applicant is seeking approval to recognise prior learning for assessment purposes.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations, and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant as a maintenance training organisation if CASA is satisfied that:
the applicant has an exposition that complies with the requirements specified in the Part 147 Manual of Standards; and

the applicant has facilities, personnel, a record management system, instructional equipment, maintenance training material and a quality management system that comply with the Part 147 Manual of Standards; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for the position of accountable manager in the organisation; and
the applicant has nominated an individual for each position of responsible manager in the organisation; and
each individual nominated for a position mentioned in paragraph (c) or (d) is appropriately qualified to hold the position.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
If CASA decides to approve an applicant as a maintenance training organisation, CASA must determine:
whether the organisation is approved to provide:
category training; or
aircraft type training; or
both category training and aircraft type training; and
if the organisation is approved to provide category training—the categories of aircraft engineer licence for which the applicant is approved to provide training; and
if the organisation is approved to provide aircraft type training—the ratings for which the applicant is approved to provide training; and
the kinds of assessment that the organisation is approved to carry out; and
whether the organisation may recognise prior learning for assessment purposes.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant to provide category training if:
CASA has approved the applicant as a maintenance training organisation; and
CASA is satisfied that the applicant meets the criteria set out in Appendices I, II and IV to the Part 66 Manual of Standards.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve an applicant to provide aircraft type training if:
CASA has approved the applicant as a maintenance training organisation; and
CASA is satisfied that the applicant meets the criteria set out in Appendix III to the Part 66 Manual of Standards.
In approving the applicant, CASA also approves the applicant’s proposed exposition.
If CASA approves an applicant as a maintenance training organisation, CASA must issue a certificate setting out the matters mentioned in subregulation 147.030(2).
The certificate issued by CASA must include an approval certificate reference number determined by CASA.
If CASA approves a significant change to a maintenance training organisation under regulation 147.055, CASA may issue a new approval certificate to the organisation.
A maintenance training organisation may:
provide maintenance training that it is approved to provide; and
carry out assessments that it is approved to carry out; and
if the organisation is approved to recognise prior learning for assessment purposes—carry out assessments based on recognition of prior learning; and
issue certificates, in the approved form, to students who have successfully completed that training and assessment.
It is a condition of approval of a maintenance training organisation that:
the organisation must, at all times, comply with the requirements of:
its approval as a maintenance training organisation; and
its exposition; and
the Part 147 Manual of Standards; and
this Part; and
the organisation must ensure that, at all times, its employees comply with the requirements mentioned in paragraph (a).
Note 1: The approval is also subject to the conditions set out in Part 11.
Note 2: Subpart 11.G empowers CASA to issue directions.
Subpart 147.C—Changes to maintenance training organisations

section.heading: Application for approval of significant changes to organisations

content.p: If a maintenance training organisation proposes to make a significant change, the organisation must apply to CASA for approval of the change.
The application must:
be in writing; and
set out the proposed change; and
include a copy of the part of the exposition consequentially affected by the proposed change, showing the proposed change.
Subject to subregulation (4), the application must be made before the change is made.
If:
the change is:
a change of the kind mentioned in paragraph 147.010(2)(c); or
a change of the kind mentioned in paragraph 147.010(2)(f) in relation to the personnel of the organisation; and
the organisation does not apply, in accordance with subregulation (2), before making the change;
the organisation must apply in accordance with subregulation (2) within 7 days after making the change.

Note 1: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
Note 2: Part 11 deals with applications and decision making.
Note 3: Making a significant change without applying for approval in accordance with this regulation will be a breach of condition of an approval—see regulation 147.045.

section.heading: Decision on application for approval of significant changes

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a significant change to a maintenance training organisation if CASA is satisfied that, after making the change, the requirements mentioned in subregulation 147.030(1) will continue to be met.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue, or cancelling, suspending or varying, an approval; or
a decision imposing a condition on an approval.
In approving the significant change, CASA also approves the consequential changes to the applicant’s exposition.

section.heading: Changes to maintenance training organisations that are not significant changes

content.p: A change that is not a significant change to a maintenance training organisation must be made in accordance with the amendment procedure set out in the organisation’s exposition.
If such a change is made, the organisation must, within 28 days after making the change:
update its exposition; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the updated part of the exposition.

section.heading: CASA may direct maintenance training organisations to change exposition

content.p: CASA may direct a maintenance training organisation to change its exposition:
to remove particular information from the exposition; or
to include particular information in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information in the exposition.

CASA may give a direction under this regulation only if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary to do so to ensure that the exposition complies with the requirements specified in the Part 147 Manual of Standards.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
Note: The maintenance training organisation must comply with the direction—see regulation 147.085.
Subpart 147.D—Requirements and offences for maintenance training organisations

section.heading: Provision of maintenance training and assessment

content.p: If a maintenance training organisation provides maintenance training, carries out assessments or issues certificates, it must do so only in accordance with:
its approval as a maintenance training organisation; and
its exposition; and
the Part 147 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
In assessing a person, a maintenance training organisation must not give credit to the person for holding a licence (however described) that was issued to the person by an excluded State.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Note 1: Subregulation 66.060 prevents the recognition of a licence issued by an excluded State.
Note 2: For recognition of a foreign licence issued by a recognised State, see regulations 66.030 and 66.035.
Note 3: For recognition of a foreign licence not issued by a recognised State, see regulations 66.040, 66.045, 66.050 and 66.055.

If a maintenance training organisation’s exposition relates to the duties of an employee of the organisation, the organisation must make the part of the organisation’s exposition that relates to those duties available to the employee before the employee begins carrying out the duties.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
If CASA gives a maintenance training organisation a direction under regulation 147.065, the organisation must comply with the direction within the time mentioned in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.

Subpart 149.A—General
If a provision of this Part refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, the person may apply to CASA, in writing, for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant the approval.
For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by these Regulations to be prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
A person must not perform an aviation administration function if the person does not hold an ASAO certificate authorising the person to perform the function.
Note: This regulation does not apply to certain sport aviation bodies for a limited period: see regulation 202.861.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the person is otherwise permitted, under these Regulations, to perform the function.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subregulation: see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Compliance with conditions of ASAO certificate

content.p: An ASAO must not contravene a condition of its ASAO certificate.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 149.B—ASAO certificates

section.heading: CASA may limit number of ASAO certificates

content.p: For the purposes of subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a legislative instrument imposing limits on the number of ASAO certificates that may be issued if CASA is satisfied that exceeding the limit is likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
A limit may be imposed:
indefinitely or for a specified period; or
generally or in relation to a specified class of aviation administration functions.
CASA may, by legislative instrument, vary or revoke an instrument made under subregulation (1).
A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for the issue of an ASAO certificate to the person.
However, a body corporate may make an application only if it is incorporated in Australia.
An application for an ASAO certificate must include the following:
the applicant’s name and contact details;

(b) any operating or business name of the organisation (the applicant’s organisation) established, or proposed to be established, by the applicant to perform the aviation administration functions covered by the application on behalf of the ASAO, including its ABN (if any);
the principal physical address at which the person proposed to be appointed as the accountable manager of the applicant’s organisation will perform their duties and responsibilities;
if the applicant is a corporation—the name of each of the officers of the corporation, its ACN and the address of its registered office;
details of the aviation administration functions covered by the application, including:
the kinds of aircraft (if any) that the applicant proposes to administer; and
the activities that the applicant proposes to administer; and
any ASAO enforcement powers that the ASAO proposes to exercise;

a written undertaking from the person proposed to be appointed as the accountable manager of the applicant’s organisation that, if CASA issues the certificate, the applicant and the applicant’s organisation will:
be capable of operating in accordance with the applicant’s exposition and the civil aviation legislation; and
operate in accordance with the applicant’s exposition and the civil aviation legislation.
The application must be:
accompanied by a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition; and
signed by the person proposed to be appointed as the accountable manager of the applicant’s organisation.
Subject to regulations 11.055 and 149.060, CASA must issue an ASAO certificate to an applicant if CASA is satisfied:
that the applicant’s proposed exposition complies with regulation 149.340; and

(b) about the following matters in relation to the organisation (the applicant’s organisation) established, or proposed to be established, by the applicant to perform, on behalf of the applicant, the aviation administration functions covered by the application:
the applicant’s organisation can perform the functions safely and in accordance with the applicant’s exposition and the civil aviation legislation;
the applicant’s organisation has the facilities and equipment required by regulation 149.280;
the applicant’s organisation has the reference materials required by regulation 149.285; and
that the applicant has nominated an individual for each of the key personnel positions of the applicant’s organisation; and

that the individuals nominated to hold the positions of accountable manager and safety manager of the applicant’s organisation have the qualifications and experience required by the applicant’s proposed exposition; and
that each individual nominated to hold any other key personnel position of the applicant’s organisation is appropriately qualified to hold the position.
If CASA decides to issue the ASAO certificate, CASA must:
determine the aviation administration functions that the applicant is authorised to perform, including:
the kinds of aircraft (if any) that the applicant is authorised to administer; and
the activities that the applicant is authorised to administer; and
the ASAO enforcement powers (if any) that the ASAO may exercise; and
determine the period (not exceeding 5 years) for which the certificate is in force.
If CASA issues an ASAO certificate to the applicant, CASA is taken to have also approved the applicant’s proposed exposition.
Each of the following is a condition of an ASAO certificate issued to an ASAO:
the ASAO must comply with the ASAO’s exposition and the civil aviation legislation;
the ASAO must comply with any direction given to the ASAO, or obligation imposed on the ASAO, by CASA under these Regulations;
each of the key personnel of the ASAO must comply with:
each provision of this Part that applies to the person; and
each direction given to the person, or obligation imposed on the person, by CASA under a provision of these Regulations; and
each other provision of the civil aviation legislation that applies to the ASAO’s approved functions;
each vacancy in the key personnel of the ASAO must be:
notified to CASA within the period specified in the ASAO’s exposition; and
filled within the period specified in the ASAO’s exposition;
each of the personnel of the ASAO must comply with each provision of the civil aviation legislation that applies to the ASAO’s approved functions;
the position of safety manager and any other key personnel position in the ASAO’s organisation may be occupied by the same person simultaneously only:
in an unforeseen circumstance, and for the period specified in the ASAO’s exposition; or
in the circumstances, and for the period, for which the ASAO holds an approval under regulation 149.005.
An ASAO certificate must include the following:
the name of the ASAO;
the date of issue of the certificate;
the aviation administration functions of the ASAO determined under paragraph 149.075(2)(a);
the period determined under paragraph 149.075(2)(b) for which the certificate is in force;
a certificate reference number determined by CASA.
Subpart 149.C—Changes to exposition or personnel

section.heading: Certain changes to exposition must be pre-approved by CASA

content.p: A change to an ASAO’s exposition must be approved by CASA under regulation 149.115 before the change is made.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the change is of a kind specified in the ASAO’s exposition in accordance with paragraph 149.340(h).
Note: Such a change may need to be notified to CASA within a specified period after the change is made: see paragraph 149.340(i).
Application for approval
An ASAO may apply to CASA for the approval of a change to the ASAO’s exposition.
The application must:
be in the approved form; and
be accompanied by a copy of the part of the ASAO’s exposition affected by the change, clearly identifying the change; and
comply with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards.
Decision on application
CASA must, by written notice given to the applicant, do one of the following within 21 days after receiving the application:
if subregulation (4) applies—grant the approval;
refuse to grant the approval.
For the purposes of paragraph (3)(a), this subregulation applies if CASA is satisfied that:
the requirements mentioned in subregulation 149.075(1) will continue to be met in relation to the ASAO; and
approving the change would not be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Request for further information
CASA may, by written notice, request further information from the applicant about the application.
If a notice is given under subregulation (5):
the 21-day period stops on the day the notice is given; and
that period begins again on the day after the information is received by CASA.
More than one notice may be given under subregulation (5) in relation to an application.

section.heading: CASA directions relating to exposition or personnel

content.p: If CASA is satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to an ASAO, direct the ASAO to change the ASAO’s exposition:
to remove particular information, procedures or instructions from the exposition; or
to include particular information, procedures or instructions in the exposition; or
to revise or vary the information, procedures or instructions in the exposition.
CASA may, by written notice given to an ASAO, direct the ASAO to remove any of the key personnel of the ASAO from the person’s position if CASA is satisfied that the person is not:
carrying out the responsibilities of the position; or
if the person is the accountable manager of the ASAO’s organisation—properly managing matters for which the person is accountable.
A notice under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.
If CASA gives an ASAO a direction under this regulation, the ASAO must comply with the direction within the time specified in the notice.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 149.D—Organisation and personnel
An ASAO’s organisation must maintain a structure that effectively manages the ASAO’s approved functions, taking into account the nature and complexity of the functions.

An ASAO’s organisation must have enough suitably competent, qualified and trained personnel to enable the ASAO to perform the ASAO’s approved functions in accordance with the ASAO’s exposition and the civil aviation legislation.
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if any of the ASAO’s key personnel carries out a responsibility of the person’s position in a way that contravenes the ASAO’s exposition or this Subpart.
An ASAO commits an offence if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Notifying CASA if key personnel cannot carry out responsibilities

content.p: If an ASAO becomes aware that any of the ASAO’s key personnel cannot carry out, or is likely to be unable to carry out, the person’s responsibilities for a period of longer than 35 days, the ASAO must tell CASA of that fact within:
if there is not another person authorised to carry out the responsibilities for all or part of the period—5 days after the ASAO becomes aware of that fact; or
if there is another person authorised to carry out the responsibilities for all or part of the period—10 days after the ASAO becomes aware of that fact.
An ASAO commits an offence if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

An ASAO must ensure that, before a person appointed as any of the ASAO’s key personnel begins to carry out the responsibilities of the position, the person has completed any training that is necessary to familiarise the person with the responsibilities.
The accountable manager of an ASAO:
must have the experience and qualifications required by the ASAO’s exposition; and
is responsible for managing, and is accountable for, the matters set out in the ASAO’s exposition.
The safety manager of an ASAO:
must have the experience and qualifications required by the ASAO’s exposition; and
is responsible for the matters set out in the ASAO’s exposition.
The key personnel of an ASAO, other than the accountable manager and the safety manager of the ASAO:
are responsible for the matters set out in the ASAO’s exposition; and
must have experience and qualifications that are commensurate with the risk associated with the ASAO’s approved functions.

section.heading: Reporting interference with decisions of key personnel

content.p: If the accountable manager of an ASAO becomes aware that a person has overridden an aviation safety-related decision of a member of the key personnel of the ASAO, the accountable manager must report the matter to CASA, in writing, as soon as practicable, and in any case not later than 7 days, after becoming aware of the matter.
Note: CASA may direct an ASAO to remove the accountable manager of the ASAO if he or she does not comply with this subregulation: see subregulation 149.120(2).

If the safety manager of an ASAO becomes aware that a person has overridden an aviation safety-related decision of a member of the key personnel of the ASAO, the safety manager must report the matter to CASA, in writing, as soon as practicable, and in any case not later than 7 days, after becoming aware of the matter.
Note: CASA may direct an ASAO to remove the safety manager of the ASAO if he or she does not comply with this subregulation: see subregulation 149.120(2).

section.heading: Register of key personnel and appointed persons

content.p: An ASAO must maintain a register containing the following information for each of the ASAO’s key personnel:
the title of the position;
the name of the person occupying the position;
the date the person began occupying the position;
if applicable—the date the person ceased to occupy the position.
An ASAO must maintain a register containing the following information for each person appointed by the ASAO to perform an approved function on behalf of the ASAO:
the name of the person;
each approved function of the ASAO that the person performs on behalf of the ASAO;
the date the person began performing each function;
if applicable—the date the person ceased performing each function.
Subpart 149.E—Systems, facilities, reference materials and rules
An ASAO must have a safety management system that:
is appropriate for the ASAO’s approved functions, taking into account the nature and complexity of the functions, and the size of the ASAO; and
complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards.
An ASAO must have an audit and surveillance system that complies with the requirements prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards.

An ASAO’s organisation must have the facilities and equipment that are necessary for performing the ASAO’s approved functions, including appropriate equipment to allow the ASAO’s personnel to perform their duties.
An ASAO must provide access to up-to-date copies of the following reference materials that are relevant to the performance of the ASAO’s approved functions:
the civil aviation legislation;
technical standards and practices;
technical bulletins and instructions;
manuals for equipment used by the ASAO’s personnel;
any other materials prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards.
An ASAO must ensure that the ASAO’s personnel have ready access to the reference materials.
(1) An ASAO must prepare rules (the aviation administration and enforcement rules) that provide for the following:
the process for applying for an authorisation from the ASAO to undertake an activity administered by the ASAO, including the information that must be included in the application;
the eligibility criteria for the issuing of an authorisation by the ASAO to undertake an activity administered by the ASAO;
conditions that may be attached to an authorisation issued by the ASAO;
procedures relating to the variation, suspension and cancellation of authorisations at the authorisation holder’s request;
procedures relating to the internal review of decisions made by the ASAO;
if the ASAO is authorised to exercise ASAO enforcement powers:
the circumstances in which those powers may be exercised; and
procedures relating to the exercise of those powers;
procedures that require safe conduct by authorisation holders at all times;
measures for providing an authorisation holder with preventative, corrective or remedial solutions to identified training or skills deficiencies;
any disciplinary action that may be undertaken by the ASAO in relation to authorisation holders;
an effective and appropriate review process in relation to any preventative, corrective, remedial or disciplinary action undertaken by the ASAO;
any other matter prescribed by the Part 149 Manual of Standards.
The aviation administration and enforcement rules of an ASAO must have due regard to procedural fairness.
Subpart 149.F—Expositions
An exposition for an ASAO must include the following:
for each of the ASAO’s key personnel, the following information:
the qualifications and experience (if any) required by the ASAO for the position in addition to the qualifications and experience required under the Part 149 Manual of Standards for the position;
each matter (if any) for which the holder of the position is responsible in addition to the responsibilities mentioned in the Part 149 Manual of Standards for the position;
the name of the person appointed to the position;
the name of each person authorised to carry out the responsibilities of the position when the position holder is absent from the position or cannot carry out the responsibilities;
a description of how the ASAO will manage the responsibilities of the position during a circumstance mentioned in subparagraph (iv);
for each position occupied by a person appointed by the ASAO to perform an approved function on behalf of the ASAO, the following information:
the duties and responsibilities of the position;
how a person will be selected, trained and authorised to perform the duties and responsibilities of the position;
the qualifications, knowledge and experience required for the position;
a description of the approved functions of the ASAO;
a description of the procedures by which the ASAO ensures that the performance of the ASAO’s approved functions comply with:
the ASAO’s exposition; and
the civil aviation legislation;
a description of the ASAO’s safety management system required by regulation 149.270;
a description of the ASAO’s audit and surveillance system required by regulation 149.275;
the ASAO’s aviation administration and enforcement rules;
the kinds of changes to the ASAO’s exposition that do not require approval by CASA;
the ASAO’s process for managing changes to the ASAO’s exposition that do not require approval by CASA, including:
procedures for notifying the ASAO’s personnel and CASA of such changes; and
the period within which such changes are to be so notified;
a description of the procedures by which the ASAO will ensure compliance with regulation 149.550, should any of the circumstances specified in that regulation arise;
any other matter required to be included in the exposition by the Part 149 Manual of Standards or these Regulations.
An ASAO must not contravene a provision of the ASAO’s exposition.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
the ASAO does not keep its exposition in a readily accessible form; or
a member of the ASAO’s personnel does not have ready access to the exposition; or
the holder of an authorisation issued by the ASAO does not have ready access to the exposition; or
CASA does not have ready access to the exposition; or
the ASAO does not keep the exposition up-to-date.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 149.G—Authorisations

section.heading: Grounds for refusal of application for authorisation

content.p: An ASAO must not reject an application by a person for an authorisation to undertake an activity administered by the ASAO on grounds other than the eligibility criteria set out in the ASAO’s aviation administration and enforcement rules.
Note: For review by CASA of decisions by ASAOs, see Subpart 149.K.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if the ASAO reasonably believes that acceptance of the application would constitute an offence against the civil aviation legislation.

section.heading: Disclosure of information in application for authorisation

content.p: A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person applies to an ASAO for an authorisation to undertake an activity; and
the person does not disclose, in the application, details of each cancellation, variation or suspension (other than at the person’s request) of authorisations:
held by the person that are the same in substance as the authorisation applied for; and
issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country;
in the period starting 10 years before the making of the application.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Authorisation holders must comply with ASAO’s exposition

content.p: The holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
a provision of the ASAO’s exposition applies to the holder; and
the holder contravenes the provision.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Notice of suspension, variation or cancellation of authorisation

content.p: CASA-issued authorisation—cancellation etc. by CASA
Subregulation (2) applies if:
(a) a person holds an authorisation (the first authorisation) issued by CASA; and
CASA suspends, varies or cancels the first authorisation other than at the person’s request; and
(c) a person holds an authorisation (the second authorisation) issued by an ASAO.
The person must, within 7 days after the suspension, variation or cancellation takes effect, give written notice of the suspension, variation or cancellation to the ASAO.
ASAO-issued authorisation—cancellation etc. by ASAO or CASA
Subregulation (4) applies if:
(a) a person holds an authorisation (the first authorisation) issued by an ASAO to undertake an activity; and
CASA or the ASAO suspends, varies or cancels the first authorisation other than at the person’s request; and
the person holds an authorisation issued by another sport aviation body.
The person must, within 7 days after the suspension, variation or cancellation takes effect, give written notice of the suspension, variation or cancellation to the other sport aviation body.
ASAO-issued authorisation—cancellation etc. by national aviation authority of a foreign country
Subregulation (6) applies if:
(a) a person holds an authorisation (the first authorisation) issued by an ASAO; and
(b) the person holds an authorisation (the other authorisation) issued by a national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the other authorisation is suspended, varied or cancelled other than at the person’s request.
The person must, within 7 days after the suspension, variation or cancellation takes effect, give written notice of the suspension, variation or cancellation to the ASAO and CASA.
Offence
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (2), (4) or (6).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Reporting conduct of authorisation holders etc.

content.p: An ASAO must give a report to CASA, in writing, if the ASAO reasonably believes that:
both of the following apply:
the holder of an authorisation issued by the ASAO has contravened the ASAO’s exposition;
despite remedial or disciplinary action taken by the ASAO, the conduct of the holder of the authorisation jeopardises the safety of civil aviation; or
both of the following apply:
a person is undertaking an activity for which the person is required, under these Regulations, to hold an authorisation issued by an ASAO;
the person does not hold an authorisation issued by the ASAO to undertake the activity; or
a person is undertaking an activity for which the person holds an authorisation issued by an ASAO in a way that contravenes the authorisation; or
an aircraft that has ceased to be registered under Part 47 or administered by the ASAO is being flown.
An ASAO must give the report to CASA within the time specified in the ASAO’s exposition.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Reporting applications for authorisations in certain circumstances

content.p: Reporting of all variations and cancellations
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation to undertake an activity; and
(b) the ASAO knows that the person holds, or has held, an authorisation (the other authorisation):
that is the same in substance as the authorisation applied for; and
that was issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the ASAO knows that the other authorisation was varied or cancelled other than at the person’s request; and
the ASAO does not report details of the application to CASA, in writing, within 7 days after the person makes the application.
Reporting of current suspensions
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation to undertake an activity; and
(b) the ASAO knows that the person holds an authorisation (the other authorisation):
that is the same in substance as the authorisation applied for; and
that was issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the ASAO knows that, at the time of the application, the other authorisation is suspended other than at the person’s request; and
the ASAO does not report details of the application to CASA, in writing, within 7 days after the person makes the application.
An ASAO commits an offence if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1) or (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: ASAO to refuse to issue authorisation if suspended etc.

content.p: Other authorisation currently suspended
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
(a) a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation (the new authorisation) to undertake an activity; and
(b) the ASAO knows that the person holds an authorisation (the other authorisation):
that is the same in substance as the new authorisation; and
that was issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the ASAO knows that, at the time of the application, the other authorisation is suspended other than at the person’s request; and
the ASAO issues the new authorisation to the person.
Other authorisation is or has been varied
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
(a) a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation (the new authorisation) to undertake an activity; and
(b) the ASAO knows that the person holds, or has held, an authorisation (the other authorisation):
that is the same in substance as the new authorisation; and
that was issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the ASAO knows that the other authorisation was varied other than at the person’s request; and
the ASAO issues the new authorisation to the person.
Other authorisation has been cancelled
An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
(a) a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation (the new authorisation) to undertake an activity; and
(b) the ASAO knows that the person has held an authorisation (the other authorisation):
that is the same in substance as the new authorisation; and
that was issued by the ASAO, another sport aviation body, CASA or the national aviation authority of a foreign country; and
the ASAO knows that the other authorisation was cancelled other than at the person’s request; and
the ASAO issues the new authorisation to the person.
Exception—CASA approval
Subregulation (1), (2) or (3) does not apply if, before the new authorisation is issued, CASA has given approval under this subregulation to the ASAO to issue the new authorisation to the person.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subregulation: see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Offence
An ASAO commits an offence if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Strict liability applies to paragraphs (1)(a) and (d), (2)(a) and (d) and (3)(a) and (d).

section.heading: ASAO to refuse to issue authorisation if exclusion period is in force

content.p: An ASAO contravenes this subregulation if:
a person applies to the ASAO for an authorisation authorising the person to undertake an activity; and

the ASAO knows that an exclusion period is in force under an order under section 30A of the Act in relation to the person and an authorisation that is the same in substance as the authorisation applied for; and
the ASAO issues the authorisation.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if, before the authorisation is issued, CASA has given approval under this subregulation to the ASAO to issue the authorisation to the person.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in this subregulation: see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
An ASAO commits an offence if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subpart 149.H—Authorisations and enforcement

section.heading: Direction to ASAO to exercise ASAO enforcement powers

content.p: CASA may, if satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of the safety of air navigation, direct an ASAO to exercise an ASAO enforcement power in relation to the holder of an authorisation issued by the ASAO.
The ASAO must comply with the direction within 20 days.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Variation, suspension and cancellation of authorisations issued by ASAOs

content.p: CASA may exercise the powers in subregulation (2):
if an ASAO does not comply with a direction under regulation 149.490 within 20 days; or
on written request of an ASAO; or
on CASA’s own initiative;
if CASA is satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of the safety of air navigation to do so.
CASA may, by written notice given to the holder of an authorisation issued by an ASAO, vary, suspend or cancel the authorisation.
Before making a decision under subregulation (2), CASA must:
give the holder of the authorisation a notice setting out the reasons why CASA is considering making the decision; and
allow the holder of the authorisation to show cause, within such reasonable time as CASA specifies in the notice, why CASA should not make the decision.
A variation or suspension has effect for the period specified in the notice, unless earlier revoked by CASA.
A cancellation takes effect on the day specified in the notice.
If CASA varies, suspends or cancels an authorisation issued by an ASAO, CASA must notify the ASAO in writing of the variation, suspension or cancellation as soon as practicable.
The suspension of an authorisation issued by an ASAO under this regulation does not prevent the revocation of the authorisation by the ASAO or by CASA.

section.heading: Effect of suspension or cancellation by CASA of authorisations issued by ASAOs

content.p: If CASA suspends an authorisation issued by an ASAO under regulation 149.495, the authorisation is taken not to be in force during the period of suspension.
If:
CASA suspends an authorisation issued by an ASAO under regulation 149.495; and
under the civil aviation legislation, a person is required to hold the authorisation to undertake an activity;
the person to whom the authorisation was issued is taken not to be the holder of the authorisation for the period of the suspension.

If an authorisation is cancelled by CASA under regulation 149.495, the person to whom the authorisation was issued is not eligible to apply for the grant of, and must not be granted, another authorisation that is the same in substance as the cancelled authorisation until 3 years after the day the cancellation takes effect.
Subpart 149.J—Information and documents

section.heading: Providing information or documents to CASA

content.p: CASA may, by notice given to an ASAO, require the ASAO to:
give to CASA information of the kind specified in the notice; or
produce to CASA documents of the kind specified in the notice.
The information or documents must relate to the ASAO’s approved functions.
The notice must:
be in writing; and
specify the manner and form in which the information or documents must be given.
If an ASAO is given a notice under this regulation, the ASAO must comply with the notice within the period specified in the notice (which must end at least 7 days after the notice is given).
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if the ASAO contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An ASAO must provide to CASA copies of all documents used by the ASAO in the performance of its approved functions if any of the following events occur:
the ASAO becomes incapable of complying with the ASAO’s obligations under the civil aviation legislation;
if the ASAO is an individual—the ASAO becomes insolvent under administration;
(c) if the ASAO is a body corporate—the ASAO becomes a Chapter 5 body corporate (within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001);
CASA cancels the ASAO certificate issued to the ASAO.
The copies of documents required by subregulation (1) must be provided to CASA within 30 days after the event occurs.
Subpart 149.K—Review of ASAO decisions

section.heading: Application for internal review by ASAO

content.p: This regulation applies if a person is dissatisfied with one of the following decisions:
a decision of an ASAO to refuse to issue an authorisation to the person;
a decision of an ASAO to issue an authorisation to the person in terms different from those applied for;
a decision of an ASAO to vary, suspend or cancel an authorisation issued to the person other than at the person’s request;
a decision to attach conditions to an authorisation issued to the person, other than at the person’s request;
a decision to vary conditions attached to an authorisation issued to the person, other than at the person’s request.
The person may apply to the ASAO for internal review of the decision, in accordance with the procedures specified in the ASAO’s aviation administration and enforcement rules.
The ASAO may:
affirm, vary or set aside the decision; and
if the ASAO sets aside the decision—make such other decision as the ASAO considers appropriate.
If the ASAO has not made a decision on the application within 21 days after receiving the application, the ASAO is taken to have affirmed the decision on that day.
(5) A decision made under subregulation (3), or taken to have been made because of the operation of subregulation (4), by an ASAO is an internal review decision.

If a person who made an application under subregulation 149.605(2) is dissatisfied with the internal review decision of the ASAO, the person may apply to CASA for a review of the internal review decision.
The application must be made:
in the approved form; and
within 21 days after the internal review decision, or such longer period as CASA allows.
An application under this regulation is not taken to have been made unless:
it is made in the manner approved by CASA for that purpose; and
it is made in the approved form; and
it includes all of the information required by the form; and
the applicant has notified the ASAO of the application in accordance with regulation 149.615; and
if a fee is payable for the application—that fee has been paid.
The making of an application to CASA for review of an internal review decision of an ASAO does not affect the operation of the decision or prevent the taking of action to implement the decision.
If a person makes an application under regulation 149.610 for review of an internal review decision made by an ASAO, the person must notify the ASAO, in writing, of that fact.

section.heading: ASAO to provide information and documents to CASA

content.p: If an ASAO receives a notice under regulation 149.615, the ASAO must, within 28 days after receiving the notice, give the following to CASA:

a statement setting out the findings on material questions of fact, referring to the evidence or other material on which those findings were based and giving the reasons for the internal review decision of the ASAO;
copies of every document that is in the ASAO’s possession or under the ASAO’s control and is relevant to the review by CASA of the internal review decision.
An ASAO commits an offence of strict liability if:
the ASAO is subject to a requirement under subregulation (1); and
the ASAO fails to comply with the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: CASA may request further information etc. from applicant for review

content.p: If CASA reasonably believes that it is necessary to do so for the purposes of conducting the review, CASA may request that the applicant for review of an internal review decision of an ASAO do one or more of the following:
provide further information or documents to CASA:
submit to an examination or test conducted by CASA;
attend an interview with CASA.
CASA may refuse to make a decision on the application for review until a request under subregulation (1) is complied with.
In conducting a review of an internal review decision of an ASAO:
the procedures for conducting the review are within the discretion of CASA; and
CASA is not bound by the rules of evidence; and
CASA may inform itself in any way it thinks fit; and
the review is to be conducted with as little technicality and formality, and as quickly and economically, as a proper consideration of the matters permit.
On review of an internal review decision of an ASAO, CASA must make a decision:
affirming the internal review decision; or
varying the internal review decision; or
setting the internal review decision aside and substituting a new decision; or
setting the internal review decision aside and remitting the matter to the ASAO for reconsideration in accordance with any directions or recommendations of CASA.
A decision under subregulation (2) comes into effect on the day specified by CASA.
CASA must, as soon as practicable after making a decision under subregulation (2), give written notice to the applicant and the ASAO of:
the decision; and
the reasons for the decision.
