Note: The following terms are defined in the Dictionary:
A certified designer is a person who is the holder of a procedure design certificate that is in force.

section.heading: What is a procedure design certificate

content.p: A procedure design certificate is a certificate that:
is granted by CASA to a person under this Part; and
certifies that the person is authorised to carry on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure of a type covered by the certificate subject to any conditions set out in the certificate.
An authorised designer is a person who is the holder of a procedure design authorisation that is in force.

section.heading: What is a procedure design authorisation

content.p: A procedure design authorisation is an authorisation that:
is granted by CASA to a person under this Part; and
authorises the person to carry on either of the following activities:

review or amend a terminal instrument flight procedure that is of a type covered by the authorisation and is for use by Australian aircraft operating under the IFR at, or in the vicinity of, an aerodrome in a foreign country;

carry on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure that is of a type covered by the authorisation and is for use by Australian aircraft operating under the IFR at, or in the vicinity of, an off-shore installation located no closer than the distance specified in the Manual of Standards from the nearest land.

section.heading: Design, review or amendment of terminal instrument flight procedures—requirement for procedure design certificate etc

content.p: A person commits an offence if:

the person carries on design work (other than work mentioned in subregulation (2) or (3)) on a terminal instrument flight procedure for use by Australian aircraft operating under the IFR, or by foreign aircraft operating under the IFR in Australian territory; and
the person is not permitted to do so under subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the following persons may carry on the work:
CASA;
a certified designer whose procedure design certificate authorises the designer to carry on design work on the procedure;
an employee of a certified designer mentioned in paragraph (b) who carries on the design work in the course of the employee’s duties.
A person commits an offence if:
the person reviews or amends a terminal instrument flight procedure for use by Australian aircraft operating under the IFR at, or in the vicinity of, an aerodrome in a foreign country; and
the person is not permitted to do so under subregulation (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (3)(b), the following persons may review or amend the procedure:
CASA;
a certified designer whose procedure design certificate authorises the designer to carry on design work on the procedure;
an employee of a certified designer mentioned in paragraph (b) who reviews or amends the procedure in the course of the employee’s duties;
an authorised designer whose procedure design authorisation authorises the designer to review or amend the procedure;
an employee of an authorised designer mentioned in paragraph (d) who reviews or amends the procedure in the course of the employee’s duties.
A person commits an offence if:
the person carries on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure for use by Australian aircraft operating under the IFR at, or in the vicinity of, an off-shore installation; and
the person is not permitted to do so under subregulation (6).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (5)(b), the following persons may carry on the work:
CASA;
a certified designer whose procedure design certificate authorises the designer to carry on design work on the procedure;
an employee of a certified designer mentioned in paragraph (b) who carries on the design work in the course of the employee’s duties;
an authorised designer whose procedure design authorisation authorises the designer to carry on design work on the procedure;
an employee of an authorised designer mentioned in paragraph (d) who carries on the design work in the course of the employee’s duties.
An offence against subregulation (1), (3) or (5) is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Designing instrument flight procedures other than terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: A person who designs an instrument flight procedure that is not a terminal instrument flight procedure must, in designing the procedure, meet any standards for the design of such a procedure set out in the Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
An offence against subregulation (1) is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 173.B—Certified designers
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for certification as a certified designer.
A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for a procedure design certificate.
Note: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
The application:
must state:
the applicant’s name and address; or

if the applicant is incorporated by or under a law of the Commonwealth or of a State or Territory, the applicant’s name, registered address and ACN and the names and addresses of the people responsible for its management and control; and
must contain or be accompanied by:
a written statement specifying the type or each type of terminal instrument flight procedure proposed to be covered by the procedure design certificate; and
a written statement setting out the name, qualifications and relevant experience of the individual who is proposed to be the chief designer for the applicant’s organisation; and

a written statement setting out the qualifications and relevant experience of any other member of the applicant’s personnel whose duties would, if the certificate were granted to the applicant, include carrying on design work under the certificate; and
must be accompanied by a copy of the operations manual under which the applicant proposes to design, or engage in design work on, terminal instrument flight procedures of the type or types concerned.
Note: Part 11 also contains provisions relating to an application for a procedure design certificate.

section.heading: Criteria for grant of procedure design certificates

content.p: For regulation 173.335, a person who has applied for the grant of a procedure design certificate must, if the certificate is granted, be able to comply with the requirements of Division 173.B.2.
If CASA grants a procedure design certificate to a person under Subpart 173.E, CASA must state on the certificate:
the person’s name and principal place of business; and
the type or each type of terminal instrument flight procedure covered by the certificate; and
any conditions applicable to it; and
the date when it comes into force; and
any other information that CASA thinks should be included.

section.heading: How long procedure design certificates remain in force

content.p: A procedure design certificate remains in force unless it is cancelled.

section.heading: Applications to vary procedure design certificates

content.p: An application to vary a procedure design certificate must contain, or have with it, a copy of the proposed variation.

division.heading: Requirements to be complied with by certified designers

section.heading: Certified designer to maintain operations manual

content.p: A certified designer must, at all times, maintain an operations manual that meets the standards for operations manuals set out in the Manual of Standards.
A certified designer:
must keep the manual in a readily accessible form; and
must ensure that each employee of the designer whose duties include carrying on design work under the designer’s procedure design certificate has ready access to the manual; and
must amend the manual whenever it is necessary to do so to keep it in an up-to-date form.
A certified designer must ensure:
that all amendments of the manual are incorporated in all copies of the manual kept by the certified designer; and
that copies of the amendments are given to CASA.
A certified designer must, in carrying on design work authorised under the designer’s procedure design certificate, comply with the designer’s operations manual.

section.heading: Standards for design of terminal instrument flight procedures etc

content.p: A certified designer designing a terminal instrument flight procedure under the certified designer’s procedure design certificate must ensure that the procedure is designed in accordance with:
any applicable standards set out or referred to in ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS); and
any applicable standards set out in the Manual of Standards.

If, apart from this subregulation, a certified designer would be required to ensure that a terminal instrument flight procedure is designed in accordance with a standard set out or referred to in the ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS) and a standard set out in the Manual of Standards, and it is not possible to comply with both standards, the designer is only required to ensure that the procedure is designed in accordance with the Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Verification of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: A certified designer must establish procedures for verifying terminal instrument procedures that it is authorised to design under the designer’s procedure design certificate or on which the designer is authorised to carry on design work.
The verification procedures:

must provide for 2 qualified designers to check independently the design of each terminal instrument flight procedure designed, or on which design work is carried on, under the certified designer’s procedure design certificate; and
must provide for one of those checks to be made by a qualified designer who did not carry on the design work concerned.

In this regulation, a reference to verifying a terminal instrument flight procedure is a reference to the process of checking the procedure (including all data, computations and drawings for the procedure) in accordance with any applicable standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
In this regulation:
qualified designer, in relation to a terminal instrument flight procedure, means an individual who:

is the holder, or an employee of the holder, of a procedure design certificate that authorises the holder to design terminal instrument flight procedures of the same type as the terminal instrument flight procedure concerned; and
has successfully completed:
an approved course of training in the methods and practices contained in ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS); and

any training for persons carrying on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures that is specified in the operations manual under which the qualified designer performs the designer’s duties; and
meets the experience requirements for performing the functions of a qualified designer set out in the Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Validation of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: A certified designer must ensure that each terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design certificate is validated by a CASA pilot in accordance with any applicable standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
In this regulation:
CASA pilot means a pilot:
who is an officer of CASA; and
who meets the standards set out in the Manual of Standards for carrying out a validation flight check of a terminal instrument flight procedure.
validation flight check has the same meaning as in the Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Publication of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: A certified designer must ensure that each terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design certificate is given to the AIS for publication in the AIP together with a certificate by the certified designer’s chief designer to the effect that the procedure is designed and validated in accordance with any applicable standards set out or referred to in ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS) and the Manual of Standards.
However, the designer need not give a terminal instrument flight procedure to the AIS if the procedure is for use only by an aircraft in a specialised helicopter operation.
A certified designer must ensure that all procedures designed under its procedure design certificate that are not given to the AIS for publication in the AIP are given to CASA.

A certified designer must ensure that a terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design certificate does not require the use of a ground-based radio-navigation aid other than one that is operated and maintained by a person certificated to do so under Part 171.

section.heading: Maintenance of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: Subject to subregulation (2), a certified designer is responsible for maintaining, in accordance with the standards for the maintenance of terminal instrument flight procedures set out in the Manual of Standards, a terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design certificate or for which that responsibility is transferred to the certified designer under regulation 173.215.
The certified designer ceases to be responsible for the maintenance of the procedure:
if the certified designer has notified CASA and, if the procedure is published in the AIP, the AIS, under regulation 173.210, that the designer has ceased to have that responsibility:
on the day when the notice is given; or
if a later day is specified in the notice—on the later day; or

if the certified designer’s responsibility for the maintenance of the procedure is transferred to another certified designer in accordance with regulation 173.215—on the day when the responsibility is transferred; or

if the certified designer has notified CASA and, if the procedure is published in the AIP, the AIS, under regulation 173.200, that the designer has ceased to design the type of terminal instrument flight procedure concerned:
on the day when the notice is given; or
if a later day is specified in the notice—on the later day; or
if the certified designer’s procedure design certificate is varied under Subpart 173.E to exclude that type of procedure—on the day when the variation takes effect; or
if the certified designer ceases to be a certified designer—on the day when the designer ceases to be a certified designer.

section.heading: Certified designer to provide facilities etc

content.p: A certified designer must provide and maintain adequate facilities for carrying on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures under the designer’s procedure design certificate, including:
providing premises and equipment appropriate for the certified designer’s employees to carry on the design work; and
ensuring that those employees have access to all necessary data for designing the procedures including:
accurate and current databases or charts detailing terrain and obstacle information; and
accurate and current navigation aid coordinate data; and
accurate and current aerodrome reference point and threshold data.

A certified designer must, if an aeronautical database and aeronautical data is required for designing a terminal instrument flight procedure under the designer’s procedure design certificate, have, and put into effect, procedures to ensure the integrity of the database and the data.

section.heading: Certified designer to have appropriate organisation

content.p: A certified designer must, at all times, maintain an appropriate organisation with a sound and effective management structure to enable the designer to carry on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures under the designer’s procedure design certificate in accordance with these Regulations.

section.heading: Certified designer to have sufficient personnel

content.p: A certified designer:

must employ a sufficient number of personnel to enable the designer to carry on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures under the designer’s procedure design certificate in accordance with these Regulations; and
must ensure that those personnel:
are suitably qualified and competent to perform their duties; and
are trained in accordance with the Manual of Standards and the designer’s operations manual.

A certified designer must ensure that each employee who is occupying or acting in a supervisory position in the designer’s organisation in relation to design work on terminal instrument flight procedures carried on under the designer’s procedure design certificate meets the standards for supervisory positions set out in the Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Certified designer to appoint chief designer

content.p: A certified designer must not carry on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure under the designer’s procedure design certificate unless:
the certified designer has appointed a person to be the chief designer for the designer’s organisation; and
the appointment is approved by CASA and is in force; and
the functions of the chief designer are being carried out by the person or, if the chief designer is temporarily absent from duty, another person:
who is appointed by the certified designer to act as chief designer; and
whose appointment is approved by CASA and is in force.

section.heading: Certified designer to provide training and checking program

content.p: A certified designer must provide a training and checking program that is of an adequate standard to ensure that the employees of the designer maintain their competence and are provided with ongoing training appropriate to their duties.

section.heading: Certified designer to have safety management system

content.p: A certified designer must have, and put into effect, a safety management system that includes the policies, procedures, and practices necessary for managing design work on terminal instrument flight procedures carried on under the designer’s procedure design certificate.
The safety management system must be in accordance with the standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
The designer must keep its safety management system under review and take any necessary corrective action to ensure that it operates properly.

section.heading: Certified designer to maintain reference materials

content.p: A certified designer must maintain reference materials of the kinds specified in the Manual of Standards.
A certified designer must keep the reference materials up-to-date and in a readily accessible form.

Each employee of the certified designer who carries on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure under the certified designer’s procedure design certificate must have ready access to the reference materials.

section.heading: Certified designer to keep documents and records

content.p: A certified designer must keep documents and records of the kinds specified in the Manual of Standards.
A document or record must be retained for as long as the Manual of Standards specifies for the particular kind of document or record.
The designer must, at CASA’s request, make the documents and records, or copies of them or extracts from them, available for inspection by CASA.

section.heading: Certified designer to have document and record control system

content.p: A certified designer must establish, and put into effect, a system for controlling documents and records relating to the terminal instrument flight procedures on which the designer carries on design work under the certified designer’s procedure design certificate, including the policies and procedures for making, amending, preserving and disposing of those documents and records.
The system must be in accordance with the standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
The documents and records must include the documents and records required to be kept under this Division.

section.heading: Approval for appointment of chief designer

content.p: A certified designer must not appoint a person as chief designer unless the appointment is approved by CASA.
To be appointed as chief designer, a person must, at the time of appointment, meet the standards for the chief designer for a certified designer’s organisation set out in the Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Approval for appointment to act as chief designer

content.p: A certified designer must not appoint a person to act as chief designer for the certified designer unless the appointment is approved by CASA.

To be appointed to act as chief designer, a person must, at the time of appointment, have sufficient qualifications and experience to enable the individual to carry out the functions of the appointment properly, having regard to the nature and scope of the design work carried on by the chief designer.

section.heading: Appointment likely to have adverse effect on air safety

content.p: Without limiting the matters that CASA may take into account in deciding whether to approve an appointment of a person as chief designer or an appointment of a person to act as chief designer, CASA is not required to approve the appointment if the approval would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
In deciding whether approval of the appointment of a person would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation, CASA may take into account the following:
the person’s record of compliance with regulatory requirements (in Australia or elsewhere) relating to aviation safety and other transport safety;
the experience of the person in aviation;
the person’s knowledge of the regulatory requirements applicable to civil aviation in Australia;
any evidence held by CASA that the person has contravened:
the Act or these Regulations; or
a law of another country relating to aviation safety; or
another law (of Australia or of another country) relating to transport safety.

Note: Section 30A of the Act allows the Court to make an order excluding a person from a particular aviation activity. Such an order may have the effect of precluding the approval or acceptance of an appointment while the order is in force.
The chief designer for a certified designer’s organisation is responsible to the certified designer for the following:
ensuring that any design work on the terminal instrument flight procedures that is carried on under the designer’s procedure design certificate is carried on in accordance with these Regulations;
appointing persons as employees of the certified designer to carry on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures under the designer’s procedure design certificate;
effectively managing work done in relation to those terminal instrument flight procedures by those persons;
issuing certificates as required by regulation 173.100.
An approval under regulation 173.165 or 173.170 stops being in force if:
the appointment to which it relates ends; or
it is withdrawn.
An approval is not in force during any period in which it is suspended.

section.heading: Withdrawal or suspension of approval of appointment

content.p: CASA may, by notice in writing to a person appointed as the chief designer, or to act as the chief designer, for a certified designer’s organisation, withdraw or suspend approval of the person’s appointment if continuing approval of the appointment would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.

In deciding whether continuing approval of a person’s appointment would be likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation, CASA may take into account the matters mentioned in subregulation 173.175(2).
The notice:
must set out the reasons for the withdrawal or suspension; and
in the case of a suspension, must specify the period of suspension or state when, or in what circumstances, it will end.
CASA must give a copy of the notice to the certified designer.
If CASA suspends approval of a person’s appointment, the person must not carry out the functions of the appointment during the period of the suspension.
If CASA withdraws approval of a person’s appointment:
for the purposes of these Regulations, the appointment is taken to end; and
the person must not continue to carry out the functions of the position to which the appointment relates.

A certified designer must tell CASA, in writing, of a change of circumstances that materially affects its capacity to design a terminal instrument flight procedure under the designer’s procedure design certificate, or engage in any design work on that procedure, within 7 days after the change occurs.

section.heading: Discontinuing design work on terminal instrument flight procedures of a particular type

content.p: If a certified designer ceases to carry on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures of a particular type, the certified designer must give written notice to that effect to CASA, and, if any of the procedures are published in the AIP, the AIS, within 7 days after ceasing to carry on the design work concerned.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if, having regard to the certified designer’s circumstances, it is not reasonably practicable for the designer to give CASA or, if applicable, the AIS, at least 7 days notice and the notice is given as soon as is reasonably practicable.

section.heading: Notifying the AIS of a variation to a procedure design certificate

content.p: If a certified designer’s procedure design certificate is varied under Subpart 173.E to exclude a particular type of terminal instrument flight procedure and the designer has given any procedures of that type to the AIS for publication in the AIP, the designer must give written notice to the AIS of the variation within 7 days after the day when the variation takes effect.

section.heading: Discontinuing maintenance of particular terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: If a certified designer ceases to be responsible for the maintenance of a terminal instrument flight procedure, the certified designer must give written notice to that effect to CASA and, if the procedure is published in the AIP, to the AIS, within 7 days after ceasing to have that responsibility.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if, having regard to the certified designer’s circumstances, it is not reasonably practicable for the designer to give CASA at least 7 days notice and the notice is given as soon as is reasonably practicable.

A certified designer may transfer the designer’s responsibility for maintaining a terminal instrument flight procedure under regulation 173.110 to another certified designer whose procedure design certificate authorises that designer to design terminal instrument flight procedures of the same type as the procedure concerned.
If a certified designer accepts responsibility for the maintenance of a terminal instrument flight procedure under this regulation, the designer:
must give written notice to the transferor to that effect; and
must give written notice of the transfer to CASA and, if the procedure is published in the AIP, to the AIS, within 14 days after the transfer.

A transfer takes effect on the day when the certified designer accepting responsibility for maintaining the procedure gives notice to the transferor under paragraph (2)(a) or, if a later day is specified in the notice, on the later day.

If a certified designer transfers the designer’s responsibility for maintaining a terminal instrument flight procedure, the designer must give written notice of the transfer to CASA and, if the procedure is published in the AIP, to the AIS, within 14 days after the transfer.
Subpart 173.C—Authorised designers
Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to an application for the grant of a procedure design authorisation.
A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for a procedure design authorisation.
Note: An application must be in the approved form, include all the information required by these Regulations and be accompanied by every document required by these Regulations—see regulation 11.030.
The application:
must state:
the applicant’s name and address; or

if the applicant is incorporated by or under a law of the Commonwealth or of a State or Territory, the applicant’s name, registered address and ACN and the names and addresses of the people responsible for its management and control; and
must contain or be accompanied by:

a written statement specifying the activity mentioned in subparagraph 173.030(b)(i) or (ii) that is proposed to be authorised under the authorisation, including specifying the type or each type of terminal instrument flight procedure proposed to be covered by the authorisation; and

a written statement setting out the qualifications and relevant experience of each member of the applicant’s personnel whose duties would, if the authorisation were granted to the applicant, include carrying on the design work concerned; and
must be accompanied by a copy of the operations manual under which the applicant proposes to carry on that activity.
Note: Part 11 also contains provisions relating to an application for a procedure design authorisation.

section.heading: Criteria for grant of procedure design authorisations

content.p: For regulation 173.335, a person who has applied for the grant of a procedure design authorisation must, if the authorisation is granted, be able to comply with the requirements of Division 173.C.2.

section.heading: How long procedure design authorisations remain in force

content.p: A procedure design authorisation remains in force unless it is cancelled.

section.heading: Applications to vary procedure design authorisations

content.p: An application to vary a procedure design authorisation must contain, or have with it, a copy of the proposed variation.

division.heading: Requirements to be complied with by authorised designers

content.p: An authorised designer must, at all times, maintain an operations manual that meets the standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
An authorised designer:
must keep the manual in a readily accessible form; and
must ensure that each employee of the designer whose duties include carrying on design work authorised by the designer’s procedure design authorisation has ready access to the manual; and
must amend the manual whenever it is necessary to do so to keep it in an up-to-date form.
An authorised designer must ensure:
that all amendments of the manual are incorporated in all copies of the manual kept by the designer; and
that copies of the amendments are given to CASA.
An authorised designer must, in carrying on the activity authorised by the designer’s procedure design authorisation, comply with the designer’s operations manual.

section.heading: Standards for design of terminal instrument flight procedures etc

content.p: An authorised designer designing a terminal instrument flight procedure under the authorised designer’s procedure design authorisation must ensure that the procedure is designed in accordance with:
any applicable standards set out or referred to in ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS); and
any applicable standards set out in the Manual of Standards.

If, apart from this subregulation, an authorised designer would be required to ensure that a terminal instrument flight procedure is designed in accordance with a standard set out or referred to in the ICAO Doc. 8168 (PANS-OPS) and a standard set out in the Manual of Standards, and it is not possible to comply with both standards, the designer is only required to ensure that the procedure is designed in accordance with the Manual of Standards.
This regulation applies to an authorised designer who is authorised to carry on the activity mentioned in subparagraph 173.030(b)(ii).
The authorised designer must ensure that a copy of each terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design authorisation is given to CASA.

The authorised designer must ensure that a terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design authorisation does not require the use of a ground-based radio-navigation aid other than one that is operated and maintained by a person certificated to do so under Part 171.

section.heading: Maintenance of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: Subject to subregulation (2), an authorised designer is responsible for maintaining, in accordance with the standards for the maintenance of terminal instrument flight procedures set out in the Manual of Standards, a terminal instrument flight procedure designed under the designer’s procedure design authorisation or a terminal instrument flight procedure for which that responsibility is transferred to the authorised designer under regulation 173.305.
The authorised designer ceases to be responsible for the maintenance of the procedure:
if the authorised designer has notified CASA, under regulation 173.300, that the designer has ceased to have that responsibility:
on the day when the notice is given; or
if a later day is specified in the notice—on the later day; or

if the authorised designer’s responsibility for the maintenance of the procedure is transferred to a certified designer or another authorised designer under regulation 173.305—on the day when the responsibility is transferred; or
if the authorised designer has notified CASA, under regulation 173.295, that the designer has ceased to design the type of terminal instrument flight procedure concerned:
on the day when the notice is given; or
if a later day is specified in the notice—on the later day; or
if the authorised designer’s procedure design authorisation is varied under Subpart 173.E to exclude that type of procedure—on the day when the authorisation is varied; or
if the authorised designer ceases to be an authorised designer—on the day when the designer ceases to be an authorised designer.

section.heading: Authorised designer to have sufficient personnel

content.p: An authorised designer:
must employ a sufficient number of personnel to enable the designer to carry on the activity authorised by the designer’s procedure design authorisation in accordance with these Regulations; and
must ensure that those personnel:
are suitably qualified and competent to perform their duties; and
are trained in accordance with the Manual of Standards and the designer’s operations manual.

section.heading: Authorised designer to maintain reference materials

content.p: An authorised designer must maintain reference materials of the kinds specified in the Manual of Standards.
An authorised designer must keep the reference materials up-to-date and in a readily accessible form.

Each employee of the authorised designer whose duties include carrying on design work that is authorised under the designer’s procedure design authorisation must have ready access to the reference materials.

section.heading: Authorised designer to keep documents and records

content.p: An authorised designer must keep documents and records of the kinds specified in the Manual of Standards.
A document or record must be retained for as long as the Manual of Standards specifies for the particular kind of document or record.
The designer must, at CASA’s request, make the documents and records, or copies of them or extracts from them, available for inspection by CASA.

section.heading: Authorised designer to have document and record control system

content.p: An authorised designer must establish, and put into effect, a system for controlling documents and records relating to the activity authorised under the authorised designer’s procedure design authorisation, including the policies and procedures for making, amending, preserving and disposing of those documents and records.
The system must be in accordance with the standards set out in the Manual of Standards.
The documents and records must include the documents and records required to be kept under this Division.

section.heading: Discontinuing design work on terminal instrument flight of a particular type

content.p: If an authorised designer ceases to carry on design work on terminal instrument flight procedures of a particular type, the authorised designer must give written notice to CASA to that effect within 7 days after ceasing to carry on the design work concerned.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if, having regard to the authorised designer’s circumstances, it is not reasonably practicable for the designer to give CASA at least 7 days notice and the notice is given as soon as is reasonably practicable.

section.heading: Discontinuing maintenance of terminal instrument flight procedures

content.p: If an authorised designer ceases to be responsible for the maintenance of a terminal instrument flight procedure, the authorised designer must give written notice to CASA to that effect within 7 days after ceasing to have that responsibility.

Subregulation (1) does not apply if, having regard to the authorised designer’s circumstances, it is not reasonably practicable for the designer to give CASA at least 7 days notice and the notice is given as soon as is reasonably practicable.
An authorised designer may transfer the designer’s responsibility for maintaining a terminal instrument flight procedure under regulation 173.270:
to a certified designer whose procedure design certificate authorises that designer to design terminal instrument flight procedures of the same type as the procedure concerned; or
to another authorised designer whose procedure design authorisation authorises that designer to design such a terminal instrument flight procedure.
If a certified designer or an authorised designer accepts responsibility for the maintenance of a terminal instrument flight procedure under this regulation, the designer:
must give written notice to the transferor to that effect; and
must give written notice of the transfer to CASA within 14 days after the transfer.

A transfer takes effect on the day when the certified designer or authorised designer accepting responsibility for maintaining the procedure gives notice to the transferor under subregulation (2) or, if a later day is specified in the notice, on the later day.

If an authorised designer transfers the designer’s responsibility for maintaining a terminal instrument flight procedure, the designer must give written notice of the transfer to CASA within 14 days after the transfer.
Subpart 173.D—Performance of design work

section.heading: Certified designer not to exceed the limitations of the designer’s procedure design certificate

content.p: A certified designer must not carry on design work on a terminal instrument flight procedure that is not of a type covered by the designer’s procedure design certificate.

section.heading: Authorised designer not to exceed the limitations of authorisation

content.p: A authorised designer must not carry on an activity mentioned in paragraph 173.030(b)(i) or (ii) unless that activity is authorised by the designer’s procedure design authorisation.
Subpart 173.E—Administration

division.heading: Grant of procedure design certificates and procedure design authorisations

content.p: Note: In addition to the provisions of this Division, Part 11 contains provisions relating to the grant of a procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation.

section.heading: CASA may require demonstrations of equipment etc

content.p: Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to a procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation.

section.heading: Grant of procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, if an applicant has applied for the grant of a procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation under this Part, CASA must grant the certificate or authorisation.
Note: Under regulation 201.004, an application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of:
a decision refusing to issue or grant, or cancelling, suspending or varying, a certificate or authorisation; or
a decision imposing a condition on a certificate or authorisation.
See also section 31 of the Act.

section.heading: CASA may grant certificate or authorisation subject to conditions

content.p: Without limiting regulation 11.056, CASA may grant a procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation subject to a condition requiring its holder to permit an authorised inspector (within the meaning given by Division 173.E.5) to exercise the powers of an authorised inspector under that Division in relation to the certificate or authorisation.
However, such a condition is not taken to require the holder to permit the exercise of those powers:
unless the inspector first shows his or her identity card to the holder, or another person on behalf of the holder, if asked to do so by the holder or other person; or
at a time other than during normal business hours.
Such a condition is not taken to authorise the inspector to use force to any extent in exercising those powers.
If CASA does not make a decision about an application under this Part within 6 months after receiving it, CASA is taken to have refused the application.

However, if CASA makes a request under regulation 11.035, 11.040 or 11.045, the time between when CASA makes the request, and when the applicant conducts the demonstration, attends the interview, or gives CASA the information or copy requested, does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA asks an applicant to make a statutory declaration under regulation 11.047 or subregulation 11.050(3A), the time between when CASA asks the applicant to do so and when the applicant gives CASA the statutory declaration does not count towards the period.

Also, if CASA invites an applicant to make a written submission under subregulation 11.050(2), the time between when CASA gives the invitation and when the applicant makes the submission does not count towards the period.
In this regulation:
application includes an application to vary a procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation.

division.heading: Directions to amend certified designer’s or authorised designer’s operations manual

section.heading: CASA may direct amendments to designer’s operations manual

content.p: If necessary in the interests of the safety of air navigation, CASA may, in writing, direct a certified designer or an authorised designer, within a reasonable period specified in the direction, to amend the designer’s operations manual by:
including in the manual the information or other things set out or described in the direction; or
altering the information or other things in the manual in the manner set out in the direction.
CASA may extend the period by written notice, before or after the end of the period referred to in subregulation (1).

division.heading: Suspension and cancellation of procedure design certificates and procedure design authorisations

section.heading: Suspension or cancellation of procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation by CASA

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to a certified designer or authorised designer, suspend or cancel the designer’s procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation if there are reasonable grounds for believing that the designer:
has breached a condition of the certificate or authorisation; or
has contravened a provision of this Part; or
does not meet, or continue to meet, a requirement of this Part for getting or holding the certificate or authorisation; or
has otherwise been guilty of conduct that renders the designer’s continued holding of the certificate or authorisation likely to have an adverse effect on the safety of air navigation.
Before suspending or cancelling a certified designer’s procedure design certificate or an authorised designer’s procedure design authorisation, CASA:
must give written notice to the designer of the facts or circumstances that, in the opinion of CASA, amount to grounds for the suspension or cancellation of the certificate; and
must invite the designer to show cause in writing, within 30 days after the date of the notice, why the certificate or authorisation should not be suspended or cancelled; and
must take into account any written representations made, within the time allowed under paragraph (b), by or on behalf of the designer explaining why the certificate should not be cancelled.
Note: Most decisions in relation to certificates and authorisations are reviewable by the Administrative Review Tribunal, see section 31 of the Act and regulation 201.004.
The Director may, in writing, appoint an officer of CASA as an authorised inspector.
The instrument of appointment may:
describe the premises and activities in relation to which the inspector may use his or her powers under regulation 173.400; and
specify the duration of the appointment; and
specify that the appointment is subject to 1 or more conditions.
CASA must issue each authorised inspector with an identity card that includes a recent photograph of the inspector.
No more than 7 days after ceasing to be an authorised inspector, a person must return his or her identity card to CASA.
Penalty: 1 penalty unit.
An offence against subregulation (2) is an offence of strict liability.
The powers that an authorised inspector may exercise are the powers to do any or all of the following:

enter and inspect premises connected with, or used for the purposes of, design work that is carried on by, or for, a certified designer or authorised designer or where any documents or records relating to that work are kept;

observe the practices and procedures of the certified designer or authorised designer (including the designer’s employees) in carrying on design work under the designer’s procedure design certificate or procedure design authorisation;
inspect the designer’s facilities used for, or in relation to, that work;
inspect and test any systems and equipment used for, or in relation to, that work;
inspect any documents or records maintained, or required to be kept under this Part, by the designer in relation to that work;
make a copy of any document or record that the authorised inspector inspects.
However, an authorised inspector may exercise his or her powers only:

at premises connected with, or used for the purposes of, design work that is carried on by, or for, a certified designer or authorised designer or where any documents or records relating to that work are kept; and
with the permission of the certified designer or authorised designer; and
if the designer, or a person on behalf of the designer, so requests—after the designer or person has been shown the inspector’s identity card; and
during normal business hours; and
to ensure that design work is being carried on in accordance with these Regulations.
The cost of any copying carried out for the purposes of paragraph (1)(f) must be met by CASA.

Subpart 175.A—Aeronautical information management—general
This Part establishes standards and requirements for the quality and integrity of data and information used in air navigation.

Subpart 175.B establishes standards and requirements for AIS providers—persons responsible for the publication of aeronautical data and aeronautical information in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package and on aeronautical charts.

Subpart 175.C establishes standards and requirements for data service providers—persons authorised to publish aeronautical data, aeronautical information or aeronautical charts, or to supply aeronautical data, that pilots may use as an alternative to the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package and aeronautical charts published by AIS providers.

Subpart 175.D sets out requirements for aeronautical data originators—persons responsible for providing aeronautical data and aeronautical information to AIS providers for publication in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package and on aeronautical charts.
Subpart 175.E contains powers that can be used to gather data about objects and structures that affect aviation safety.
Note: The data gathered under Subpart 175.E will be used in air navigation applications, including the following:
the design of terminal instrument flight procedures;
the calculation of lowest safe altitudes;
aircraft operating limitations analysis;
minimum safe altitude warning systems;
the publication of visual navigation charts.
This Part does not apply to the following:
a person who is providing an AIS in the course of his or her duties for the Defence Force;
an AIS provided by the Defence Force.
In this Part:
corporation has the meaning given by regulation 11.015.
officer, of a corporation, means:
(a) for a corporation that is a company (within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001)—a director, secretary or executive officer of the corporation; or

(b) for a corporation of any other kind—a person exercising responsibility, in relation to the corporation, as nearly as possible the same as that of a director, secretary or executive officer of a company (within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001).

section.heading: References in Part 175 to Annexes 3, 4 and 15

content.p: In this Part, a reference to Annex 3, 4 or 15 to the Chicago Convention is a reference to the Annex subject to the differences mentioned in Gen 1.7 of Part 1 of the AIP.

section.heading: Issue of Manual of Standards for Part 175

content.p: For subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue a Manual of Standards for this Part prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Part to be prescribed by the Manual of Standards; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.
CASA must give a copy of a notice mentioned in subregulation 11.275(3) or regulation 11.280, about a Manual of Standards for this Part, to each AIS provider and data service provider.
Subpart 175.B—Aeronautical information management—AIS providers
In this Subpart:
accountable manager, for an AIS provider, means the individual, appointed by the provider, who has the following responsibilities:
responsibility for ensuring that the provider’s AIS is provided in accordance with the provider’s exposition and this Subpart;
responsibility for ensuring that the provider is able to finance, and has adequate resources to provide, its AIS in accordance with the provider’s exposition and this Subpart;
responsibility for the provider’s safety management system required by regulation 175.225 and its implementation.
exposition, for an AIS provider, means:
the documents approved by CASA under regulation 175.060 in relation to the provider; or
if the documents are changed under regulation 175.070, 175.075 or 175.080—the documents as changed.
A person commits an offence if:
the person provides an AIS; and
the person does not hold a certificate under regulation 175.055 that authorises the person to provide the AIS.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A person mentioned in subregulation (2) may apply to CASA, in writing, for a certificate authorising the person to provide an AIS.
For subregulation (1), the persons are the following:
the Commonwealth;
AA;
a person who proposes to provide the AIS:
(i) in cooperation with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(b) of the Air Services Act 1995;
(ii) by arrangement with AA, in accordance with paragraph 11(3)(c) of the Air Services Act 1995.
However, an application cannot be made:
by 2 or more persons jointly; or
on behalf of a partnership.
An application under regulation 175.040 must include the following:
the applicant’s name (including any operating or trading name), contact details and ABN (if any);
if the address of the applicant’s operational headquarters is different from its mailing address—the address of its operational headquarters;
if the applicant is a corporation—the name of each of the officers of the corporation;
if the applicant is a corporation registered in Australia that has an ACN—its ACN and the address of its registered office;
if the applicant is a corporation not registered in Australia—the place it was incorporated or formed;
the services that the applicant proposes to provide as part of the AIS;
the following information about each service:
the location from which the service is proposed to be provided;
the area of Australian territory, and the aerodromes, airspace and ATS routes, that the service is proposed to cover;
the hours during which the service is proposed to be available;
a written undertaking from the person appointed, or proposed to be appointed, as the applicant’s accountable manager that, if CASA issues the certificate, the applicant will:
be capable of operating in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart; and
operate in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart.
The application must be accompanied by a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition.

section.heading: AIS provider certificates—CASA may ask for demonstration of service, facility or equipment

content.p: Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to a certificate under regulation 175.055.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must issue a certificate to an applicant if satisfied that:
the applicant’s proposed exposition complies with regulation 175.200; and
the individual named in the applicant’s exposition as the applicant’s accountable manager:
has the authority to carry out the responsibilities of the position; and
has an understanding of this Part and the applicant’s exposition; and
the applicant is able and willing to conduct the AIS safely and in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart; and
if the applicant proposes to provide the AIS in cooperation or by arrangement with another person—the AIS will be provided in accordance with any agreement relating to the cooperation or arrangement.
If CASA decides to issue the certificate, CASA must determine:
the services that the applicant is authorised to provide as part of the AIS; and
the following about each service:
the location from which the service is to be provided;
the area of Australian territory, and the aerodromes, airspace and ATS routes, that the service is to cover;
the hours during which the service is to be available.
The certificate must include the following:
the applicant’s name and operational headquarters;
the matters mentioned in subregulation (2);
a certificate reference number determined by CASA.
CASA must issue a new certificate to an AIS provider if CASA:
approves a change under subregulation 175.070(4); or
directs a change under regulation 175.080 that causes the certificate to contain anything that is not, or is no longer, correct.
If CASA issues the certificate to the applicant, CASA is taken to have also approved the applicant’s proposed exposition.
It is a condition of a certificate issued to an AIS provider that the provider must comply with:
this Subpart; and
any direction given to the provider, or obligation imposed on the provider, by CASA under a provision of these Regulations.
An AIS provider commits an offence if the provider contravenes the condition mentioned in subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: AIS provider certificates—cancellation of certificate if cooperation or arrangement ceases

content.p: CASA must cancel a certificate under regulation 175.055 held by a person mentioned in subparagraph 175.040(2)(c)(i) if the cooperation mentioned in that subparagraph ceases.
CASA must cancel a certificate under regulation 175.055 held by a person mentioned in subparagraph 175.040(2)(c)(ii) if the arrangement mentioned in that subparagraph ceases.

section.heading: AIS providers—changes to services—matters included in certificate

content.p: An AIS provider must not make a change to the services that it provides as part of its AIS unless the change has been approved by CASA.
An AIS provider must not make a change to any of the following about a service that it provides as part of its AIS unless the change has been approved by CASA:
the location from which the service is provided;
the area of Australian territory, and the aerodromes, airspace and ATS routes, that the service covers;
the hours during which the service is available.
An application for approval of a change must:
be in writing; and
set out the change; and
be accompanied by a copy of the part of the provider’s exposition affected by the change, clearly identifying the change.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a change for an AIS provider if satisfied that the requirements mentioned in regulation 175.055 will continue to be met.
If CASA approves the change, CASA is taken to have also approved the changes to the provider’s exposition covered by the application.
An AIS provider must not make a change other than a change mentioned in regulation 175.070 unless the AIS provider has:
amended its exposition to reflect the change; and
given CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the amended part of the exposition clearly identifying the change.

section.heading: AIS providers—CASA directions relating to exposition

content.p: If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to an AIS provider, direct the provider to change its exposition.
A notice under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.

section.heading: AIS providers—notifying CASA of changes in circumstances

content.p: An AIS provider must give CASA written notice of any change of circumstance which significantly affects its ability to provide its AIS within 7 days after the change occurs.

division.heading: AIS providers—requirements for provision of AIS

section.heading: AIS providers—provision of AIS must comply with laws

content.p: The requirements of this Subpart are in addition to requirements that apply to an AIS provider under the following:
the civil aviation legislation, other than this Subpart;
(b) the Airspace Act 2007;
(c) the Airspace Regulations 2007.

However, if it is not possible for an AIS provider to comply with both a requirement under legislation mentioned in subregulation (1) and a requirement under this Subpart in relation to a particular matter, the provider is required to comply only with the requirement under the legislation mentioned in subregulation (1) in relation to the matter.
If a circumstance mentioned in subregulation (2) arises, the AIS provider must, as soon as practicable after the circumstance arises, give CASA written notice of the circumstance.
An AIS provider must comply with its exposition.

section.heading: AIS providers—provision of AIS must comply with standards

content.p: An AIS provider must provide a service that it provides as part of its AIS in accordance with the standards mentioned in the following that apply to the service:
the Part 175 Manual of Standards;
Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents;
the aeronautical data processing standards.

However, if 2 standards mentioned in different documents mentioned in subregulation (1) apply in relation to a particular matter, and it is not possible for the provider to comply with both standards in relation to the matter, then the provider is required to comply only with the standard mentioned in the document that is first mentioned in subregulation (1) in relation to the matter.
If a circumstance mentioned in subregulation (2) arises, the provider must, as soon as practicable after the circumstance arises, give CASA written notice of the circumstance.

section.heading: AIS providers—standards for development and publication of Integrated Aeronautical Information Package and aeronautical charts

content.p: An AIS provider must publish aeronautical data and aeronautical information as an Integrated Aeronautical Information Package or on aeronautical charts.
The data and information must be developed from data that complies with the standards for data accuracy and integrity mentioned in Annexes 11 and 14 to the Chicago Convention.
The format and quality of the data and information must be suitable for the intended end use of the data and information.
The data and information must be published in accordance with the standards mentioned in the following:
the Part 175 Manual of Standards;
Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents.

However, if 2 standards mentioned in different documents mentioned in subregulation (4) apply in relation to a particular matter, and it is not possible for the provider to comply with both standards in relation to the matter, then the provider is required to comply only with the standard mentioned in the document that is first mentioned in subregulation (4) in relation to the matter.
If a circumstance mentioned in subregulation (5) arises, the provider must, as soon as practicable after the circumstance arises, give CASA written notice of the circumstance.
An aeronautical chart published by the provider must:
be a chart of a type mentioned in Annex 4 to the Chicago Convention; and
contain the aeronautical data and aeronautical information required for the function of a chart of that type as mentioned in Annex 4 to the Chicago Convention.
AIS provided in cooperation or arrangement with AA
If an AIS provider is providing its AIS in cooperation, or by arrangement, with AA, AA must ensure that subregulation (1) is complied with.

section.heading: AIS providers—standards for aeronautical data processing system

content.p: An AIS provider must:
have an automated system for the processing of aeronautical data and aeronautical information as part of providing its AIS; and
update the data in the system as necessary; and
ensure that the system:
allows the digital exchange and supply of aeronautical data and aeronautical information; and
can provide the data and information in a format suitable for its intended use; and
ensure that the format and standards for the exchange and supply of aeronautical data and aeronautical information comply with the following:
Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents; and
ensure that aeronautical data and aeronautical information is exchanged and supplied as required by the following:
Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents.

However, if 2 documents mentioned in paragraph (1)(d) apply in relation to a particular matter, and it is not possible for the provider to comply with both documents in relation to the matter, then the provider is required to comply only with the document that is first mentioned in paragraph (1)(d) in relation to the matter.

Also, if 2 documents mentioned in paragraph (1)(e) apply in relation to a particular matter, and it is not possible for the provider to comply with both documents in relation to the matter, then the provider is required to comply only with the document that is first mentioned in paragraph (1)(e) in relation to the matter.
If a circumstance mentioned in subregulation (2) or (3) arises, the provider must, as soon as practicable after the circumstance arises, give CASA written notice of the circumstance.

section.heading: AIS providers—contravention of exposition or standards

content.p: An AIS provider may contravene regulation 175.095, 175.100, 175.105 or 175.110 if the contravention is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
The provider must, as soon as practicable after the contravention occurs, give CASA written notice of the contravention, including an estimate of how long the contravention will last.
If an AIS provider provides a NOTAM service, the provider must ensure that the service:
operates 24 hours a day, every day of the year; and
issues a NOTAM in the following circumstances:
the circumstances mentioned in Annex 15 to the Chicago Convention;
when required by Australian law;
when it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety; and
has agreements with international NOTAM offices for the exchange of NOTAMS; and
is connected to the aeronautical fixed service.
If an AIS provider provides a briefing service, the provider must ensure that the service:
is an automated pre-flight information service; and
operates 24 hours a day, every day of the year; and
allows self-briefing by flight crew members and other operational personnel; and
is capable of providing flight crew members and other operational personnel with:
aeronautical data and aeronautical information to enable pre-flight planning of flights; and
pre-flight information bulletins, within the meaning of Annex 15 to the Chicago Convention; and
NOTAMS that are relevant to a proposed flight; and
meteorological information that is relevant to a proposed flight; and
allows flight crew members or other operational personnel to enter a flight plan; and
provides information that assists in the provision of a flight information service.
If an AIS provider provides a post-flight information service, the provider must ensure that the service:
is capable of receiving reports by flight crew members on:
the state and operation of air navigation facilities and services; and
the presence of birds and other wildlife that may affect aircraft operations; and
disseminates the information received in a format and timeframe appropriate to the operational significance of the information.

section.heading: AIS providers—CASA directions about NOTAMS for a location

content.p: CASA may, by written notice given to an AIS provider, direct the provider to do the following:
allow NOTAMS to be published that relate only to a particular location;
publish NOTAMS:
that relate only to the location; and
that contain details stated in the notice.
A notice under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.

section.heading: AIS providers—aerodromes not covered by Part 139—removal of references in AIP

content.p: This regulation applies if an AIS provider becomes aware of an aeronautical data originator:
who is responsible for aeronautical data or aeronautical information about an aerodrome that is not a certified aerodrome; and
who has not complied with Subpart 175.D in relation to the aerodrome.
The provider must remove any references to the aerodrome that the provider has published in the AIP from the AIP when the AIP is next amended.
Note: The aeronautical data or aeronautical information for which the aeronautical data originator is responsible must be specified in a data product specification: see paragraph 175.160(4)(a).

section.heading: AIS providers—publication of aeronautical charts relating to areas etc. outside authority

content.p: This regulation applies if an AIS provider publishes an aeronautical chart that includes aeronautical data or aeronautical information that relates to an area, aerodrome, airspace or ATS route not covered by the provider’s certificate.
This Subpart, other than this regulation, does not apply to the publication of the data or information if the data or information accurately reflects data or information that is published:
by another AIS provider under this Subpart; or
by an AIS of a foreign country.

division.heading: AIS providers—requirements about aeronautical data and aeronautical information

section.heading: AIS providers—CASA directions relating to aeronautical data or aeronautical information

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to aeronautical data or aeronautical information that an AIS provider publishes:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to the provider, direct the AIS provider to do the following:
add to, amend, or remove the data or information;
give CASA stated information or records relating to any change to the data or information.
A notice under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.

section.heading: AIS providers—integrity of aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to aeronautical data or aeronautical information that an AIS provider publishes:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
The provider must ensure that the integrity of the data or information is maintained during the processing of the data and information by the provider.
The provider must ensure that the data or information:
is obtained from entities responsible for the data or information; and
is kept up-to-date; and
is traceable to its origin.
The provider must verify that the data or information:
has not been altered from the source data while it is in storage or transit or while it is being formatted; and
has been checked for accuracy against the source data before publication; and
has been published only during the period when the data or information is valid.
The provider must verify:
that the data or information is complete; and
that all of the data or information needed to support the intended use of the data or information has been published.
If the data or information was provided to the provider, the provider must verify that the data or information was provided in a format that is suitable for use by the provider.
If the data or information is for inclusion in a NOTAM, the provider must verify that the data or information was provided to the provider by a NOTAM authorised person.

section.heading: AIS providers—giving data product specifications to aeronautical data originators

content.p: An AIS provider must give a person a written data product specification that complies with subregulation (4) if the person is responsible for aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider has published, or will publish:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
Subregulation (3) applies if the provider is also responsible for aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider has published, or will publish:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
The provider must give a written data product specification that complies with subregulation (4) to the area of the provider’s organisation responsible for the data or information.
For subregulations (1) and (3), the data product specification must include the following:
the aeronautical data or aeronautical information for which the person or area is responsible;
the standards for the accuracy and resolution of the data or information that the person or area will provide to the provider;
the dates by which the data or information must be provided;
the format for the data or information;
the details of the authenticated electronic means for providing the data or information;
the procedures for managing requests for alterations to the data or information;
the procedures for giving notice of, and for rectifying, errors and omissions detected in the data or information;
the procedures the provider will follow to verify that changes to the data or information have been approved by the person or area;
the circumstances (if any) in which the person or area must ask the provider to issue a NOTAM.

An AIS provider must, in writing, revoke a data product specification given to a person, or an area of the provider’s organisation, under regulation 175.160, if the person or part of the organisation is no longer responsible for the aeronautical data or aeronautical information mentioned in the data product specification.

section.heading: AIS providers—compliance with data product specification

content.p: An AIS provider must comply with the procedures mentioned in a data product specification given by the provider under regulation 175.160.

section.heading: AIS providers—correction and notification of errors and omissions in aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: This regulation applies if an AIS provider becomes aware of an error or omission in aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider publishes:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
The provider must, as soon as practicable after the provider becomes aware of the error or omission:
record and investigate the error or omission; and
ensure that the error or omission is corrected by the most appropriate means taking into account the operational significance of the error or omission; and
ensure that notice of the corrected aeronautical data or aeronautical information is given to persons who had received the data or information; and
identify the root cause of the error or omission; and
establish and implement processes to eliminate the root cause of the error or omission.

The provider must give CASA written notice of any significant error or omission that may affect the safety of air navigation as soon as practicable after the provider becomes aware of the error or omission.

section.heading: AIS providers—storage and security of aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: An AIS provider must ensure that aeronautical data and aeronautical information necessary for the provision of its AIS:
is stored digitally; and
is kept secure to prevent unauthorised access or alteration.

section.heading: AIS providers—timing of effective dates and distribution of certain documents and information

content.p: An AIS provider that publishes any of the following documents or information must ensure that the document or information becomes effective only on an AIRAC effective date:
an AIP Amendment;
an AIP Supplement;
an aeronautical chart;
information mentioned in Appendix 4 (Information to be notified by AIRAC) of Annex 15 to the Chicago Convention.
The provider must distribute the document or information so that a recipient receives the document or information at least 28 days before the document or information becomes effective.

However, if the document or information contains, or is, information mentioned in Part 3 of Appendix 4 (Information to be notified by AIRAC) of Annex 15 to the Chicago Convention, the provider must distribute the document or information so that a recipient receives the document or information at least 56 days before the document or information becomes effective.

The provider must ensure that a document or information that becomes effective in accordance with subregulation (1) and is distributed in accordance with subregulation (2) or (3) is identified by the acronym “AIRAC”.
However, the provider may contravene subregulation (1), (2) or (3) if the contravention is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
If the provider contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (3), the provider must give CASA written notice of the contravention as soon as practicable after the contravention occurs.

section.heading: AIS providers—licence agreements with data service providers for supply of data sets

content.p: An AIS provider must enter into a licence agreement with each data service provider.
The licence agreement must cover any of the following that the data service provider requires for its authorised data service activities:
aeronautical data and aeronautical information that the AIS provider publishes in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package;
aeronautical charts that the AIS provider publishes.
The licence agreement must:
require the AIS provider to supply data sets containing the data, information or charts covered by the agreement to the data service provider; and
allow the data service provider to use, format and publish the data, information or charts; and
include a complete data product specification of the data sets; and
detail when the data sets will be supplied to the data service provider; and
detail the authenticated electronic means by which the data sets will be supplied to the data service provider; and
describe the method of protection to be applied to the data sets to ensure that data is not corrupted during the transfer; and
include the method by which requests, by either party, for alterations to the data, information or charts are to be managed; and
describe how errors and omissions detected in the data, information or charts are to be notified and rectified.
The licence agreement may include charges for the supply of the data sets to the data service provider.
An AIS provider must comply with each licence agreement it has entered into under regulation 175.190.
The exposition of an AIS provider must contain the following:
the provider’s name (including any operating or trading name), contact details and ABN (if any);
the location and address of:
the provider’s operational headquarters; and
each of the provider’s operational facilities;
the name of the provider’s accountable manager;
a description and diagram of the provider’s organisational structure showing formal reporting lines;
if the provider is a corporation—a description of the provider’s corporate structure;
for each operational position, including each operational supervisory position, within the organisational structure:
a statement of the duties and responsibilities of the position; and
the recent experience requirements for the position (if any); and
the endorsements and qualifications required for the position (if any); and
the currency requirements (if any) for the endorsements or qualifications;
a description of how the provider determines the number of operational personnel, including operational supervisory personnel, required to provide its AIS;
a list of the services that the provider provides as part of its AIS;
the following information about each service:
the location from which the service is provided;
the area of Australian territory, and the aerodromes, airspace and ATS routes, that the service covers;
the hours during which the service is available;
a description of the procedures that ensure that each service is provided in accordance with this Subpart;
a description and an example of the format used for the publication of the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package and aeronautical charts published by the provider;
a description of the format for the digital exchange or supply of aeronautical data;
a description of the arrangements that ensure that the AIS provider receives, on a daily basis, the aeronautical data and aeronautical information necessary for providing its AIS;
a description of the arrangements that ensure that the provider is able to continue to provide its AIS to persons who reasonably require the service;
a copy of each agreement (if any) entered into by the provider to provide its AIS in cooperation or by arrangement with another person;
a copy of:
each data product specification given by the provider under regulation 175.160; and
each licence agreement entered into by the provider under regulation 175.190;
a copy of any data product specification the provider has in relation to any aeronautical data it supplies or receives as part of its AIS;
a copy of the provider’s data, personnel and physical security program;
a description of the processes and documents used to present to personnel the relevant standards, rules and procedures mentioned in the following:
the Part 175 Manual of Standards;
