Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents;
the aeronautical data processing standards;
the provider’s instructions for the provision of its AIS (if any) that relate to particular operational facilities;
details of any recommended practices mentioned in the following documents that the provider does not follow:
Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents;
the aeronautical data processing standards;
a copy of each document that contains operational instructions for personnel;
a description of the procedures that ensure all operational personnel are familiar with any operational changes that have occurred since they last performed operational duties;
a description of the provider’s training and checking system, as required by regulation 175.220;
a description of the provider’s safety management system, as required by regulation 175.225;
a description of the provider’s quality management system, as required by regulation 175.230;
a copy of the provider’s contingency plan, as required by regulation 175.240;
a description of the provider’s record keeping procedures, as required by regulation 175.255;
a description of the procedures used in commissioning new facilities, equipment and services;
a description of the procedures that ensure that all equipment, including software, is operated in accordance with the manufacturer’s operating instructions and manuals;
a description of the procedures for making changes.
The provider must:
keep the exposition in a readily accessible form; and
ensure that operational personnel and CASA have ready access to the exposition; and
keep the exposition up-to-date.
An AIS provider must have an appropriate organisation with a sound and effective management structure that enables the provider to provide its AIS in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart.
An AIS provider must have enough suitably competent, qualified and trained personnel to:
enable the provider to provide its AIS in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart; and
supervise the provision of each service it provides as part of its AIS.
An AIS provider must have an accountable manager.

section.heading: AIS providers—personnel—training and checking system for operational personnel

content.p: An AIS provider must have a training and checking system that ensures that the provider’s operational personnel maintain their competence and are provided with ongoing training appropriate to their duties.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the training and checking system must ensure that each person who is a member of the provider’s operational personnel:
is trained and proven to be proficient in the performance of the person’s duties; and
meets the recent experience requirements (if any) under the provider’s exposition for the person’s position; and
holds each endorsement or qualification (if any) that is required under the provider’s exposition for the person’s position; and
meets the currency requirements (if any) under the provider’s exposition for the endorsements and qualifications.
An AIS provider must have a safety management system that:
is a systemic approach to managing safety; and
integrates human factors principles; and
includes the matters mentioned in subregulation (2).
For paragraph (1)(c), the matters are the following:
organisational structures, accountabilities, policies and procedures necessary to manage safety in a systemic way;
a statement of the provider’s safety policy, objectives and planning, including details of the following:
the management commitment to, and responsibility for, safety;
the safety accountabilities of managers;
the appointment of safety management personnel;
how human factors principles are integrated into the safety management system;
a safety management system implementation plan;
relevant third party relationships and interactions;
coordination of an emergency response plan;
safety management system documentation;
a safety risk management process, including:
hazard identification processes; and
risk assessment and mitigation processes;
a safety assurance system, including details of processes for:
safety performance monitoring and measurement; and
internal safety investigation; and
management of change; and
continuous improvement of the safety management system;
a safety training and promotion system, including details of the following:
safety management system training and education;
safety management system safety communication.
An AIS provider must have a quality management system that:
is based on the elements of the latest edition of the ISO 9001 standard, as in force from time to time, that are relevant to the provision of AIS; and
includes quality management procedures that address the quality management requirements mentioned in the aeronautical data processing standards.

section.heading: AIS providers—facilities, equipment, data and information

content.p: An AIS provider must have the facilities and equipment that are necessary for providing its AIS, including appropriate premises and equipment to allow operational personnel to perform their duties.

An AIS provider must provide its operational personnel with access to the aeronautical data and aeronautical information required for the publication of the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package, or the aeronautical charts, that the provider publishes.
An AIS provider must have a contingency plan that sets out the procedures to be followed if a service provided as part of its AIS is interrupted.
The contingency plan must include:
the actions to be taken by personnel responsible for providing the service; and
possible alternative arrangements for providing the service; and
arrangements for resuming normal provision of the service.
An AIS provider must have up-to-date copies of the following reference materials in a readily accessible form:
the civil aviation legislation relevant to the provision of its AIS;
Annexes 4, 11, 14 and 15 to the Chicago Convention;
if PANS-AIM is in force—that document;
ICAO Documents 8126 and 8697;
the other AIS applicable ICAO documents;
the aeronautical data processing standards;
any instructions issued by the provider to its personnel in relation to the provision of its AIS;
manuals for equipment used by personnel in the provision of its AIS.
The provider must ensure that operational personnel have ready access to the reference materials.

section.heading: AIS providers—annual review by accountable manager

content.p: An AIS provider must ensure that its accountable manager:
conducts an annual review of the provider against the requirements of its exposition and this Subpart; and
addresses any deficiencies that are identified during the review; and
gives CASA a report of the annual review, including:
any significant deficiencies identified since any previous annual review; and
how the deficiencies are to be addressed.
An AIS provider must have procedures for making, collecting, indexing, storing, securing, maintaining, accessing and disposing of the following:
records that identify all incoming and outgoing aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that identify each person who is authorised by the provider to process, check, edit, publish or supply aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that list the endorsements, qualifications and competencies of personnel who process, check, edit, publish or supply aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that identify each AIP responsible person for an aeronautical data originator that provides aeronautical data or aeronautical information to the provider;
records that identify each NOTAM authorised person for an aeronautical data originator that requests the provider to issue NOTAMS;

records that identify each occurrence of an error or omission in aeronautical data or aeronautical information published by the provider in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package or on an aeronautical chart;
records that contain the results of any audit or review of the provider’s AIS.
The provider must ensure that a record mentioned in subregulation (1) is legible and permanent.

section.heading: AIS providers—retention period for aeronautical data, aeronautical information and records

content.p: Aeronautical data and information
Subregulation (2) applies if aeronautical data or aeronautical information necessary for the provision of an AIS provider’s AIS:
has been published by the provider; and
has become effective; and
(c) is not a Commonwealth record within the meaning of the Archives Act 1983.
The provider must keep the data or information for at least 7 years after the data or information ceases to be effective.
Records
(3) Subregulation (4) applies if a record mentioned in subregulation 175.255(1) is not a Commonwealth record within the meaning of the Archives Act 1983.
The provider must keep the record:
if the record relates to aeronautical data or aeronautical information mentioned in subregulation (1)—for as long as the data or information is required to be kept; or
otherwise—for at least 7 years after the record is made.
Subpart 175.C—Aeronautical information management—data service providers
In this Subpart:
accountable manager, for a data service provider, means the individual, appointed by the provider, who has the following responsibilities:
responsibility for ensuring that the provider’s authorised data service activities are conducted in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart;
responsibility for ensuring that the provider is able to finance, and has adequate resources to conduct, its authorised data service activities in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart;
responsibility for the provider’s safety management system required by regulation 175.405 and its implementation.
exposition, for a data service provider, means:
the documents approved by CASA under regulation 175.300 in relation to the provider; or
if the documents are changed under regulation 175.310, 175.315 or 175.320—the documents as changed.

section.heading: Conduct of data service activity—requirement for certificate

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person conducts a data service activity; and
the person does not hold a certificate under regulation 175.295 that authorises the person to conduct the activity.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to an AIS provider publishing aeronautical data, aeronautical information or an aeronautical chart in the course of providing an AIS.
Subregulation (1) does not apply to an aerodrome operator publishing one of the following charts, as mentioned in Annex 4 to the Chicago Convention:
an Aerodrome Obstacle Chart—ICAO Type A;
an Aerodrome Obstacle Chart—ICAO Type B;
an Aerodrome Terrain and Obstacle Chart—ICAO (Electronic);
a Precision Approach Terrain Chart—ICAO.

Subregulation (1) does not apply to a person who supplies navigation equipment or a navigation system containing aeronautical data in a database, if the database has been supplied to the person by a third party for use in the equipment or system.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulations (2), (3) and (4): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: CASA to publish list of data service providers

content.p: CASA must publish a list of:
data service providers; and
the matters mentioned in subregulation 175.295(2) for each of the data service providers.
CASA must keep the list up-to-date.

section.heading: Data service provider certificates—who may apply

content.p: A person may apply to CASA, in writing, for a certificate authorising the person to conduct a data service activity.
However, an application cannot be made:
by 2 or more persons jointly; or
on behalf of a partnership.

section.heading: Data service provider certificates—requirements for application

content.p: An application under regulation 175.280 must include the following:
the applicant’s name (including any operating or trading name), contact details and ABN (if any);
if the address of the applicant’s operational headquarters is different from its mailing address—the address of its operational headquarters;
if the applicant is a corporation—the name of each of the officers of the corporation;
if the applicant is a corporation registered in Australia that has an ACN—its ACN and the address of its registered office;
if the applicant is a corporation not registered in Australia—the place it was incorporated or formed;
a description of the data service activities the applicant proposes to conduct;
the area of coverage of the aeronautical data, aeronautical information or aeronautical charts covered by the activities;
a written undertaking from the person appointed, or proposed to be appointed, as the applicant’s accountable manager that, if CASA issues the certificate, the applicant will:
be capable of operating in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart; and
operate in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart.
The application must be accompanied by a copy of the applicant’s proposed exposition.

section.heading: Data service provider certificates—CASA may ask for demonstration of service, facility or equipment

content.p: Regulation 11.045 applies in relation to a certificate under regulation 175.295.

section.heading: Data service provider certificates—issue of certificate

content.p: Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must issue a certificate to an applicant if satisfied that:
the applicant’s proposed exposition complies with regulation 175.380; and
the individual named in the applicant’s exposition as the applicant’s accountable manager:
has the authority to carry out the responsibilities of the position; and
has an understanding of this Part and the applicant’s exposition; and
the applicant is able and willing to conduct the data service activities mentioned in the application safely and in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart.
If CASA decides to issue the certificate, CASA must determine:
the data service activities the applicant is authorised to conduct; and
the area of coverage of the aeronautical data, aeronautical information or aeronautical charts covered by the activities.
The certificate must include the following:
the applicant’s name and operational headquarters;
the matters mentioned in subregulation (2);
a certificate reference number determined by CASA.
CASA must issue a new certificate to a data service provider if CASA:
approves a change under subregulation 175.310(4); or
directs a change under regulation 175.320 that causes the certificate to contain anything that is not, or is no longer, correct.

section.heading: Data service provider certificates—approval of exposition

content.p: If CASA issues the certificate to the applicant, CASA is taken to have also approved the applicant’s proposed exposition.
It is a condition of a certificate issued to a data service provider that the provider must comply with:
this Subpart; and
any direction given to the provider, or obligation imposed on the provider, by CASA under a provision of these Regulations.
A data service provider commits an offence if the provider contravenes the condition mentioned in subregulation (1).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—changes to authorised data service activities—matters included in certificate

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider makes a change to the provider’s authorised data service activities; and
the change has not been approved by CASA.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider makes a change to the area of coverage for aeronautical data, aeronautical information or an aeronautical chart covered by an authorised data service activity; and
the change has not been approved by CASA.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An application for approval of a change must:
be in writing; and
set out the change; and
be accompanied by a copy of the part of the provider’s exposition affected by the change, clearly identifying the change.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must approve a change for a data service provider if satisfied that the requirements mentioned in regulation 175.295 will continue to be met.
If CASA approves the change, CASA is taken to have also approved the changes to the provider’s exposition covered by the application.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider makes a change other than a change mentioned in regulation 175.310; and
the provider did not, before making the change, comply with subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the provider must:
amend its exposition to reflect the change; and
give CASA written notice of the change and a copy of the amended part of the exposition clearly identifying the change.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—CASA directions relating to exposition

content.p: If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to a data service provider, direct the provider to change its exposition.
A direction under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.
The provider commits an offence if the provider does not comply with the direction within the time stated in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—notifying CASA of changes in circumstances

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
a change of circumstance occurs which significantly affects the provider’s ability to conduct its authorised data service activities; and
the provider does not give CASA written notice of the change of circumstance within 7 days after the change occurs.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—notifying CASA of intention to cease activities

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider ceases to conduct an authorised data service activity; and
the provider did not, at least 2 months before ceasing to conduct the activity, give CASA written notice of the following:
the provider’s intention to cease conducting the activity;
the date on which the provider intended to cease conducting the activity.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

division.heading: Data service providers—requirements for provision of data service

section.heading: Data service providers—standards for data service provision

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider publishes or supplies aeronautical data or aeronautical information in conducting a data service activity; and
the data or information does not meet the requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the data or information must be the same as the data or information published in the following:
the AIP;
an AIP Amendment;
an AIP Supplement;
a permanent NOTAM;
an aeronautical chart published by an AIS provider;
an aeronautical chart mentioned in subregulation 175.270(3) published by an aerodrome operator.
A data service provider commits an offence if the provider contravenes a provision of the Part 175 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider processes aeronautical data or aeronautical information; and
the provider does so other than in accordance with the aeronautical data processing standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulation (4) does not apply in relation to a particular matter if:
2 standards mentioned in the Part 175 Manual of Standards and the aeronautical data processing standards apply in relation to the matter; and
it is not possible for the provider to comply with both standards in relation to the matter.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
A data service provider commits an offence if:
a circumstance mentioned in subregulation (5) arises; and
the provider does not, as soon as practicable after the circumstance arises, give CASA written notice of the circumstance.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A data service provider commits an offence if the provider contravenes a provision of its exposition.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—standards for aeronautical data processing system

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if the provider does not meet a requirement mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), the requirements are the following:
the provider must have an automated system for the processing of aeronautical data and aeronautical information as part of conducting its authorised data service activities;
the provider must update the data in the system as necessary.
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider has a system mentioned in paragraph (2)(a); but
the system does not:
allow the digital exchange and supply of aeronautical data and aeronautical information; or
provide the data and information in a format suitable for its intended use.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

division.heading: Data service providers—requirements about aeronautical data and aeronautical information

section.heading: Data service providers—CASA directions to amend aeronautical data or aeronautical information

content.p: If satisfied that it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety, CASA may, by written notice given to a data service provider, direct the provider to add to, amend, or remove any aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider publishes or supplies in conducting a data service activity.
A direction under this regulation must state the time within which the direction must be complied with.
The provider commits an offence if the provider does not comply with the direction within the time stated in the direction.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—integrity of aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider publishes or supplies aeronautical data or aeronautical information in conducting a data service activity; and
the provider has not verified the matters mentioned in subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the matters are the following:
that the data or information was not altered from the source data while in storage or transit or while being formatted;
that the data or information was checked for accuracy against the source data before publication or supply;
that the data or information is complete;
that all of the data or information needed to support the intended use of the data or information has been published or supplied.

section.heading: Data service providers—correction and notification of errors and omissions in aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: Correction of errors and omissions
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider becomes aware of an error or omission in aeronautical data or aeronautical information that it publishes or supplies in conducting a data service activity; and
the provider does not comply with subregulation (2) as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the error or omission.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (1)(b), the provider must do the following:
record and investigate the error or omission;
ensure that the error or omission is corrected by the most appropriate means taking into account the operational significance of the error or omission;
ensure that notice of the corrected aeronautical data or aeronautical information is given to persons who had received the data or information;
identify the root cause of the error or omission;
establish and implement processes to eliminate the root cause of the error or omission.
Notifying CASA of errors and omissions
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider becomes aware of an error or omission in aeronautical data or aeronautical information that it publishes or supplies in conducting a data service activity; and
the error or omission is a significant error or omission that may affect the safety of air navigation; and
the provider does not give CASA written notice of the error or omission as soon as practicable after the provider becomes aware of the error or omission.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Notifying AIS provider of errors and omissions
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider identifies an error or omission in aeronautical data or aeronautical information supplied by an AIS provider; and
the provider does not tell the AIS provider of the error or omission as soon as practicable after identifying the error or omission.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Data service providers—storage and security of aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if aeronautical data or aeronautical information necessary for its authorised data service activities:
is not stored digitally; or
is not kept secure to prevent unauthorised access or alteration.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—effective dates and validity of aeronautical data, information and charts

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider publishes or supplies aeronautical data, aeronautical information or an aeronautical chart in conducting a data service activity; and
the data, information or chart does not become effective on the same date, or remain valid for the same period, as the corresponding data, information or chart contained in the following:
the AIP;
an AIP Amendment;
an AIP Supplement;
a permanent NOTAM;
an aeronautical chart published by an AIS provider;
an aeronautical chart mentioned in subregulation 175.270(3) published by an aerodrome operator.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Subregulation (1) does not apply if:
the corresponding data, information or chart was:
published by an AIS provider in contravention of subregulation 175.185(1); or
distributed by an AIS provider in contravention of subregulation 175.185(2) or (3); and

the data service provider publishes or supplies the data, information or chart by the next effective AIRAC date following the publication or distribution of the corresponding data, information or chart.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (2): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Data service providers—compliance with licence agreement with AIS providers

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if the provider contravenes a provision of a licence agreement, mentioned in regulation 175.190, entered into by the provider.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
The exposition of a data service provider must contain the following:
the provider’s name (including any operating or trading name), address, contact details and ABN (if any);
the location and address of:
the provider’s operational headquarters; and
each of the provider’s operational facilities;
the name of the provider’s accountable manager;
a description and diagram of the provider’s organisational structure showing formal reporting lines;
if the provider is a corporation—a description of the provider’s corporate structure;
for each operational position, including each operational supervisory position, within the organisational structure:
a statement of the duties and responsibilities of the position; and
the recent experience requirements for the position (if any); and
the qualifications required for the position (if any); and
the currency requirements (if any) for the qualifications;
a description of how the provider determines the number of operational personnel, including operational supervisory personnel, required for the provider’s authorised data service activities;
a description of the data service activities that the provider conducts;
the area of coverage of the aeronautical data, aeronautical information and aeronautical charts covered by the activities;
a description of the procedures that ensure that each of the provider’s authorised data service activities is provided in accordance with this Subpart;

a description and an example of the formats used for the aeronautical data, aeronautical information and aeronautical charts published or supplied by the provider in conducting its authorised data service activities;
a description of the format for the digital exchange or supply of aeronautical data;

a description of the arrangements that ensure that the provider receives, on a daily basis, the aeronautical data and aeronautical information necessary for conducting the provider’s authorised data service activities;

a description of the arrangements that ensure that the provider is able to continue to publish or supply aeronautical data or aeronautical information, in conducting its authorised data service activities, to persons who reasonably require the data or information;
a copy of any licence agreement mentioned in regulation 175.190 entered into by the provider;
a copy of any data product specification in relation to any aeronautical data that the provider receives from an AIS provider;
a copy of the provider’s data, personnel and physical security program;
a description of the processes and documents used to present to personnel the relevant aeronautical data and aeronautical information contained in the following:
the AIP;
AIP Amendments;
AIP Supplements;
permanent NOTAM;
aeronautical charts;
the provider’s instructions for conducting its authorised data service activities that relate to particular operational facilities;
a description of the processes and documents used to present to personnel the relevant standards, rules and procedures contained in:
the Part 175 Manual of Standards; and
the aeronautical data processing standards;
a copy of each document that contains operational instructions for personnel;
a description of the procedures that ensure all operational personnel are familiar with any operational changes that have occurred since they last performed operational duties;
a description of the provider’s training and checking system, as required by regulation 175.400;
a description of the provider’s safety management system, as required by regulation 175.405;
a description of the provider’s quality management system, as required by regulation 175.410;
a copy of the provider’s contingency plan, as required by regulation 175.420;
a description of the provider’s record keeping procedures, as required by regulation 175.435;
a description of the procedures used in commissioning new facilities, equipment and services;
a description of the procedures that ensure that all equipment, including software, is operated in accordance with the manufacturer’s operating instructions and manuals;
a description of the procedures for making changes.
The provider commits an offence if:
the provider does not keep the exposition in a readily accessible form; or
operational personnel do not have ready access to the exposition; or
CASA does not have ready access to the exposition; or
the provider does not keep the exposition up-to-date.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

A data service provider must have an appropriate organisation with a sound and effective management structure that enables the provider to conduct its authorised data service activities in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart.
A data service provider must have enough suitably competent, qualified and trained personnel to:
enable the provider to conduct its authorised data service activities in accordance with its exposition and this Subpart; and
supervise the conduct of each of its authorised data service activities.
A data service provider must have an accountable manager.

section.heading: Data service providers—personnel—training and checking system for operational personnel

content.p: A data service provider must have a training and checking system that ensures that the provider’s operational personnel maintain their competence and are provided with ongoing training appropriate to their duties.
Without limiting subregulation (1), the training and checking system must ensure that each person who is a member of the provider’s operational personnel:
is trained and proven to be proficient in the performance of the person’s duties; and
meets the recent experience requirements (if any) under the provider’s exposition for the person’s position; and
holds each qualification (if any) that is required under the provider’s exposition for the person’s position; and
meets the currency requirements (if any) under the provider’s exposition for the qualifications.
A data service provider must have a safety management system that:
is a systemic approach to managing safety; and
integrates human factors principles; and
includes the matters mentioned in subregulation (2).
For paragraph (1)(c), the matters are the following:
organisational structures, accountabilities, policies and procedures necessary to manage safety in a systemic way;
a statement of the data service provider’s safety policy, objectives and planning, including details of the following:
the management commitment to, and responsibility for, safety;
the safety accountabilities of managers;
the appointment of safety management personnel;
how human factors principles are integrated into the safety management system;
a safety management system implementation plan;
relevant third party relationships and interactions;
coordination of an emergency response plan;
safety management system documentation;
a safety risk management process, including:
hazard identification processes; and
risk assessment and mitigation processes;
a safety assurance system, including details of processes for:
safety performance monitoring and measurement; and
internal safety investigation; and
management of change; and
continuous improvement of the safety management system;
a safety training and promotion system, including details of the following:
safety management system training and education;
safety management system safety communication.
A data service provider must have a quality management system that:

is based on the elements of the latest edition of the ISO 9001 standard, as in force from time to time, that are relevant to the processing, publication and supply of aeronautical data and aeronautical information for the provider’s authorised data service activities; and
includes quality management procedures that address the quality management requirements mentioned in the aeronautical data processing standards.

section.heading: Data service providers—facilities, equipment, data and information

content.p: A data service provider must have the facilities and equipment that are necessary for conducting its authorised data service activities, including appropriate premises and equipment to allow operational personnel to perform their duties.
A data service provider must provide its operational personnel with access to the aeronautical data and aeronautical information required for conducting its authorised data service activities.
A data service provider must have a contingency plan that sets out the procedures to be followed if an authorised data service activity for the provider is interrupted.
The contingency plan must include:
the actions to be taken by personnel responsible for conducting the activity; and
possible alternative arrangements for conducting the activity; and
arrangements for resuming normal conduct of the activity.
A data service provider must have up-to-date copies of the following reference materials in a readily accessible form:
the civil aviation legislation relevant to the conduct of the data service provider’s authorised data service activities;
the AIP;
any AIP Amendments;
any AIP Supplements;
any permanent NOTAM;
any aeronautical charts published by an AIS provider;
any aeronautical charts mentioned in subregulation 175.270(3) published by an aerodrome operator;
the aeronautical data processing standards;
any instructions issued by the provider to its personnel in relation to the conduct of the data service provider’s authorised data service activities;
manuals for equipment used by personnel in the conduct of the provider’s authorised data service activities.
The provider must ensure that operational personnel have ready access to the reference materials.

section.heading: Data service providers—annual review by accountable manager

content.p: A data service provider commits an offence if the provider’s accountable manager contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), the accountable manager must:
conduct an annual review of the provider against the requirements of its exposition and this Subpart; and
address any deficiencies that are identified during the review; and
give CASA a report of the annual review, including:
any significant deficiencies identified since any previous annual review; and
how the deficiencies are to be addressed.
A data service provider must have procedures for making, collecting, indexing, storing, securing, maintaining, accessing and disposing of the following:
records that identify all incoming and outgoing aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that identify each person who is authorised by the provider to process, check, edit, publish or supply aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that list the qualifications and competencies of personnel who process, check, edit, publish or supply aeronautical data and aeronautical information;
records that identify each occurrence of an error or omission in:
aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider receives; or
aeronautical data or aeronautical information that the provider publishes or supplies in conducting a data service activity;
records that contain the results of any audit or review of the provider’s activities.
The provider must ensure that a record mentioned in subregulation (1) is legible and permanent.

section.heading: Data service providers—retention period for aeronautical data, aeronautical information and records

content.p: Aeronautical data and information
A data service provider commits an offence if:
the provider publishes or supplies aeronautical data or aeronautical information in conducting a data service activity; and
the provider does not keep a copy of the data or information for at least 7 years after the data or information ceases to be effective.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Records
A data service provider commits an offence if the provider does not keep a record mentioned in subregulation 175.435(1):
if the record relates to aeronautical data or aeronautical information mentioned in subregulation (1)—for as long as the data or information is required to be kept; or
otherwise—for at least 7 years after the record is made.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.
Subpart 175.D—Aeronautical information management—aeronautical data originators

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—AIP responsible person and NOTAM authorised persons

content.p: AIP responsible persons
An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if:
the originator provides aeronautical data or aeronautical information to an AIS provider; and
the originator has not appointed a single senior manager within the originator’s organisation as the AIP responsible person for the originator.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An AIP responsible person is responsible for the provision of aeronautical data or aeronautical information, other than in NOTAMS, from the originator to an AIS provider.
An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if:
the originator appoints a person as the AIP responsible person for the originator; and
the person does not have the knowledge and competence to carry out the responsibilities of an AIP responsible person.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
NOTAM authorised persons
An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if:
the originator asks an AIS provider to issue, review or cancel a NOTAM; and
the originator has not appointed a person in the originator’s organisation as a NOTAM authorised person for the originator.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A NOTAM authorised person is responsible for requesting the issue, review and cancellation of NOTAMS for the originator.
An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if:
the originator appoints a person as a NOTAM authorised person for the originator; and
the person does not have the knowledge and competence to request the issue, review and cancellation of NOTAMS.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—telling AIS provider of AIP responsible person and NOTAM authorised persons

content.p: An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if:
the originator provides aeronautical data or aeronautical information to an AIS provider; and
the originator has not told the AIS provider, in writing, of the following:
the name of the AIP responsible person for the originator;
the names of the NOTAM authorised persons (if any) for the originator;
any changes (if any) to the persons who occupy the positions mentioned in subparagraphs (i) and (ii) since any previous provision of aeronautical data or aeronautical information to the AIS provider.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—requirement to provide updated aeronautical data or aeronautical information published other than in NOTAMS

content.p: This regulation applies if an aeronautical data originator becomes aware of a change that is needed to aeronautical data or aeronautical information:
for which the originator is responsible; and
that has been published by an AIS provider:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package (other than in NOTAMS); or
on an aeronautical chart.
Note: The aeronautical data or aeronautical information for which the aeronautical data originator is responsible must be specified in a data product specification: see paragraph 175.160(4)(a).
The originator commits an offence if the originator does not, as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the need for the change, provide the AIS provider with the following:
updated aeronautical data or aeronautical information;
the date the updated data or information becomes effective.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—requirements in relation to providing aeronautical data or aeronautical information published other than in NOTAMS

content.p: This regulation applies if an aeronautical data originator provides aeronautical data or aeronautical information to an AIS provider for publication:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package (other than in NOTAMS); or
on an aeronautical chart.
Requirements for providing data or information
The originator must:

provide the data or information to the AIS provider in accordance with the requirements of the data product specification given to the originator by the AIS provider, including in relation to the standards for accuracy and resolution and timeframes; and
provide the data or information so that the AIS provider can readily identify any changes from existing published data or information; and
provide, with the data or information, a statement of any consultation undertaken under subregulation (4); and
provide, with the data or information, any consequential changes that need to be made to other aeronautical data or aeronautical information published:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package (other than in NOTAMS); or
on aeronautical charts.
Note: Compliance with the timeframes specified in the data product specification allows the AIS provider to comply with regulation 175.185.
Additional requirement for Bureau of Meteorology
If the originator is the Bureau of Meteorology, the originator must provide the data or information in accordance with the standards and format mentioned in Annex 3 to the Chicago Convention.
Consultation with aviation organisations about data or information

If the data or information will cause an aviation organisation to make plans for changes to the organisation’s operations or procedures, the originator must, before providing the data or information to the AIS provider, consult the organisation about the data or information.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—annual review of aeronautical data and aeronautical information

content.p: An aeronautical data originator commits an offence if the originator contravenes subregulation (2).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For subregulation (1), the originator must:

review, at least annually, the aeronautical data and aeronautical information in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package (other than in NOTAMS), and on aeronautical charts, for which the originator is responsible; and
keep a record of a review mentioned in paragraph (a) for at least 3 years; and
if CASA requests a copy of a record mentioned in paragraph (b)—comply with the request.
Note: The aeronautical data or aeronautical information for which the aeronautical data originator is responsible must be specified in a data product specification: see paragraph 175.160(4)(a).
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—requirements in relation to requests for issue of NOTAMS

content.p: This regulation applies if:
an aeronautical data originator becomes aware that a circumstance exists; and
the circumstance is specified in a data product specification given to the originator by an AIS provider as a circumstance that requires the originator to ask the AIS provider to issue a NOTAM.
Requesting issue of NOTAM
The originator must, as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the circumstance, ask the AIS provider to issue a NOTAM in accordance with the data product specification.
Changes to data and information to be readily identifiable
If the request for a NOTAM will change any existing published aeronautical data or aeronautical information, the originator must ensure that the change can be readily identified.
Data and information to be suitable for publication
The originator must ensure that the aeronautical data or aeronautical information included in the request for a NOTAM is suitable for publication in NOTAM format.
Consultation with aviation organisations about NOTAM

If a NOTAM that the originator asks the AIS provider to issue will cause an aviation organisation to make plans for changes to the organisation’s operations or procedures, the originator must, before asking the AIS provider to issue the NOTAM, consult the organisation about the NOTAM.

section.heading: Aeronautical data originators—responsibilities of Geoscience Australia

content.p: The Commonwealth of Australia as represented by Geoscience Australia is responsible for:
providing AIS providers with magnetic variation updates; and
providing AIS providers with terrain, topographic and cultural data, as mentioned in Annexes 4 and 15 to the Chicago Convention, for publication:
in the Integrated Aeronautical Information Package; or
on an aeronautical chart.
Subpart 175.E—Aeronautical information management—objects and structures that affect aviation safety

section.heading: Objects and structures that affect aviation safety—application of Subpart 175.E

content.p: This Subpart applies to an object or structure:
that has a maximum height of at least 100 m above ground level; or
that penetrates an obstacle limitation surface of an aerodrome; or
that penetrates an obstacle data collection surface, as mentioned in Appendix 8 of Annex 15 to the Chicago Convention; or
that is an obstacle that is required to be included on an Aerodrome Obstacle Chart—ICAO Type A, as mentioned in Annex 4 to the Chicago Convention; or
that is an obstacle that is required to be included on an Aerodrome Obstacle Chart—ICAO Type B, as mentioned in Annex 4 to the Chicago Convention; or
if AA requires data about the object or structure in the interests of aviation safety.

section.heading: Objects and structures that affect aviation safety—requests for data by AA

content.p: Under this Subpart, AA may request the following data about an object or structure:
the person who owns, controls or operates the object or structure;
the name, identification or designation of the object or structure;
the type of object or structure, including whether the object or structure is a building, telecommunications tower or wind turbine;
the geographic location of the object or structure;
the height of the object or structure;
the elevation above mean sea level of the object or structure;
whether the object or structure is marked;
if the object or structure is marked—how it is marked;
whether the object or structure is lit;
if the object or structure is lit—how it is lit;
any other data that is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
A request for data under this Subpart must state the following:
the format in which the data must be provided;
that the request must be complied with within 28 days after receiving the request.
A request for data under this Subpart may state other requirements in relation to the data (for example, the degree of accuracy or resolution of the data).
Extension of time for compliance
The recipient of a request may, before the end of 28 days after receiving the request, ask AA for an extension.
AA may, by written notice given to the recipient, grant the extension.

section.heading: Objects and structures that affect aviation safety—requests for data from owners etc.

content.p: AA may, by written notice given to a person who owns, controls or operates an object or structure, request the person to give AA data mentioned in subregulation 175.485(1) about the object or structure.
A person commits an offence if:
AA gives the person a request under this regulation; and
the person does not comply with subregulation (3) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
For paragraph (2)(b), the person must comply with the request within:
if AA grants an extension under subregulation 175.485(5)—the time stated in the notice of extension; or
if paragraph (a) does not apply—28 days after receiving the request.
For paragraph (2)(b), the person must specify the degree of accuracy of the data the person supplies.
Subregulation (2) does not apply if:
the person does not possess the data requested; and
the person has taken all reasonable steps available to the person to obtain the data requested and has been unable to obtain the data.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Objects and structures that affect aviation safety—requests for data from aerodrome operators

content.p: AA may, by written notice given to an aerodrome operator, request the operator to give AA data mentioned in subregulation 175.485(1), that the operator possesses, about an object or structure.
An aerodrome operator commits an offence if:
AA gives the operator a request under this regulation; and
the operator does not comply with the request within:
if AA grants an extension under subregulation 175.485(5)—the time stated in the notice of extension; or
if subparagraph (i) does not apply—28 days after receiving the request.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
An offence against this regulation is an offence of strict liability.

section.heading: Objects and structures that affect aviation safety—requests for data from government authorities

content.p: AA may, by written notice given to a Commonwealth, State, Territory or local government authority, request the authority to give AA data mentioned in subregulation 175.485(1), that the authority possesses, about an object or structure.
The authority must comply with the request.

This is a compilation of the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998 that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 30 June 2026 (the compilation date).
The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.
For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

The Legislation Act 2003 provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.
If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

Subpart 200.B—Exemption from certain Regulations
A parasail is exempt from CASR (other than this regulation) if the conditions in section 95.14 of the Civil Aviation Orders, as in force from time to time, are complied with.
In these Regulations:

parasail means a parachute tethered to a point or vehicle on the ground or to a watercraft and deriving lift chiefly from aerodynamic reactions on flexible surfaces remaining fixed under given conditions of flight.

section.heading: Defence Force aircraft operated by civilian flight crew

content.p: This regulation applies to a Defence Force aircraft that is being flown and operated by persons, other than members of the Defence Force, who hold commercial or higher category licences, and that is engaged in:
flight testing; or
search and rescue; or
support of aircraft development and flight test programs; or
any other activity authorised by the Defence Force.
The aircraft is exempt from CASR (other than this regulation) if the conditions in section 95.20 of the Civil Aviation Orders, as in force from time to time, are complied with.
In this regulation:

flight testing, of an aircraft, means flying performed on behalf of the contractor or Defence Force to establish that the aircraft meets all the requirements of the contractor or Defence Force after manufacture or major servicing and inspection.
Subpart 200.C—Authorisation to fly

section.heading: Authorised flight without certificate of airworthiness

content.p: For paragraph 20AA(3)(b) of the Act, an Australian aircraft that is exempt from CASR is authorised to fly without a certificate of airworthiness.

For paragraph 20AB(1)(a) of the Act, a person is taken to hold a civil aviation authorisation that is in force and authorises the person to perform a duty that is essential to the operation of an unregistered Australian aircraft during flight time if:
the person holds a pilot certificate granted by a sport aviation body (other than an ASAO) that administers aviation activities in the aircraft; and
the person operates the aircraft in accordance with the sport aviation body’s operations manual.
A person commits an offence if:
the person pilots an unregistered Australian aircraft; and
a sport aviation body (other than an ASAO) administers aviation activities in the aircraft; and
the person does not:
hold a pilot certificate granted by the sport aviation body; and
operate the aircraft in accordance with the sport aviation body’s operations manual.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

201.030 Approvals by CASA—definitions in these Regulations
CASA may appoint a person, or the persons included in a class of persons, to be an authorised person in relation to any one or more of the following:
CASR;
a particular provision of CASR;
CAR;
a particular provision of CAR.
CASA may appoint a person only if CASA is satisfied that the person has the qualifications and experience to be an authorised person.
CASA may appoint a class of persons only if CASA is satisfied that each person included in the class has the qualifications and experience to be an authorised person.
An appointment may be made subject to conditions stated in the instrument of appointment.
CASA must issue identity cards
CASA must issue an authorised person with an identity card if the person:
is an officer; and
performs functions or duties or exercise powers under any one or more of the following provisions:
subregulation 30(4) of CAR;
subregulation 33(2) of CAR;
regulation 43A of CAR;
regulation 50D of CAR;
regulation 53 of CAR;
regulation 290 of CAR;
regulation 302 of CAR;
regulation 305 of CAR;
a provision of CASR under which the person may enter premises or exercise inspection powers.
The identity card is valid for the period that the person has been appointed as an authorised person for.
The identity card must:
contain a photograph of the person that is no more than 5 years old; and
specify which of the following the person is appointed as an authorised person for:
CASR;
a particular provision of CASR;
CAR;
a particular provision of CAR; and
specify any conditions of the appointment.
Returning identity cards
A person contravenes this subregulation if:
the person has been issued with an identity card; and
the person ceases to be an authorised person for any or all of the provisions specified in the card; and
the person does not return the card to CASA within 7 days of the person ceasing to be an authorised person.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (4).
Penalty: 10 penalty units.
Display and production of identity cards
If an authorised person is performing functions or exercising powers in accordance with CASR or CAR, the person must:
wear their identity card so that it can be readily seen; and
upon request, show their identity card.

section.heading: Authorised persons requesting cockpit entry or occupation of seat etc.

content.p: The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, an authorised person requests to enter the cockpit; and
the request is for the purposes of, or in connection with, the authorised person performing their duties; and
the authorised person produces or displays their identity card; and
the pilot in command refuses or fails to comply with the request.
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
during the flight, an authorised person requests to occupy a particular seat or particular position on the aircraft; and
the request is for the purposes of, or in connection with, the authorised person performing their duties; and
the authorised person produces or displays their identity card; and
the pilot in command refuses or fails to comply with the request.

Subregulation (1) or (2) does not apply if the pilot in command is satisfied that the safety of the aircraft, or of any person or property, is likely to be endangered as a result of the entry of the authorised person to the cockpit, or the occupation of the seat or position by the authorised person (as the case may be).
The pilot in command of an aircraft for a flight contravenes this subregulation if:
(a) subregulation (1) or (2) applies in relation to a request (the first request) by an authorised person; and
the authorised person requests the pilot in command to report to CASA the reasons for the refusal or failure to comply with the first request; and
the pilot in command fails to give the report to CASA in the approved form within 7 days of the refusal or failure.
Note: Under regulation 11.018, a report in the approved form is not complete unless it contains all of the information required by the form.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if the person contravenes subregulation (1), (2) or (4).
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subregulation (3): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

section.heading: Commonwealth and CASA not liable in certain cases

content.p: Neither the Commonwealth nor CASA is liable in negligence or otherwise for any loss or damage incurred by anyone because of, or arising out of, the design, construction, restoration, repair, maintenance or operation of a limited category aircraft or an experimental aircraft, or any act or omission of CASA done or made in good faith in relation to any of those things.

Neither the Commonwealth nor CASA is liable in negligence or otherwise for any loss or damage incurred by anyone because of, or arising out of, CASA exercising powers to conduct tests under regulation 139.135, or any act or omission of CASA done or made in good faith in relation to those powers.

Decisions made by other decision-makers
Applications may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of a decision mentioned in subregulation (5) that is made:
under a provision of these Regulations; and
by a person mentioned in subregulation (4) who may make the decision under the provision.
For paragraph (3)(b), the persons are the following:
an authorised person;
an examiner;
an instructor;
the holder of an approval under regulation 61.040, 141.035 or 142.040;
a limited category organisation.
For subregulation (3), the decisions are the following:
a decision refusing to grant or issue an authorisation;
a decision varying an authorisation otherwise than on the application of the authorisation-holder;
a decision refusing to vary an authorisation;
a decision imposing a condition on, or varying a condition of, an authorisation otherwise than on the application of the authorisation-holder;
under subregulation 21.176(5) or Division 132.D.2, a decision by a limited category organisation:
to assign a permit index number to a limited category aircraft; or
to refuse to assign a new permit index number requested by the registered operator of a limited category aircraft.
Note: Section 266 of the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 requires a person who makes a reviewable decision to give a person, whose interests are affected by the decision, notice of:
the making of the decision; and
the person’s right to have the decision reviewed.
Safety of air navigation
(1) CASA is authorised to disclose information covered by subregulation (2) in the circumstance that:
the disclosure is to a person:
providing an air traffic service (within the meaning of Part 172) in Australian territory; or
carrying out search and rescue operations in Australian territory; and
the disclosure is necessary for the safety of air navigation.
Note: For further authorisation to collect, use and disclose information covered by this subregulation that is personal information, see the Privacy Act 1988.
The information is the following about an individual who holds a civil aviation authorisation:
the person’s name;
the person’s ARN (if any);
the person’s address;
the person’s telephone number;
details of each civil aviation authorisation and any medical certificate that the person holds.
Registered RPA
CASA is authorised to disclose information relating to an aircraft registered under Division 47.C.2 in the circumstance that:
the disclosure is to a person providing an air traffic service (within the meaning of Part 172) in Australian territory; or

(b) the disclosure is to an enforcement body (within the meaning of the Privacy Act 1988) and is for the purposes of one or more enforcement related activities conducted by, or on behalf of, the enforcement body.
Note: For further authorisation to collect, use and disclose information covered by this subregulation that is personal information, see the Privacy Act 1988.
Despite section 28A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, service may be effected on CASA only at its principal office at:
16 Furzer Street
Phillip ACT 2606

section.heading: Carriage of medicines—relationship with other laws

content.p: This regulation applies if a provision of these Regulations or of a Manual of Standards:
requires that a medicine or drug must be carried on an aircraft; or
prescribes a requirement in relation to the carriage or use of a medicine or drug on an aircraft.
None of the following persons are required to obtain or have a licence, approval or permission for carrying or using the medicine or drug on the aircraft:
the operator of the aircraft;
the pilot in command of the aircraft;
a crew member of the aircraft.
This regulation applies despite any other law of a State or Territory.

section.heading: Prescription of matters for definitions in these Regulations

content.p: For subsection 98(5A) of the Act, CASA may issue instruments prescribing matters for definitions in these Regulations relating to matters mentioned in the subsection.

section.heading: Approvals by CASA—definitions in these Regulations

content.p: If a definition in these Regulations refers to a person holding an approval under this regulation, a person may apply, in writing, to CASA for the approval.
Subject to regulation 11.055, CASA must grant the approval.
Subregulation 11.055(1B) applies to the granting of an approval under this regulation.
