division.heading: Transitional provisions relating to certification of aircraft and aircraft components

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by Civil Aviation and Civil Aviation Safety Amendment Regulations 2011 (No. 1)

section.heading: Certain design standards taken to be applicable airworthiness standards for regulation 21.017

content.p: A design standard for an aircraft:
that was issued under regulation 21 of CAR; and
that was in force immediately before 27 June 2011;
is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an applicable airworthiness standard for the aircraft for regulation 21.017.
A design standard for an aircraft component:
that was issued under regulation 21A of CAR; and
that was in force immediately before 27 June 2011;
is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an applicable airworthiness standard for the aircraft component for regulation 21.017.

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by Civil Aviation Amendment Regulations 1999 (No. 5)

content.p: A certificate of type approval for an aircraft, or an aircraft engine or a propeller, that was, immediately before 1 October 1998, in force under regulation 22 of CAR as then in force continues in force on and after that date as if it were a type certificate issued under regulation 21.013A or 21.029.

A certificate of type approval for an aircraft that was, immediately before 1 October 1998, in force under regulation 22A of CAR as then in force continues in force on and after that date as if it were a type acceptance certificate issued under regulation 21.029A.
A certificate of type approval continued in force under this regulation remains subject to any condition to which it was subject immediately before 1 October 1998.

A certificate of airworthiness that was, immediately before 1 October 1998, in force under regulation 24 of CAR as then in force continues in force on and after that date as if it were a certificate of airworthiness issued under regulation 21.176.
A certificate of airworthiness continued in force under subregulation (1) remains subject to any condition to which it was subject immediately before 1 October 1998.

Subject to Division 7 of Part 4A of CAR, a direction that was, immediately before 1 October 1998, in force under paragraph 25(1)(b) of CAR as then in force continues in force on and after that date according to its terms.

An export certificate of airworthiness that was, immediately before 1 October 1998, in force under regulation 28 of CAR as then in force continues in force on and after that date as if it were an export airworthiness approval issued under regulation 21.324.

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Part 132) Regulation 2016

content.p: In this Subdivision:
commencement time means the commencement of the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Part 132) Regulation 2016.

section.heading: Applications for certain limited category certificates made but not finally determined before commencement time

content.p: This regulation applies if, before the commencement time, an application for a limited category certificate for an aircraft was made but had not been finally determined.
The application must be determined in accordance with regulations 21.176 and 21.189 as in force before the commencement time.

section.heading: Application of subregulations 21.176(5) and (5A)—limited category certificates issued on or after commencement time

content.p: Subregulations 21.176(5) and (5A) apply to a limited category certificate for an aircraft issued on or after the commencement time.

section.heading: Certain special purpose operations for limited category aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies if, immediately before the commencement time, a person held a special certificate of airworthiness for operating an historic or ex-military aircraft in adventure style operations.
The person is taken, on and after the commencement time, to hold a special certificate of airworthiness for conducting adventure flights in an historic or ex-military aircraft.

section.heading: Certain experimental certificates for certain ex-armed forces aircraft expire no later than 6 months after the commencement time

content.p: This regulation applies to an experimental certificate for an ex-armed forces aircraft if:
it was in force or under suspension immediately before the commencement time; and
it was issued for a purpose mentioned in paragraph 21.191(d) (exhibition).
Note: A suspended certificate is taken not to be in force: see regulations 11.132, 21.002C and 21.195B.
The certificate expires at the earliest of the following times:
if a period for which the certificate is in force is specified in the certificate—the end of the period;
when a limited category certificate is issued for the aircraft;
when the certificate is cancelled;
when the aircraft ceases to be registered in Australia;
the day after the end of the period of 6 months beginning at the commencement time.
This regulation applies despite subregulation 21.195B(2).

division.heading: Transitional provisions relating to approvals of designs of modifications and repairs

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation and Civil Aviation Safety Amendment Regulations 2011 (No. 1)

section.heading: Approvals of systems of certification under regulation 34 of CAR

content.p: Despite the repeal of regulation 34 of CAR:

an approval of a system of certification under that regulation, being an approval that was in force immediately before 27 June 2011, continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and
CASA may vary, suspend or revoke the approval as if that regulation had not been repealed.

section.heading: Approvals of designs of modifications and repairs under regulation 35 of CAR

content.p: Despite the repeal of regulation 35 and subregulations 47(4) and (7) of CAR:

an approval of a design of a modification or repair that was in force under subregulation 35(2) or (6) of CAR immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and
an authorisation that was in force under subregulation 35(3) of CAR immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and

subregulations 47(4) and (7) of CAR, as in force immediately before 27 June 2011, continue to apply to such an authorisation as if neither regulation 35 of CAR, nor those subregulations, had been repealed; and
CASA may vary, suspend or revoke such an approval or authorisation as if regulation 35 of CAR had not been repealed.
If:
before 27 June 2011, an application was made to CASA or an authorised person under regulation 35 of CAR for the approval of the design of a modification or repair; and
the application was not finally determined by CASA or the authorised person immediately before 27 June 2011;
the application is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an application for a modification/repair design approval made to CASA or the authorised person under regulation 21.405.

section.heading: Approvals of aircraft components for use as replacements under regulation 36 of CAR

content.p: Despite the repeal of regulation 36 and subregulations 47(4) and (7) of CAR:

an approval of an aircraft component, or aircraft components included in a type of aircraft component, for use as a replacement that was in force under subregulation 36(2) or (6) of CAR immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and
an authorisation that was in force under subregulation 36(3) of CAR immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and

subregulations 47(4) and (7) of CAR, as in force immediately before 27 June 2011, continue to apply to such an authorisation as if neither regulation 36 of CAR, nor those subregulations, had been repealed; and
CASA may vary, suspend or revoke such an approval or authorisation as if regulation 36 of CAR had not been repealed.
If:
before 27 June 2011, an application was made to CASA or an authorised person for an approval under regulation 36 of CAR; and
the application was not finally determined by CASA or the authorised person immediately before 27 June 2011;
the application is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an application for a modification/repair design approval made to CASA or the authorised person under regulation 21.405.

section.heading: Use of aircraft material for particular purposes under regulation 36A of CAR

content.p: Despite the repeal of regulation 36A of CAR:
a direction under subregulation 36A(2) of CAR that was in force immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and
subregulation 36A(3) of CAR, as in force immediately before 27 June 2011, continues to apply to such a direction as if regulation 36A of CAR had not been repealed; and
CASA may vary, suspend or revoke such a direction as if regulation 36A of CAR had not been repealed.
Despite the repeal of regulation 36A of CAR:

an approval of an aircraft material, being an approval that was in force under subregulation 36A(3A) of CAR immediately before 27 June 2011, continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 according to its terms; and
CASA may vary, suspend or revoke such an approval as if regulation 36A of CAR had not been repealed.
If:
before 27 June 2011, a person asked CASA or an authorised person to approve the use of aircraft material for a particular purpose under regulation 36A of CAR; and
CASA or the authorised person has not, before 27 June 2011, decided whether or not to approve the use of the material;
the request is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an application for a modification/repair design approval made to CASA or the authorised person under regulation 21.405.

section.heading: Approval of changes to flight manuals under regulations 55 and 55A of CAR

content.p: Despite the repeal of regulation 55 of CAR, an approval of a change to an aircraft’s flight manual that was in force under that regulation immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 as if it were an approval given under regulation 21.006A.
If:
before 27 June 2011, a person asked CASA or an authorised person to approve a change to an aircraft’s flight manual under regulation 55 of CAR; and
CASA or the authorised person has not, before 27 June 2011, decided whether or not to give the approval;
the request is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an application for approval of the change made to CASA or the authorised person under regulation 21.006A.

Despite the repeal of regulation 55A of CAR, an approval of a change to an aircraft’s flight manual that was in force under that regulation immediately before 27 June 2011 continues in force on and after 27 June 2011 as if it were an approval given by CASA under regulation 21.006A.
If:
before 27 June 2011, an application was made under regulation 55A of CAR for the approval of a change to an aircraft’s flight manual; and
the application was not finally determined by CASA immediately before 27 June 2011;
the application is taken, on and after 27 June 2011, to be an application for approval of the change under regulation 21.006A.

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Part 21) Regulation 2014

section.heading: Approval of damage as permissible unserviceability under regulation 21.007

content.p: Despite the amendment of regulation 21.007 by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Part 21) Regulation 2014, an approval of damage as a permissible unserviceability that was in force immediately before 1 May 2014 continues in force in accordance with its terms.

division.heading: Transitional provisions relating to authorised persons

subDivision.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation and Civil Aviation Safety Amendment Regulations 2011 (No. 1)

section.heading: Authorised persons for regulations 35, 36 and 36A of CAR

content.p: This regulation applies to a person who was, immediately before 27 June 2011, an authorised person appointed under regulation 6 of CAR for the purposes of regulation 35, 36 or 36A of CAR (as in force before 27 June 2011).
CASA is taken to have appointed the person on 27 June 2011 under regulation 201.001 to be an authorised person for regulations 21.006A and 21.009 and the provisions of Subpart 21.M.
The appointment is subject to the conditions to which the person’s appointment as an authorised person under regulation 6 of CAR was subject to immediately before 27 June 2011.
However, the appointment expires:
when the person’s appointment as an authorised person for regulation 35, 36 or 36A of CAR would have expired; or
at the end of 26 June 2013; or
when it is revoked;
whichever happens first.
Subpart 202.AK—Transitional provisions for Part 22 (Airworthiness standards for sailplanes and powered sailplanes)

section.heading: Approvals under airworthiness instruments in force before 1 July 2009

content.p: Despite the amendments of Part 22 taking effect on 1 July 2009:
an approval that:
was given by CASA under a repealed provision; and
was in effect immediately before 1 July 2009;
has effect on and after 1 July 2009 as if those amendments had not been made; and
CASA may suspend or cancel an approval mentioned in paragraph (a) if it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
In this regulation:
repealed provision means regulation 22.006, 22.007, 22.008 or 22.009 as in force immediately before 1 July 2009.
Subpart 202.AL—Transitional provisions for Part 23 (Airworthiness standards for aeroplanes in the normal, utility, acrobatic or commuter category)

section.heading: Approvals under airworthiness instruments in force before 1 July 2009

content.p: Despite the amendments of Part 23 taking effect on 1 July 2009:
an approval that:
was given by CASA under a repealed provision; and
was in effect immediately before 1 July 2009;
has effect on and after 1 July 2009 as if those amendments had not been made; and
CASA may suspend or cancel an approval mentioned in paragraph (a) if it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
In this regulation:
repealed provision means regulation 23.007 or 23.008 as in force immediately before 1 July 2009.
Subpart 202.AN—Transitional provisions for Part 25 (Airworthiness standards for aeroplanes in the transport category)

section.heading: Approvals under airworthiness instruments in force before 1 July 2009

content.p: Despite the amendments of Part 25 taking effect on 1 July 2009:
an approval that:
was given by CASA under the former regulation 25.006; and
was in effect immediately before 1 July 2009;
has effect on and after 1 July 2009 as if those amendments had not been made; and
CASA may suspend or cancel an approval mentioned in paragraph (a) if it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
In this regulation:
the former regulation 25.006 means regulation 25.006 as in force immediately before 1 July 2009.

section.heading: Approvals under airworthiness instruments in force before 1 July 2009

content.p: Despite the amendments of Part 32 taking effect on 1 July 2009:
an approval that:
was given by CASA under the former regulation 32.004; and
was in effect immediately before 1 July 2009;
has effect on and after 1 July 2009 as if those amendments had not been made; and
CASA may suspend or cancel an approval mentioned in paragraph (a) if it is necessary in the interests of aviation safety.
In this regulation:

If an airworthiness directive issued under regulation 37A of CAR, or such an airworthiness directive as subsequently varied, had effect immediately before 1 January 2000, then, subject to these Regulations, the airworthiness directive, or the airworthiness directive as varied, continues to have effect on and after that day as if it were an airworthiness directive issued by CASA under regulation 39.001.

section.heading: Application for exemption from, or variation of, requirement of airworthiness directive

content.p: If an application under regulation 42ZR of CAR for an exemption from, or a variation of, a requirement of an airworthiness directive, in so far as it relates to a particular aircraft, was still pending immediately before 1 January 2000, the application has effect as if it were a written request made by the applicant, on that day, for CASA to exclude, under regulation 39.004, the aircraft from the operation of the airworthiness directive.

section.heading: Exemption from requirement of airworthiness directive

content.p: If an exemption from a requirement of an airworthiness directive granted, under regulation 42ZS of CAR, in relation to an aircraft was still in force immediately before 1 January 2000, then, subject to these Regulations, the exemption has effect as if it were an instrument issued under regulation 39.004, on that day, excluding the aircraft from the operation of the airworthiness directive.
Subpart 202.BA—Transitional provisions for Part 42 (Continuing airworthiness requirements for aircraft and aeronautical products)
Part 42 applies to:
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct a Part 121 operation that is a scheduled air transport operation; and
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct a Part 135 operation that is a scheduled air transport operation; and
a registered aircraft for which an election under regulation 202.181 is in force; and
an aeronautical product for an aircraft mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b).
Part 42 applies to a Part 145 organisation that is providing maintenance services for:
an aircraft mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b); or
an aeronautical product for an aircraft mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).
Part 42 applies to an independent maintainer mentioned in item 4 or 5 of table 42.300 who is carrying out maintenance on an aircraft mentioned in paragraph (1)(a) or (b).

section.heading: Election that Part 42 is to apply to an aircraft

content.p: This regulation applies to any of the following:
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct a Part 121 operation that is not a scheduled air transport operation;
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct a Part 133 operation;
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct a Part 135 operation that is not a scheduled air transport operation;
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct an aerial work operation under an aerial work certificate;
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct an aerial application operation under an AOC;
a registered aircraft that is used to conduct authorised Part 141 flight training or an authorised Part 142 activity;
a registered large aircraft that is not authorised to operate under an AOC, an aerial work certificate or a Part 141 certificate.
The registered operator of the aircraft may, by written notice given to CASA, elect that Part 42 is to apply to the aircraft.
An election under this regulation must be in the approved form.
An election under this regulation is not revocable.
However, an election under this regulation for an aircraft ceases to be in force if there is a change of registered operator for the aircraft.

section.heading: Application of subparagraph 42.030(2)(c)(ii) (airworthiness review certificates) to existing and new aircraft

content.p: Existing aircraft

Subparagraph 42.030(2)(c)(ii) applies to the registered operator of an existing aircraft of a particular type and model on and after the day that is 3 years after the approval day for the operator for that type and model of aircraft.

(2) An aircraft of a particular type and model is an existing aircraft for a registered operator if the aircraft is mentioned in the registered operator’s AOC on the approval day for the operator for that type and model of aircraft.
New aircraft

Subparagraph 42.030(2)(c)(ii) applies to the registered operator of a new aircraft of a particular type and model on and after the day after the approval day for the operator for that type and model of aircraft.

(4) An aircraft of a particular type and model is a new aircraft for a registered operator if the aircraft was added to the registered operator’s AOC after the approval day for the operator for that type and model of aircraft.
Approval day
In this regulation:

approval day, for the registered operator of a particular type and model of aircraft, means the day when the operator is approved as a continuing airworthiness management organisation for that type and model of aircraft.

section.heading: Approved maintenance programs taken to include approved systems of maintenance

content.p: For Part 42, a reference to an approved maintenance program for an aircraft is taken to include an approved system of maintenance for the aircraft.

section.heading: Approved reliability programs taken to include reliability programs included in approved systems of maintenance

content.p: For Part 42, a reference to an approved reliability program for an aircraft is taken to include a reliability program included in an approved system of maintenance for the aircraft.

For regulation 42.355, if a maintenance release that is in force for an aircraft immediately before Part 42 begins to apply to the aircraft is endorsed with information about a defect in the aircraft, the defect is taken to be recorded in the continuing airworthiness records system for the aircraft.
In this regulation:
maintenance release, for the registered operator of an aircraft, includes another document approved by CASA for use by the operator as an alternative for the purposes of regulation 49 or 50 of CAR.

section.heading: References to authorised release certificates (subparagraphs 42.420(5)(a)(i) and (b)(i))

content.p: For subparagraphs 42.420(5)(a)(i) and (b)(i), a reference to an authorised release certificate is taken to include an authorised release certificate, within the meaning given by subclause 18(1) of Part 2 of the Dictionary, that is issued before 27 June 2013.

section.heading: Maintenance certification taken to include certification of completion of maintenance (paragraph 42.745(c))

content.p: This regulation applies to an approved maintenance organisation that, before becoming an approved maintenance organisation:
was the holder of a certificate of approval that covered maintenance of aircraft or aircraft components; and
carried out maintenance on an aircraft.

For paragraph 42.745(c), a reference to maintenance certification having been performed for maintenance carried out on an aircraft is taken to include, in relation to maintenance mentioned in paragraph (1)(b), certification of the completion of the maintenance in accordance with regulation 42ZE or 42ZN of CAR.

section.heading: Reference to maintenance carried out in accordance with Part 42 (subparagraph 42.795(c)(i))

content.p: This regulation applies to an approved maintenance organisation that, before becoming an approved maintenance organisation:
was the holder of a certificate of approval that covered maintenance of aircraft or aircraft components; and
carried out maintenance:
on an aeronautical product that is an aircraft component; and
in accordance with the approved maintenance data for the component.
Note: For the definition of approved maintenance data, see subsection 2(1) of CAR.
For subparagraph 42.795(c)(i), a reference to maintenance having been carried out on the product in accordance with Part 42 is taken to include maintenance mentioned in paragraph (1)(b).

section.heading: CASA may direct making of applications under regulation 42.585

content.p: CASA may direct the registered operator of an aircraft of a particular type and model to make an application under regulation 42.585 for approval as a continuing airworthiness management organisation for that type and model of aircraft.
A direction under this regulation must:
be in writing; and
specify the time within which the direction must be complied with.
A person to whom a direction is given must comply with the direction within the time specified in the direction.
Note: CASA intends to give directions under this regulation to assist it in managing the implementation of Part 42.
Subpart 202.BD—Transitional provisions for Part 45 (Display of nationality and registration marks)

division.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Amendment Regulation 2000 (No. 3)

section.heading: Australian aircraft marked in accordance with CAR

content.p: Despite Part 45, an Australian aircraft registered before 1 October 2000 need not bear markings that comply with that Part until it is repainted if, until then, the aircraft bears nationality marks and registration marks in accordance with Division 7 of Part 3 of CAR (as in force immediately before 1 October 2000).

division.heading: Amendments made by Schedule 3 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Airworthiness and Other Matters—2015 Measures No. 1) Regulation 2015

content.p: This regulation applies to an approval that was in force under regulation 45.090 immediately before 4 July 2016.
The approval has effect, on and after 4 July 2016, as if it were an approval granted under regulation 45.060.

Despite the amendments of these Regulations made by Schedule 3 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Airworthiness and Other Matters—2015 Measures No. 1) Regulation 2015, regulation 45.100 (as in force immediately before 4 July 2016) continues to apply to an aircraft covered by paragraphs 45.100(1)(a) and (b) until the aircraft is repainted as if a reference in that regulation to regulations 45.045, 45.050, 45.055, 45.060, 45.065, 45.070, 45.075, 45.080 and 45.085 were a reference to the requirements prescribed by the Part 45 Manual of Standards under regulation 45.050.
This regulation applies to a written direction that was in force under regulation 45.105 immediately before 4 July 2016.
The direction has effect, on and after 4 July 2016, as if it were an approval granted under regulation 45.065.
This regulation applies to a written direction that was in force under regulation 45.150 immediately before 4 July 2016.
The direction has effect, on and after 4 July 2016, as if it were an approval granted under regulation 45.140.
Subpart 202.BF—Transitional provisions for Part 47 (Registration of aircraft and related matters)

division.heading: Transitional provisions relating to the commencement of Part 47

content.p: In this Division:
certificate of registration means a certificate of registration issued under the old Regulations.
eligible person has the meaning given by regulation 47.010.
old Regulations means CAR as in force immediately before 15 November 2004.
property interest has the meaning given by the old Regulations.
registered operator has the meaning given by regulation 47.100.
(1) For Subpart 47.B, the Aircraft Register mentioned in regulation 8 of the old Regulations (the Aircraft Register) continues in existence under the name Australian Civil Aircraft Register.
Entries made in the Aircraft Register under Part 3 of the old Regulations are incorporated in, and form part of, the Australian Civil Aircraft Register.

section.heading: Reference to holder of a certificate of registration

content.p: A reference in CAR to the holder of a certificate of registration of an aircraft is taken to be a reference to the registered operator of the aircraft.
A duty imposed on the holder of a certificate of registration of an aircraft is taken to be imposed on the registered operator of the aircraft.
The registration of an aircraft in the Aircraft Register continues as if the old Regulations were still in force until:
the day when CASA registers, or refuses to register, the aircraft under Part 47; or
CASA cancels the registration.
Note: After 15 November 2005, CASA may cancel or suspend the registration of an aircraft if the owner of the aircraft does not reply to a request made under subregulation 202.225(5).
However, CASA must not accept an application for a change of any details about an aircraft that are kept in the Aircraft Register, other than an application for:
a change of name or address of the holder of the certificate of registration, or a property interest holder, of the aircraft; or
the cancellation of the registration of the aircraft.
If the registration of an aircraft is suspended under the old Regulations, the suspension continues as if the old Regulations were still in force.
This regulation applies if:
before 15 November 2004, a person applied to CASA or sent CASA a notice under Part 3 of the old Regulations; and
on or after 15 November 2004, CASA had not decided about the application or acted on the notice.
CASA must decide about the application or act on the notice as if the old Regulations were still in force.

section.heading: Application to register aircraft under Part 47

content.p: The owner of an aircraft that is registered in the Aircraft Register may apply to CASA to register the aircraft under Part 47.
The application must be made in an approved form and include:
the aircraft’s registration mark, manufacturer, model and serial number; and
the name, address and signature of the owner of the aircraft; and
the registered operator’s name and postal address, and:
if the registered operator is an individual—his or her home address; or
if the registered operator is a corporation—the address of the corporation’s registered office; and
the name, address and signature of the person who holds the certificate of registration; and
the name, address and signature of each person who holds a property interest in the aircraft.
If CASA receives an application in accordance with subregulation (2), CASA must register the aircraft.
However, CASA may approve an application without 1 or more of the signatures required by paragraph (2)(e), if there is other evidence available to demonstrate that the application is genuine.

If, after 15 November 2005, CASA asks an applicant, or the owner of an aircraft, to provide information, or take an action, to complete an application in the approved form, the applicant, or owner, must provide the information, or take the action, within 90 days of CASA making the request.
Note: Regulation 47.045 of CASR sets out relevant directions about communicating with CASA.
CASA may cancel or suspend the registration of the aircraft if the applicant, or owner of the aircraft, fails to comply with subregulation (5).
Note: An explanation of the procedures that apply in relation to a suspension are set out in the advisory circular AC 47-1 which can be viewed at, or downloaded from, CASA’s website: www.casa.gov.au.

division.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Cape Town Convention) Regulation 2014

content.p: In this Division:
amending regulation means the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Cape Town Convention) Regulation 2014.
commencement means the commencement of the amending regulation.
Regulation 47.131A applies if:

CASA became aware, before commencement, that a registered operator of an aircraft was not an eligible person, but CASA has not, as at commencement, issued a notice cancelling the registration of the aircraft; or
CASA becomes aware, after commencement, that a registered operator of an aircraft is not an eligible person (whether the aircraft is registered before or after commencement).

The amendment of regulation 47.165 made by the amending regulation applies in relation to applications under that regulation approved after commencement (whether the application is made before or after commencement).
Subpart 202.CB—Transitional provisions for Part 61 (Flight crew licensing)

division.heading: Amendments made by regulations commencing 1 September 2014

content.p: Note: The regulations comprise:
(a) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment Regulation 2013 (No. 1); and
(b) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing and Other Matters) Regulation 2013; and
(c) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing) Regulation 2014.
This Division does not apply in relation to an old authorisation for a balloon.
In this Division:
amendments means:
the amendments of these Regulations made by:
(i) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment Regulation 2013 (No. 1); and
(ii) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing and Other Matters) Regulation 2013; and
(iii) the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing) Regulation 2014; and
(b) the amendments of the following commencing immediately before the commencement of the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment Regulation 2013 (No. 1):
Civil Aviation Order 29.6;
Civil Aviation Order 29.10;
Civil Aviation Order 29.11; and
the amendments of Civil Aviation Order 82.6 commencing on 1 September 2014.
approved course of training: see regulation 61.010.
Certificate IV in Training and Assessment: see regulation 61.010.
cessation time, for an old authorisation that is continued in force under this Division, means the earliest of the following:
when the old authorisation expires or is surrendered or cancelled;
when CASA grants a new authorisation to the holder of the old authorisation as a replacement for the old authorisation;
the end of 31 August 2018.
continued authorisation means an old authorisation that is continued in force under subregulation 202.263(1) or subparagraph 202.264(2)(b)(ii).
new authorisation means a flight crew licence, rating or endorsement granted under Part 61.
old authorisation:

(a) means a civil aviation authorisation to carry out an activity essential to, or associated with, the operation of an aircraft in flight (a flight activity) issued under either of the following before 1 September 2014:
Part 5 of CAR;
a relevant CAO; and
includes the following:
an appointment as an approved person under a relevant CAO for a flight activity;
an approval or certification, including a certification in a personal log book, under CAR or a relevant CAO to carry out a flight activity;
a delegation under CAR to give a permission (however described) to conduct a flight activity.

relevant CAO means any of the following: a Civil Aviation Order made under Part 5 of CAR; Civil Aviation Order 29.6; Civil Aviation Order 29.10; Civil Aviation Order 29.11; Civil Aviation Order 82.6. time-limited authorisation: see regulation 11.015.
a Civil Aviation Order made under Part 5 of CAR;
Civil Aviation Order 29.6;
Civil Aviation Order 29.10;
Civil Aviation Order 29.11;
Civil Aviation Order 82.6.
time-limited authorisation: see regulation 11.015.

section.heading: Application of Division 202.CB.1 to student pilot licences

content.p: This Division applies to a student pilot licence issued under Part 5 of CAR only if the holder of the licence passed a general flying progress test under Part 5 of CAR before 1 September 2014.
For this Division, the student pilot licence is taken to be equivalent to a recreational pilot licence.
Despite the amendments, an old authorisation that was in force immediately before 1 September 2014 is continued in force on and after 1 September 2014 according to its terms.
Part 61 applies to the continued authorisation as if it were the equivalent new authorisation.

For subregulation (2), if the old authorisation is an aircraft endorsement for a type of aircraft for which there is no equivalent pilot type rating, the aircraft endorsement is taken to be equivalent to a class rating for the class of aircraft that includes the type of aircraft.
The continued authorisation ceases to be in force at its cessation time.
Subregulation (3) applies despite Parts 11 and 61.
This regulation applies to an old authorisation that was under suspension immediately before 1 September 2014.
Despite the amendments:
the suspension continues according to its terms on and after 1 September 2014; and
if the suspension ends before the cessation time for the authorisation:
the old authorisation comes back into force at the end of the suspension; and
the old authorisation is continued in force on and after the time mentioned in subparagraph (i) according to its terms; and
Part 61 applies to the old authorisation as if it were the equivalent new authorisation; and
the old authorisation ceases to be in force at its cessation time.
Subparagraph (2)(b)(iv) applies despite Parts 11 and 61.

section.heading: Non-finalised action to vary, suspend or cancel old authorisations

content.p: Action to vary, suspend or cancel a person’s old authorisation that, immediately before 1 September 2014, had not been finally determined is taken to be the same action in relation to the person’s continued authorisation.

section.heading: Removal of conditions on certain continued authorisations

content.p: Pilot licence conditions about airspace
Subregulation (2) applies to a continued authorisation that is equivalent to a pilot licence if the authorisation is subject to the condition that operations are limited to:
flight within 25 nautical miles of the departure aerodrome; or
flight within a flight training area; or
flight direct between the departure aerodrome and a flight training area.
If this subregulation applies, CASA must remove the condition if:
the licence holder applies to CASA, in writing, for the removal of the condition; and
the licence holder meets the requirements for the grant of a private pilot licence or commercial pilot licence under Part 61.

Subregulation (4) applies to a continued authorisation that is equivalent to a pilot licence if the authorisation is subject to the condition that operations as pilot in command are limited to uncontrolled airspace and any other class of airspace endorsed in the licence holder’s personal log book by an instructor before 1 September 2014.
If this subregulation applies, CASA must remove the condition if:
the licence holder applies to CASA, in writing, for the removal of the condition; and
the licence holder meets the requirements for the grant of a controlled airspace endorsement under Part 61.
Instrument rating conditions about acting as pilot in command under IFR

Subregulation (6) applies to a continued authorisation that is equivalent to an instrument rating if the authorisation is subject to the condition that the holder is not authorised to act as pilot in command under the IFR.
If this subregulation applies, CASA must remove the condition, to the extent that it relates to a particular aircraft category or class, if:
the holder applies to CASA, in writing, for the removal of the condition; and
the holder meets the requirements for the grant, under Part 61, of:
an instrument rating; and
an instrument endorsement that would authorise the holder to pilot an aircraft of that category or class under the IFR.
Type rating conditions about acting as pilot in command

Subregulation (8) applies to a continued authorisation that is equivalent to an aircraft type rating if the authorisation is subject to the condition that the holder must not act as pilot in command of the relevant aircraft type.
If this subregulation applies, CASA must remove the condition if:
the holder applies to CASA, in writing, for the removal of the condition; and
the holder meets the requirements for the grant of the type rating under Part 61.
In this regulation:
instructor: see regulation 61.010.
pilot licence: see regulation 61.010.

section.heading: Flight review and proficiency check requirements

content.p: Subregulation (2) applies to the holder of a continued authorisation at a particular time if:
the continued authorisation is equivalent to a private instrument rating; and
the holder would have met the flight review requirements for the continued authorisation at that time if the amendments had not been made.
Despite Part 61, the holder is taken to meet the flight review requirements for the continued authorisation at that time.
(3) Subregulation (4) applies to the holder of a continued authorisation (the first authorisation) at a particular time if:
the first authorisation is equivalent to a rating, other than a private instrument rating, for which there are flight review requirements under Part 61; and
(b) the holder also holds a continued authorisation (the second authorisation), other than a student pilot licence, that is equivalent to a flight crew licence; and
the holder would have met the flight review requirements for the second authorisation at that time if the amendments had not been made.
Despite Part 61, the holder is taken to meet the flight review requirements for the first authorisation at that time.
Subregulation (6) applies at a particular time if:
an old authorisation that is continued in force under this Division was, before the amendments, a time-limited authorisation; and
the old authorisation would have remained in force at that time if the amendments had not been made.
Despite Part 61, the holder of the old authorisation is taken to meet the proficiency check requirements for the equivalent new authorisation at that time.

section.heading: Removal of limitation on exercise of privileges of private or commercial pilot licences—multi-crew operations

content.p: Regulation 61.510 does not apply to the holder of a continued authorisation that is equivalent to a private pilot licence if, before 1 September 2015, the holder conducted a multi-crew operation.
Regulation 61.575 does not apply to the holder of a continued authorisation that is equivalent to a commercial pilot licence if, before 1 September 2015, the holder conducted a multi-crew operation.

Note: Under regulations 61.510 and 61.575, a licence holder is authorised to exercise the privileges of the licence only if the holder has completed an approved course of training in multi-crew cooperation.

section.heading: Removal of limitation on exercise of privileges of class rating for aircraft prescribed under regulation 61.062

content.p: Regulation 61.747 does not apply to the holder of a continued authorisation that is equivalent to a class rating if:
the holder held an aircraft endorsement, for an aircraft covered by the class rating, that was in force immediately before 1 September 2014; and
the endorsement was for a type of aircraft prescribed in an instrument under regulation 61.062.

section.heading: Personal log books under regulation 5.51 of CAR—certain continued authorisations

content.p: This regulation applies to the holder of a continued authorisation that is equivalent to:
a flight crew licence; or
a certificate of validation for a flight crew licence.

Regulation 61.355 (Retention of personal logbooks) applies to the holder as if a reference to a personal logbook under regulation 61.345 or 61.350 included a reference to the personal logbook that the holder was required to keep under regulation 5.51 of CAR as in force immediately before 1 September 2014.

Regulation 61.365 (Production of personal logbooks) applies to the holder as if a reference to the holder’s personal logbook included a reference to the personal logbook that the holder was required to keep under regulation 5.51 of CAR as in force immediately before 1 September 2014.

section.heading: Extended meaning of licence document in Part 61

content.p: This regulation applies to the holder of a continued authorisation.

A reference to a licence document in Part 61 is taken to include a reference to the document issued to the holder by CASA showing the authorisations that were granted to the holder before 1 September 2014 under:
Part 5 of CAR; or
a relevant CAO.

section.heading: Expiry of Subdivision 202.CB.1.2 at end of 31 August 2018

content.p: This Subdivision, and the entries for this Subdivision in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2018 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

subDivision.heading: New authorisations for holders of old authorisations

section.heading: Grant of equivalent new authorisations for certain holders of old authorisations

content.p: Certain holders of old authorisations taken to meet requirements for grant of equivalent new authorisations
This regulation applies in relation to a person if:
the person held an old authorisation at any time before 1 September 2014 (other than an old authorisation that is equivalent to a flight examiner rating); and
the old authorisation was not surrendered or cancelled at any time before 1 September 2018; and
on or after 1 September 2018, the person applies in accordance with these Regulations to CASA for the grant under Part 61 of the equivalent new authorisation.
The person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of the equivalent new authorisation, despite Part 61.

However, if the old authorisation was an aircraft endorsement, the person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of the equivalent aircraft class or type rating only if the person also held, immediately before 1 September 2014, an old authorisation that is equivalent to a flight crew licence.
Grant of equivalent new authorisation

CASA must (subject to subregulations (2) and (3) and Part 11) grant the equivalent new authorisation to the person under the provision of Part 61 that provides for the grant of the equivalent new authorisation.

If, when CASA grants the equivalent new authorisation, the old authorisation would have been suspended if the old authorisation had continued in force, the equivalent new authorisation is suspended until the time the suspension of the old authorisation would, according to its terms, have ended.

If, when CASA grants the equivalent new authorisation, the old authorisation would have been subject to a condition (other than a condition set out in a relevant CAO) if the old authorisation had continued in force, the equivalent new authorisation must be granted subject to an equivalent condition.

section.heading: References to authorisations granted on the basis of regulation 202.272

content.p: A reference in these Regulations to an authorisation (however described) granted on the basis of regulation 202.272 is a reference to an authorisation granted under that regulation whether before or after the commencement of the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing Measures No. 1) Regulations 2018.

An application for the issue of an old authorisation that, immediately before 1 September 2014, had not been finally determined is taken to be an application for the grant of the equivalent new authorisation.

For subregulation (1), and despite Parts 11 and 61, if a person met the requirements for the grant of an old authorisation before 1 September 2014, but the old authorisation had not been granted, the person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of the equivalent new authorisation on 1 September 2014.
This regulation, and the entry for this regulation in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2018 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

section.heading: Eligibility for ratings—former holders of time-limited authorisations

content.p: This regulation applies to a person if:
before 1 September 2014, the person held an old authorisation that is equivalent to an operational rating (other than a flight examiner rating); and
the old authorisation was time-limited; and
the old authorisation expired before 1 September 2014.
Despite Parts 11 and 61, the person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of the equivalent operational rating.
In this regulation:
operational rating: see regulation 61.010.
This regulation, and the entry for this regulation in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2018 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

section.heading: Flight review and proficiency check requirements for certain new authorisations

content.p: Subregulation (2) applies at a particular time to the holder of a new authorisation granted on the basis of regulation 202.272 if:
the new authorisation has flight review requirements; and
the holder would have met the flight review requirements for the equivalent continued authorisation if it were still in force at that time.
Despite Part 61, the holder is taken to meet the flight review requirements for the new authorisation at that time.
To avoid doubt, the holder of an aircraft class rating or type rating granted on the basis of regulation 202.272 must meet the flight review requirements for the rating under Part 61.
Subregulation (4) applies at a particular time to the holder of a new authorisation granted on the basis of regulation 202.272 if:
the new authorisation has proficiency check requirements; and
the new authorisation is equivalent to an old authorisation that was a time-limited authorisation; and
the old authorisation would not have expired by that time if the amendments had not been made.
Despite Part 61, the holder is taken to meet the proficiency check requirements for the new authorisation at that time.
This regulation, and the entry for this regulation in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2018 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

section.heading: Personal logbooks—obligations for holders of old authorisations etc.

content.p: (1) Subregulation (2) applies to a person who, immediately before 1 September 2014, was required under regulation 5.51 of CAR to have a personal log book (the old logbook).

Regulations 61.355 (retention of personal logbooks) and 61.365 (production of personal logbooks) apply to the person as if the old logbook was a personal logbook required to be kept under regulation 61.345 or 61.350.

section.heading: English competency for certain holders of student pilot licences

content.p: Subregulation (2) applies to a person who:
held a student pilot licence immediately before 1 September 2014; and
had not passed a general flying progress flight test under Part 5 of CAR before that day.
The person is taken to have been assessed by CASA as meeting the general English language proficiency standard mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards.

section.heading: Grant of pilot type ratings on basis of overseas training and assessment

content.p: An applicant for a pilot type rating is taken to meet the requirements of subregulation 61.810(3) (Requirements for grant of pilot type ratings) if CASA is satisfied that:

the applicant has completed training, conducted by a training provider that is authorised by the national aviation authority of a recognised foreign State to conduct the training, for the grant of an overseas rating; and

the applicant has been assessed, by a person who is authorised by the national aviation authority of the recognised foreign State to conduct the assessment, as meeting the flight test standard for the grant of the overseas rating; and
the training meets the standards specified in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for training for the rating; and
the overseas rating is at least equivalent to the rating.
This regulation, and the entry for this regulation in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2023 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

section.heading: Instrument proficiency checks partially conducted by foreign-authorised person

content.p: This regulation applies in relation to:
an instrument proficiency check mentioned in paragraph 61.650(3)(d) or (e) for the holder of a multi-crew pilot licence; and
an instrument proficiency check mentioned in paragraph 61.695(3)(d) or (e) for the holder of an air transport pilot licence; and
an instrument proficiency check mentioned in paragraph 61.880(3)(e) or (f) for the holder of an instrument rating.
The holder is taken to have successfully completed the instrument proficiency check if:
a person who is authorised by the national aviation authority of a recognised State to conduct an instrument proficiency check (however named) conducts a check of the holder; and
the check meets the authority’s flight standards for a proficiency check; and
CASA or a flight examiner:
assesses the holder against the knowledge standards mentioned in the Part 61 Manual of Standards for the instrument proficiency check; and
is satisfied that the holder meets the knowledge standards; and
endorses the holder’s licence document to the effect that the holder has completed the instrument proficiency check.
This regulation, and the entry for this regulation in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2023 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

section.heading: Expiry of Division 202.CB.1 at end of 31 August 2025

content.p: This Division, and the entries for this Division in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2025 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

division.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing Measures No. 1) Regulations 2020

section.heading: Flight test requirements for 3D instrument approach operations endorsement

content.p: The amendments of paragraphs 61.640(1A)(a), 61.680(2A)(a) and 61.900(2)(a) by the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing Measures No. 1) Regulations 2020 do not apply in relation to a 3D instrument approach operation (the authorised operation) conducted on or after the commencement of those amendments by the holder of a pilot licence or endorsement if:
the holder passed the flight test for the licence or endorsement before the commencement of those amendments; and
the flight test included a 3D instrument approach operation; and
the authorised operation is conducted within the period:
starting when the holder passed the flight test; and
ending 24 months later, or when the holder next attempts an instrument proficiency check, whichever is earlier.

division.heading: Amendments made by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026

section.heading: Application of amendments relating to flight crew licensing

content.p: (1) Subregulations 61.745(3AA) and 61.800(5A), as inserted by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026, apply in relation to the successful completion of a flight review on or after the commencement of this regulation.
(2) The amendments of regulation 61.805 made by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 apply in relation to the following:
a flight test passed before, on or after the commencement of this regulation;
an operator proficiency check completed before, on or after the commencement of this regulation;
participation in an operator’s training and checking system, and an approval granted under regulation 61.040, before, on or after the commencement of this regulation;
an instrument proficiency check that is completed on or after the commencement of this regulation.

(3) The repeal of regulation 61.1055, and the amendments of regulation 61.1060, made by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 apply on and after the commencement of this regulation in relation to a person who is the holder of a low-level rating, whether the person became the holder of the rating before, on or after that commencement.

(4) The amendment of regulation 61.1080, and the insertion of regulation 61.1082, made by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 apply on and after the commencement of this regulation in relation to a person who is the holder of an endorsement, whether the person became the holder of the endorsement before, on or after that commencement.

(5) The amendment of regulation 61.1225 made by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 applies in relation to an approval that is covered by paragraph 61.1225(4)(a) and is given on or after the commencement of this regulation.

(6) The amendments of regulation 141.305 made by Schedule 1 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 apply in relation to a solo flight that is conducted on or after the commencement of this regulation.
Subpart 202.CE—Transitional provisions for Part 64 (Authorisations for non-licensed personnel)

Despite the amendments:

section.heading: Non-finalised action to vary, suspend or cancel old authorisations

content.p: Action to vary, suspend or cancel a person’s old authorisation that, immediately before 1 September 2014, had not been finally determined is taken to be the same action in relation to the person’s continued authorisation.

section.heading: Grant of aeronautical radio operator certificates for certain holders of old authorisations

content.p: Certain holders of old authorisations taken to meet requirements for grant of aeronautical radio operator certificate
This regulation applies in relation to a person if:
the person held an old authorisation at any time before 1 September 2014; and
the old authorisation was not surrendered or cancelled at any time before 1 September 2018; and
on or after 1 September 2018, the person applies in accordance with these Regulations to CASA for the grant under Part 64 of an aeronautical radio operator certificate.
The person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of the aeronautical radio operator certificate, despite Part 64.
Grant of aeronautical radio operator certificate
CASA must (subject to subregulation (2) and Part 11) grant the aeronautical radio operator certificate to the person under regulation 64.030.

If, when CASA grants the aeronautical radio operator certificate, the old authorisation would have been suspended if the old authorisation had continued in force, the aeronautical radio operator certificate is suspended until the time the suspension of the old authorisation would, according to its terms, have ended.

If, when CASA grants the aeronautical radio operator certificate, the old authorisation would have been subject to a condition if the old authorisation had continued in force, the aeronautical radio operator certificate must be granted subject to an equivalent condition.

section.heading: References to aeronautical radio operator certificates granted on the basis of regulation 202.304

content.p: A reference in these Regulations to an aeronautical radio operator certificate granted on the basis of regulation 202.304 is a reference to an aeronautical radio operator certificate granted under that regulation whether before or after the commencement of the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Flight Crew Licensing Measures No. 1) Regulations 2018.

An application for the issue of an old authorisation that, immediately before 1 September 2014, had not been finally decided is taken to be an application for the grant of an aeronautical radio operator certificate.

For subregulation (1), and despite Parts 11 and 64, if a person met the requirements for the grant of an old authorisation before 1 September 2014, but the old authorisation had not been granted, the person is taken to meet the requirements for the grant of an aeronautical radio operator certificate on 1 September 2014.

the amendments of Civil Aviation Order 20.22 commencing on 1 September 2014.

the old authorisation ceases to be in force at the cessation time for the authorisation.
Subparagraph (2)(b)(iv) applies despite Parts 11 and 64.

section.heading: Non-finalised action to vary, suspend or cancel old authorisations

content.p: Action to vary, suspend or cancel a person’s old authorisation that, immediately before 1 September 2014, had not been finally determined is taken to be the same action in relation to the person’s continued authorisation.
This regulation applies to the holder of an old authorisation that is continued in force under this Subpart.
Regulation 64.060 (Production of certificate of competency) applies to the holder as if a reference to the holder’s certificate of competency were a reference to the holder’s old authorisation.
The early expiry provisions, and the entries for the early expiry provisions in the Part 202 table of contents, expire at the end of 31 August 2018 as if they had been repealed by another regulation.

Subpart 202.CF—Transitional provisions for Part 65 (Air traffic services licensing)
A document called ‘Manual of Standards (MOS) – Part 65’ published by CASA before 1 May 2003 is taken to be a Manual of Standards issued under regulation 65.033.
The procedures in regulations 65.033A, 65.033B and 65.033C (as in force on 1 May 2003) are taken to have been complied with in relation to the issue of the Manual of Standards.
In this regulation:
old licence means an air traffic controller licence or a flight service officer licence issued under CAR and in force (or suspended) immediately before 1 May 2003.
A person who, immediately before 1 May 2003, held an old licence (including a licence that is suspended) is taken to hold a corresponding licence issued under Part 65.
A rating, endorsement or qualification endorsed on an old licence is taken to continue in force for the period during which it would have been in force but for that Part.

A licence that a person is taken to hold under subregulation (2), or a rating, endorsement or qualification mentioned in subregulation (3), may be suspended or cancelled as if it had been granted under that Part.
An old licence that, immediately before 1 May 2003, was suspended is taken, on and after that day, to continue to be suspended.

(6) For the purposes of action against the holder of an old licence mentioned in subregulation (5), the amendments of CAR by regulation 4 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Civil Aviation Amendment Regulations 2002 (No. 2) are to be disregarded.
Subpart 202.CG—Transitional provisions for Part 66 (Continuing airworthiness—aircraft engineer licences and ratings)

section.heading: Having regard to other airworthiness authorities in granting aircraft engineer licences

content.p: If:
a person holds, or has held, an airworthiness authority of the kind mentioned in paragraph 33B(1)(a) of CAR; and
CASA grants an aircraft engineer licence to the person;
CASA must have regard to the authority in granting the licence.

section.heading: Category A licence holders and certification of completion of maintenance

content.p: Despite anything in Part 4A of CAR, a person may certify completion of maintenance if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the maintenance is mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
the person certifies completion of the maintenance:
in accordance with regulation 42ZE of CAR; and
on behalf of a holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR.

If a person certifies completion of maintenance in accordance with subregulation (1), the person is taken, for the purposes of regulation 42ZC of CAR, to be permitted by that regulation to carry out the maintenance.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the person certifies completion of maintenance:
in accordance with regulation 42ZE of CAR; and
on behalf of a holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR; and
one or more of the following apply:
the person did not carry out the maintenance;
the maintenance is not mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A reference in subregulation (3) to maintenance does not include supervision of maintenance.

section.heading: Category A licence holders and final certificates for completion of maintenance

content.p: Despite anything in Part 4A of CAR, a person may issue a final certificate for completion of maintenance for an aircraft in relation to maintenance carried out on the aircraft if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the maintenance is mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
he or she issues the final certificate for completion of maintenance:
in accordance with Part 4 of Schedule 6 of CAR; and
on behalf of the holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR.

If a person issues a final certificate for completion of maintenance in accordance with subregulation (1), the person is taken, for the purposes of regulation 42ZC of CAR, to be permitted by that regulation to carry out the maintenance.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the person issues a final certificate for completion of maintenance:
in accordance with Part 4 of Schedule 6 of CAR; and
on behalf of the holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR; and
the maintenance is not mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A reference in subregulation (3) to maintenance does not include supervision of maintenance.

section.heading: Category A licence holders and endorsing maintenance releases

content.p: Despite anything in Part 4A of CAR, a person may endorse a maintenance release for an aircraft for the purposes of regulation 48 of CAR if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the maintenance is mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards; and
the endorsement is on behalf of the holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR.

If a person endorses a maintenance release in accordance with subregulation (1), the person is taken, for the purposes of regulation 42ZC of CAR, to be permitted by that regulation to carry out the maintenance.
A person commits an offence of strict liability if:
the person is a category A licence holder; and
the person endorses a maintenance release on behalf of the holder of a certificate of approval under regulation 30 of CAR; and
the maintenance is not mentioned in Appendix II to the Part 145 Manual of Standards.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.

section.heading: Validation of certain licences and ratings granted subject to exclusions during relevant period

content.p: This regulation applies to a licence granted, or purportedly granted, under regulation 66.026, or to a rating granted, or purportedly granted, under regulation 66.095, if the licence or rating was granted, or purportedly granted:
during the relevant period; and
subject to an exclusion that did not relate to a type rated aircraft type.

(2) The licence or rating is valid and effective, and is taken always to have been as valid and effective, as it would have been if the amendments made by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Regulation 2016 had been in force during the relevant period.

(3) Any act or thing done under the licence or rating is valid and effective, and is taken always to have been as valid and effective, as it would have been if the amendments made by the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Regulation 2016 had been in force during the relevant period.
In this regulation:
relevant period means the period:
beginning at the start of 4 July 2016; and
(b) ending at the commencement of the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Regulation 2016.

section.heading: Application of amendments relating to the removal of an exclusion from an aircraft engineer licence

content.p: The amendments of regulation 66.072 made by Schedule 4 to the Civil Aviation Legislation Amendment (Minor Changes) Regulations 2026 apply in relation to an application for the removal of an exclusion on an aircraft engineer licence made on or after the commencement of that Schedule.
Subpart 202.CH—Transitional provisions for Part 67 (Medical)

section.heading: Medical certificates issued under Civil Aviation Regulations 1988

content.p: A medical certificate or special medical certificate issued before 3 September 2003, under Part 6 of CAR, as in force at any time before that day, continues to have, on and after that day, the same force and effect as it would have had if that Part had continued in force.
Such a certificate may be suspended or cancelled under Part 67.
Subject to subregulation (4), such a certificate expires at the time it would have expired if Part 6 of CAR had continued in force.

The period during which such a certificate is in force may be extended under Part 67, but not beyond the end of 1 year after the day when the certificate would expire if the period had not been extended.

section.heading: Designated aviation medical examiners appointed under Civil Aviation Regulations 1988

content.p: The appointment of a person, before 3 September 2003, as a designated aviation medical examiner continues to have effect according to its terms.
Such an appointment may be cancelled in accordance with Part 67.

section.heading: Actions by Director of Aviation Medicine

content.p: In this regulation:

Principal Medical Officer means the officer of CASA occupying, or performing the duties of, the position in CASA of that title, and includes a person who occupied, or performed the duties of, the former position in CASA known as ‘Director of Aviation Medicine’.

An approval given by the Principal Medical Officer, before 3 September 2003, for the purposes of a provision of Schedule 1 to CAR, as in force at any time before that day, continues to have effect according to its terms, on and after that day, as if CASA had given the approval for the purposes of the corresponding provision of table 67.150, table 67.155 or table 67.160.

section.heading: Applications for issue of medical certificates pending on 3 September 2003

content.p: This regulation applies if:
an application under Part 6 of the old regulations for the issue of a medical certificate was pending immediately before 3 September 2003; and
the application was in accordance with that Part as then in force.
The application is taken, for these Regulations, to be an application for the issue of the medical certificate, made, on 3 September 2003, in accordance with Subpart 67.C.

If an examination required for the issue of the medical certificate under Part 6 of the old regulations had commenced but was not completed before 3 September 2003, the examination is taken to have commenced under Subpart 67.C.
In this regulation:
old regulations means CAR as in force at any time before 3 September 2003.

a particular act, event, case or circumstance.

section.heading: Meaning and effect of new Regulations

content.p: For the purposes of Subdivisions 202.EAA.1.1 to 202.EAA.1.7, assume that the following regulations (and any Manuals of Standards issued under those regulations) commence at the early commencement time:
(a) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 91) Regulations 2018;

(c) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 119) Regulations 2018;
(d) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 121) Regulations 2018;
(e) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 133) Regulations 2018;
(f) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 135) Regulations 2018;
(g) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Part 138) Regulations 2018;
(h) the Civil Aviation Safety Amendment (Operations Definitions) Regulations 2019.
(2) The new Regulations means these Regulations as amended by the regulations mentioned in subregulation (1) and any includes Manuals of Standards issued under those regulations.

section.heading: Relationship with section 7 of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901

content.p: Nothing in this Division limits the effect of section 7 of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (as it applies because of paragraph 13(1)(a) of the Legislation Act 2003).

section.heading: AOC holders to give CASA proposed operations manuals and expositions etc. before main commencement time

content.p: (1) An operator mentioned in column 1 of an item in the following table must, during the period mentioned in column 3 of the item, give CASA the documents and information (the compliance material) mentioned in column 2 of the item.

If:
